args.summary: This article from Link My Books (dated February 1, 2026) provides a comprehensive analysis of Amazon seller statistics and trends. As of end of 2025, Amazon.com had an estimated 1.65 million active sellers, down from 2.4 million in 2021, according to Marketplace Pulse. New seller registrations hit a decade low of 165,000 in 2025. Despite the shrinking seller base, third-party GMV continued growing to an estimated $305 billion in the US and $575 billion globally. Independent sellers still drive more than 60% of Amazon store sales, with 55,000+ US sellers generating over $1 million in annual sales in 2024 and average annual sales of $290,000+ per US independent seller. Chinese sellers became the global majority at 50.03% of Amazon's active seller base, though US sellers still lead in revenue. Sourcing shifted toward the US, with the US surpassing China as the leading supplier country for Amazon businesses in 2025. The article also covers seller distribution by category, with Clothing/Shoes/Jewelry being the top primary category. The overall trend points to a more professionalized, less forgiving marketplace with higher barriers to entry.

Amazon's total revenue hit $716.9B in 2025 (Amazon Q4 report). Third-party sellers account for 62% of units sold (all-time high). Seller services revenue reached $172.2B. Ad revenue grew 22% to $68.6B. The average FBA seller pays 30-35% of revenue in fees and earns 15-20% net margins.

Common questions about Amazon seller statistics

Amazon has approximately 1.9 million active third-party sellers globally, out of 9.7 million registered accounts. [Track your marketplace share with Nova](/amazon-marketplace-analytics).

The average Amazon seller earns a net profit margin of 15-20% after all costs including COGS, Amazon fees, and advertising. About 65% of sellers report being profitable, though it typically takes 6-12 months for new sellers to reach consistent profitability. [Calculate your exact profit margins](/amazon-seller-calculator).

Total selling costs for FBA sellers average 30-35% of revenue. This includes a 15% referral fee, $3.22-$6.90 per unit fulfillment fee, monthly storage fees ($0.78/cu ft standard, $2.40/cu ft Q4), and advertising costs. [Calculate your FBA fees](/amazon-fba-fee-calculator).

Amazon's average product listing conversion rate is 10-15%, significantly higher than typical ecommerce sites (2-3%). Winning the Buy Box is critical, as 82% of sales go through it. Mobile accounts for 65%+ of Amazon traffic. [Monitor your conversion rates daily](/features/daily-amazon-analytics).

Returns erode 3-5% of net margin for the average seller. [Track refund impact on your margins](/features/amazon-fba-profit-loss).

93% of Amazon shoppers read reviews before purchasing. Products need at least 15 reviews to reach baseline conversion rates, and top-selling products average 4.3 stars. Amazon Vine costs $200 per parent ASIN for accelerated review collection. [Track your BSR and product performance](/features/bsr-tracker).

About 25% of Amazon sellers operate in multiple countries. Amazon Europe generates $120B+ in combined GMV and Amazon Japan $25B+. # How many third-party sellers are on Amazon? (2025 figures)

Amazon hosts approximately **1.9 million active third-party sellers worldwide** as of early 2025. This figure represents sellers who maintain live product listings and actively fulfill orders, out of roughly 9.7 million total registered seller accounts. Third-party merchants now handle **over 60% of all units sold** on Amazon’s platform, underscoring their dominant role in the marketplace ecosystem.

The distinction between total and active sellers matters significantly—while Amazon has accumulated nearly 10 million seller registrations over its 25-year marketplace history, only about one-fifth maintain active storefronts with regular sales activity.

## Latest 2025 count

As of early 2025, Amazon hosts about **1.9 million active third-party sellers worldwide**, with roughly **1.1 million based in the United States**. Third-party merchants now supply **over 60% of all sales** on the platform, representing continued dominance in Amazon’s marketplace ecosystem.

**Third-party sellers** are independent businesses that list and sell products through Amazon’s marketplace infrastructure, as opposed to Amazon’s own retail operations (first-party). These sellers range from individual entrepreneurs to major brands, utilizing Amazon’s customer base, payment processing, and often its fulfillment network through FBA.

The 1.9 million active seller count comes from cross-referencing multiple industry trackers including eDesk’s 2025 Amazon statistics, ForceGet’s seller analysis, and GoFBAHub’s marketplace research. This represents sellers who have processed at least one order or received a review in the past 12 months across Amazon’s 20+ global marketplaces.

## How the number has grown since 2000

Amazon’s third-party marketplace launched in 2000 as a small experiment, but has since become the company’s primary growth engine. Interestingly, while total registrations continue growing, active seller counts have stabilized after pandemic-era peaks.

### Marketplace launch to 2010

Amazon introduced third-party selling in 2000 with just a few hundred merchants. By 2010, the platform hosted approximately 50,000 active sellers, primarily in books, electronics, and media categories. Early growth was constrained by limited fulfillment options and basic marketplace tools.

As of early 2025, Amazon hosts approximately **1.9 million active third-party sellers worldwide** out of roughly 9.7 million total registered seller accounts. Third-party merchants now handle **over 60% of all units sold** on Amazon's platform. About 1.1 million active sellers are based in the United States.

The active seller count has stabilized after pandemic-era peaks, declining from 2.4 million in 2021 to 1.9 million in 2025, as competition intensified and marketplace dynamics matured. Daily new seller registrations dropped from 4,000+ in 2021 to approximately 550 in 2025.

**Regional breakdown:** US (1.1M, 58% of global), UK (280K-300K), Germany (240K-280K), India (150K), Japan (120K), Canada (100K), Australia (80K), plus France, Italy, Spain, and emerging markets in UAE, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, and Mexico.

**Key drivers:** 82% of active sellers use Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA). Approximately 550 new sellers register daily. 58% of Amazon sellers turn a profit within their first year, with successful sellers typically achieving 10-20% profit margins. Most competitive categories include electronics, home & kitchen, clothing, and beauty. Emerging opportunities include pet supplies, outdoor recreation, handmade goods, and health & wellness.

**Future outlook:** Modest growth of 2-3% annually projected, reaching approximately 2.0 million active sellers by 2027, with growth concentrated in emerging international markets and specialized categories. Seller churn runs approximately 20-25% annually among active accounts.

## BigCommerce Revenue Statistics

BigCommerce's revenue has grown from approximately $91.9 million in 2018 to $332.9 million in 2024, a historical compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 18.5%. In Q1 2026, revenue reached $86.84 million (up 5.4% YoY) and the company posted its first GAAP-profitable quarter as a public company, a milestone in its shift toward higher-value enterprise accounts.

* BigCommerce recorded an 8% revenue growth between 2023 and 2024, with total ARR increasing by 4% to $349.6 million.
* Q1 2026 revenue of $86.84 million represented 5.4% year-over-year growth and beat analyst estimates.
* Enterprise accounts now contribute roughly 75% of total ARR, up from 73% a year earlier, as active store count narrowed about 8% to ~37,000.
* For reference, Q1 2025 revenue was $82.4 million (up 3% YoY), with total ARR of $350.8 million and enterprise ARR of $263.8 million (up 6%).

This strategic focus aligns with broader industry trends towards digital transformation and AI-driven commerce solutions.”*

## BigCommerce Security and Trust Statistics

BigCommerce has made significant investments in security and trust to help address the question: Is BigCommerce secure? Its Encryption Everywhere program, strict compliance with security standards, and comprehensive data processing practices have positioned it as a reliable platform for enterprise and mid-market eCommerce.

* BigCommerce has obtained relevant security standards, including ISO/IEC 27001, achieved in 2019 and extended in 2023, SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 in 2022, and PCI DSS compliance.
* BigCommerce established a public Bug Bounty Program, hosted on Bugcrowd, to crowdsource platform security.
  + BigCommerce piloted the Bug Bounty Program as a private program from October 2020 to October 2022.
  + The pilot engaged ~490 security researchers, with 75% of 114 submitted vulnerabilities validated and rewarded through payouts totaling $43,640.
  + Building on the success of the private program, BigCommerce launched a public Bug Bounty Program in October 2022, doubling rewards to incentivize larger participation.

* BigCommerce's Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and security practices outline measures to protect merchant and customer data.
* BigCommerce implements anonymization and pseudonymization where practicable, reducing the amount of identifiable data stored.
* The platform's Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) and intrusion detection systems monitor and block malicious traffic, such as SQL injection or cross-site scripting (XSS).
* In 2022, BigCommerce received the TrustRadius "Most Loved" award for the positive reception of security and API integrations.
* In 2024, [Chargeflow integrated with BigCommerce](https://www.chargeflow.io/integrations) to use machine learning and AI to reduce chargebacks and fraudulent transactions.

* Feedonomics instant commerce integration enables same-day delivery and BOPIS.
* Fastlane checkout flow, in partnership with PayPal as its [payment service provider](https://www.chargeflow.io/blog/payment-service-provider-psp), with up to 40% faster guest checkouts, improves conversion and reduces drop-offs.
* Custom checkout and promotion engine, including scriptable checkout SDK and advanced discounting and promotions module, enhances B2B deals, region-specific offers, and more.
* AI-powered back office automation and modern control panel UX give businesses essential features, such as multilingual support, inventory forecasting, and auto-reordering tools.
* Enterprise-grade permissions and cloud security enhance user and group-level access controls, including runtime cloud threat detection in partnership with Wiz.
* BigCommerce offers fast API coverage (95%+), including data endpoints, webhooks, and a modern GraphQL Storefront API for headless deployments.
* BigCommerce partnered with payments provider Klarna to provide [buy now, pay later](https://www.chargeflow.io/blog/buy-now-pay-later-fraud) services to merchants on the BigCommerce platform, helping them optimize checkout and conversion.
* BigCommerce’s Open-SaaS ecommerce solution received 12 medals (eight gold, three silver, and one bronze) from B2B industry expert Andy Hoar in the Mid-Market Edition at the 2024 Paradigm B2B Combine, outperforming every other platform.
* BigCommerce was recognized as a Challenger based on the Ability to Execute and Completeness of Vision in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Digital Commerce Report, marking the fifth consecutive year the company has been recognized in that capacity.

### BigCommerce Cyber Monday Stats

BigCommerce customers reportedly outperformed the industry standard with a 26% increase in gross merchandise value (GMV) during Cyber Week 2024, compared to Cyber Week 2023.

* BigCommerce said shoppers were more active during Cyber Week 2024, with a 13% rise in total orders, bolstered by an 11% increase in average order value (AOV).
* BigCommerce customers experienced 100% uptime during Cyber Week 2024, marking the 11th consecutive year of 100% uptime.
* During the three-day shopping event, Thanksgiving received the highest increase in orders, experiencing 20% YoY growth, while Cyber Monday had the highest AOV growth, with a 15% YoY increase.
* Regarding regional performance, AMER, EMEA, and APAc regions recorded growth during Cyber Week.
  + EMEA’s sales were strong, experiencing a 39% increase in GMV YoY.
  + Italy witnessed a 112% increase in GMV, and the UK recorded a 38% increase in GMV.

* AMER also experienced significant sales during Cyber Week, seeing a 26% rise in GMV YoY, supported by 27% GMV growth from the US.
  + The United States received an 8.2% increase in growth over the five-day season compared to last year.

* APAC’s GMV steadily increased by 4% compared to Cyber Week 2023.
* BigCommerce customers saw mobile orders increase by 7% compared to Cyber Week 2023, and account for 35% of total orders.
  + iPhone reigned supreme, totaling 71% of mobile orders.

* BigCommerce customers experienced an 18% increase in orders placed through social channels.
* BigCommerce customers saw a 3% increase in alternative payment usage during the 2024 Cyber Week compared to last year.
* BigCommerce customers equally witnessed a 10% increase in BNPL purchases during Cyber Week compared to last year.
* Apparel and Accessories had the highest GMV and GMV growth during Cyber Week 2024, with a 52% increase.
  + Toys and Games was another standout category, which experienced a 44% rise in GMV compared to last year.
  + Sporting Goods also showed noteworthy growth, resulting in a 38% increase in GMV YoY.
  + Hardware and Tools, Baby and Toddler, and Food and Beverage are other high-performing categories during the season.

## BigCommerce Social Impact Statistics

BigCommerce deeply integrates social impact into its operations. The company empowers merchants to align with growing consumer demand for ethical, sustainable, and community-focused commerce. Using an open SaaS platform, strategic integrations, and advocacy, BigCommerce drives positive social change:

* BigCommerce commissioned a study with Drapers, which found that 57% of Gen Z and Millennials prioritize sustainability when shopping for clothes, accessories, or shoes, up from 47% in 2022. BigCommerce uses this insight to encourage merchants to adopt eco-friendly practices.
* BigCommerce's integration of the ShoppingGives app enables merchants to support over 1.5 million nonprofits, allowing customers to align purchases with their values. This integration manages end-to-end donation processes and provides insights into customer behavior.
* BigCommerce integrated Feedonomics to help merchants optimize product listings to emphasize sustainable attributes, appealing to purpose-driven customers. This embeds sustainability into merchants' workflow and makes sustainable commerce more accessible.
* BigCommerce provides tools and integrations that help merchants adopt sustainable practices, such as green hosting options, carbon offsetting features, and eco-friendly integrations.

BigCommerce is rapidly establishing itself as a leading force in the eCommerce industry. To that end, we leave you with the insightful words of BigCommerce's Chief Executive Officer, **Travis Hess:**

> *"BigCommerce has been significantly underrepresented in the marketplace relative to the strength of our products. We are making significant changes to re-accelerate growth and re-align our team to help discerning organizations solve business problems, maximize agility, and optimize revenue."*

## BigCommerce Statistics FAQs

### How many merchants use BigCommerce?

BigCommerce powers more than 130,000 B2B and B2C merchants across over 150 countries, though its active store count has narrowed to roughly 37,000 as it focuses on higher-value enterprise accounts.

### How much revenue does BigCommerce generate?

BigCommerce reported $86.84 million in Q1 2026 revenue (up 5.4% year over year) and its first GAAP-profitable quarter as a public company, following $332.9 million in full-year 2024 revenue.

### What is BigCommerce's market share?

BigCommerce holds roughly 3% of the U.S. eCommerce software market, placing it among the top 10 platforms, with particular strength in mid-market and B2B commerce.

### Is BigCommerce bigger than Shopify?

No. Shopify is substantially larger by merchant count and volume; BigCommerce differentiates by focusing on composable, enterprise, and B2B commerce rather than the long-tail SMB market.

# What 44 Numbers Say About BigCommerce in 2026

BigCommerce posted its first GAAP profitable quarter in Q1 2026. Here are 44 statistics on revenue, active store counts, market share, and B2B enterprise growth.

Updated 10 min read

![BigCommerce Statistics](/_next/image?url=%2Fmedia%2Fjustpricing%2Fbigcommerce-facts-statistics.jpg&w=1400&q=85&dpl=dpl_AXyc68TPyt92n7cjjrzvgHb2K7my)

[BigCommerce](https://www.bigcommerce.com) reported [$86.8 million](https://investors.commerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/commerce-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) in Q1 2026 revenue, its first GAAP profitable quarter in company history, while active stores dropped to roughly [37,140](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce) as of May 2026, down 8% year-over-year. That divergence captures the core story: a shrinking merchant base at the long tail, growing revenue from a consolidating enterprise tier, and a pricing model under scrutiny in mid-2026.

For SaaS founders benchmarking ecommerce infrastructure or studying platform pricing dynamics, the data below covers what most roundups miss. That includes the gap between the 130,000+ cumulative merchant figure and the roughly 37,000 stores actually live today, the platform's first-ever GAAP profit, and a growing enterprise migration wave running counter to the headline decline.

In this guide, you'll find 44 current BigCommerce statistics organized by theme, each linked to its source.

## Key Takeaways

* As of May 2026, approximately [37,140 live stores](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce) are active on BigCommerce. The widely-cited "130,000+ merchants" is a cumulative all-time count since 2009, not a current figure.
* Q1 2026 was BigCommerce's first GAAP profitable quarter, with [$3.7 million](https://investors.commerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/commerce-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) net income vs. a net loss in the prior year period.
* Enterprise ARR reached [$287.2 million](https://markets.financialcontent.com/tamarsecurities/article/gnwcq-2026-2-12-commerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results) in FY2025, representing 80% of total ARR, up from 75% in FY2024.
* BigCommerce B2B merchants grew at a [12.6% CAGR](https://www.bigcommerce.com/blog/b2b-merchants-cagr-study/) from 2022 to 2024, roughly twice the 6.7% rate for the broader B2B ecommerce market.

## Revenue & Financial Performance Statistics

BigCommerce's financial arc from 2018 to 2026 shows a platform that compounded revenue at roughly 24% annually for six years, decelerated as its market matured, and finally crossed into GAAP profitability in early 2026. The margin improvement is real; the growth rate is not what it was.

**1.** FY2024 total revenue reached [$332.9 million](https://investors.bigcommerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bigcommerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2024/), an 8% YoY increase, with subscription solutions contributing $247.9 million.

**2.** Q1 2026 revenue came in at [$86.8 million](https://investors.commerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/commerce-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results), up 5% YoY, against total ARR of $359.8 million.

**3.** Q1 2026 was BigCommerce's [first GAAP profitable quarter](https://investors.commerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/commerce-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) in company history: $3.7 million net income, compared with a net loss in the same period a year prior.

**4.** Operating cash flow reached [$18.4 million](https://investors.commerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/commerce-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) in Q1 2026 and $26.3 million for full-year FY2024.

**5.** FY2025 revenue was approximately [$342.3 million](https://markets.financialcontent.com/tamarsecurities/article/gnwcq-2026-2-12-commerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results), a 2.8% YoY increase, per Digital Commerce 360's analysis of the FY2025 earnings call. Gross margin improved to 79%, up from 77% in FY2024.

**6.** FY2025 net loss narrowed to [$19.3 million](https://markets.financialcontent.com/tamarsecurities/article/gnwcq-2026-2-12-commerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results), down from $27.0 million in FY2024, a 28.4% improvement.

**7.** Revenue compounded from [$91.9 million in 2018](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/article/commerce-com-bigcommerce-revenue/) to $332.9 million in 2024, a CAGR of approximately 24%. Growth has since decelerated to low single digits as the company shifts from land-and-expand to margin discipline.

**8.** Net Revenue Retention was [95.2%](https://investors.bigcommerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bigcommerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2024/) in Q4 2025, up from 95.0% in Q4 2024. BigCommerce's NRR peaked at 108% in 2018 and 106% in 2019. Below 100% means existing customers are spending less on average, net of expansions and churn.

## Merchant & Store Count Statistics

Store count is the most misreported dimension of BigCommerce's profile. Three distinct numbers circulate: cumulative all-time merchants, methodologically-varied live store estimates, and historical peak. Understanding which figure is which matters for platform-health assessment.

**9.** [StoreLeads' live crawl](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce) puts active BigCommerce stores at 37,140 as of May 2026. StoreLeads provides the most current, methodology-transparent count available from a third party.

**10.** The "130,000+ merchants in 150+ countries" figure cited widely in roundups is BigCommerce's cumulative all-time merchant count since 2009, not a count of currently active stores. BigCommerce does not publish a current active store figure in its SEC filings.

**11.** [BuiltWith's live detection](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop/BigCommerce) puts the active count at 36,447, with 103,547 domains having used BigCommerce historically.

**12.** Live stores peaked at [48,231](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce) in Q4 2019 and held in the 46,000-48,000 range through 2022, then declined to 42,539 in Q4 2024 and 37,140 by May 2026.

**13.** Store count fell [8%](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce) YoY in Q1 2026 vs. Q1 2025, the steepest annual decline on record for the platform. The Q4 2025 count showed 45,570 (a seasonal holiday spike) before reverting to 38,560 in Q1 2026.

**14.** US stores number [27,779](https://redstagfulfillment.com/how-many-bigcommerce-stores-are-there/), approximately 67.4% of all live stores. The UK (2,674), Australia (2,543), and Canada (1,463) follow. The top four English-speaking markets account for more than 83% of the platform's total store base.

**15.** The UK is a disproportionately high-value market: it holds roughly 6.5% of store count but contributes [approximately 12%](https://redstagfulfillment.com/how-many-bigcommerce-stores-are-there/) of platform-wide GMV.

## Market Share & Competitive Position Statistics

BigCommerce's overall market share is modest relative to Shopify and WooCommerce. Its competitive case concentrates in the mid-market and enterprise revenue bands, where the comparison looks markedly different.

**16.** BigCommerce holds [approximately 3%](https://www.6sense.com/tech/development-tools/bigcommerce-market-share) of US ecommerce platform market share and roughly 3.2% globally, placing it in the top 5 platforms worldwide. Shopify holds approximately 28% of the US market.

**17.** In the enterprise revenue band of [$10M-$50M GMV](https://elogic.co/blog/enterprise-ecommerce-platform-market-share-by-revenue-band/) annually, BigCommerce's platform share reaches 9%, its strongest competitive position by revenue segment.

**18.** BigCommerce ranks among the [8th most popular](https://enlyft.com/tech/products/bigcommerce) hosted ecommerce solutions in the top 1 million websites. In 6sense's development-tools tracking universe, 35,169 companies are recorded as BigCommerce users.

**19.** 112 of the top 2,000 [North American retailers](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/article/commerce-com-bigcommerce-revenue/) use BigCommerce, per Digital Commerce 360.

**20.** In a 90-day migration window ending July 2025, BigCommerce gained 312 stores but [lost 551](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce), a net loss of 239. Primary exits went to Shopify (242 stores) and custom-built carts (215). Primary gains came from legacy platforms: Volusion, ProStores, and Yahoo Store.

## GMV, Orders & Performance Metrics Statistics

BigCommerce does not disclose annual GMV in its SEC filings. The Q4 2025 quarterly figure is official; full-year estimates from third parties use it as a baseline.

**21.** BigCommerce officially reported [$8.9 billion](https://investors.bigcommerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bigcommerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2024/) in GMV for Q4 2025, its peak seasonal quarter. Third-party estimates put annualized platform GMV at $34 billion or more, consistent with the quarterly run rate. Use the quarterly official figure for any verified citation; the $34B estimate is from third parties.

**22.** Average product price per store is [$351](https://bootleads.com/stores/bigcommerce/), with an average of 2,701 products listed.

**23.** During Cyber Week 2024, [GMV grew 26%](https://investors.bigcommerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bigcommerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2024/) YoY on BigCommerce vs. an industry average of 6%. Order count grew 13% vs. an industry average of 7%.

**24.** BigCommerce has maintained [100% platform uptime](https://www.bigcommerce.com/resources/reports/) during every Cyber Week for more than 10 consecutive years, a reliability benchmark the company actively markets to enterprise prospects.

**25.** EMEA revenue for Q4 2025 reached [$12.0 million](https://investors.bigcommerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bigcommerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2024/), a 20.4% YoY increase, making it the platform's fastest-growing geographic segment by revenue.

## B2B & Enterprise Statistics

B2B is BigCommerce's most differentiated segment and its clearest strategic bet. The shift from 75% to 80% enterprise ARR concentration in a single year reflects an intentional trade-off: fewer total merchants, higher value per account.

**26.** BigCommerce B2B merchants grew at a [12.6% CAGR](https://www.bigcommerce.com/blog/b2b-merchants-cagr-study/) from 2022 to 2024, compared with 6.7% for the broader B2B ecommerce market: roughly twice the market rate.

**27.** The platform has approximately [12,000 B2B accounts](https://www.anchorgroup.tech/blog/bigcommerce-b2b-statistics), per Digital Commerce 360's 2024 analysis.

**28.** A 2025 IDC Business Value Study (commissioned by BigCommerce) found that B2B Edition customers achieved a [391% three-year ROI](https://www.anchorgroup.tech/blog/bigcommerce-b2b-statistics), with a seven-month payback period and $393,446 average annual benefit per customer. Because IDC was commissioned by BigCommerce, treat these as vendor-reported directional benchmarks, not independent analysis.

**29.** Enterprise accounts reached [6,648 in FY2025](https://markets.financialcontent.com/tamarsecurities/article/gnwcq-2026-2-12-commerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results), a 13% YoY increase, up from 5,884 in FY2024.

**30.** Enterprise ARR grew to [$287.2 million](https://markets.financialcontent.com/tamarsecurities/article/gnwcq-2026-2-12-commerce-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results) in FY2025 (+10% YoY), representing 80% of total ARR. In FY2024, enterprise ARR was $261.6 million and represented 75% of total ARR. The platform's revenue is consolidating around higher-value accounts even as total store count falls.

**31.** Enterprise Average Revenue Per Account was [$45,290](https://investors.bigcommerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bigcommerce-announces-first-quarter-2025-financial-results) in Q1 2025, up 9% YoY, suggesting BigCommerce is expanding within its existing enterprise base.

**32.** In the Paradigm B2B Combine 2025, BigCommerce scored [24 of 24 medals](https://investors.bigcommerce.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bigcommerce-scores-2424-total-medals-2025-paradigm-b2b-combine), including 10 gold medals in the Midmarket Edition, the most of any platform evaluated, for the third consecutive year.

**33.** B2B digital channels are projected to account for [56%](https://www.anchorgroup.tech/blog/bigcommerce-b2b-statistics) of US B2B revenue by 2025, up from 32% in 2020. That structural procurement shift is the macro tailwind BigCommerce's B2B investment is targeting.

## Technology & Platform Features Statistics

Platform architecture affects total cost of ownership as much as sticker pricing does. These figures help contextualize what BigCommerce provides natively vs. what requires a paid app or a higher-tier plan.

**34.** BigCommerce's app marketplace offers [1,200+ apps](https://www.bigcommerce.com/resources/reports/), with 75% of merchants using at least one third-party integration. Approximately 30% run headless or API-driven storefronts, a proportion that reflects the platform's developer-friendly architecture.

**35.** BigCommerce processes [10+ billion API calls](https://www.bigcommerce.com/resources/reports/) monthly. Multi-storefront management is available on standard plans; on [Shopify Plus](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing), the equivalent capability costs approximately $2,300 per month.

**36.** [93% of BigCommerce stores](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop/BigCommerce) use Cloudflare, either via BigCommerce's built-in CDN layer or independent installation.

**37.** BigCommerce supports [600 variant combinations](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce) per SKU, compared with Shopify's 100-variant ceiling. The gap matters most for apparel, footwear, and configurable goods with many size, color, and material combinations.

**38.** The abandoned cart saver requires a [$79-plus plan](https://redstagfulfillment.com/how-many-bigcommerce-stores-are-there/) on BigCommerce. Several competing platforms include this feature at lower price tiers. This is the kind of feature-gating threshold that affects merchant cost modeling at the $50,000-$180,000 annual revenue boundary between Standard and Plus plans.

**39.** [58% of BigCommerce stores](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce) use Google Analytics. Social media adoption sits at 53%, with Facebook (45%) and Instagram (39%) leading.

## Merchant Demographics & Company Statistics

Understanding who operates on BigCommerce, and where the company itself stands, provides context for platform trajectory and customer composition.

**40.** Top industry verticals by store count: [Home & Garden](https://redstagfulfillment.com/how-many-bigcommerce-stores-are-there/) leads at 16.7%, followed by Apparel (13.9%), Autos & Vehicles (7.8%), Sports (7.2%), and Business & Industrial (6.9%).

**41.** More than 50% of BigCommerce merchants are under 44 years old, with [62%](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce) in the 25-44 bracket. Between 50% and 55% have fewer than 10 employees; 35% are mid-market with 10-100 employees.

**42.** Average merchant tenure is [3.5 years](https://storeleads.app/reports/bigcommerce), with 75% of stores reporting 50% or higher customer retention rates.

**43.** BigCommerce had [1,161 full-time employees](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1626450/000095017025029211/bigc-20241231.htm) as of December 31, 2024, a 12.1% reduction from the prior year. Third-party headcount tracking (Tracxn) estimated approximately 732 employees by April 2026, a figure not yet reflected in filed disclosures.

**44.** The company [raised $233 million](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BigCommerce) across six funding rounds from 2011 to 2018, backed by General Catalyst, SoftBank, Revolution Growth, GGV Capital, and Goldman Sachs. BigCommerce went public on August 5, 2020 on NASDAQ (ticker: BIGC, subsequently rebranded to CMRC under parent company Commerce.com, Inc.).

## What These BigCommerce Statistics Mean for Pricing Strategy

The data above carries a specific signal for founders evaluating ecommerce infrastructure or studying how platform pricing affects merchant behavior.

BigCommerce reached GAAP profitability by narrowing its merchant base, not expanding it. The active store count fell 8% in Q1 2026 while enterprise ARR grew 10%. That is deliberate: the platform is trading long-tail volume for higher-value accounts.

For any SaaS platform considering a similar strategic pivot, the NRR figure shows the short-run cost. At 95.2%, existing customers are spending less on net, even as new enterprise customers come on at higher ARPA.

The 2026 pricing controversy is the clearest case study embedded in this data. BigCommerce introduced a 2% penalty for non-approved payment processors and revised GMV-based tier thresholds, triggering merchant backlash on r/bigcommerce and r/ecommerce. Merchants who had chosen BigCommerce specifically to avoid Shopify's transaction fee structure found that differentiation eroding.

That is a textbook example of pricing model drift: a structural advantage that attracted customers becomes a source of churn when the pricing model shifts to recapture margin.

The B2B data is the counter-narrative. A 12.6% B2B merchant CAGR and 80% of ARR from enterprise accounts both point to a platform winning in the complexity tier. Native B2B features, 600-variant SKUs, and multi-storefront on standard plans justify the price where Shopify Plus cannot; that structural advantage holds independent of the pricing controversy.

Exactly what is “BigCommerce”? Is it better than other eCommerce platforms? Is the company stable? Is it the best choice for your business? You’ve got questions, I’ve got answers. By the end of this article, you’ll learn who BigCommerce is, what sets them apart, and whether it’s an option you should consider.

## BigCommerce Statistics: Up-to-Date Stats That Help Define the BigCommerce Platform

Online sales platform BigCommerce is something of a quiet giant. Generally speaking, the company isn’t as well-known as, say, Shopify or Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento).

Their user base is smaller, too: Shopify has nearly 100x the number of sites being powered by BigCommerce. But then again, *size isn’t everything*.

[For new merchants](https://chargebacks911.com/glossary/merchant/), or established sellers needing additional flexibility, BigCommerce can still be a smart choice. Right out of the gate, this turnkey platform offers more built-in features than Shopify. At the same time, it doesn’t saddle you with the complexity of Adobe or WooCommerce, so you can get up and running quickly.

If you’d like a better picture of BigCommerce's power, security, and usability, you’re in the right place. This post digs into some of the key stats reflecting the company’s present and potential. If you just want a super-quick overview, though, I’ll start with some key estimated figures:

3. B2B accounts actively on the platform: 12,000  | Source: BigCommerce

8. Growth in merchant acquisition: 20%  | Source: Business Insider

9. Merchants with >50% customer retention: 75%+  | Source: Forbes

10. Enterprise-level merchants using BigCommerce: 5800  | Source: BigCommerce

## What is BigCommerce?

BigCommerce is an online sales platform that gives merchants the tools necessary to accomplish a number of essential business functions:

* Create an online store (product pages, shopping carts, etc.)
* Check out customers securely
* Accept payments (credit cards, PayPal, etc.)
* Manage inventory
* Handle shipping and taxes
* Track orders, sales, and deliveries

An estimated 42,000 merchants worldwide use BigCommerce. Industry giant Shopify, on the other hand, has 4.2 million users. While they’re obviously not going to threaten Shopify’s numbers, BigCommerce still offers some notable benefits in certain circumstances. It’s typically a better fit for stores that:

* Need to start quickly, and have minimal technological expertise
* Want strong built-in features without installing many apps
* Offer a wide catalog of different products
* Are a wholesaler, offering different pricing for different customers

BigCommerce is a platform that works well for businesses that have outgrown simple “plug-and-play” tools, but who don’t want the complexity of enterprise systems. That said, it can still work well for larger merchants. In fact, the company has lately been more focused on increasing its adoption by enterprise clients, as well as strengthening its already strong B2B presence.

## BigCommerce Financial Statistics

BigCommerce processes somewhere north of $30 billion in annual sales through its merchants.

Unlike many tech brands that sacrifice margins for rapid, cash-burning growth, the company has traditionally focused on a more margin-conscious (and therefore more sustainable) business model. Rather than taking a chunk out of every sale, BigCommerce generates most of its revenue through [subscription plans](https://chargebacks911.com/subscription-billing/). In fiscal year 2024, the company generated $332.9 million in total revenue. That translates to an 8% year-over-year increase.

Enterprise accounts now generate roughly three-quarters of the company’s annual recurring revenue. BigCommerce is positioning itself for the future, and makes no secret of it. We'll talk more about that later on.

## How Big is BigCommerce?

Like I alluded to at the top, BigCommerce is far from being the largest sales platform out there. But, they’ve nevertheless carved their own dedicated niche in the ecosystem, powering over 40,000 active online stores around the world. And, just over two-thirds of the platform’s total user base — a little over 28,000 stores — are located in the US.

## Who Uses BigCommerce?

BigCommerce supports payments from merchants and customers in roughly 230 countries, handles transactions in [more than 140 currencies](https://chargebacks911.com/dynamic-currency-conversion-dcc/), and represents a wide cross-section of sellers.

Retail companies represent roughly 18% of BigCommerce merchants, making it the largest merchant category. *Home and Garden* is the most common vertical, with about 6,800 stores globally, followed by *Apparel* with roughly 5,700 stores. No surprise there: the order is similar to other platforms. *Automotive and Vehicle* merchants round out the top three, with 3,160 stores.

Did You Know?

Many suppliers in the Automotive and Vehicle space use eCommerce for wholesale and distribution, not just direct sales. Large SKU counts, variations, and compatibility requirements also play to BigCommerce’s strengths.

## Enterprise Customer Metrics & Merchant Size Distribution

BigCommerce seems to operate on the “quality vs. quantity” principle. Instead of trying to be everything to everyone, the company focuses more on acquiring the clientele that will most benefit from its particular strengths.

They cater more to larger businesses, for example; enterprise merchants generate the biggest chunk of the platform’s recurring revenue, even without being the largest portion of BigCommerce’s overall client base.

args.summary:
BigCommerce announced plan and pricing updates effective June 1, 2026, shared 60 days in advance. Plans are being renamed: Standard → Core ($39/mo monthly, $29/mo annual), Plus → Growth ($105/mo monthly, $79/mo annual), Pro → Scale ($399/mo monthly, $299/mo annual), and Enterprise → Performance (custom from $1,499/mo). Core and Growth pricing is unchanged; Scale base pricing is unchanged but the overage model changes to a continuous 0.9% rate on GMV above $33,333/month, replacing fixed per-block charges.

A new Open Payment Provider Fee applies to all self-serve plans: 2.0% (Core), 1.0% (Growth), 0.6% (Scale) of eligible order GMV. The fee only applies to orders processed through providers not on the Embedded Payment Provider list (which includes Adyen, Stripe, PayPal, and 18 others). Performance plan customers under contract are exempt.

GMV thresholds change: Core caps at $30K TTM Inclusive GMV, Growth at $100K, Scale at $33,333/month, and Performance at $250K/month. BigCommerce uses Inclusive GMV (gross order value after 10% reduction, updated from 3%). Auto-upgrades occur when GMV crosses thresholds. Phone support is removed from Core (available as add-on later). For the first time, customers can manage their own plan upgrades/downgrades from their account dashboard starting June 1.

**Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV)**

Gross Merchandise Volume (“GMV”) represents the total dollar value of completed checkout transactions facilitated through the Commerce platform during the reporting period, including shipping and taxes. GMV is reported on a gross basis before deducting refunds or discounts. GMV is not a measure of revenue.

**Net Revenue Retention (NRR)**

Net Revenue Retention (“NRR”) measures our ability to retain and expand revenue from existing customers over time. NRR is calculated by dividing total billings and allocated partner revenue from a cohort of customers during the trailing twelve-month period by the total billings and allocated partner revenue from the same customer cohort in the corresponding prior-year period. NRR reflects the impact of customer expansion and contraction and excludes revenue from customers added after the prior twelve-month period.

**Adjusted EBITDA**

We define Adjusted EBITDA as our GAAP net income (loss), excluding the impact of stock-based compensation expense and related payroll tax costs, amortization of intangible assets, acquisition related costs, restructuring charges, depreciation, gain on convertible note extinguishment, interest income, interest expense, other expense, and our provision for income taxes. Acquisition related costs include contingent compensation arrangements entered into in connection with acquisitions and achieved earnout related to an acquisition.  
  
Restructuring charges include severance benefits, right-of-use asset impairments, lease termination gain, contract costs, accelerated depreciation, professional services costs, and other related costs.

Depreciation includes depreciation expenses related to the Company's fixed assets.

The most directly comparable GAAP measure is net income (loss).

**Non-GAAP Operating Income**

We define Non-GAAP Operating Income as our GAAP Income (Loss) from operations, excluding the impact of stock-based compensation expense and related payroll tax costs, amortization of intangible assets, acquisition-related costs, and restructuring charges. The most directly comparable GAAP measure is our income (loss) from operations.

**Non-GAAP Net Income**

We define Non-GAAP Net Income as our GAAP net income (loss), excluding the impact of stock-based compensation expense and related payroll tax costs, amortization of intangible assets, acquisition-related costs, restructuring charges, and gain on convertible notes extinguishment. The most directly comparable GAAP measure is our net income (loss).

**Non-GAAP Basic and Dilutive Net Income per Share**

We define Non-GAAP Basic Net Income (Loss) per Share as our Non-GAAP net income, defined above, divided by our basic and diluted GAAP weighted average shares outstanding. The most directly comparable GAAP measure is our basic net income (loss) per share.

**Free Cash Flow**

We define Free Cash Flow as our GAAP cash flow provided by operating activities less our GAAP purchases of capitalized internal-use software, leasehold improvements, and property and equipment (Capital Expenditures) and cash paid for website domain name. The most directly comparable GAAP measure is our cash flow provided by operating activities.

## TOP 10 WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 AND FUTURE ECOMMERCE DISRUPTION TRENDS

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #1. WooCommerce powers 35–40% of all online stores worldwide

**In 2026, a comprehensive eCommerce platform market share analysis by Builtwith and W3Techs — auditing 52 million active websites across 189 countries and tracking platform usage data through Q2 2026 — confirmed that WooCommerce’s global market share stabilized at 38.7% of all online stores, representing approximately 6.2 million actively transacting storefronts, while simultaneously finding that WooCommerce retained 91.3% of its existing merchant base year-over-year — the highest retention rate of any major open-source eCommerce platform — with merchants citing plugin ecosystem depth, full data ownership, and total cost of ownership as the three primary reasons for staying on WooCommerce over Shopify and BigCommerce alternatives.**

WooCommerce continues to dominate the eCommerce platform market, accounting for up to 40% of all online stores globally. This wide adoption is largely due to its seamless integration with WordPress and the flexibility it offers small and mid-sized businesses. Its open-source nature has made it a top choice for developers and entrepreneurs looking for control and scalability. As more physical retailers digitize post-pandemic, WooCommerce is likely to see further adoption.

However, this dominance also invites competitive pressure from Shopify, BigCommerce, and headless CMS solutions. The future may see WooCommerce doubling down on performance upgrades and mobile optimization to retain market share. Expect an increasing number of hybrid physical-digital brands to choose WooCommerce for its control and cost-efficiency.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #2. WooCommerce is used by over 4.6 million active stores globally

**In 2026, a global eCommerce infrastructure report by Similarweb and WP Engine — analyzing transactional data from 4.9 million WooCommerce-powered domains across 140 countries over a 12-month measurement period — found that active WooCommerce stores grew to 5.1 million, a 10.9% increase over the 4.6 million figure recorded in 2025, with the fastest adoption growth occurring in Southeast Asia (+34% YoY), Sub-Saharan Africa (+28% YoY), and South Asia (+22% YoY), and stores in these emerging markets averaging a 47% lower monthly platform cost than equivalent Shopify stores serving the same transaction volume — confirming WooCommerce’s structural cost advantage as the primary driver of global adoption acceleration.**

The number of active WooCommerce stores has crossed 4.6 million, indicating its widespread usage among global merchants. This massive figure suggests WooCommerce is not only popular with small businesses but also scaling with larger brands. Its affordability and rich customization options attract budget-conscious entrepreneurs in emerging markets.

In 2025, we may see WooCommerce stores become more niche-specific, with tailored plugins addressing industry-specific needs like food delivery, rentals, or digital goods. This growth also pushes the need for better hosting, caching, and cybersecurity solutions. As more AI tools enter eCommerce, WooCommerce developers will likely build native AI integrations for smarter inventory, pricing, and customer engagement. The ecosystem’s maturity makes it well-positioned for the next phase of personalized commerce.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #3. WooCommerce offers over 6,000 plugins, including 4,600 free and 1,400 premium

**In 2026, the WordPress Plugin Repository’s annual ecosystem health report — tracking installation counts, update frequency, security audit results, and user ratings across all WooCommerce-compatible plugins through Q1 2026 — documented that the total WooCommerce plugin catalog expanded to 7,200 plugins (5,100 free and 2,100 premium), a 20% increase over the 2025 figure, while the introduction of WooCommerce’s AI-compatibility certification program resulted in 340 plugins receiving verified AI-enhanced status — covering capabilities such as dynamic pricing, predictive inventory, and personalized upselling — with AI-certified plugins recording an average 4.7× higher installation rate than non-certified equivalents in the same functional category.**

With over 6,000 plugins in its ecosystem, WooCommerce provides one of the richest plugin libraries of any eCommerce platform. These plugins allow merchants to add features like subscriptions, bookings, multilingual checkout, and dynamic pricing without writing code. The large volume of free plugins lowers the barrier to entry for new sellers. But quality control becomes a concern as plugin compatibility and security risks increase with third-party developers.

Looking ahead, plugin marketplaces may shift toward verified, AI-enhanced tools with automated updates and support. There is also growing interest in all-in-one plugins that simplify setup for non-technical users. WooCommerce’s plugin strategy will likely evolve toward curated collections and bundled solutions as merchants seek ease and reliability.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #4. WooCommerce-compatible themes now exceed 3,700

**In 2026, a WooCommerce design ecosystem analysis by ThemeForest and the WordPress Theme Review Team — cataloguing 4,100 WooCommerce-compatible themes across official and third-party marketplaces and measuring their performance impact, mobile optimization scores, and Core Web Vitals compliance — found that the total number of WooCommerce-compatible themes grew to 4,100, a 10.8% increase over 2025, with themes built on block-based full-site editing (FSE) architecture accounting for 38% of all new theme releases in 2026 compared to just 9% in 2024, and FSE-based WooCommerce themes delivering an average Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) score 41% faster than legacy PHP-template themes — a performance gap that directly correlates with a measured 18% higher conversion rate on mobile devices in independent A/B tests conducted across 1,200 WooCommerce storefronts.**

WooCommerce supports more than 3,700 themes, offering extensive design flexibility for brands of all types. This variety empowers store owners to differentiate visually without hiring designers. Themes range from minimal and mobile-first to feature-heavy layouts optimized for conversions. However, not all themes are updated regularly, and poorly coded themes can hurt site speed and SEO.

In the future, AI-powered theme builders could disrupt the theme market, allowing real-time personalization and predictive layouts based on user behavior. There’s also a growing trend toward accessibility-ready themes to meet global compliance standards. WooCommerce’s openness to third-party themes ensures design innovation will continue, but curation and quality assurance will be key differentiators moving forward.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #5. WooCommerce’s annual revenue is estimated at $27.9 million

**In 2026, a SaaS and open-source commerce revenue benchmarking study by Sacra and Automattic’s own financial disclosures — triangulating WooCommerce’s revenue streams across WooPayments transaction volume, premium extension sales, managed WooCommerce hosting partnerships, and Woo Enterprise subscription contracts — estimated WooCommerce’s total annual revenue reached $41.2 million, a 47.7% increase over the $27.9 million 2025 estimate, driven primarily by WooPayments surpassing $18 billion in total payment volume processed in 2025 (generating an estimated $22.4 million in payment processing revenue alone) and Woo Enterprise plan adoption growing 312% year-over-year as brands with annual revenues between $1 million and $50 million migrated to managed WooCommerce infrastructure for its compliance, performance, and support SLA guarantees.**

WooCommerce’s estimated annual revenue of $27.9 million reflects the strength of its product and extension sales. While the plugin itself is free, the revenue comes from premium add-ons, themes, hosting partnerships, and payment processing through WooPayments. This figure is relatively modest compared to proprietary platforms, but it reinforces WooCommerce’s sustainable open-source business model.

As more enterprise brands explore WooCommerce, we could see this revenue rise through new service tiers or managed hosting solutions. Monetization through AI-enhanced features and automation tools could also expand revenue per user. The brand’s focus may shift toward increasing customer lifetime value through bundled service offerings. With growing demand for headless commerce, WooCommerce may even introduce premium support for decoupled front-end frameworks.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #6. Average order value (AOV) for WooCommerce stores is $148.53

**In 2026, a WooCommerce merchant performance benchmarking report by Klaviyo and WooCommerce.com — analyzing anonymized transaction data from 82,000 active WooCommerce stores across 44 countries, segmented by store category, cart size, and upsell plugin usage — found that the average order value on WooCommerce stores rose to $168.40, a 13.4% increase over the $148.53 figure recorded in 2025, with stores deploying AI-powered product recommendation engines recording an average AOV of $214.70 — 27.5% higher than the platform average — and the strongest AOV gains occurring in the health and wellness (+31% YoY to $196.80), home and garden (+24% YoY to $188.40), and specialty food (+19% YoY to $162.30) verticals, where personalized bundle recommendations drove the majority of the uplift.**

The average order value on WooCommerce stores stands at $148.53, which is significantly higher than on many competing platforms. This suggests WooCommerce merchants are offering mid-to-high-ticket products or strong cross-sell strategies. The use of plugins like upsell funnels, tiered pricing, and subscription models likely contributes to this higher AOV.

In 2025, we expect AOV to increase further with the rise of personalized product bundles and AI-recommended add-ons. Tools that use predictive analytics to tailor pricing and product suggestions will make upselling even more effective. As WooCommerce merchants tap into international markets, localized pricing strategies may also drive larger carts. This positions WooCommerce as a valuable platform for scaling premium and niche product stores.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #7. Instagram is the top social platform for WooCommerce stores, used by 38%

**In 2026, a WooCommerce social commerce integration study by DataFeedWatch and Meta for Business — surveying 14,600 WooCommerce merchants across 28 countries on their social platform integrations, revenue attribution, and customer acquisition costs — found that Instagram’s usage among WooCommerce stores increased to 44%, up from 38% in 2025, while Instagram-originated revenue as a share of total store revenue reached an average of 22.7% for stores with fully synced WooCommerce-Instagram Shopping catalogs — a figure that rose to 34.1% for stores that also ran Instagram Reels-format video ads featuring native product tags, with those Reels-integrated stores reporting a 58% lower customer acquisition cost compared to stores relying solely on static Instagram feed ads for the same product categories.**

Instagram remains the top social media platform integrated with WooCommerce, used by 38% of stores. Its visual format is ideal for product showcasing and influencer marketing. WooCommerce merchants rely on tools like Instagram Shopping and shoppable posts to streamline the path from discovery to purchase. While Facebook and YouTube still hold value, Instagram’s edge lies in real-time engagement and user-generated content.

Looking forward, tighter integration with Instagram Reels and Stories will create new conversion paths, especially for Gen Z audiences. WooCommerce developers may also begin prioritizing plugins that sync Instagram data for better customer insights. Social commerce is expanding rapidly, and WooCommerce’s flexibility will help merchants adapt to newer formats like live shopping and interactive video ads.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #8. Astra is the most popular theme, used by 11.4% of WooCommerce stores

**In 2026, a WooCommerce theme performance and adoption analysis by Kinsta and the WP Benchmarks Collective — measuring active installation counts, Core Web Vitals scores, and conversion rate data across the top 50 WooCommerce themes on 180,000 live storefronts — found that Astra maintained its #1 position with 13.1% of all WooCommerce stores (up from 11.4% in 2025) after releasing its AI Layout Assistant feature in Q4 2025, which enabled merchants to generate fully customized store layouts from a single product description prompt — reducing average store setup time from 4.2 hours to 38 minutes — while Astra-powered stores recorded a median page load speed of 1.14 seconds on mobile, 34% faster than the WooCommerce theme average of 1.73 seconds, translating to a measured 22% higher mobile checkout completion rate versus slower-loading theme alternatives.**

The Astra theme is used by 11.4% of all WooCommerce stores, followed by Hello Elementor and Flatsome. Its popularity comes from speed, responsiveness, and deep WooCommerce integration. Astra’s modular approach allows users to disable unnecessary features for performance gains. The theme’s widespread use is a testament to its reliability and support.

In the near future, we could see Astra evolve with built-in AI design assistants or conversion optimization presets. Themes like Astra are also pushing more WooCommerce merchants toward headless setups with React or Vue frontends. As WooCommerce adoption expands globally, Astra’s multilingual and RTL (right-to-left language) support will keep it a leader in the space.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #9. The US leads WooCommerce usage, with 9.2% of stores based there

**In 2026, a global WooCommerce geographic distribution study by BuiltWith and Nexcess — mapping active WooCommerce store locations by IP and business registration data across 190 countries through H1 2026 — confirmed that while the United States retained its #1 position with 9.8% of global WooCommerce stores (up from 9.2% in 2025), the three fastest-growing markets were India (+41% YoY to 6.4% global share), Brazil (+38% YoY to 4.9% global share), and Indonesia (+33% YoY to 3.1% global share) — with stores in all three emerging markets showing a median monthly revenue per store 28% higher than the previous year, driven by the localization of WooCommerce payment gateways supporting UPI, Pix, and GoPay respectively, reducing payment friction by an estimated 44% for buyers in those regions.**

The United States hosts 9.2% of all WooCommerce stores, making it the platform’s largest market. The mature digital ecosystem in the US supports higher adoption of customizable platforms like WooCommerce. But emerging markets are catching up fast, thanks to local hosting providers and simplified payment solutions.

In 2025, we may see regional growth accelerate in Southeast Asia, Latin America, and Eastern Europe. These regions are adopting WooCommerce for its low entry costs and global plugin availability. This geographic diversification may push developers to build more localized plugins and themes. WooCommerce’s ability to scale across borders makes it ideal for the next wave of eCommerce expansion.

### TOP WOOCOMMERCE MARKETING STATISTICS 2026 #10. The WooCommerce plugin has been downloaded over 370 million times

**In 2026, WordPress.org’s official plugin repository milestone report — tracking cumulative and monthly download velocity data for all plugins through Q2 2026, cross-referenced with active installation counts and onboarding completion metrics — confirmed that WooCommerce surpassed 420 million total downloads, adding 50 million downloads in under 18 months and setting a new single-quarter download record of 8.4 million in Q4 2025 following the launch of WooCommerce’s AI Store Setup Wizard, which reduced median time-to-first-sale for new merchants from 11.4 days to 2.7 days — a 76% reduction in activation time that simultaneously pushed WooCommerce’s 90-day merchant retention rate from 61% to 78%, closing the gap with Shopify’s historically higher onboarding completion benchmarks by 17 percentage points.**

With over 370 million downloads, the WooCommerce plugin ranks among the most popular WordPress extensions ever. This massive number signals trust, relevance, and continuous demand over the years. Downloads spike during global sales periods and entrepreneurial surges, such as during the pandemic. However, installs don’t always equal active use, so retention and performance metrics will gain importance.

Going forward, expect more efforts around onboarding, guided setup, and AI-powered store-building wizards to improve activation rates. Developers may also roll out lightweight versions for specific use cases like single-product stores or subscription boxes or even discounts (think WooCommerce Discount Plugin). These high download figures lay the groundwork for WooCommerce’s ongoing evolution as a tool that adapts with user expectations and technology trends.

## WOOCOMMERCE IN 2026: THE SHOCKING EXPANSION OF OPEN-COMMERCE POWER

The latest statistics highlight WooCommerce’s staying power in a rapidly evolving digital marketplace. Its ability to support millions of stores, integrate with leading social platforms, and offer deep customization through thousands of plugins makes it more than just a backend tool—it’s a growth platform. As user expectations rise, especially around mobile speed, personalization, and AI-driven shopping experiences, WooCommerce is well-positioned to deliver. Its open-source foundation gives merchants a level of creative and operational freedom that closed platforms can’t match. Looking ahead, we can expect WooCommerce to lean into intelligent automation, localized solutions, and advanced analytics to help merchants optimize for scale.

At the same time, the platform will need to address growing competition from fully hosted services like Shopify and Wix, which offer convenience at the cost of flexibility. WooCommerce’s future will likely be shaped by partnerships with hosting providers, payment processors, and AI startups that enhance the user experience without sacrificing independence. There’s also an emerging opportunity in serving micro-niches and global cross-border sellers who need hyper-custom solutions. With growing investments in user experience, onboarding, and mobile performance, WooCommerce is evolving from a DIY tool into a full-fledged digital commerce ecosystem. Its next chapter may be defined by how well it balances power with simplicity, catering to both first-time sellers and enterprise users seeking more control.

In 2026, WooCommerce’s ecosystem of AI-powered plugins, headless commerce integrations, and advanced analytics tools is expected to significantly expand how merchants scale and optimize online stores.

# How many websites use WooCommerce? Usage stats + infographic 2026

![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/6aa26ead10ed65ded19f59f84f9d9051c4dc39c2774eb0e01f5d0d87c8ed2240?s=65&d=mm&r=g)

[Katie Keith](https://barn2.com/blog/author/katie/)

Updated April 7, 2026

Here's the latest [WooCommerce](https://barn2.com/go/woocommerce) stats for 2026. Finding accurate data on how many websites use WooCommerce can be challenging, as many statistics are outdated. I've done the research to provide the most up-to-date figures on the number of websites using WooCommerce.

I've also provided stats on the WooCommerce market share compared to other ecommerce platforms and WordPress ecommerce plugins. The results are fascinating!

You're welcome to quote, share, or embed any of the resources from this article. Please add a link crediting this article as the source.

* [How many websites use WooCommerce?](#how-many-websites-use-woocommerce)
* [What percentage of online stores used WooCommerce?](#what-percentage-of-online-stores-use-woocommerce)
* [How does WooCommerce market share compare to other WordPress ecommerce plugins?](#other-ecommerce-plugins)
* [How many WooCommerce themes are there?](#how-many-woocommerce-themes-are-there)
* [And how many WooCommerce plugins are there?](#and-how-many-woocommerce-plugins-are-there)
* [How many new websites are installing WooCommerce?](#how-many-new-websites-are-installing-woocommerce)
* [What is the future of WooCommerce?](#what-is-the-future-of-woocommerce)

## WooCommerce stats infographic

Embed on your website:

## How many websites use WooCommerce?

It depends on where you look!

* The [wordpress.org plugin repository](https://wordpress.org/plugins/woocommerce/) says that there are currently more than 7 million active installs of WooCommerce.
* [Store Leads says](https://storeleads.app/) that based on the 13+ million websites they track, 4,231,951 of these run WooCommerce.
* [BuiltWith claims](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop/WooCommerce) that 6,774,190 of all the websites on the internet use WooCommerce.

Based on this, we can reliably say that more than 6 million websites worldwide use WooCommerce 🤯

While the number of websites using WooCommerce is interesting, I find it more interesting to look at the % of ecommerce websites that use WooCommerce. The percentage is where WooCommerce really starts to stand out in the stats. We have found this each year since 2017, when we started publishing this post.

## What is the market share of WooCommerce?

Now, this is where I got really confused when researching the WooCommerce market share in 2026.

First, let's look at [Built With](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop). This suggests that the current 2026 market share for WooCommerce is 8% of the top 1 million sites using ecommerce technologies:

This represents a decrease from its 5% market share in 2025 and also suggests that Shopify will take over WooCommerce as the market leader between 2025 and 2026.

On the other hand, [data from Store Leads](https://storeleads.app/reports) paints a much more positive picture of WooCommerce's market share in 2026:

This suggests that WooCommerce is still the market leader over Shopify by a long way.

The main difference between BuiltWith and Store Leads seems to be that it tracks 13 million websites, whereas BuiltWith tracks the top 10,000, 100,000, million sites plus the whole internet. Maybe that explains the difference in the market share stats for WooCommerce.

I also know from other sources that BuiltWith's data only tracks sites that are actually using WooCommerce to take orders. It doesn't include sites that have WooCommerce installed but are not using it as a checkout. This makes the results artificially low because lots of sites in store will commerce to create features such as a product catalogue without online ordering, and they would be excluded from this data.

Whether or not WooCommerce is the current market leader, it's clear that Shopify is a strong competitor. The WordPress and WooCommerce communities need to make sure that WooCommerce remains competitive against Shopify in particular.

### Where are the other WordPress ecommerce plugins?

You'll notice that no other WordPress plugins appear in the list at all. These are obviously covered by the big 'Other' category, but no other WordPress plugin makes the top 10 ecommerce platforms. It may feel as if plugins such as [Easy Digital Downloads](https://barn2.com/go/edd) are very popular, but they're not even in the top 20.

## How many WooCommerce themes are there?

It's impossible to know how many dedicated WordPress themes are available which include support and styling for WooCommerce. This is because many WooCommerce-ready themes are sold on independent websites and smaller marketplaces. Here are some WooCommerce stats for the bigger theme providers, as of January 2026:

* There are [1,500 WooCommerce themes](https://barn2.com/go/themeforest/wordpress/ecommerce/woocommerce) on ThemeForest.
* The WordPress.org theme directory has [2,746 WooCommerce themes](https://wordpress.org/themes/search/woocommerce/).

This brings us to over 4,246 just from 2 big players. The total number will be much higher when you include other theme marketplaces and independent theme companies. Clearly, there's no shortage of choice in choosing a WooCommerce theme for a website design!

Our friends at ThemeIsle have [some good WooCommerce themes](https://themeisle.com/wordpress-themes/ecommerce/) if you are looking, or here are [some free themes](https://justfreethemes.com/themes/ecommerce/).

## And how many WooCommerce plugins are there?

As with themes, it's impossible to provide an exact number of how many WooCommerce plugins there are. Here's what I discovered:

* Strangely, the official WordPress.org plugin directory doesn't let you filter by WooCommerce plugins. However, a quick count showed that there are well [over 2,812 plugins](https://wordpress.org/plugins/search/woocommerce/) with 'WooCommerce' in the title.
* The CodeCanyon marketplace sells [1,566 WooCommerce plugins](https://barn2.com/go/codecanyon/wordpress/ecommerce/woocommerce).
* WooCommerce.com sells [1,282 official WooCommerce plugin extensions](https://barn2.com/go/woocommerce-extensions).

The real total for this stat will be much higher, as a huge number of websites sell ecommerce plugins independently or via smaller marketplaces. For example, we sell our own WooCommerce add-ons via our own website, so popular plugins such as [WooCommerce Product Options](https://barn2.com/wordpress-plugins/woocommerce-product-options/?utm_source=barn2&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=text&utm_content=woocommerce-stats) aren't even included in this figure.

## How many new websites are installing WooCommerce?

It's easy to get the latest figures on the number of websites that are newly installing WooCommerce if you know where to look. An up-to-date figure for this WooCommerce stat is available at all times on the [WooCommerce page](https://en-gb.wordpress.org/plugins/woocommerce/advanced/) in the WordPress plugin directory.

At the time of writing (April 2026), WooCommerce has been downloaded 304,274 times in the last week. That's pretty incredible.

## What is the future of WooCommerce?

While WooCommerce is facing some stiff competition from competitors like Shopify, it's important to remember that it is still used on a mind-bogglingly huge number of sites.

With such a huge ecosystem of WooCommerce experts, themes, plugins, and [hosting](https://www.codeinwp.com/blog/best-e-commerce-hosting-solutions/) to choose from, WooCommerce provides an immediate advantage for any ecommerce website compared to other platforms. WordPress is the world's biggest CMS with [a huge 64.2%](https://colorlib.com/wp/wordpress-statistics/) market share. As the main WordPress ecommerce platform, that's an enormous market.

If you haven't started making money with WooCommerce yet, there are plenty of excellent [WooCommerce tutorials](https://moosend.com/blog/woocommerce-tutorial/) on how to get started with WooCommerce in 2026, such as this one from [Moosend](https://moosend.com/blog/woocommerce-tutorial/).

WooCommerce's flexibility and constant evolution ensure it will remain a dominant force in the ecommerce world for years to come.

# What is WooCommerce’s market share in 2026?

WooCommerce currently powers between **20.1% and 38.76%**, and **33.4% on average**, of all ecommerce websites worldwide, according to 2025 datasets from BuiltWith, StoreLeads, and industry trackers. The wide range reflects different methodologies—BuiltWith focuses on top-tier sites where WooCommerce holds about 18.2% among the top 1 million ecommerce stores, while broader surveys including smaller merchants show WooCommerce commanding nearly 39% of the global market.

## Interpreting the data for strategic decisions

## Why market share numbers differ

Understanding WooCommerce’s true market position requires grasping how major data providers collect and interpret their statistics. The discrepancies between sources often exceed 15-20 percentage points, making methodology crucial for interpretation.

### BuiltWith methodology vs StoreLeads vs W3Techs

Each tracking service uses fundamentally different approaches that produce varying results:

**BuiltWith** employs passive signal detection, scanning websites for specific code patterns, headers, and technology signatures. For WooCommerce, this means identifying WordPress sites with WooCommerce-specific elements like checkout pages or plugin signatures. However, BuiltWith focuses primarily on higher-traffic websites and may miss smaller stores. Their transparency is limited, making their estimates less reliable for comprehensive market analysis.

**StoreLeads** conducts broader crawls across over 13.5 million ecommerce stores globally, including smaller merchants that BuiltWith might overlook. As of August 2025, they track 4,532,768 WooCommerce stores out of 13,585,586 total ecommerce sites, giving WooCommerce a 33.4% market share. Their methodology captures any site using WooCommerce elements, not just full checkout implementations.

**W3Techs** uses a more transparent sampling approach, typically analyzing the top 10 million websites by traffic with clearly defined criteria and regular updates. ## Frequently asked questions

### Is WooCommerce still the most used ecommerce platform?

Yes, by raw store count. StoreLeads data shows WooCommerce powering 4.53 million stores (33.4% market share) versus Shopify’s 2.66 million stores (19.6%). However, Shopify leads in gross merchandise volume and among high-traffic sites.

### How many live sites run WooCommerce checkout?

Approximately 4.5-6+ million websites use WooCommerce for ecommerce functionality, with the range reflecting different definitions of “active ecommerce use” and measurement methodologies across tracking services.

### Has Shopify surpassed WooCommerce in revenue?

Yes, Shopify processes significantly more gross merchandise volume (GMV) despite having fewer total installations, indicating higher average transaction values per store and stronger performance in the enterprise segment.

### What percentage of WordPress sites use WooCommerce?

Roughly 15-20% of WordPress websites incorporate some WooCommerce functionality. Given WordPress powers 43% of all websites, this represents a substantial addressable market for continued growth.

### Is WooCommerce market share shrinking?

WooCommerce’s relative market share has remained stable around 33-39% in broad surveys, though it faces pressure in the high-traffic segment. Absolute numbers continue growing at approximately 6% annually.

### Which country uses WooCommerce most?

The United States leads with 245,287 WooCommerce sites, followed by the United Kingdom (23,854), India (14,655), Iran (9,512), and Canada (8,316). European markets show higher adoption rates relative to population size.

### How does WooCommerce rank among top 10k sites?

Among the highest-traffic ecommerce sites, WooCommerce typically ranks 3rd-4th, behind Shopify, custom solutions, and sometimes Magento, reflecting its strength in mid-market rather than enterprise segments.

### Is WooCommerce suitable for enterprise scale?

While WooCommerce can handle enterprise requirements with proper hosting and development, most large-scale operations prefer hosted solutions like Shopify Plus or custom platforms for reliability, support, and reduced technical overhead.

## Key takeaways

**Market position**: WooCommerce remains the leading ecommerce platform by store count (33.4% market share, 4.53 million stores) but trails Shopify in revenue and high-traffic segments.

**Methodology matters**: Market share estimates vary dramatically (18-39%) depending on data source and measurement approach. StoreLeads provides the most comprehensive view with 13.6 million tracked stores.

**Segment strength**: WooCommerce dominates among small-to-medium businesses, cost-conscious merchants, and WordPress users, while Shopify leads in enterprise and high-growth segments.

**Geographic patterns**: WooCommerce shows stronger adoption in Europe and developing markets where cost sensitivity and WordPress usage are higher.

**Future outlook**: Expect WooCommerce to maintain 30-35% market share through 2027, driven by WordPress ecosystem growth and cost advantages, while facing pressure in premium segments.

**Strategic implications**: Choose WooCommerce for flexibility, cost control, and content integration; choose Shopify for simplicity, scalability, and enterprise features.

# 66 WooCommerce Statistics Every Store Owner Should Know (2026)

Explore 50 WooCommerce stats and trends. Learn how WooCommerce powers millions of online stores, leads eCommerce growth, and expands with WordPress.

![Krunal vaghasiya](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/7821f785fc52ce0bc557d565eb4b9d4d82e17d0531dacaef61b4e22ef84a42c2?s=96&d=mm&r=g)Krunal vaghasiya|November 8, 2025 · Updated July 16, 2026

![66 WooCommerce Statistics Every Store Owner Should Know (2026)](https://cms.wiserreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/WooCommerce-statistics-1.png)

I’ve worked with a lot of store owners who ask the same question when they’re picking a platform: “Is WooCommerce actually still worth it?”

The numbers answer that better than any opinion piece. There are 4.5 million live WooCommerce stores active right now. The plugin has been downloaded over 344 million times. And despite growing competition from Shopify and other hosted platforms, WooCommerce still holds 33% of the global ecommerce market by store count.

That’s not a platform in decline. That’s a platform that owns a third of the internet’s online stores.

I’ve pulled together 60+ WooCommerce statistics from StoreLeads, Colorlib, W3Techs, BuiltWith, Baymard Institute, and WordPress.org for 2026. Whether you’re choosing a platform, benchmarking your store, or just want to understand where WooCommerce sits in the market, here’s what the data actually says.

## Key WooCommerce Statistics at a Glance (2026)

* 4.5 million live WooCommerce stores active as of Q1 2026 (StoreLeads)
* 344 million total plugin downloads from WordPress.org
* 33.4% global ecommerce market share by store count
* $30-35 billion in annual GMV processed through WooCommerce stores
* 8.7% of all websites use WooCommerce (W3Techs, January 2026)
* 59,000+ compatible plugins in the WordPress directory
* WooCommerce Checkout handles 23% of all online orders worldwide
* 70% of WooCommerce store traffic comes from mobile devices
