<webpage_content>
# Shopify Pricing Plans Compared: What Each Tier Really Costs

Use`←``→`keys to navigate posts

![Faisal Hourani](/images/faisal-hourani.webp)Faisal Hourani· Founder & eCommerce Growth Strategist

April 5, 2026Updated August 16, 202615 min read

![Faisal Hourani, WebMedic founder](/images/faisal-hourani.webp)

### Audit your Shopify store in 90 minutes. The exact 47-point list we use on every engagement.

Print it, work top to bottom. Most stores fail 18 of 47 on the first run.

Same checklist used on 80+ Shopify audits since 2016. No tools needed — just the PDF.

PDF in your inbox in 30 seconds. 1 email. No follow-up unless you ask.

*The real cost is not the monthly fee. It is the transaction fees you are ignoring.*

## What Are Shopify's Pricing Plans in 2026?

Five plans. Big price gaps.

> **Shopify offers five pricing plans in 2026: Starter ($5/month), Basic ($39/month), Grow ($105/month), Advanced ($399/month), and Plus (from $2,300/month). Each tier reduces credit card and transaction fees, so the cheapest monthly plan is not always the cheapest total cost. According to [Shopify's official pricing page](https://www.shopify.com/pricing), the break-even between Basic and Grow sits around $7,500/month in sales.**

Shopify pricing is a tiered subscription model where you pay a fixed monthly fee plus variable transaction fees on every sale. The monthly fee gets the headlines. The transaction fees determine the actual cost.

Most store owners pick Basic because it is the cheapest upfront. That makes sense at low volume. But the moment your revenue crosses a threshold, the higher monthly fee of the Grow or Advanced plan saves you money through lower per-transaction rates.

Here is the full picture.

### Shopify Pricing Comparison: All Five Plans at a Glance

| Plan | Monthly Price | Annual Price (per month) | Credit Card Rate (Online) | Transaction Fee (3rd-party gateway) | Staff Accounts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Starter** | $5 | $5 | 5% + 30¢ | 5% | 1 |
| **Basic** | $39 | $29 | 2.9% + 30¢ | 2% | 2 |
| **Grow** | $105 | $79 | 2.7% + 30¢ | 1% | 5 |
| **Advanced** | $399 | $299 | 2.5% + 30¢ | 0.6% | 15 |
| **Plus** | $2,300 | $2,300 | 2.15% + 30¢ | 0% (Shopify Payments) | Unlimited |

*Source: [Shopify.com/pricing](https://www.shopify.com/pricing), updated March 2026. Prices in USD.*

One thing that table does not show: if you use Shopify Payments (their built-in payment processor), the third-party transaction fee drops to 0% on every plan. That single decision can save you thousands per year. And that is exactly where most Malaysian store owners get confused, because Shopify Payments availability varies by country.

Only comparing the $5 tier? Read the dedicated [Shopify Starter plan breakdown](/shopify-starter-plan-guide) instead. This page covers all five plans.

Let me break each plan down.

## What Features Differ Between Each Shopify Plan?

Staff accounts and reports separate the tiers more than price does.

> **Beyond cost, Shopify plans gate features: staff account limits (1 to unlimited), professional reporting (locked until Grow), carrier-calculated shipping and duty collection (Advanced only), and checkout customisation (Plus only). Shopify's own [plan comparison page](https://www.shopify.com/pricing) confirms professional reporting, available from the Grow plan upward, is a leading reason merchants upgrade off Basic.**

The cost table above answers "what will this plan charge me." This table answers "what will this plan let me do."

### Complete Feature Comparison Table

| Feature | Starter | Basic | Grow | Advanced | Plus |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Monthly price** | $5 | $39 | $105 | $399 | $2,300+ |
| **Annual price (per month)** | $5 | $29 | $79 | $299 | $2,300 |
| **Online store** | No (link page only) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Staff accounts** | 1 | 2 | 5 | 15 | Unlimited |
| **Inventory locations** | 2 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 200 |
| **Online credit card rate** | 5% + 30¢ | 2.9% + 30¢ | 2.7% + 30¢ | 2.5% + 30¢ | 2.15% + 30¢ |
| **3rd-party transaction fee** | 5% | 2% | 1% | 0.6% | 0% (Shopify Payments) |
| **Basic analytics** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Professional reports** | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Custom report builder** | No | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Calculated shipping rates** | No | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Duties & import taxes** | No | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Checkout customisation** | No | No | No | No | Yes (Checkout Extensibility) |
| **Shopify Flow automation** | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Discount code limit** | N/A | 25,000 | 25,000 | 25,000 | Unlimited |
| **Markets (international)** | 1 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 50 |
| **POS Lite** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Abandoned cart recovery** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Gift cards** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

*Source: [Shopify.com/pricing](https://www.shopify.com/pricing). Prices in USD.*

Three rows matter more than the rest. Professional reports show where revenue actually comes from. Calculated shipping rates show exact carrier prices at checkout instead of a flat guess. Checkout customisation controls the highest-leverage page on the whole site. Everything else is incremental.

### The Two Staff Account Limit

This is the first wall most growing stores hit, and it hits before revenue does. Two staff accounts means the store owner plus one employee. The moment you hire a third person who needs backend access, a customer service rep, a warehouse picker, a marketing assistant, you either share logins (a security risk with no audit trail) or upgrade.

We see this with Shopify stores in Malaysia regularly. The store launches with the founder running everything. Six months later, three people are touching the backend. Shared logins lead to mistakes, no audit trail, and the inevitable "who deleted that product" conversation. Five staff accounts, unlocked on the Grow plan, covers the typical growing team: founder, operations manager, customer service, marketing, and a warehouse or fulfilment role.

## Which Shopify Plan Is Best for Beginners?

Start with Basic. Upgrade when the math says so.

> **Shopify Basic at $39/month (or $29/month billed annually) is the best plan for new stores doing under $7,500/month in revenue. It includes a full online store, discount codes, abandoned cart recovery, and 2 staff accounts. Most new merchants start on Basic, upgrading when revenue crosses the break-even threshold.**

### Starter ($5/month): Not a Real Store

The Starter plan is not a standalone ecommerce store. You do not get a customisable online storefront. You get a link-in-bio page and the ability to sell through social media, messaging apps, and email. Think of it as Shopify's answer to Linktree with a checkout.

**Who it fits:** Creators selling a handful of products through Instagram or TikTok. Side hustlers testing demand before committing to a full store.

**Who it does not fit:** Anyone who wants a real online store with collections, custom pages, or any kind of brand experience.

The 5% credit card rate is steep. At RM10,000/month in sales, you would pay RM500 in card fees alone. That is more than the cost of upgrading to Basic.

We cover the $5 tier in full detail (what you get, the $1,500 breakeven, and who should skip it) in the [Shopify Starter plan guide](/shopify-starter-plan-guide).

### Basic ($39/month): The Starting Line

This is where real ecommerce begins. You get a full online store, up to 77% shipping discounts, abandoned cart recovery, and Shopify's standard analytics.

**Key limitations:**

* Only 2 staff accounts
* No professional reports (you get basic analytics only)
* No third-party calculated shipping rates at checkout
* Higher credit card rate (2.9% vs 2.7% on Grow plan)

For a store doing RM15,000/month ($3,300 USD), the credit card fees on Basic would be approximately $96/month. On the Grow plan, they would be $89/month. The $7 savings does not justify the $66 higher monthly fee at this volume.

The math only flips at higher revenue. And that is the question everyone should ask before upgrading.

## When Should You Upgrade From Basic to Grow?

The break-even sits around $7,500/month in sales.

> **Upgrade from Basic ($39/month) to the Grow plan ($105/month) when your monthly revenue exceeds approximately $7,500 USD. At that volume, the lower credit card rate (2.7% vs 2.9%) and eliminated third-party transaction fee (1% vs 2%) save more than the $66/month price difference. Use our [Shopify Total Cost Calculator](/tools/shopify-total-cost-calculator) to find your exact break-even point.**

Here is the maths. The Grow plan costs $66 more per month than Basic. But it saves you 0.2% on every credit card transaction. On $7,500 in monthly sales, that 0.2% saves $15. Not enough on its own.

The real savings come from the third-party transaction fee. If you use a payment gateway other than Shopify Payments (common in Malaysia where stores use iPay88, Billplz, or Revenue Monster), the fee drops from 2% to 1%. On $7,500/month, that is $75 in savings.

Combined: $15 + $75 = $90 saved per month, minus the $66 higher subscription. Net savings: $24/month.

At $10,000/month in sales, the net savings jump to $44/month. By $15,000/month, you are saving $84/month by being on the Grow plan instead of Basic.

### Break-Even Table by Monthly Revenue

| Monthly Revenue (USD) | Basic Total Cost | Grow Total Cost | Savings on Grow | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $3,000 | $39 + $87 + $60 = **$186** | $105 + $81 + $30 = **$216** | -$30 | Stay on Basic |
| $5,000 | $39 + $145 + $100 = **$284** | $105 + $135 + $50 = **$290** | -$6 | Stay on Basic |
| $7,500 | $39 + $218 + $150 = **$407** | $105 + $203 + $75 = **$383** | +$24 | **Upgrade** |
| $10,000 | $39 + $290 + $200 = **$529** | $105 + $270 + $100 = **$475** | +$54 | **Upgrade** |
| $15,000 | $39 + $435 + $300 = **$774** | $105 + $405 + $150 = **$660** | +$114 | **Upgrade** |
| $25,000 | $39 + $725 + $500 = **$1,264** | $105 + $675 + $250 = **$1,030** | +$234 | **Upgrade** |

*Assumes 2.9%/2.7% credit card rate + 2%/1% third-party gateway fee. Shopify Payments users: remove the third-party column.*

Want the exact number for your store? Plug your revenue into our [Shopify Total Cost Calculator](/tools/shopify-total-cost-calculator). It factors in your payment gateway, average order value, and transaction volume.

## What Does the Advanced Plan Give You That Grow Doesn't?

Advanced is for stores that need better shipping rates and international selling tools.

> **Shopify Advanced ($399/month) adds third-party calculated shipping rates, duty and import tax collection, 0.6% third-party transaction fees (vs 1%), and up to 15 staff accounts. According to [Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/pricing), the plan also includes advanced analytics with custom reports. The break-even versus the Grow plan sits around $30,000/month in revenue when using a third-party payment gateway.**

The jump from Grow to Advanced is $294/month. That is significant. The credit card rate improvement is only 0.2% (2.7% to 2.5%), and the third-party gateway fee drops from 1% to 0.6%.

On $30,000/month in sales, the savings work out to:

* Credit card savings: $60/month
* Third-party gateway savings: $120/month
* Total: $180/month

Still $114 short of the $294 price increase. So on fees alone, Advanced does not break even until roughly $50,000/month.

But fees are not the only reason to upgrade. Advanced gives you:

* **Third-party calculated shipping rates at checkout.** Critical for stores shipping heavy or oversized items
* **Duties and import tax collection.** Essential for cross-border selling to Singapore, Australia, or the US
* **Custom report builder.** Create reports that Shopify's standard analytics cannot generate
* **Up to 15 staff accounts.** Necessary for teams with warehouse staff, customer service, and marketing
* **Enhanced inventory management.** Better for multi-location fulfilment

If your [Shopify store in Malaysia](/shopify-malaysia) ships internationally and you need calculated shipping rates at checkout, the Advanced plan may make sense even before the break-even point.

> **Does this sound like your store?** Find out where you're leaking revenue. Take the [free Revenue Score](/scorecard). 3 minutes. Free. No pitch.

## Is Shopify Plus Worth It for Growing Brands?

Only if you are doing $500K+ per month.

> **Shopify Plus starts at $2,300/month and targets brands doing $500K+ in monthly revenue. It includes checkout customisation via Checkout Extensibility, up to 200 inventory locations, unlimited staff accounts, and a dedicated merchant success manager. According to Shopify, Plus merchants process over $10 billion annually, with the platform handling 10,000+ checkouts per minute during peak events like Black Friday.**

Plus is not a pricing plan. It is a different product. The checkout is fully customisable. You get Shopify Flow for automation (free on other plans now, but Plus unlocks advanced triggers). You get the Script Editor for custom discounts, bundling logic, and payment method restrictions.

### Who Actually Needs Plus

* Stores doing $500K+/month that need checkout-level customisation
* Brands selling in 10+ countries that need multi-currency storefronts
* Companies with complex B2B and DTC operations on the same backend
* Businesses that need SLA-backed uptime guarantees and priority support

If you are doing under $500K/month, Plus is almost never worth it. The $2,300/month fee is only the starting point. Implementation costs, custom development, and Plus-specific apps add up fast.

We have seen Malaysian brands rush to Plus at $100K/month in revenue because they thought they needed the checkout customisation. In every case, the standard Grow plan with third-party apps achieved 90% of what they wanted at a fraction of the cost.

## How Do Transaction Fees Change the Real Cost?

The monthly fee is the decoy. Transaction fees are the real price.

> **Transaction fees account for 60-80% of total Shopify costs for most stores, according to WebMedic's analysis of 40+ Malaysian Shopify stores. A store doing $20,000/month on Basic pays $580 in credit card fees alone, plus $400 in third-party gateway fees, totalling $1,019/month when you add the subscription. Switching to the Grow plan drops that total to $915/month, saving $104/month or $1,248/year.**

This is where store owners make the most expensive mistake. They compare $39 vs $105 and choose the cheaper plan. They ignore the fees that dwarf the subscription.

### Shopify Payments vs Third-Party Gateways

If Shopify Payments is available in your country and you activate it, the third-party transaction fee disappears entirely. Zero. On every plan.

For stores in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and several EU countries, this is straightforward. Activate Shopify Payments and your only variable cost is the credit card processing rate.

For stores in Malaysia, the situation is more nuanced. Shopify Payments is not available in Malaysia as of 2026. Malaysian merchants must use a third-party gateway, and that means paying the additional transaction fee on top of whatever your gateway charges.

This makes plan selection even more important for Malaysian stores. The difference between 2% and 1% on a third-party gateway fee at scale is serious money.

### Real Cost Comparison: Malaysian Store at RM50,000/Month (~$11,000 USD)

| Cost Component | Basic | Grow | Advanced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly subscription | $39 | $105 | $399 |
| Credit card fees (gateway rate) | ~3.0% = $330 | ~3.0% = $330 | ~3.0% = $330 |
| Shopify transaction fee | 2% = $220 | 1% = $110 | 0.6% = $66 |
| **Total monthly cost** | **$589** | **$545** | **$795** |
| **Annual cost** | **$7,068** | **$6,540** | **$9,540** |

*Note: Malaysian gateway rates (iPay88, Billplz, Revenue Monster) typically charge 2.5-3.5%, independent of Shopify's transaction fee. Both fees apply.*

At RM50,000/month, the Grow plan saves $528/year versus Basic. Advanced costs $2,472 more than Grow. Not worth it unless you need the shipping and reporting features.

This is why a calculator matters. The answer changes based on your revenue, your gateway, and your country. Try the [Shopify Total Cost Calculator](/tools/shopify-total-cost-calculator) with your actual numbers.

## What Hidden Costs Should You Budget For?

The subscription and transaction fees are just the starting point.

> **Beyond Shopify's listed prices, stores typically spend an additional $50-500/month on apps, $0-350 on themes, and $500-5,000+ on initial setup and customisation. WebMedic's data across 40+ Malaysian Shopify builds shows the average store runs 8-12 paid apps at a combined cost of $150-300/month. These recurring app costs often exceed the Shopify subscription itself.**

### App Costs

Shopify's app ecosystem is both a strength and a cost trap. The free plan gives you a basic store, but most stores need apps for:

* **Email marketing:** Klaviyo ($20-150/month), Shopify Email (free for 10K emails/month)
* **Reviews:** Judge.me ($15/month), Loox ($10-100/month)
* **Upsells and cross-sells:** ReConvert ($5-30/month), Bold Upsell ($10-60/month)
* **SEO:** SEO Manager ($20/month), Plug in SEO ($30/month)
* **Loyalty programmes:** Smile.io ($49-999/month), LoyaltyLion ($159+/month)

We audit stores that are paying $400-600/month in app subscriptions, more than the Advanced plan itself. Most have 3-4 apps that duplicate functionality or are no longer used.

### Theme Costs

Shopify offers free themes that work. The paid themes ($250-350 one-time) offer more sections, better design flexibility, and faster load times. For most stores, a paid theme is worth the investment.

However, theme customisation beyond the built-in editor typically requires a developer. Budget $500-3,000 for custom theme work depending on complexity.

### Other Recurring Costs People Forget

| Cost | Amount | Frequency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Custom domain | $14 to $20 | Annual |
| Professional email (Google Workspace) | $7/user/month | Monthly |
| SSL certificate | Free (included) | N/A |
| Shopify POS hardware | $49 to $399 | One-time |
| Stock photography | $0 to $30/month | Monthly |
| Custom development/maintenance | $500 to $3,000+ | As needed |

None of these show up on the Shopify pricing page. All of them show up on the credit card statement.

### Development and Setup Costs

If you are comparing [Shopify vs WooCommerce](/shopify-vs-woocommerce-which-platform-fits-your-business), factor in the total cost of ownership. WooCommerce's "free" plugin requires hosting ($10-200/month), security management, plugin updates, and developer time for maintenance. Shopify's subscription covers all of that.

For a professional Shopify store launch in Malaysia, budget:

* **Basic store setup:** RM3,000-8,000
* **Custom theme development:** RM8,000-25,000
* **Migration from another platform:** RM5,000-15,000
* **Ongoing maintenance:** RM500-2,000/month

## How Does Shopify Pricing Compare to Other Platforms?

Shopify is mid-range on sticker price. Lower on total cost of ownership once hosting and maintenance are counted.

> **Shopify's total cost of ownership runs lower than self-hosted platforms like WooCommerce once hosting, security, and developer maintenance are factored in, per a 2025 Forrester study commissioned by Shopify. BigCommerce carries similar subscription pricing ($39-$399/month) but charges no transaction fees on any plan. Squarespace starts cheaper at $33/month but caps at 200 products on its entry commerce plan.**

| Platform | Monthly Cost | Transaction Fee | Hosting | Maintenance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Shopify** (Basic) | $39 | 2% (3rd party) | Included | Included |
| **WooCommerce** | Free (plugin) | 0% | $10 to $200/month | $100 to $500/month dev time |
| **BigCommerce** (Standard) | $39 | 0% | Included | Included |
| **Squarespace** (Business) | $33 | 3% | Included | Included |
| **Wix** (Business) | $36 | 0% | Included | Included |

WooCommerce looks free until hosting, SSL management, plugin updates, security patching, and developer time for maintenance get added in. See our full [Shopify vs WooCommerce comparison](/shopify-vs-woocommerce-which-platform-fits-your-business) if you are weighing both.

BigCommerce's zero transaction fee is appealing for stores using third-party gateways, but its app ecosystem is smaller and Malaysian gateway support is thinner. For most ecommerce brands in Malaysia and Singapore, Shopify's ecosystem, apps, themes, developer availability, and payment gateway integrations, makes it the more practical choice despite the transaction fee.

## How Does POS Pricing Work With Shopify?

Shopify POS is free on every plan. POS Pro costs extra per location.

> **Shopify POS Lite is included free with every Shopify plan and supports in-person sales with basic inventory tracking. POS Pro costs $89/month per location and adds staff management, unlimited registers, and exchange support. According to [Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/pos), POS Pro drops to $79/month per location on annual billing. Hardware ranges from $49 for a card reader to $399 for a complete countertop kit.**

If you sell in a physical location, pop-up markets, retail stores, or showrooms, POS costs are part of your real Shopify bill.

### POS Hardware Costs

| Hardware | Price |
| --- | --- |
| Shopify Tap & Chip Card Reader | $49 |
| Shopify POS Go (mobile device) | $299 |
| Countertop Kit (dock + reader) | $219 |
| iPad Stand | $149 |
| Receipt Printer | $369 |
| Barcode Scanner | $199 to $399 |

Hardware is a one-time cost. POS Pro is recurring. A single retail location running POS Pro with a countertop kit adds roughly $100-$120/month to total Shopify cost.

## How Do You Pick the Right Plan for Your Store?

Match the plan to your current revenue, not your goals.

> **Choose your Shopify plan based on current monthly revenue: under $7,500/month stick with Basic ($39/month), $7,500-$30,000/month move to the Grow plan ($105/month), $30,000-$500,000/month evaluate Advanced ($399/month) for its shipping and reporting tools, and above $500,000/month consider Plus. Re-evaluate quarterly as your revenue grows. WebMedic recommends checking your total cost against the next tier every 90 days.**

Here is the decision framework:

### Step 1: Calculate Your Current Monthly Revenue in USD

Malaysian stores, convert your monthly GMV from Ringgit to USD. Use the current exchange rate, not an estimate.

### Step 2: Check Your Payment Gateway

Are you using Shopify Payments? If yes, ignore the third-party transaction fee column. If you are in Malaysia using iPay88, Billplz, or Revenue Monster, the third-party fee applies.

### Step 3: Use the Break-Even Points

| Your Monthly Revenue | Recommended Plan | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Under $1,000 | Starter or Basic | Starter if social-only, Basic for a full store |
| $1,000 - $7,500 | Basic | Fee savings do not justify upgrade |
| $7,500 - $30,000 | Grow | Lower fees save more than the subscription increase |
| $30,000 - $50,000 | Shopify or Advanced | Advanced only if you need calculated shipping or reports |
| $50,000+ | Advanced | Fee savings justify the price at this volume |
| $500,000+ | Plus | Checkout customisation, SLA, dedicated support |

### Step 4: Re-Evaluate Every Quarter

Your break-even shifts with revenue. A store growing 10% month-over-month can cross a threshold in a single quarter. Set a calendar reminder. Or use the [Shopify Total Cost Calculator](/tools/shopify-total-cost-calculator) every 90 days to check if you are overpaying.

## What About Annual vs Monthly Billing?

Annual billing saves 25% on most plans.

> **Paying annually instead of monthly saves up to 25% on Shopify subscriptions: Basic drops from $39 to $29/month, Shopify from $105 to $79/month, and Advanced from $399 to $299/month. According to Shopify's pricing page, annual billing saves merchants an average of $180-$1,200/year depending on plan. The trade-off is a 12-month commitment with no refunds for downgrading mid-cycle.**

| Plan | Monthly Billing | Annual Billing (per month) | Annual Savings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $39 | $29 | $120/year |
| Grow | $105 | $79 | $312/year |
| Advanced | $399 | $299 | $1,200/year |

If your store has been running for 6+ months and you are confident in the platform, switch to annual billing. The savings are meaningful. $312/year on the Grow plan is essentially three months of the Basic plan for free.

The risk is minimal. Shopify has a 14-day free trial for new stores and a 3-day $1 trial extension. By the time you are considering annual billing, you already know if the platform works for you.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does Shopify cost per month in Malaysia?

Shopify costs $39-$399/month (approximately RM175-RM1,800/month) depending on plan, plus transaction fees. Malaysian merchants pay an additional 2-0.6% Shopify transaction fee since Shopify Payments is not available in Malaysia as of 2026. Total effective cost including gateway fees typically ranges from RM700-RM4,500/month for stores doing RM30,000-RM100,000 in monthly revenue.

### Which Shopify plan is best for small businesses?

Shopify Basic at $39/month (or $29/month annually) is the best plan for small businesses doing under $7,500 USD in monthly revenue. It includes a full online store, abandoned cart recovery, discount codes, and 2 staff accounts. Most new merchants stay on Basic for 12-18 months before the transaction fee savings justify upgrading to the $105/month Grow plan.

### Does Shopify charge transaction fees on top of credit card fees?

Yes. Shopify charges a separate transaction fee of 0.6-2% on top of credit card processing fees when you use a third-party payment gateway instead of Shopify Payments. Using Shopify Payments eliminates this fee entirely on all plans. In countries where Shopify Payments is unavailable (including Malaysia), this additional fee is unavoidable and should be factored into total cost calculations.

### Is Shopify Plus worth it for growing ecommerce brands?

Shopify Plus at $2,300/month is worth it for brands doing $500,000+ in monthly revenue that need checkout customisation, multi-currency storefronts, or SLA-backed uptime guarantees. For stores under that threshold, the standard Grow or Advanced plan with third-party apps achieves 90% of Plus functionality at a fraction of the cost. WebMedic has seen Malaysian brands overspend by upgrading to Plus too early.

### How do I calculate my true Shopify cost?

Add your monthly subscription + credit card processing fees + Shopify's third-party transaction fee (if not using Shopify Payments) + app subscriptions. For a store on the Basic plan doing $10,000/month with a third-party gateway, expect roughly $529/month in total Shopify-related costs. Use WebMedic's free Shopify Total Cost Calculator at webmedic.com/tools/shopify-total-cost-calculator for an exact breakdown.

## Pick the Plan, Then Fix the Leak

Picking the right plan saves you a few hundred a month. Fixing a broken checkout saves you a few thousand.

Most stores we audit are on roughly the right plan and still losing revenue somewhere else: a slow product page, a checkout that drops mobile buyers, an abandoned cart flow that never got switched on.

# Shopify Pricing Plans Compared (2026)

This article by Faisal Hourani (WebMedic founder) provides a comprehensive breakdown of Shopify's five pricing plans in 2026, emphasizing that transaction fees—not the monthly subscription—determine the real cost.

## The Five Plans

| Plan | Monthly Price | Annual (per month) | Online Credit Card Rate | 3rd-Party Transaction Fee | Staff Accounts |
|------|--------------|-------------------|----------------------|------------------------|---------------|
| **Starter** | $5 | $5 | 5% + 30¢ | 5% | 1 |
| **Basic** | $39 | $29 | 2.9% + 30¢ | 2% | 2 |
| **Grow** | $105 | $79 | 2.7% + 30¢ | 1% | 5 |
| **Advanced** | $399 | $299 | 2.5% + 30¢ | 0.6% | 15 |
| **Plus** | $2,300+ | $2,300 | 2.15% + 30¢ | 0% (Shopify Payments) | Unlimited |

## Key Recommendations

**Beginners:** Start with Basic ($39/month) for stores under $7,500/month in revenue.

**Upgrade from Basic to Grow:** Break-even is ~$7,500/month in sales. At that volume, lower credit card rates (2.7% vs 2.9%) and reduced third-party fees (1% vs 2%) save more than the $66/month price difference.

**Advanced ($399/month):** Best for stores needing calculated shipping rates, duty/import tax collection, and custom reports. Break-even vs Grow is ~$30,000/month with third-party gateways.

**Plus ($2,300/month):** Only worth it for brands doing $500K+/month needing checkout customisation, multi-currency, and SLA-backed uptime.

## Critical Insights

- **Transaction fees account for 60-80% of total Shopify costs** for most stores.
- **Using Shopify Payments eliminates the third-party transaction fee** entirely, but it's unavailable in Malaysia as of 2026.
- **Annual billing saves ~25%** (Basic $29/month, Grow $79/month, Advanced $299/month).
- **Hidden costs:** Stores typically spend $50-500/month on apps, $0-350 on themes, and $500-5,000+ on initial setup.
- **The average store runs 8-12 paid apps** at $150-300/month—often exceeding the Shopify subscription itself.

## For Malaysian Merchants

Since Shopify Payments is unavailable in Malaysia, stores using iPay88, Billplz, or Revenue Monster pay both gateway fees (2.5-3.5%) AND Shopify's transaction fee (2-0.6%). At RM50,000/month (~$11,000 USD), the Grow plan saves $528/year vs Basic.

## Plan Selection Framework

- Under $1,000/month: Starter or Basic
- $1,000-$7,500/month: Basic
- $7,500-$30,000/month: Grow
- $30,000-$50,000/month: Grow or Advanced (only if needing calculated shipping/reports)
- $50,000+/month: Advanced
- $500,000+/month: Plus

Re-evaluate every 90 days as revenue grows.

Shopify pricing can feel confusing i.e. monthly fees, transaction fees, POS add-ons, app costs, and Shopify Plus pricing all vary depending on your store's needs. This guide breaks down *exactly how Shopify pricing works*, what each plan includes, and how to choose the right one for your business. Whether you're just starting out or scaling to millions, this 2026 Shopify pricing breakdown covers everything you need to know.

## What is Shopify Pricing & How Does It Work?

Shopify pricing is based on a monthly subscription plus transaction fees. Each plan includes ecommerce features like product management, payments, checkout, and reports. But higher plans offer lower payment fees, more staff accounts, and advanced reporting. You'll also pay separately for apps, themes, and POS hardware if needed.

> If you need help tailoring your Shopify store, hiring a [Shopify developer](https://shopexperts.com/) can make setup, customization, and growth much easier.

## Shopify Pricing Plans (Starter → Advanced → Plus)

| **Starter** | $5 per month | Annual not available | Sell through social media and messaging apps with buy buttons; no full online store or blog; 5% transaction fee. Best for solopreneurs testing online sales.  **Staff Accounts:** None | Online: 5.0% In-Person: Not applicable **Transaction Fee (if not using Shopify Payments):** 5.0% |

## Shopify Transaction Fees Explained

Shopify charges payment processing fees on every order. These vary by plan and whether you use Shopify Payments. Higher plans reduce these fees — which is why upgrading often makes sense for brands with high monthly order volume.

## Additional Shopify Costs (Apps, Themes, Add-Ons, POS)

Beyond monthly subscription fees, Shopify stores also pay for apps, themes, email tools, shipping labels, and POS hardware. Most stores spend **$30–$300/month** on apps depending on complexity, sales channels, and automation needs.

#### **Transaction Fees**

When you make a sale on Shopify, you'll pay a payment processing fee. If you use Shopify Payments, the fee is the credit card rate (e.g., 2.9% + 30¢ on Basic, 2.5% + 30¢ on Advanced). Shopify does not take an extra cut if you use Shopify Payments.

However, if you use an external payment provider like PayPal or Stripe, Shopify charges an additional fee (2% on Basic, 1% on Grow, and 0.6% on Advanced). To minimize fees, Shopify Payments is usually the best option.

#### **Shopify Payments vs. Third Party Processors**

Shopify Payments simplifies payments by handling everything through the Shopify admin, with no extra fees beyond the standard card rate. Third party gateways incur extra fees from Shopify, but some merchants prefer external options like PayPal, which also incurs additional Shopify fees if not used through Shopify Payments. Shopify Payments is usually more cost effective if available in your region.

#### **Credit Card Rates for Online vs In-Person**

 For in-person sales using [Shopify POS](https://www.skailama.com/blog/shopify-pos-system), the processing rates are slightly lower than online rates. For example, Basic plan in-person rates are 2.6% + 10¢ (compared to 2.9% online). These fees are competitive with other POS systems, so if you have a physical store, consider the Shopify Retail plan or POS Pro for more advanced features, with rates aligned with your base plan.

#### **Optional add-ons and services**

While your Shopify subscription includes hosting for your online store, there are a few optional costs you might incur to fully set up your shop:

#### Custom Domain Name

Shopify offers a free subdomain (yourstorename.myshopify.com), but for branding, you'll likely want a custom domain (yourstore.com). Domains typically cost $10–$20/year for standard .com addresses. Shopify allows easy domain purchase and management through their platform (around $14/year). This cost is separate from your Shopify pricing.

#### Premium Themes

Shopify provides free themes, but you can buy a premium theme from the Shopify Theme Store for $150–$350. Premium themes are a one time purchase, and many merchants start with free themes until they need a more unique design. This cost is optional and depends on your business needs, impacting Shopify pricing.

#### Shopify Apps

The Shopify App Store offers free and paid apps to extend functionality. Apps range from a few dollars to $50+/month depending on the feature. While these apps enhance your store, they contribute to your Shopify pricing and should be selected based on ROI. Some examples of Shopify apps are [Easy Bundle Builder](https://apps.shopify.com/bundle-builder), [Checkout Wiz](https://apps.shopify.com/checkout-pro) and [Kite: Discount & Free Gift App](https://apps.shopify.com/kite-free-gift).

With mobile commerce continuing to grow, some brands also explore using a [Shopify mobile app builder](https://www.appbrew.com/blogs/best-shopify-mobile-app-builders) to create app-based shopping experiences for their customers. Features like push notifications and faster checkout can help improve engagement and repeat purchases depending on the brand’s mobile strategy.

#### Email Hosting or Google Workspace

Shopify doesn't provide email hosting, so you'll need a separate service like Google Workspace ($7/user/month). Some domain providers offer free email forwarding, but for a professional setup, expect to pay a few dollars each month. This adds to your overall Shopify pricing.

#### Point of Sale Hardware

For in-person sales via [Shopify POS](https://www.skailama.com/blog/shopify-pos-system), you'll need hardware like card readers, barcode scanners, and receipt printers. Shopify offers a basic $49 card reader, which is a one-time purchase. This cost should be considered if your business operates offline, influencing your total Shopify pricing.

#### Shipping and Fulfillment

While Shopify pricing doesn't include shipping fees, Shopify provides discounted rates for shipping labels via Shopify Shipping. You'll pay the carrier directly (UPS, USPS, etc.), and fulfillment costs are operational expenses tied to running your store.

#### Shopify Email / Marketing

Shopify Email is free for the first 2,500 emails/month, with additional emails costing around $1 per 1,000. If you use a third-party platform like Klaviyo or Omnisend, expect tiered pricing based on the number of contacts or emails sent, which will affect your Shopify pricing.

In short, Shopify's base pricing covers the essentials to get your store online, but you should budget for a few extras like a custom domain, possibly a theme, and perhaps a couple of apps or services that your specific business might need. Many of these costs are flexible – you can start with free options (free theme, no paid apps) and only add paid extras once you see the need or ROI.

## Understanding Shopify's Pricing Structure

#### **Monthly vs. Annual Subscription Costs**:

Shopify plans can be paid monthly or annually. Paying annually gives about a 25% discount on the Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans. For example, the Basic plan drops from $39/month to ~$29/month when billed annually. Similarly, higher tier plans drop from $105 to $79 and $399 to $299. Opting for annual billing saves 2-3 months' worth of fees, but it's a commitment. Cancelling mid-term doesn't provide a prorated refund.

#### **Upgrade or Downgrade Flexibility**:

Shopify allows easy plan upgrades or downgrades. If you change plans monthly, you're charged the new rate immediately, and any unused time from the old plan is credited. There's no penalty for switching, except for Shopify Plus, which involves a contract.

#### **Free Trial and Introductory Offers**:

Shopify now offers a 3-day free trial, and after that, you can continue your first month for just $1. Occasionally, Shopify provides further promotions like "3 months for $1/month". After the trial, regular billing begins. If Shopify isn't the right fit, you can cancel anytime.

In summary, Shopify pricing is straightforward: you pay a subscription fee, which you can reduce by paying annually, and transaction fees on sales. There are no hidden fees, and you can cancel anytime on standard plans.

## Tips to Reduce Shopify Costs (For Small Businesses)

For small businesses, managing Shopify pricing is key to staying within budget. Here are some actionable tips to optimize costs:

#### **Choose the Right Plan**:

Start with the plan that fits your current needs. The Basic plan is likely sufficient if you're just launching. Upgrade to a higher plan only,when necessary, as each upgrade should justify cost savings or more sales. For example, moving from Basic to Grow can save 0.2% in transaction fees, but it only makes sense if that savings exceeds the $66 price difference at higher sales volumes.

#### **Use Annual Billing**:

If possible, opt for annual billing to save 25% on Shopify pricing. For example, the Basic plan costs $29/month with annual billing instead of $39/month, saving you $120 annually. Many businesses start with monthly billing and switch to annual once they see consistent sales.

#### **Leverage Free Resources**:

Shopify provides free themes and many apps to cover basic needs like SEO, product reviews, and marketing. Use these before paying for premium versions. Shopify pricing also includes built-in tools like abandoned cart recovery, which can save you from paying for additional apps.

#### **Minimize App Costs**:

Install only necessary apps and regularly remove those you no longer use. Apps can add significant recurring costs, so focus on those that drive sales or save time.

#### **Use Shopify Payments**:

Stick to Shopify Payments to avoid the extra 1-2% transaction fee for using third party gateways. This simplifies payouts and keeps your costs lower.

#### **Take Advantage of Discounts**:

Keep an eye out for Shopify promotions like shipping or advertising credits, especially if you're switching from another platform. Also, make use of free trials for apps to test their value before committing. You can also look for coupons and deals to lower your upfront costs. For example, websites like Cybernews share helpful [Shopify coupon codes](https://cybernews.com/website-builders-coupons/shopify-coupon-codes/).

#### **Optimize for Efficiency**:

Shopify's tools can save you time, reducing the need for outsourcing. Use free resources like the Shopify help center and community forums to handle tasks in-house, which can lower costs.

#### **Monitor Your Usage**:

Watch for any apps that may increase costs based on usage (e.g., emails sent, page views). Check your Shopify billing page to avoid surprises.

By following these strategies, you can manage Shopify pricing effectively, keeping costs low while scaling your business. Many small businesses start with basic plans and minimal apps, which can keep expenses below $50/month. As your sales grow, reinvest profits to improve your store's performance.

## Conclusion

Shopify's pricing in 2026 offers flexible options for businesses of all sizes, from the $5 Starter plan to the enterprise level Shopify Plus. Higher tier plans reduce transaction fees and provide advanced tools, while Shopify Payments helps avoid extra charges. Optional costs like domains, themes, and apps can be managed to keep expenses low.

By choosing the right plan, using free resources, and monitoring expenses, businesses can scale profitably while keeping Shopify pricing manageable. Take advantage of Shopify's free trial to explore which plan suits your needs and drive your online success.

## Shopify Pricing FAQs

How much does Shopify really cost?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/600a7682415ab7d3aafe3a5c/60151633cb58213f20aa80ae_Group%20434.svg)

Shopify’s pricing depends on the plan. The Basic plan costs $39/month ($29/month if paid annually), the Grow plan is $105/month ($79/month annually), and the Advanced plan is $399/month ($299/month annually). The Starter plan is available for $5/month, and the Plus plan starts at $2,300/month. Additional costs like transaction fees or apps may apply.

Is Shopify $1 for 3 months?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/600a7682415ab7d3aafe3a5c/60151633cb58213f20aa80ae_Group%20434.svg)

Yes, Shopify offers new users a 3-day free trial, followed by $1/month for the first three months. After this period, the plan switches to standard pricing (e.g., Basic reverts to $39/month). Promotions may change, so check Shopify’s website for updates.

Is Shopify actually worth it?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/600a7682415ab7d3aafe3a5c/60151633cb58213f20aa80ae_Group%20434.svg)

For most businesses, yes. Shopify is a leading e-commerce platform offering an easy-to-use, all-in-one solution for online selling. It simplifies website setup, payments, and inventory management, making it worth the cost for serious store owners. However, for small hobby projects, you should consider whether the investment is necessary.

Can I cancel Shopify after 3 months?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/600a7682415ab7d3aafe3a5c/60151633cb58213f20aa80ae_Group%20434.svg)

Yes, Shopify has no long-term contracts, and you can cancel anytime. If you're on the $1 for 3 months deal, you won’t be billed after cancellation. Annual plan users, however, need to wait until the term ends, as those are prepaid.

Do I have to pay for each store on Shopify?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/600a7682415ab7d3aafe3a5c/60151633cb58213f20aa80ae_Group%20434.svg)

Yes, each Shopify store requires a separate subscription, and there’s no bulk discount for multiple stores. However, Shopify Plus allows multiple store setups under one agreement, but it’s designed for large businesses and comes at a higher cost.

How much does Shopify take per sale?

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/600a7682415ab7d3aafe3a5c/60151633cb58213f20aa80ae_Group%20434.svg)

Shopify charges 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction on the Basic plan, 2.7% + 30¢ on the Grow plan, and 2.5% + 30¢ on the Advanced plan when using Shopify Payments. If you use an external payment gateway like PayPal, Shopify charges an additional 2% on Basic, 1% on Grow, and 0.6% on Advanced. Using Shopify Payments avoids these extra transaction fees.

# Shopify Pricing Plans and Fees - How much does Shopify cost in 2026?

Shopify Pricing

![Preslav Nikov](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7)

Calculating your total monthly Shopify fees shouldn't be a guessing game.

Your bottom-line costs for running an ecommerce store depend on your subscription tier, your payment processing configuration, and secondary ecosystem variables.

Shopify costs range from $5 per month on the Starter plan to $2,300 or more per month on Shopify Plus. The three core plans in between are Basic at $29, Standard at $79, and Advanced at $299 per month.   
  
Every plan adds payment processing of roughly 2.4% to 2.9% plus 30 cents per transaction through Shopify Payments. For a scaling store, apps and development usually cost more each month than the plan itself.

It is reviewed by the craftberry engineering team. craftberry is a certified Shopify Plus partner based in Europe, with over a decade of work exclusively inside the Shopify ecosystem.

Here is the comprehensive Shopify fees explained to help you protect your margins, evaluate your overhead, and scale your business efficiently.

#### Key takeaways:

* Shopify's entry price is $5 per month (Starter); its enterprise tier starts at $2,300 per month (Plus).
* Payment processing applies on every plan and is a higher cost than the subscription for most stores.
* Using a payment gateway other than Shopify Payments adds a per-transaction fee of 0.15% to 2%, depending on the plan.
* Shopify Plus moves to variable pricing at 0.25% of monthly revenue once a store passes roughly $800,000 per month.
* Real monthly cost equals plan plus processing plus apps plus development, and the plan is often under 15% of the total.

The number that dominates most pricing conversations is the one that matters least.

#### "Merchants fixate on the monthly plan fee, but it is the smallest line in the budget. What actually sets the cost of running a Shopify store is how much custom engineering replaces a stack of recurring app subscriptions, and how much revenue the storefront captures per visitor. A store optimized at the code level costs less to operate and earns more per session than one carrying a dozen third-party apps."

- Preslav Nikov, CEO and Founder of craftberry, Forbes 30 Under 30 and a systems developer with over a decade in the Shopify ecosystem.

This is the lens craftberry applies to every cost audit: total cost of ownership and revenue per visitor, not the sticker price of the plan.

## Shopify Pricing Plans

Shopify offers four main subscription tiers for different business sizes. Plans range from $5/month for social media selling to $2,300+/month for enterprises.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20version=%271.1%27%20width=%272160%27%20height=%271350%27/%3e)![Storyblok Image](https://a.storyblok.com/f/248745/2160x1350/601687c592/c7f228da-a5c3-4899-8bcb-8f7bd61ac43c.png/m/2000x0/filters:quality(75)/)

* While the Shopify Starter plan streamlines early social commerce, it doesn't allow you to build a standalone storefront or leverage Shopify’s powerful backend tools to their full potential, acting instead as a simple "Buy Button" for social media pages.
* High-volume brands require Shopify Plus as an enterprise solution, brick-and-mortar retailers need Shopify POS Pro, and the Shopify Agentic plan is designed strictly as a specialized infrastructure for autonomous AI sales channels.
* The vast majority of scaling merchants find their perfect fit among Shopify’s three core subscription tiers (Basic Shopify, Standard, and Advanced Shopify) to unlock complete customization, lower transaction fees, and a fully functional e-commerce website.

Choosing how to pay for your subscription can significantly impact your operational overhead.

While paying month-to-month offers maximum flexibility, switching to an annual billing cycle allows you to lock in substantial discounts on your core Shopify pricing plans.

#### In fact, opting for an annual plan reduces your monthly subscription costs by 25% on core tiers.

Below is the breakdown of the upfront monthly fees versus paid-annually monthly costs to help you choose the most cost-effective path for your e-commerce operations.

### Shopify Free Trial - $1 for 3 months

Before we jump into Shopify’s active plans, let’s take a look at Shopify’s cheapest option - their 3-day free trial followed by a 3-month trial for $1.

#### If you want to validate a new ecommerce store without upfront financial commitment, this trial provides the perfect low-risk opportunity to test the ecosystem backend and see if its features align with your long-term business goals.

All core plans include SSL certificates and secure web hosting.

With Shopify's free trial, you can:

* Build and [customize your store](https://craftberry.co/services/bespoke-e-commerce-ui-ux-design-for-shopify-and-shopify-plus), add products and collections, and you can play around with the admin settings for managing and fulfilling orders.

* Explore Shopify’s extensive apps and integrations to extend your store’s functionality.
* Leverage a development store environment free of charge to design and iterate without any time pressure.

However, keep in mind that checkout capabilities remain inactive until you launch a live Shopify website by choosing a paid plan.

Without a live subscription, customers cannot add items to their carts or complete purchases. To start selling, you need to choose a paid Shopify plan.

Similar Post - [Shopify Success Rate](https://craftberry.co/articles/why-do-shopify-stores-fail)

### Shopify Starter - $5/month

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20version=%271.1%27%20width=%272160%27%20height=%27900%27/%3e)![Storyblok Image](https://a.storyblok.com/f/248745/2160x900/6debd25691/db6235b5-86e8-4638-8bb8-fd0320c42582.png/m/2000x0/filters:quality(75)/)

*Source:* [*Shopify Starter Plan*](https://www.shopify.com/pricing)

#### The Shopify Starter plan is excellent for individuals and small businesses who sell products on social media and want to leverage Shopify’s powerful backend for their e-commerce operations.

The Starter plan costs $5/month but lacks a full storefront. Shopify's pricing plans can include sales through social media and basic reporting features.

Starter plan streamlines and simplifies the entire sales process. You can:

* Centralize and efficiently manage your order processing, inventory management, and customer communications all within one user-friendly interface.
* Easily integrate various social platforms into Shopify’s platform to share product links directly with your audience.

#### Keep in mind that the Starter plan has the highest card processing and transaction fees.

Overall, the Shopify Starter plan is a cost-effective solution for those just getting started with their e-commerce journey.

They can explore many of Shopify’s features at a fraction of the cost of other plans.

### Shopify Basic - $39/month ($24/mo billed annually)

Shopify's Basic plan costs $39/month for a full online store.

The Shopify Basic plan includes everything you need to create your Shopify store, ship products, and process payments.

The Basic plan includes features for launching an online store such as unlimited products and 24/7 support.

#### This infrastructure is particularly suitable for smaller stores, offering essential e-commerce features without overwhelming complexity.

With Basic Shopify, you can:

* Take advantage of features like abandoned cart recovery, which are common across Shopify's plans.
* Customize your store and make it an omnichannel sales machine, controlled from Shopify’s admin panel.

When it comes to card processing and payment processing fees, the Basic Shopify plan carries standard rates for both online and offline transactions.

If you use Shopify Payments, you won’t face any other transaction fees from the platform.

However, opting for a third-party payment gateway incurs their standard processing rates plus an additional 2.0% Shopify transaction surcharge.

### Grow Shopify - $92/month ($69/mo billed annually)

The Shopify plan, priced at $92 per month, is tailored for small businesses experiencing rapid growth and in need of a more robust e-commerce toolbox.

#### The Grow plan makes the most strategic sense for brands with a lean team and monthly revenues ranging between $50k and $200k.

This plan builds upon the features offered in the Basic Shopify plan, providing additional tools and capabilities essential for scaling businesses.

#### Some of its features include:

* Advanced analytics and reporting
* Reduced processing and transaction fees
* Features for international sales via Shopify markets
* Abandoned cart recovery
* Gift card functionality
* Automation workflows via Shopify Flow

International selling features include handling local currencies and taxes.

When it comes to card processing and transaction fees, Shopify applies specific baseline rates for online checkouts and in-person payments on this tier.   
  
These operational fees fluctuate based on your store's regional billing location and the type of credit card processed.

If you use Shopify Payments, you won’t have to pay any extra fees.

However, if you use a third-party payment provider, you’ll have to pay them a processing fee and an extra 1% transaction fee to Shopify.

### Shopify Advanced - $399/month ($299/mo billed annually)

The Advanced plan supports up to 15 staff accounts for $399/month.

The Shopify Advanced plan:

* Empowers high-growth, medium-to-large enterprises to scale complex operations.
* Unlocks advanced market metrics and deep data analytics.
* Includes lower payment processing rates and robust support for international selling.

#### Merchants generating over $80,000 -$100,000 monthly revenue and looking to scale their operations are well-suited for Shopify’s Advanced plan.

The Shopify Advanced plan brings a variety of features to the table, such as:

* Custom reporting and analytics

* Third-party calculated shipping rates

* Lower transaction fees

* 15 staff accounts

* Cart recovery

* Discount codes

* Gift card support

When it comes to payment processing, Shopify Advanced offers significantly reduced baseline rates for both online and in-person transactions, though the exact percentages vary depending on your store's regional location.

#### Moreover, the extra fee for not using Shopify Payments is only 0.6%.

### Shopify Plus - Starting at $2300/month

Shopify Plus starts at $2,300/month and includes unlimited staff accounts.

It’s an all-in-one solution for multi-channel selling, built for performance and scalability. Businesses seeking performance optimization can benefit from Shopify Plus offerings.

#### It is designed to equip high-performing brands with all the tools they need to sell more, faster, almost anywhere in the world (175 countries).

The platform excels in performance, handling over 10,000 checkouts per minute, and provides advanced security and fraud protection.

#### Upgrading to Plus unlocks critical infrastructure for market leaders:

* 24/7 priority enterprise support.
* Deep checkout customization experiences through the advanced [Shopify checkout](https://craftberry.co/articles/migrate-from-checkout-liquid-to-extensibility-checkout-on-shopify).
* Native wholesale and B2B expansion using Shopify Collective.
* A vast ecosystem of dedicated enterprise apps and integrations.
* Higher-tier plans offer better discounts on shipping and logistics.

Moreover, the extra transaction fee that you pay to Shopify if you use a payment processor other than Shopify Payments is just 0.2% of your transaction. Again, if you stick to Shopify Payments, there are no extra transaction fees.

Overall, while these exact numbers may change, Shopify Plus offers the cheapest card processing and transaction fee rates out of any Shopify plan.

For more up-to-date information, see [Shopify Plus pricing.](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing)

With its ability to support large-scale operations, Shopify Plus is an ideal choice for businesses aiming for significant growth and requiring a platform that can accommodate high traffic volumes and complex operational needs.

### When Shopify Plus Costs More Than the Base Fee: Variable Revenue Pricing

Shopify Plus lists at a $2,300 monthly platform fee on a standard multi-year term, but high-volume merchants do not stay on the flat rate.

Once monthly revenue passes roughly $800,000, Plus shifts to variable pricing calculated at 0.25% of monthly revenue, capped at $40,000 per month.

A merchant processing $2,000,000 a month therefore pays around $5,000 in platform fees rather than $2,300.

Any brand modeling a move to Plus should calculate cost against projected revenue, not the headline number, since the variable band changes the economics well before the cap.

### Shopify POS Pro - €89/month per location

Unlocking brick-and-mortar success requires breaking down the complete Shopify POS pricing structure to protect your real margins.

#### It is important to note that Shopify POS is split into two versions:

* Shopify POS Lite is included with all Shopify plans at no additional cost.

This basic version offers essential POS functionalities suitable for businesses just starting with in-person sales, pop-up events, or casual markets.

* Shopify POS Pro is a premium upgrade for full-scale retail locations. The cost for POS Pro is €89 USD per month for each physical store.

This upgrade fits omnichannel brands with physical retail locations that need to eliminate inventory discrepancies and streamline in-person operations.

#### Key capabilities:

* Enables buy-online-pick-up-in-store (BOPIS) and cross-channel returns to increase customer lifetime value.
* Reduces stockouts through automated demand forecasting and purchase order management using inventory management tools.
* Improves operational control with unlimited staff accounts and custom role permissions.
* Delivers granular reporting on daily sales, staff performance, and inventory turnover.

Using Shopify Payments eliminates extra transaction fees. Alternative hardware or external payment gateways incur standard plan-specific transaction fees.

### Shopify Agentic (AI Channels)

Shopify Agentic optimizes your product infrastructure for autonomous AI buyers, conversational search engines, and LLM marketplaces.

This setup is built for high-volume enterprise brands looking to secure early market share in AI-driven commerce channels.

#### Key capabilities:

* Structures your product catalog data for immediate indexing and accurate recommendation by AI discovery engines.
* Eliminates traditional UI friction by using secure API protocols that allow autonomous AI agents to execute purchases directly.
* Validates inventory levels and dynamic pricing instantly during automated AI search queries.
* Tracks and analyzes conversion rates, revenue, and AOV originating specifically from AI assistants.

#### This infrastructure allows you to capture high-intent traffic directly at the point of search, lowering customer acquisition costs (CAC) and removing friction from the purchase funnel.

All transactions route through your established Shopify checkout, maintaining your standard enterprise credit card processing rates.

In terms of e-commerce features, Shopify’s closest match is [Bigcommerce](https://craftberry.co/articles/shopify-vs-bigcommerce-which-e-commerce-platform-is-best).

### Shopify vs Bigcommerce

The two platforms are very close with regard to their pricing.

Shopify’s Basic and Standard plans are slightly more affordable than Bigcommerce, but the difference is even greater, if it’s your first year on Shopify, due to the $1 three-month trial period.

However, Shopify and Bigcommerce differ in their transaction fees.

* While Shopify charges transaction fees for third-party gateways, it does not cap your revenue or force upgrades based on sales volume.
* BigCommerce avoids transaction fees but locks you into rigid revenue thresholds that force you into higher pricing tiers as you grow.

Evaluating these platforms based on monthly software fees miscalculates your true costs.

### Shopify vs. WooCommerce

People often compare Shopify with open-source platforms like Woocommerce.  
  
 However, direct price comparisons with them do little justice to Shopify’s utility, robustness, customer support, and performance.

It has some of the best features to support your e-commerce journey and empower you to move with speed and confidence.

[Platforms like Woocommerce](https://craftberry.co/articles/shopify-vs-woocommerce-which-e-commerce-platform-is-best) may have lower costs upfront, but are more complicated to maintain and may require having a dedicated developer or administrator on your team.

Ultimately, investing in Shopify eliminates this technical debt, paying for itself through superior conversion rates and zero infrastructure headaches.   
  
By migrating to a fully managed ecosystem, you shift your focus from fixing broken plugins to driving predictable revenue growth.

## Shopify Credit Card Rates and Transaction Fees

In the world of commerce, every time a credit card is used to facilitate a purchase, the merchant has to pay a credit card processing fee to their bank or payment processor.

#### The exact rates depend on your Shopify plan, but the more expensive your plan, the lower your processing fees will be

Extra transaction fees on Shopify are applicable to all transactions that aren’t made through its in-house payment processor Shopify Payments.

However, [Shopify Payments](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/shopify-payments/supported-countries) is currently available only in selected countries and regions.

If Shopify Payments isn’t supported in your location, there is no need to worry.  
  
 Shopify seamlessly integrates with over 100 alternative third-party payment providers globally to ensure your business can accept payments smoothly.

## Does Shopify Charge for Refunds?

Yes, even if you refund or cancel an order, you won’t receive your credit card processing fee. Shopify is unable or unwilling to refund your fees, as the failed payments still incur costs on their end.

You may find information stating the contrary and this is likely because it hasn’t been updated.

As of 2020, Shopify updated its terms of service to no longer refund card processing fees.

## Does Shopify have any hidden fees?

Absolutely not. Shopify is transparent with its prices and you shouldn’t be surprised by anything on your invoice.

However, there are additional costs for domain names, premium themes, and apps, which we will discuss more in the following section.

#### From the craftberry Shopify team:

The most common hidden cost craftberry finds is not on the invoice at all.

When a merchant uninstalls an app, its code rarely leaves cleanly. Orphaned Liquid snippets, leftover metafields, and lingering script tags stay embedded in the theme, still loading on every page and still degrading Time to First Byte long after the subscription is cancelled.

On a typical audit our team removes dozens of these artifacts from stores that switched apps repeatedly over the years. The subscription stopped, the performance cost did not.

However, customizing your store, extending its functionality, and transforming it into the shop of your dreams will cost you extra.

Depending on the complexity of your requirements, these implementation costs can range from $10,000 to $150,000.

### Apps and Integrations

The Shopify App Store currently boasts over 17,600 apps. Each of them is designed to solve a specific problem that merchants face.

Apps can help you improve customer experiences, automate processes, extend and customize your store’s functionality, scale and streamline your operations, and more.

#### The average store we work with has about 8 paid apps integrated into their store. Most brands spend $350 to $1,400/month on apps.

All Shopify apps vary in price, most often between $10 and $100 per month, but what they have in common is that they are vetted, reliable, and maintained by customer support teams.

All in all, if you have specific business requirements, you may have to include Shopify apps in your budget.

### Premium Themes

Shopify boasts a variety of free themes. However, they are limited in terms of [functionality and customization options.](https://craftberry.co/services/custom-theme-development-for-shopify-and-shopify-plus)

#### Many businesses prefer to pay for a premium Shopify theme, to take greater control of how their store looks, feels, and interacts with customers.

Premium themes usually range from around $140 to over $400.

### Domain Name

Another cost that’s not covered by your Shopify plan is your domain name.

Although Shopify, can get you started with a myshopify domain ending, most businesses find that unprofessional so they opt for a custom domain.

Domain names typically cost $10 to $30 per year.

### Email Marketing

Shopify Email provides email hosting. This means that you don’t have to use a third-party integration if you want to leverage email marketing at the start. Costs there vary depending on your usage and the volume of emails sent.

The first 10,000 emails are free, and then each 1,000 emails cost $1, but this price gets lowered after your first 300,000 emails.

However, we consider Shopify emails to be an entry tool. For more sophisticated email marketing, we recommend integrating Kklavyio.

Each plan comes with its own set of features and credit card processing rates, with higher-tier plans offering lower transaction fees.

## FAQ

### Is Shopify a good fit for small businesses?

Yes, Shopify has affordable plans that equip small businesses with all the tools they need to begin selling effectively online.

Moreover, Shopify’s robust backend, user-friendly interface, and rockstar customer support ensure that even non-tech-savvy owners will have an easy time setting up their online store.

### Which Shopify plan should I choose?

The right Shopify plan for you will depend on your exact situation and business needs.

Generally speaking, if you are generating less than $5,000 per month you can stick to Shopify Basic, and if you are generating over $10,000 a month in sales, you can consider looking into the Advanced Shopify Plan.

Large companies and enterprises should check out Shopify Plus.

If you’d like some help finding out which is the best Shopify plan for you, you can get in touch with our team for a free [Shopify consultation](https://craftberry.co/contact-us).

### Can I try Shopify before committing?

Yes! Shopify offers a free 3-day trial, followed up by a 3-month deal for $1.

You can also create a development store with which you can play around, but won’t be able to sell.

### What are the credit card and transaction fees of Shopify?

Exact credit card and transaction fees on Shopify depend on your Shopify Plan, as well as your payment processor, and the exact type of card.

Generally, more premium plans offer lower card processing costs and transaction fees.

If you’re using Shopify Payments, you aren’t charged any extra transaction fees, apart from the card processing fee.

### How much do Shopify templates cost?

Shopify templates or themes can cost anywhere from $100 to over $450 as a one-time purchase.

However, more advanced themes offer extended functionalities and customization options, which larger organizations require.

### How much do Shopify apps cost?

It’s difficult to put an exact number. Many apps have free, as well as paid versions.

Some apps cost a few bucks, while others can cost hundreds or even thousands of dollars every month, while others depend on your usage.

### What are the billing cycles of Shopify?

Your monthly Shopify subscription is billed every 30 days. Apps that have subscription-based charges for merchants operate on their own independent 30-day billing cycles.

### How much does headless Shopify cost?

The cost of a headless Shopify build is usually in the tens of thousands and is dependent on multiple factors.

The price of a headless Shopify setup can vary based on several factors, including the scale and intricacy of the project, the geographical location of the developer, the nature of the development, the technology used, any bespoke features, integrations, and licensing fees.

If you are serious about [exploring the possibility of a headless Shopify build](https://craftberry.co/services/shopify-headless-development-agency-you-can-trust), you can reach out to our team for a free consultation.

### How to save money with Shopify?

When it comes to saving money with Shopify there are two things you can always do.

First, paying for your plans annually or even 2 or 3 years in advance can make a big difference, compared to paying for it month for month.

Second, merchants should keep an eye on all the apps they use and cancel subscriptions that they don’t need since it’s common to forget about some apps altogether.

Another thing that many people miss is the ability to pause your Shopify subscription if you need to take a break from the platform or your priorities change.

### How do Shopify's prices compare to other e-commerce platforms?

Shopify’s prices are mid to high-tier compared to other e-commerce platforms when it comes to their more advanced plans.

However, their cheaper plans pack a mighty punch and offer features that competitors at Bigcommerce offer only in their more premium plans.

Moreover, the utility, user-friendliness, global performance, hassle-free maintenance, and stellar customer support make Shopify one of the global e-commerce leaders.

See also: [Best Shopify Loyalty & Rewards Apps](https://craftberry.co/articles/5-best-shopify-loyalty-and-reward-apps) and [Average Revenue of Shopify Stores](https://craftberry.co/articles/average-revenue-of-shopify-stores).

### At what sales volume does Shopify Plus become cost-effective versus Advanced?

Rarely on processing rates alone. The plan-fee gap between Advanced ($299) and Plus ($2,300) is roughly $2,000 a month, and closing that gap through the lower Plus card rate requires very high card volume.

The real trigger is capability: checkout extensibility, Shopify Functions, native B2B, higher API rate limits, and expanded staff accounts.

Most merchants move to Plus when those features unlock revenue or remove an operational ceiling, not when the processing math breaks even.

### How much does custom app development cost compared to paid apps?

A custom app is a one-time build, often in the low-to-mid five figures, versus $500 to $2,000 or more per month for a stack of paid apps that compounds as the catalog grows. Break-even depends on the combined monthly cost of the apps it replaces.

When several overlapping apps each charge a monthly fee and degrade page performance, a single custom app usually pays for itself inside 12 to 18 months and improves Core Web Vitals at the same time.

### Do transaction fees still apply when using a third-party payment gateway on Shopify Plus?

Yes. Routing payments through a gateway other than Shopify Payments adds a per-transaction fee on top of the gateway's own processing rate, in the range of 0.15% to 0.30% on Plus.

Shopify Payments removes that additional transaction fee, though standard card processing rates still apply.

For high-volume merchants, the third-party transaction fee alone can outweigh a lower processing rate offered elsewhere, so the total effective rate should be modeled on real order volume.

### What does migrating to an upgraded Shopify plan or to Plus actually cost?

Direct answer: the subscription is the smallest part. Migration cost is driven by catalog size, integration complexity, custom logic that must be rebuilt, and whether a redesign is in scope.

Directional ranges run from $5,000 to $15,000 for a small store, $15,000 to $50,000 for a mid-market build with ERP or CRM connections, and $50,000 or more for enterprise migrations involving custom architecture and multi-market setups.

The reliable figure comes from a technical audit of the current store, not a flat quote.

Understanding Shopify plans and pricing can help you choose the right plan and prevent overpaying for features you may not need. Shopify caters to complete beginners and seasoned merchants who want to migrate their stores to Shopify.

Read this guide where we break down Shopify plan prices and features to help find the right option for your store.

## Shopify pricing and plans

Shopify has 4 plans to offer for businesses of any size – Starter, Basic, Grow, Advanced, and Plus. The Starter plan is the cheapest but very limited and provides you with features to build a simple storefront with the Spotlight theme rather than a complex website.

All of the other plans come with **unlimited products, themes, Analytics, unlimited hosting, free SSLs, collaborator accounts**, and more.

Here’s a quick Shopify pricing plan comparison and their monthly vs yearly plans:

| Costs | Starter | Basic | Grow | Advanced | Shopify Plus |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Price (paid yearly)** | $5/month | $29/month | $79/month | $299/month | $2,300/month |
| **Price (paid monthly)** | $5/month | $39/month | $105/month | $399/month | - |
| **Credit card rates (online)** | 5% + 30¢ | 2.9% + 30¢ | 2.7% + 30¢ | 2.5% + 30¢ | Custom |
| **Credit card rates (in person), USD** | 5% | 2.6% + 10¢ | 2.5% + 10¢ | 2.4% + 10¢ | Custom |
| **Best for** | Merchants who want to sell on social media | Small stores, solopreneurs | Startups with a small team | Medium to large businesses for international selling | Enterprise-level businesses with custom needs |

Turn your passion into an empire
