<webpage_content>
# Amazon Seller Central Pricing Explained: Fees & Costs Guide 2026

last updated on 21 July 2026

![](https://unicorn-images.b-cdn.net/889a7add-0636-489d-8207-7869bb9254c8?optimizer=gif) 

Amazon selling fees include referral fees, FBA fulfillment and storage charges, selling-plan fees, closing fees, return-related costs, and optional advertising spend. Depending on category, fulfillment method, inventory age, and ad spend, total marketplace costs can consume roughly 30%–45% of the selling price, so calculate profitability at the SKU level.

Your total Amazon Seller Central cost depends on product category, fulfillment method, item size, item weight, selling price, return rate, storage time, and ad spend.

A product may look profitable before launch, then lose margin after Amazon Seller Central charges are included. That is why sellers need to calculate costs at the SKU level, not only at the account level.

This guide explains Amazon Seller Central pricing, common charges, how to calculate total seller cost, where to find fee reports, and how to reduce margin leaks.

 ![](https://unicorn-images.b-cdn.net/f7e26021-cf2d-46c9-b4ab-79fd2e3e0b4e?optimizer=gif) 

## Amazon Seller Central Charges at a Glance

Amazon Seller Central charges include account plan fees, referral fees, fulfillment fees, storage fees, return-related charges, removal or disposal fees, and optional costs like advertising.

Use this table as a quick reference before reviewing each fee in detail.

| Charge type | Typical 2026 cost or range | When it applies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Individual selling plan | $0.99 per item sold | When using the Individual plan |
| Professional selling plan | $39.99 per month | When using the Professional plan |
| Referral fee | Commonly 8%–15%; some categories reach 45%, with minimum fees where applicable | On each sale |
| Media closing fee | $1.80 per eligible media item | Books, DVD, Music, Software, Video, and applicable media categories |
| FBA fulfillment | Approximately $3.22–$10.48+ per standard-size unit before applicable surcharges | When Amazon fulfills the order |
| Standard-size storage | Approximately $0.87 per cubic foot from January–September and $2.40 from October–December | When inventory is stored in FBA |
| Inbound placement | Approximately $0.21–$1.58 per unit | When Amazon distributes eligible inbound inventory |
| Low-inventory-level fee | Approximately $0.32–$0.97 per unit | When eligible inventory falls below Amazon’s historical days-of-supply thresholds |
| Refund administration fee | Lesser of $5.00 or 20% of the applicable referral fee | When Amazon issues an eligible refund |
| Advertising | Variable CPC and campaign spend | When the seller runs Amazon Ads |

Note: Amazon changes fee schedules periodically. Verify every rate against Seller Central, Fee and Economics Preview, and Amazon’s official pricing pages immediately before publication.

These are the main cost buckets sellers should model before setting prices.

The most important rule is simple: calculate Amazon seller fees at the SKU level. Account averages can hide products that are losing money.

## Amazon Selling Plans: Individual vs Professional

[Amazon selling plans](https://sell.amazon.com/pricing#selling-plans): Individual and Professional. The Individual plan is usually better for low-volume sellers, while the Professional plan is better for sellers who sell more than 40 units per month or need advanced tools.

| Selling Plan | Cost | Best For | Watchout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Individual | $0.99 per item sold | Low-volume sellers or testing Amazon | Limited access to advanced selling tools |
| Professional | $39.99/month | Sellers moving more than 40 units/month or using advanced tools | Monthly fee applies even if sales are low |

### Individual Selling Plan

The Individual plan charges a per-item fee when a product sells. It can work for sellers testing Amazon or selling a small number of products.

This plan is simple, but it has limits. Sellers may not get the same access to advertising, automation, reporting, bulk tools, and brand-building options available on the Professional plan.

### Professional Selling Plan

The Professional plan is billed on a monthly subscription basis. It is usually the better choice for sellers with higher sales volume or more serious marketplace operations.

A simple rule:

If your sales cross 40 units per month, the Professional plan is usually more cost-effective than paying $0.99 per item.

For most growing Amazon brands, the Professional plan is the standard choice.

## Amazon Referral Fees by Category

Amazon referral fees are category-based commissions Amazon charges on each sale. In most categories, the referral fee is counted as a percentage of the total sale price or a minimum referral fee, whichever is greater.

[Referral fees](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/help/hub/reference/external/GTG4BAWSY39Z98Z3) are one of the biggest Amazon Seller Central charges because they apply to every sale.

| Amazon fee category | Referral fee | Minimum referral fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Amazon Device Accessories | 45% | $0.30 |
| Baby Products | 8% at $10 or less; 15% above $10 | $0.30 |
| Beauty, Health & Personal Care | 8% at $10 or less; 15% above $10 | $0.30 |
| Clothing & Accessories | 5% at $15 or less; 10% above $15 through $20; 17% above $20 | $0.30 |
| Consumer Electronics | 8% | $0.30 |
| Grocery & Gourmet Food | 8% at $15 or less; 15% above $15 | No minimum listed in the supplied table |
| Home & Kitchen | 15% | $0.30 |
| Jewelry | 20% on the portion up to $250; 5% on the portion above $250 | $0.30 |
| Pet Supplies | 15%; 22% for veterinary diets | $0.30 |

A product’s Amazon fee category may differ from the customer-facing browse category, so confirm the assigned fee category before pricing,

Do not assume your product’s referral fee based only on the broad category name. Amazon fee categories can be more specific than product categories.

Before launch, check the official [Amazon referral fee schedule](https://sell.amazon.com/pricing#referral-fees) and model the fee against your actual selling price.

## Amazon FBA Fees and Fulfillment Costs

Amazon FBA fees are fulfillment-related costs for sellers who use Amazon to store, pick, pack, ship, and support customer service for orders.

FBA can improve operations and Prime eligibility, but it can also reduce margin if inventory, returns, and size tiers are not managed carefully.

| FBA Cost Type | What It Means | Why It Matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fulfillment fee | Cost to pick, pack, ship, and handle the order | Usually one of the largest FBA costs |
| Monthly storage fee | Cost to store inventory in Amazon fulfillment centers | Can rise with excess inventory or Q4 demand |
| Aged inventory surcharge | Extra charge for slow-moving inventory | Hurts products with poor sell-through |
| Removal fee | Cost to return inventory to you | Applies when pulling stock out of FBA |
| Disposal fee | Cost to dispose of inventory | Applies when liquidating or removing unsellable stock |
| Return processing cost | Return-related cost for some categories | Affects high-return products |
| Low inventory or placement charges | Possible inventory-related fees depending on current Amazon rules | Verify against the latest fee schedule |

### FBA Fulfillment Fees

FBA fulfillment fees are charged per unit and vary by size tier, shipping weight, product price, and category. As a practical 2026 reference, standard-size fees commonly begin around $3.22 per unit and can exceed $10 for heavier standard-size products, while bulky products cost more. Because Amazon may revise rates and surcharges, confirm each ASIN through Fee and Economics Preview or the Revenue Calculator before publishing or repricing.

Review the current Amazon FBA pricing schedule for size-tier rules, applicable surcharges, and current per-unit rates.

### Monthly Storage and Seasonal Storage Costs

For standard-size inventory, a useful 2026 planning benchmark is approximately $0.87 per cubic foot from January through September and $2.40 per cubic foot from October through December. Oversize rates differ, and aged-inventory or storage-utilization surcharges can apply in addition to monthly storage. Verify the final figures in Seller Central before publication.

### Aged Inventory and Long-Term Storage Charges

Amazon applies aged-inventory surcharges monthly to FBA units stored for more than 181 days. The charge increases across inventory-age bands and may be assessed per cubic foot or per unit, so sellers should review the Inventory Age and FBA fee reports before stock crosses the next threshold. Slow-moving inventory can therefore create both cash-flow pressure and progressively higher carrying costs.

### Removal, Disposal, and Return Processing Fees

Inbound placement and low-inventory-level fees: Amazon may charge an inbound placement service fee when it distributes standard-size or large-bulky inventory across fulfillment centers. The amount varies by size, weight, and shipment-split option. A separate low-inventory-level fee may apply when historical days of supply remain below Amazon’s threshold. Model both charges at the ASIN level because they can materially change per-unit margin.

## FBA vs FBM vs Seller Fulfilled Prime: Cost Comparison

FBA, FBM, and Seller Fulfilled Prime each have different cost structures. The cheapest option depends on product size, margin, fulfillment capability, customer expectations, and operational control.

| Fulfillment Method | Main Costs | Best For | Watchout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FBA | Fulfillment, storage, surcharges, removal/disposal | Prime-eligible scale and outsourced operations | Storage and return costs can hurt margins |
| FBM | Shipping, packaging, labor, customer service | Large/heavy items, custom handling, margin control | Seller handles operations and service |
| Seller Fulfilled Prime | Seller fulfillment plus Prime performance standards | Sellers with strong logistics | Hard to maintain speed and service standards |

FBA streamlines operations and enhances the customer experience, but sellers must monitor storage, size tiers, returns, and inventory age.

FBM can be better for large, heavy, fragile, custom, or low-margin products where FBA fees are too high. Seller Fulfilled Prime can work for sellers with strong logistics capabilities, but only if they meet speed and service standards.

## Hidden Amazon Seller Central Charges Sellers Miss

Hidden Amazon Seller Central charges are costs sellers often forget to model before launch. These charges may not appear in the headline selling plan fee, but they can quickly reduce margin.

| Hidden Charge | Why It Happens | How to Reduce It |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Refund administration fee | Customer returns | Reduce return drivers and improve listing accuracy |
| Variable closing fee | Media products | Model it before pricing media items |
| High-volume listing fee | Very large catalogs | Audit inactive or low-value ASINs |
| Removal/disposal fees | Slow-moving or unsellable FBA stock | Improve forecasting and liquidation plans |
| Aged inventory surcharge | Inventory sits too long | Track sell-through and inventory age |
| Storage utilization surcharge | Overstock vs sales velocity | Improve inventory planning |
| Lithium battery fees | Battery product handling | Classify and package correctly |
| Advertising costs | Optional ad spend | Track ACoS, ROAS, and TACoS |
| Return processing | High-return categories | Improve product content and quality control |
| Prep and labeling costs | Packaging or labeling requirements | Fix packaging workflow before inbound shipping |

### Refund Administration Fee

When an item is returned, Amazon may refund part of the referral fee but keep a refund administration fee. When Amazon issues a refund, it generally returns the referral fee but retains a refund administration fee equal to the lesser of $5.00 or 20% of the applicable referral fee. This is separate from any FBA returns-processing fee that may apply when Amazon provides free return shipping for eligible products.

This matters for products with high return rates. Apparel, electronics, fragile goods, and products with unclear sizing may see higher return-related costs.

### Variable Closing Fee

Variable closing fees can apply to media products such as books, music, video, DVD, software, and similar categories. Amazon charges a $1.80 closing fee per media item sold in categories such as Books, DVD, Music, Software, and Video, in addition to the referral fee. Standard Home & Kitchen products do not normally incur the media closing fee; they generally pay the applicable Home & Kitchen referral fee instead, which is currently 15% with a $0.30 minimum. Therefore, a seller asking about a ‘closing fee on kitchen items’ should first confirm whether the ASIN is actually classified in a media fee category or is simply subject to a referral-fee minimum.

Sellers in media categories should model this fee before pricing products.

### Advertising Costs

[Amazon advertising costs](https://salesduo.com/amazon-advertising-agency/) are optional, but they often become a major variable expense for growing sellers. Include ad spend in SKU-level profitability and use [Amazon Ads Campaign Manager](https://advertising.amazon.com/solutions/products/sponsored-products) to review campaign spend, clicks, CPC, attributed sales, ACoS, and budget delivery.

Ad spend should be included in SKU-level profitability. A product with strong gross margin can still lose money if ACoS is too high or if ads do not support total sales growth. Brands that need integrated control over ACoS, TACoS, and contribution margin may benefit from support from an experienced Amazon advertising agency.

### Other Conditional Fees

Large catalogs may incur a high-volume listing fee of $0.005 per eligible active non-media ASIN per month once the account exceeds 100,000 qualifying listings. International sellers may also pay Amazon Currency Converter for Sellers fees, while textbook-rental, Multi-Channel Fulfillment, liquidation, and other program charges apply only to participating sellers. Confirm eligibility and rates inside Seller Central before including them in margin models.

## How to Calculate Total Amazon Seller Central Cost

To calculate total Amazon Seller Central cost, use this formula:

* Total Amazon fees = Selling-plan fee + Referral fee + Fulfillment fee + Storage fee + Return/refund charges + Optional program fees + Advertising spend

A simple example:

What You May Pay on a $25 Amazon Sale

| Line item | Illustrative amount |
| --- | --- |
| Selling price | $25.00 |
| Referral fee at 15% | −$3.75 |
| FBA fulfillment estimate | −$4.08 |
| Storage allocation | −$0.15 |
| Inbound placement allocation | −$0.27 |
| Advertising allocation | −$2.50 |
| Returns allowance | −$0.50 |
| Product cost | −$5.00 |
| Estimated net before overhead | $8.75 |
| Estimated margin before overhead | 35% |

Note: This example is illustrative. Actual fees vary by category, dimensions, weight, inventory age, return rate, and fulfillment method, so confirm the ASIN in Amazon’s Revenue Calculator.

Use contribution-margin analysis to identify which products to scale and where to make operational changes to [maximize your Amazon profits](https://salesduo.com/maximize-amazon-profits/). The key is to calculate at the SKU level. Product-level margin analysis shows which SKUs are worth scaling and which need changes to pricing, packaging, fulfillment, or advertising.

## Where to Find Seller Central Pricing and Charges

Use Fee and Economics Preview for downloadable estimates across FBA inventory, the Revenue Calculator to compare Amazon fulfillment with seller fulfillment for a current or future product, and Payments/Transaction View for actual order-level charges, refunds, and adjustments.

In Seller Central, report names and navigation may vary by account and interface version. The Revenue Calculator accepts inputs for dimensions, weight, category, price, shipping,

Review the official [Amazon pricing page](https://sell.amazon.com/pricing/estimate) for current selling-plan fees, referral rates, and links to fee-estimation tools.

| Need | Seller Central / Amazon Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Estimate fees before launch | Amazon Revenue Calculator |
| Check referral fee category | Referral fee schedule |
| Check FBA fulfillment estimate | FBA Revenue Calculator |
| Find transaction-level charges | Payments / Transaction View |
| Track FBA storage | Inventory reports |
| Check removals/disposals | Fulfillment reports |
| Review ad spend | Campaign Manager |
| Audit account profitability | Business Reports + fee exports |

### Amazon Revenue Calculator

Sellers can estimate fees before launch or when changing fulfillment methods using the [Amazon Revenue Calculator](https://sell.amazon.com/tools/revenue-calculator).

Use it to compare FBA and seller-fulfilled cost estimates. Update the inputs when any of the following change: product dimensions, weight, category, price, shipping charges, or fulfillment method.

### Payments and Transaction View

Access transaction-level charges from Seller Central payment reports.

Use these reports to understand exactly what Amazon charged on each order, refund, or adjustment.

### Inventory and FBA Reports

Many FBA costs stem from inventory planning mistakes. Utilize Inventory reports to track storage, inventory age, sell-through, fulfillment-related issues, and removals.

## How to Reduce Amazon Seller Central Costs

The fastest way to control Amazon costs is to identify the largest SKU-level margin leak—such as size tier, storage age, returns, or advertising—and fix that issue first. For a step-by-step optimization framework, see [how to reduce your FBA fees](https://salesduo.com/reduce-amazon-fba-fees/).

## Common Amazon Seller Fee Mistakes

Most Amazon seller fee mistakes occur because sellers price products before calculating the full cost. Other common reasons are poor inventory planning, weak listing content, or ignored reports.

Use this checklist before launching or scaling a SKU:

* Pricing without checking referral fee category
* Ignoring Q4 storage changes
* Sending slow-moving inventory to FBA
* Not accounting for refunds and returns.
* Treating ad spend separately from product margin.
* Overlooking packaging size and shipping weight
* Not reviewing transaction-level fees.
* Keeping inactive ASINs live at scale.
* Using FBA when FBM would be cheaper
* Ignoring fee updates
* Not reviewing storage and aged inventory reports.
* Scaling ads before confirming product-level profit

Track contribution margin at the SKU level because account-wide averages can hide products that generate revenue while losing profit.

When to Get Expert Help Managing Seller Central Costs

Get expert help when Amazon costs are rising, but the cause is unclear. This often happens when fee data, listing issues, FBA charges, advertising spend, and returns are tracked in disconnected reports.

You may need support if:

* Fees rise, but the margin effect is unclear.
* FBA charges are hard to reconcile
* Ad spend is masking product-level losses.
* Returns are eroding profit.
* Reporting is scattered across Seller Central exports.
* Category or fee changes affect pricing strategy.
* Your team needs product-level profitability reporting.
* You cannot tell which SKUs are worth scaling.

Full-service [Amazon account management](https://salesduo.com/full-service-amazon-account-management/) can integrate Seller Central fees, advertising, inventory, listing quality, and SKU-level profitability into a single operating model.

## Conclusion: Seller Central Pricing Is a Profit System

Amazon Seller Central pricing is more than a list of fees. It is a profit system that affects pricing, fulfillment, advertising, inventory, returns, and SKU-level margin.

Sellers should review Amazon Seller Central charges before launch and keep auditing them after sales begin. Referral fees, FBA costs, storage, returns, removals, and ad spend can all affect a product's actual profitability.

The best sellers do not only ask, “What does Amazon charge?” They ask, “After every fee, return, storage cost, and ad dollar, is this product still worth scaling?”

If you can answer that at the SKU level, you can make better decisions about pricing, fulfillment, inventory, and advertising.

4. Maintain the chronological order of events if the content is time-sensitive or historical.

# Amazon Seller Central Pricing Guide (Updated July 2026)

This guide provides a comprehensive overview of Amazon seller fees and costs for 2026. Total marketplace costs typically consume 30%–45% of the selling price, depending on category, fulfillment method, inventory age, and ad spend.

## Key Fee Categories

**Selling Plans:**
- Individual plan: $0.99 per item sold (best for low-volume sellers)
- Professional plan: $39.99/month (best for sellers moving >40 units/month)

**Referral Fees:** Category-based commissions, commonly 8%–15%, with some categories reaching 45%. Minimum referral fees (typically $0.30) apply where applicable.

**FBA Fulfillment:** Standard-size fees range from approximately $3.22 to $10.48+ per unit before surcharges.

**Storage Fees (standard-size):** ~$0.87/cubic foot (Jan–Sep), ~$2.40/cubic foot (Oct–Dec).

**Other Notable Fees:** Media closing fee ($1.80 per eligible media item), inbound placement fees ($0.21–$1.58/unit), low-inventory-level fees ($0.32–$0.97/unit), refund administration fee (lesser of $5.00 or 20% of referral fee), and variable advertising costs.

## Hidden Costs to Watch For

Refund administration fees, aged inventory surcharges (for units stored >181 days), storage utilization surcharges, removal/disposal fees, high-volume listing fees ($0.005/ASIN/month for accounts >100,000 listings), and advertising costs.

## Cost Calculation Approach

The recommended formula: Total Amazon fees = Selling-plan fee + Referral fee + Fulfillment fee + Storage fee + Return/refund charges + Optional program fees + Advertising spend.

An illustrative example on a $25 sale shows ~35% net margin before overhead after all fees, product cost, and ad allocation.

## Key Tools

- **Amazon Revenue Calculator** – for fee estimation before launch
- **Payments/Transaction View** – for actual order-level charges
- **Inventory Reports** – for tracking storage and aged inventory
- **Campaign Manager** – for ad spend tracking

## Recommendations

Calculate Amazon fees at the SKU level (not account-wide averages), as account averages can hide unprofitable products. Common mistakes include pricing without checking referral fee categories, ignoring Q4 storage changes, and not accounting for returns and refunds. The guide is authored by Nandita Nair of SalesDuo and ends with a call to book a 1:1 growth call.

**Amazon 2026 US Fee Update Announcement (via Seller Forums)**

Amazon announced 2026 updates to US Referral and Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) fees on its Seller Forums. FBA fees will increase by an average of $0.08 per unit sold (less than 0.5% of an average selling price), following no increase in 2025. Amazon claims the fee changes are significantly less than inflation and less than the 3.9%-5.9% annual increases from major US carriers over the last two years.

Amazon states it is creating a more granular fee structure with lower fees where costs are lower and higher fees for enhanced services. No new FBA fee types will be introduced in 2026. Amazon is providing tools such as the Revenue Calculator, Fee and Economics Preview report, and a new Profit Analytics dashboard for sellers to assess impacts. All changes will take effect January 15, 2026, with at least 90 days' notice.

**Seller Reactions (Summary of Top Replies):**
- Many sellers disputed the "$0.08 average" claim, with one calling it "more like 30+ cents."
- A highly upvoted reply (550 votes) sarcastically noted that while there was no fee increase in 2025, Amazon introduced new fees including inventory placement fees, low-level inventory surcharges, long-term inventory surcharges, increased return fees, and slashed reimbursements for lost inbound shipments—calling 2025 "the biggest fee hike to date."
- A seller expressed concern about slow-moving items seeing slower delivery promises or limited nationwide availability.
- A grocery seller requested an increase in the threshold for the 8% referral fee discount, saying it's impossible to price products below $15.
- A small business seller highlighted combined pressures from tariffs, advertising costs (PPC), and fee increases on thin profit margins.
- One seller noted they will continue pricing higher on Amazon than on their own website.
- A seller compared Amazon's increases unfavorably to Walmart, which has not raised similar fees.

Overall, the announcement was met with significant seller skepticism and frustration, particularly regarding the accuracy of the average increase claim and the cumulative burden of various fees introduced in prior years.

month that you have inventory in their warehouse. From January to September, they charge you 78 per 
cubic foot per month. From October to December, they charge $2.40 per cubic foot because that's 
peak holiday season and everyone wants warehouse space. Now, the good news is for most small to 
mediumsiz products, storage fees are pretty cheap. We're talking pennies per unit per month. But it 
adds up fast if your product is bulky or if you're storing a lot of inventory for a long time. Now, 
here's where it gets serious. Amazon has something called the aged inventory searchcharge. This used 
to be called the long-term storage fee, and it used to only kick in after 365 days, but Amazon 
changed this and made it way more aggressive. Now, they start charging you extra after just 181 days. 
That's about 6 months. And the penalties go up in tiers. At 181 to 270 days, they charge around 
50 cents per cubic foot on top of your regular storage fees. At 271 to 365 days, it jumps 
to $1.50 per cubic foot per month. And beyond 365 days, it goes even higher. Now, keep in mind, 
this only applies if your products aren't selling. If you send in a 100 units, sell through them 
within a few months. The clock resets when the new stock comes in. The search charge only hits 
items that are sitting there collecting dust. One hack to avoid it is to watch your levels 
closely. If you see products aren't moving and you're getting close to that six-month mark, 
ask Amazon to send them back. Even if you're just going to repackage everything and send it right 
back in, this could save you money. But ideally, the best way to avoid it is to figure out exactly 
how much stock you should send into Amazon. and I go into depth about that and a bunch of other 
secrets in my free Amazon FBA course that I'll put a link to down below. It's completely free YouTube 
video. If you're just starting on Amazon, I highly recommend checking it out. These next few fees are 
the ones that catch people completely offguard. And one of them changed everything in 2026. The 
first fee is the return fee. If your customer decides within 30 days to return the product, you 
have to pay a fee that covers return shipping and processing. If the product is in good condition, 
Amazon can put it back into your inventory or you can have them dispose of it for around 50 cents 
per unit. Now, Amazon restructured how they charge return fees recently. They use a threshold-based 
system. For most categories, they only charge the return processing fee when your return rate goes 
above a certain threshold. So, if you have a low return rate, you might not have to pay this 
at all. But apparel and shoes get charged on every single return with no threshold. And if your 
product ships fewer than 25 units a month, you're exempt entirely. But I want to pause here for a 
second because there's a big mistake most beginner sellers overlook. A lot of sellers think that 
because they have an LLC, they're protected. And yeah, your LLC does separate your personal assets 
from your business assets, which is great. But here's the thing. Your LLC does not protect your 
business if a customer claims your product injured them or if you get hit with some kind of liability 
claim. And look, I know insurance is not the most exciting topic, but this stuff happens more than 
you think. That's where Erggo Next comes in. It is specifically built for small business owners. 
You go to their website, answer a few questions, and you can get a free quote in less than 7 
minutes. No phone calls, no dealing with an agent. It's all online. plans start at $29 a month, which 
is honestly nothing when you think about what you're protecting. And one thing that's actually 
super useful as an Amazon seller is that you can generate a certificate of insurance instantly 
from their app. A lot of 3PL's and suppliers are going to ask you for that. So, go check them 
out and get your free quote. The link is in the description down below. Now, here's a fee that 
had a huge change in 2026, the prepping fee. Every product you send into Amazon needs an FNQ 
barcode on it. In the past, you could pay Amazon 30 cents per unit to label everything for you. And 
they used to offer services like polybagging. But as of January 1st, 2026, Amazon permanently ended 
all FBA prep and labeling services in the United States. No more labeling, no more polybagging, no 
more prep work of any kind. Every single unit you send in has to arrive fully prepped and labeled. 
If it doesn't, they can reject your shipment and send it back at your cost. So now you have two 
options. Have your manufacturer handle the FN SKQ labels and prepping, which is what I recommend, 
or use a third-party prep service. If you're using custom packaging, just print the barcode right on 
the box and boom, that's the cheapest and easiest solution. Now, here's a fee that a lot of people 
don't know about because it's relatively new, the low inventory level fee. Amazon now charges 
you if your inventory drops too low. If both your 30 and 90day supply fall below 28 days worth 
of stock, Amazon charges you anywhere from 32 cents to 90 cents per unit. Think about that. 
They charge you if you have too much inventory with the aged inventory search charge. And they 
charge you if you don't have enough with a low inventory level fee. You have to find that sweet 
spot. The sweet spot is keeping between 1 and 6 months of inventory in Amazon's warehouse at all 
times. In 2026, Amazon made grocery products and slower moving items exempt, but for most sellers, 
this is something you need to watch. Another fee that catches sellers by surprise is the inbound 
placement service fee. When you send inventory to Amazon, you can either split your shipment 
costs across multiple warehouses yourself or send everything to one location and let Amazon 
distribute it. If Amazon distributes it, they charge you a fee. The hack is to ship to 
five or more locations yourself, and you don't pay this fee at all. Now, the biggest way 
to lower your fees across the board is to make your packaging smaller. The size and weight 
directly impact every FBA charge you pay. Even shaving a fraction of an inch off your packaging 
could drop you into a lower size tier and save you a dollar or more per unit. When you're moving 
thousands of units, that adds up fast. If you're selling a lowerpriced item, Amazon has something 
called the low price FBA fees. This replace the old small and light program. If your item is 
priced under $10, it automatically qualifies. You don't have to enroll or do anything. Amazon 
just gives you the lower rate that comes out to a discount of around 86 cents per unit. If 
you're selling thousands of units a month, that's hundreds, if not thousands of dollars in 
savings. One thing to know is that the old small and light program covered items up to $12. The new 
low price program only covers items under $10. So, if you're priced between $10 and $12, you actually 
lost that discount. You also need to make sure that Amazon has the correct dimensions of your 
product in their system. Sometimes they put you in a higher tier than you're supposed to be. You 
want to catch this as soon as possible and contact them. Sometimes they'll even reimburse you for 
the overcharges. And to be honest, there's a lot more ways to save money with Amazon FBA fees. And 
this is something that we can talk about in the free coaching call that you can get by clicking 
the link down below. When you click on the link down below, you can apply for a completely free 
call. There's no catch. There's nothing like that. And on that call, we will see if you're a good fit 
for our accelerator program. And in this program, we hold people's hands and we show them step by 
step how to sell on Amazon. And in this program, we talk about how to avoid a lot of different 
fees. A lot of times, people will come to me and they'll start selling on Amazon and they'll spend 
thousands of dollars on fees that they could have avoided if they just would come and talk to me 
before that. And that's part of the reason why I'm doing these free calls. So, click on the link down 
below, apply for the free call, and not everyone that applies will get a free call with my team, 
but if you do, I recommend getting on that call. I also have a completely free Amazon FBA course 
that you can get by clicking right here. It's a YouTube video, so click on that video. I'll see 
you in the next video and thanks for watching.

This is a YouTube video transcript from Travis Marziani (10+ years e-commerce entrepreneur, $10M+ in sales) explaining Amazon FBA fees as of 2026. The video covers three main fee categories and several smaller ones:

**Three Main Fees:**
1. **Amazon Referral Fee** — Flat 15% for selling on the platform. On a $27.99 product, this is $4.20/unit. Can be reduced to 5% via the Brand Referral Bonus Program by driving external traffic through a special link.
2. **FBA Pick and Pack Fee** — Covers picking, packing, and shipping. Depends on size/weight and now (2026) product price tier (under $10, $10–$50, over $50). Typically $3–$7 per unit. Apparel costs 30–40¢ more.
3. **Storage Fee** — Monthly charge for inventory in Amazon warehouses. Jan–Sep: $0.78/cubic foot. Oct–Dec: $2.40/cubic foot.

**Other Fees & 2026 Changes:**
- **Account Fee** — Individual plan (free, $0.99/sale) vs. Professional ($39.99/month unlimited).
- **Aged Inventory Surcharge** — Starts at 181 days (was 365). $0.50/cu ft (181–270 days), $1.50/cu ft (271–365 days), higher beyond.
- **Low Inventory Level Fee** — New fee. Charged if both 30-day and 90-day supply fall below 28 days. $0.32–$0.90/unit.
- **Return Fee** — Threshold-based for most categories; apparel/shoes charged on every return.
- **Prepping & Labeling Fee** — As of Jan 1, 2026, Amazon permanently ended all prep/labeling services. Sellers must have units fully prepped and labeled before arrival.
- **Inbound Placement Service Fee** — Avoided by shipping to 5+ Amazon locations yourself.
- **Low Price FBA Fees** — Automatic for items under $10 (~$0.86/unit discount). Replaced old Small & Light program (which covered up to $12).

**Real $2M Sales Breakdown:**
- Revenue: $2,000,000
- Referral fees: $295,000
- Pick & pack fees: $255,000
- Other fees (storage, etc.): $39,000
- Product cost: $545,000
- Other expenses: $50,000
- **Total profit: $650,000+**

**Key Advice:**
- The 33/33/33 Rule: 33% product cost, 33% Amazon fees, 33% profit.
- Shrinking packaging can reduce pick & pack costs significantly.
- Switching from FBM (seller-fulfilled) to FBA increased sales 4–5x.
- Keep 1–6 months of inventory to avoid both aged inventory surcharges and low inventory fees.
- Ensure Amazon has correct product dimensions to avoid overcharges.

[Book a demo](https://meetings.hubspot.com/wizcommerce-book-a-demo/demo?ref=BigCommerce+Pricing+in+2026%3A+How+Much+It+Costs+and+Is+It+Worth+It%3F)

If you are looking to build a website on BigCommerce, understanding the **BigCommerce pricing plan** structure is important. Unlike other platforms that charge based solely on the features you use, BigCommerce ties your monthly cost directly to your annual sales volume. This means as your business grows, your cost of platform automatically increases.

In this article, we break down the **BigCommerce pricing plans for 2026**, reveal their “hidden” costs, and compare them against B2B-first alternatives like WizCommerce, so that you can make informed decisions.

## **What is BigCommerce?**

BigCommerce is an ecommerce platform that enables businesses to create online stores and sell products directly to their consumers and wholesale buyers. Built to support both [B2C and B2B ecommerce](/blog/b2b-vs-b2c-ecommerce/),

BigCommerce provides the infrastructure to manage product catalogs, process orders across multiple sales channels, accept payments, and handle inventory management, all without needing extensive technical expertise or custom development.

## **BigCommerce pricing explained**

The four BigCommerce pricing plans are categorized by features and annual online sales volume. Here’s an overview of the cost:

1. **Standard Plan**: $39 when paid monthly and $29 per month when paid annually
2. **Plus Plan**: $105 when paid monthly and $79 per month when paid annually
3. **Pro Plan**: $399 when paid monthly and $299 per month when paid annually
4. **Enterprise Plan**: Custom (starting ~$1,000+/month)

### **BigCommerce Standard Plan**

The BigCommerce Standard plan costs $39 per month on a month-to-month basis, or $29 per month ($348 total) when billed annually. This plan is designed for businesses with an online sales threshold of up to $50,000 per year.

Here’s what you will get in the Standard pricing plan:

* Unlimited products, file storage, bandwidth, and staff accounts.
* Online storefront, Point of Sale, and sales channels (Amazon, eBay, Walmart, Facebook/Instagram).
* Marketplace channels carry their own costs on top of your BigCommerce plan. If home goods is your category, compare those against the [Wayfair business login](https://wizcommerce.com/blog/wayfair-pricing/) and seller fee structure before adding the channel.
* Single-page checkout, Apple Pay/Google Pay/Amazon Pay, multi-currency support, real-time shipping quotes, professional reporting tools, built-in blog, and product ratings/reviews.
* 24/7 tech support (phone, chat, & ticket).

> Note: Once your trailing 12-month sales exceed $50,000, you will have to upgrade your account to the Plus plan ($105/mo) to continue using the platform.

### **BigCommerce Plus Plan**

BigCommerce Plus plan costs $105 per month on a monthly cycle or $79 per month ($948 total) when billed annually. This tier is required for businesses with annual online sales between $50,000 and $180,000.

Everything covered in the Standard plan plus:

* Customer groups and segmentation.
* Abandoned cart saver and persistent cart.
* Stored credit cards.
* Up to 5 storefronts (Multi-Storefront).

### **BigCommerce Pro Plan**

For high-volume merchants, the BigCommerce Pro plan costs $399 per month (billed monthly) or $299 per month when billed annually. This plan accommodates businesses with annual sales up to $400,000/ year.

If your revenue exceeds the $400k mark, BigCommerce adds an incremental fee of $150 per month for every additional $200k in sales, up to $1 million.

Pro plan covers everything included in the previous tier, plus:

* Google customer reviews.
* Product filtering and custom product filtering.
* Up to 8 storefronts (Multi-Storefront).

### **BigCommerce Enterprise Plan**

The BigCommerce Enterprise plan is a custom-priced solution tailored for large-scale operations and high-volume B2B merchants.

While there is no fixed public price, most Enterprise contracts start at approximately $1,000 to $2,000+ per month, depending on your annual GMV (Gross Merchandise Volume) and specific feature requirements.

Additional features offered in the Pro pricing plan are:

* Unlimited API calls.
* Price lists.
* Express routing, priority support, customer success management, and API support.
* ShipperHQ shipping rules engine.
* Custom Multi-Storefront limits.

> > A critical limitation of BigCommerce pricing plans is that if your annual sales exceed your plan’s threshold, you are forced to upgrade to the next plan, even if you don’t need the additional features.

**Also read:** [**15 BigCommerce Alternatives You Can Try This Year**](/blog/bigcommerce-alternatives-and-competitors/)

## **Additional BigCommerce cost beyond subscription**

### **Payment gateway cost**

While BigCommerce does not charge its own transaction fees on any plan, you will still encounter processing fees from payment providers. Those add-on layers are what separate a plan fee from real total cost. Our guide to [B2B ecommerce pricing](https://wizcommerce.com/blog/b2b-commerce-platform-pricing/) breaks down how subscription, transaction, integration, and implementation costs stack up across platforms. Rates typically range from 2.2% to 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction, depending on the processor (e.g., Stripe, PayPal).

However, using the built-in “BigCommerce Payments” (powered by Braintree) can unlock pre-negotiated rates that decrease as you upgrade your plan tier.

### **Third-party app cost**

Although BigCommerce offers more native features than competitors, most scaling businesses still require 3-7 third-party apps to operate fully.

You should budget an additional **$75–$300+ per month** for essential tools such as email marketing (Klaviyo, Mailchimp), advanced reviews (Yotpo), loyalty programs (Smile.io), and shipping integrations, all of which charge their own recurring subscription fees.

### **Hidden costs**

* **Forced Upgrades:** This is the most significant “hidden” cost. If you exceed your annual sales threshold (e.g., $50k/year for Standard), BigCommerce automatically moves you to a more expensive tier, regardless of whether you need the additional features. Selling through marketplaces adds a parallel set of costs your plan fee never shows — our guide on [how to sell on Wayfair](https://wizcommerce.com/blog/how-to-sell-on-wayfair-wholesaler-onboarding-guide/) covers the commission and onboarding requirements on that side.
* **B2B Edition:** Accessing professional wholesale tools like advanced quoting and net terms would require you to purchase the **“B2B Edition” add-on**.
* **Themes & Design:** While there are free options, professional premium themes cost between **$150 and $400**. Furthermore, because BigCommerce uses the complex Stencil framework, custom design changes often require hiring specialized developers, which can range anywhere from **$3,000 to $20,000 and more.**
* **Domain Names:** Custom domains are not included in your subscription and must be purchased separately (approx. $6–$20/year).
* **POS Systems:** If you sell in person, you will need to budget for third-party POS subscriptions (like Clover or Square). These often involve both upfront hardware costs and ongoing monthly software fees.

## **How does BigCommerce compare to WizCommerce?**

To help you evaluate your options, here’s how BigCommerce stacks up against WizCommerce across key capabilities:

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Capability** | **BigCommerce** | **WizCommerce** |
| **Platform focus** | B2C + limited B2B | B2B wholesale commerce |
| **Pricing model** | Tiered by sales volume + features | Quote-based, plan-led |
| **Sales thresholds** | Must upgrade when exceeding thresholds | No forced upgrades based on revenue |
| **B2B functionality** | Basic on all plans; advanced only on Enterprise | Built-in, full-featured across plans |
| **User interface** | Complex, steep learning curve | Intuitive, user-friendly platform |
| **Implementation** | Self-service or agency (often $5K-$20K+) | Included onboarding support |
| **AI sales assistant** | Third-party apps or custom development | Built-in [Kai](/co-worker/ai-sales-copilot/): AI sales co-pilot for reps |
| **AI order automation** | Manual or requires apps | Built-in [Ella](/co-worker/ai-order-quote-automation/): Automates email orders and quotes |
| **AI product images** | Requires third-party tools/apps | Native WizStudio image generator |
| **Wholesale/quoting** | Requires Enterprise tier or apps | Native functionality on all plans |
| **ERP integration** | Limited native options, often requires middleware | Seamless integration with [QuickBooks](https://wizcommerce.com/quickbooks/) Desktop, QuickBooks Online, NetSuite, and major ERPs |
| **Free trial** | 14-day free trial period | Demo-based evaluation |

The most significant difference between BigCommerce and WizCommerce lies in their approach.

BigCommerce is built for businesses that are willing to handle technical complexity and developer costs. WizCommerce, on the other hand, is purpose-built for B2B wholesale commerce, where you can create workflows to manage customer-specific catalogs, quotes, and order-taking.

For a detailed comparison of other platforms, explore our guide on the [best B2B ecommerce platforms.](/blog/best-b2b-wholesale-platform/)

## **WizCommerce features that B2B brands appreciate**

**Native B2B tools without enterprise costs:** Access customer-specific pricing, quote management, net terms, volume discounts, and separate wholesale portals on all plans without forced upgrades or third-party apps.

**Predictable, growth-friendly pricing:** We believe your software costs shouldn’t spike just because you had a good sales month. WizCommerce eliminates revenue-based thresholds and platform transaction fees.

**AI-driven sales and operations:** Stop paying for fragmented app stacks. Our built-in assistants, **Kai** and **Ella**, automate quote generation and order entry directly from your inbox, saving your team hours of manual data entry.

**Fast implementation:** While BigCommerce migrations can take months, WizCommerce is designed for speed. Launch in weeks with native B2B workflows that don’t require hiring a specialized developer team.

**All-in-one functionality:** Replaces fragmented app stacks with native [inventory management](/blog/inventory-management-in-manufacturing/), sales rep territory tracking, customer segmentation, promotional tools, and detailed analytics.

**Integrated ecosystem:** Features flexible [B2B payment processing](/product/b2b-payment-solution/) (**WizPay**) with custom terms, [AI product photography](/product/ai-product-photo-generator/) (**WizStudio**), and seamless QuickBooks and ERP syncing ([NetSuite](/integrations/netsuite-ecommerce/), Sage, etc.) for real-time data accuracy.

## **Conclusion**

Although popular, BigCommerce’s revenue-based pricing thresholds, technical complexity, and enterprise-only B2B features create challenges for wholesale businesses looking to scale efficiently.

Understanding the true cost, including forced upgrades, developer requirements, and limited native wholesale functionality, is essential before committing. For B2B operations seeking full wholesale capabilities without enterprise pricing or technical overhead, purpose-built platforms offer a more direct path to growth.

## **FAQs**

### **How much does BigCommerce cost?**

BigCommerce costs start at $39/month for the Standard plan (up to $50K annual sales), $105/month for Plus (up to $180K), $299/month for Pro (up to $400K), and custom pricing starting around $2,000+/month for Enterprise. Your actual cost will be higher when factoring in payment processing fees (2.2%-2.9% + $0.30 per transaction), apps ($75-$300+/month), premium themes ($150-$400), domain registration ($14-$20/year), and custom development ($3,000-$20,000+). Most businesses spend $6,000-$20,000+ annually depending on sales volume and customization needs.

### **Is BigCommerce good for a small business?**

BigCommerce can work for small businesses with technical expertise and straightforward B2C needs, but it has a steeper learning curve than simpler platforms. The right plan also depends on what you’re selling — a low-margin, high-volume [wholesale business example](https://wizcommerce.com/blog/best-wholesale-business-ideas/) will hit BigCommerce’s revenue thresholds far sooner than a niche one. The forced upgrade when exceeding sales thresholds can be challenging for growing businesses, and small B2B or wholesale operations often find better value in platforms like [WizCommerce](https://wizcommerce.com/) that provide native wholesale features without requiring Enterprise plan pricing.

### **What is the cheapest website for ecommerce?**

The cheapest option depends on your business model. Shopify Starter ($5/month) and Etsy (no monthly fee) are cheaper for very low volumes, while BigCommerce Standard ($39/month) and Shopify Basic ($39/month) are entry points for full online stores. However, apps, transaction fees, and development costs often triple the base price. B2B and wholesale businesses typically find WizCommerce offers better total cost of ownership with native features included.

### **What are the pros and cons of BigCommerce?**

BigCommerce’s pros include a strong set of built-in ecommerce features (reducing reliance on apps), no extra transaction fees when you use third-party payment processors, solid SEO tools, scalability for large catalogs and high traffic, broad multi-channel integrations, and unlimited products/bandwidth on many plans; the cons are a steeper learning curve, potential forced plan upgrades as sales grow, deeper customization that often needs developer help, more advanced B2B capabilities typically gated behind Enterprise, support that can feel uneven on lower tiers, fewer free themes, and add-on costs that can push total spend beyond the base subscription.

### **What is the processing fee for BigCommerce?**

BigCommerce doesn’t charge additional transaction fees beyond payment processor rates. With BigCommerce Payments, credit card rates start at 2.59% + $0.49 (Standard), decreasing to 2.29% + $0.49 (Plus) and 1.99% + $0.49 (Pro/Enterprise). Third-party processors like Stripe or PayPal typically charge 2.2%-2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. This is better than Shopify’s dual-fee structure, and Enterprise customers can negotiate better rates.

### **Is BigCommerce free to use?**

No, BigCommerce is not free to use and doesn’t offer a permanent free plan. The platform requires a paid subscription starting at $39/month for the Standard plan. BigCommerce offers a 14-day free trial to test the platform, but you’ll need a paid subscription plus funds for payment processing, apps, themes, domain registration, and potential custom development to launch successfully.

### **Is Shopify cheaper than BigCommerce?**

Shopify and BigCommerce both start at $39/month, but total costs depend on your needs. Shopify charges transaction fees (0.5%-2%) when not using Shopify Payments, while BigCommerce doesn’t. However, BigCommerce forces upgrades based on sales volume thresholds, which can make it more expensive as you grow. For B2B and wholesale businesses, both require expensive upgrades (Shopify Plus or BigCommerce Enterprise), making WizCommerce a more cost-effective alternative.

### **Does BigCommerce take a percentage of sales?**

No, BigCommerce does not take a percentage of sales as a platform fee. There are no transaction fees or license fees when using third-party payment processors. However, you still pay payment processing fees to your gateway (typically 2.2%-2.9% + $0.30) and must upgrade to higher-priced plans when exceeding sales thresholds, which indirectly increases costs as revenue grows.

This plan is made for **new online stores and small businesses that earn** **yearly revenue of up to $50,000**. **Its monthly cost is $39.**

Although this plan aims at beginners, it is not basic by any means. BigCommerce Standard **gives you enough functionality (without any extra plugins) to run a feature-rich eStore.**

However, BigCommerce Standard **doesn’t include some major functions** such as abandoned cart recovery, customer group and segment, etc. If your website needs them, you must do it manually or pay for alternative apps in the BigCommerce marketplace.

By leveraging them, you can increase the connection with your customers and promote the use of your products.

BigCommerce Pro **scales your business up with a comprehensive system of features.** One notable feature of this package is Google customer reviews.

This program allows you to collect customers’ feedback and then show them in the search result. Also, when you participate, you can display a badge with the Google brand and your seller rating. These help you improve your click-through rate (CTR) and overall conversion rate.

In addition, **Product filtering** and **Customer product filtering** are two important features of this plan. You can get the exact necessary data and get a comprehensive view of your entire business.

## **BigCommerce Pricing – Additional Fees**

### #1. Domain name

The domain name plays an important role in brand awareness. **A brand-oriented and memorable domain name helps your customers easily visit your website to shop**. Furthermore, a good domain name can improve your SEO.

![BigCommerce pricing ](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20786%20443'%3E%3C/svg%3E)![BigCommerce pricing ](https://litextension.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/rtaImage.png)

BigCommerce Domain Name

Because of that, choosing a domain name should be one of the first things you research when building your brand. Please remember that your domain name does not have to be taken by any other organizations on the Internet.

After choosing your own domain name, you can purchase it from BigCommerce for $12 per year. You may also buy a domain name through reputation websites like [Domain.com](https://www.domain.com/), [Google Domain](https://domains.google/), etc. Its cost ranges from **$10 to $20/year**.

If you already have a domain name, you can easily move it to your BigCommerce store in some ways. The most popular one is changing your nameservers in your domain registrar. The process may take **up to 72 hours** for the fully DNS settings.

### #2. Themes

**Choosing a suitable theme for your online store is very important**. It helps you easier manage your products and attract more buyers to your website. Customers will feel more convenient and happy when purchasing in a store with eye-catching decoration and a friendly interface.

Currently, there are [**15 free themes and around 130 paid themes**](https://litextension.com/blog/go/bigcommerce-theme-store-26728) in the BigCommerce marketplace. In addition, you can also find high-quality themes in several marketplaces like [Themeforest](https://themeforest.net/) or [Templatemonster](https://www.templatemonster.com/). Their price is lower than BigCommerce’s, **from $70 to $160**.

### #3. Apps & Integrations

As a hosted platform, BigCommerce provides a wide range of apps to grow your store**.** **There are over 600 apps that are put in many different categories** like Analytics & Reporting, Marketing, Payment & Security and Accounting, etc.

Please follow these guidelines to create your summary:

1. Identify and preserve the main topic or purpose of the webpage.
2. Retain key facts, statistics, and data points that are central to the content's message.
3. Keep important quotes from credible sources or experts.
4. Maintain the chronological order of events if the content is time-sensitive or historical.
5. Preserve any lists or step-by-step instructions if present.
6. Include relevant dates, names, and locations that are crucial to understanding the content.
7. Summarize lengthy explanations while keeping the core message intact.

When handling different types of content:

- For news articles: Focus on the who, what, when, where, why, and how.
- For scientific content: Preserve methodology, results, and conclusions.
- For opinion pieces: Maintain the main arguments and supporting points.
- For product pages: Keep key features, specifications, and unique selling points.

Your summary should be significantly shorter than the original content but comprehensive enough to stand alone as a source of information. Aim for about 25-30 percent of the original length, unless the content is already concise.

}

Described as "the ideal plan for users of all types and sizes."

3. **Pro Plan** – $399/month (monthly) or $299/month (annually, save up to 25%). For revenue up to $400k/year. Adds Google customer reviews and product filtering. PayPal rate: 2.05% + $0.49.

4. **Enterprise Plan** – Custom pricing negotiated directly with BigCommerce, typically starting at $1,000/month and ranging up to $15,000/month. Includes full-featured store, headless capabilities, customizable checkout, and dedicated VIP service.

**Additional Fees:**
- **Domain name**: $12/year from BigCommerce; $10–$20/year from third-party registrars.
- **Themes**: 15 free themes and ~130 paid themes ($150–$399 from BigCommerce, or $70–$160 from marketplaces like ThemeForest).
- **Apps & Integrations**: Over 600 apps; paid apps typically cost $20–$29 each.
- **Transaction fees**: BigCommerce charges 0% transaction fees. PayPal/Braintree credit card rates range from 2.05%–2.59% + $0.49 depending on plan. PayPal Digital Payments: 3.49% + $0.49.
- **POS (Point of Sale)**: Free or paid integrations ($49–$150/month) with 14-day free trial. No additional POS connection fees.

**Key Features:**
- All plans include hosting and enterprise-level security.
- Automatic plan upgrades as revenue thresholds are exceeded.
- Paying annually saves 10% on Plus and Pro plans.
- BigCommerce competes with Shopify, offering more built-in sales tools out of the box.
