## Mobile Commerce Statistics

### Three Out of Four Consumers Shop From Their Smartphones

The [Pew Research Center survey](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2022/11/21/for-shopping-phones-are-common-and-influencers-have-become-a-factor-especially-for-young-adults/) found that about **76%** of U.S. adults shop online using their smartphones. The number is even higher for adults under 50, **91%** of people aged 18 to 49 use their phones for online shopping. By comparison, **69%** shop on desktop or laptop computers, and just **28%** use tablets.

### 65% of Shoppers Look Up Price Comparisons on Mobile While in a Physical Store

[65%](https://saleslion.io/sales-statistics/65-percent-of-shoppers-look-up-price-comparisons-on-their-mobile-device-while-in-a-physical-store/) of shoppers look up price comparisons with their mobile devices while they are in the physical store. Mobile devices provided consumers with real-time ability to make purchasing decisions, and ensured retailer pricing was competitive, which ultimately may prompt a purchase. Retailers can ensure competitive pricing suppose their business requires that. However, offering a mobile-friendly site is a must.

### 52% of Customers Say a Poor Mobile Website Experience Breaks Their Trust

[52%](https://www.zippia.com/advice/user-experience-statistics/) of customers are discouraged by a poor mobile website experience or turned away by an outdated [mobile experience](https://webandcrafts.com/blog/user-experience-design-strategies-for-business-growth). Utilizing responsive design and websites with fast load times can help retain customers' attention.

### Women Are More Likely to Shop on Their Phones

According to the GSMA Mobile Gender Gap Report 2024, women are more likely to shop from their phones. In low and middle-income countries, **66%** of women use mobile internet, compared to **78%** of men. Retailers may use gender‑specific mobile marketing to better reach and engage female users.

## Consumer Behavior Trends

### Nearly half of Gen Z shoppers are prone to making last-minute purchases

[60%](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/impulse-buying-statistics/) of [Gen Z](https://webandcrafts.com/blog/gen-z-shopping-trends) consumers are spontaneous buyers, typically driven by social media or advertising promotions. Flash sales and strategic advertising can lead to successful outreach strategies for this target market.

### Most consumers read online reviews before purchasing

Almost **90%** of people check [reviews](https://www.hostinger.com/in/tutorials/ecommerce-statistics) before making a purchase. More than half usually read four or more reviews, and around **44%** look at up to three. On top of that, about three-quarters like to share their own experiences by leaving reviews.   
Nearly all shoppers who read reviews also want to see the store’s replies, so responding to feedback helps build trust. And when negative reviews come up, addressing them quickly can prevent things from getting worse.

## E-commerce Trends Statistics for 2025

### 1. Increased usage of augmented reality while Shopping

The use of augmented reality (AR) in shopping is growing quickly. According to [SellersCommerce](https://www.sellerscommerce.com/blog/ecommerce-statistics/), about **32%** of shoppers use AR to see products before making a purchase.

In addition, a 2024 survey in the United States found that [75%](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1484077/ai-tradition-marketing-materials-ecommerce/) of consumers feel AR gives a clearer and more accurate view of products than regular images or descriptions ([Statista, 2024](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1484077/ai-tradition-marketing-materials-ecommerce/)). Using AR can help shoppers feel more confident when buying.

### 2. Customers desire to buy from more sustainable brands

According to a survey by [Specright](https://www.specright.com/press-releases/survey-reveals-consumers-prioritize-purchasing-sustainable-products-and-desire-greater-transparency-from-companies-on-sustainability-progress?utm_source=chatgpt.com), **80%** of consumers are more likely to trust companies that openly share data supporting their sustainability claims. The survey also found that **40%** of consumers feel uncomfortable buying from companies that aren’t actively working toward sustainability goals.

### 3. Subscriptions are on the rise. But they should come with perks!

The [subscription](https://www.mytotalretail.com/article/how-subscription-models-help-prepare-dtc-brands-for-a-recession/) eCommerce market is set to grow from **$15 billion in 2019** to more than **$450 billion by 2025**. Subscriptions work well for everyone: customers get to pick what they want, and exclusive experiences drive continuous sales.

### 4. Concentrate on advanced customer loyalty programs

More and more businesses are planning to start loyalty programs.  About a third of those without one now will have one by [2027](https://www.ft.com/content/56db7f30-2d63-451a-81bd-e3743f5ffe96). And most marketers, around [78%](https://www.marketingcharts.com/customer-centric/datadriven-118124), say they use data to keep customers engaged. It shows that using customer info to make loyalty programs personal and meaningful is becoming important.

## Conclusion

The e-commerce numbers for 2025 show that the digital marketplace is growing rapidly, driven by mobile commerce, social media, and consumer trends. Businesses need to focus on mobile-first, social commerce, and sustainability.  
  
Companies can capitalize by using eCommerce growth statistics and consumer behavior data to adjust planning for effective strategies to meet customer intent and increase conversions. Sustaining a competitive edge means keeping pace with changes like augmented reality, voice search, and loyalty programs, but always consider your ecommerce site search statistics and payment experience as critical touchpoints.

But the story isn't just about growth. It's about where that growth is happening, who's leading, and where the opportunities are.

This guide breaks down ecommerce market size by country, including the largest markets, fastest-growing regions, and penetration rates that reveal how much runway each market still has.

## The 10 Largest Ecommerce Markets by Revenue

Here's an up to date list of the world's top ecommerce markets, along with their value, and the relative dominance of ecommerce in each country:

| Rank | Country | Revenue | Penetration |

| 1 | China | $3.45 trillion | 47% |

### 1. China ($3.45 trillion)

China isn't just the largest ecommerce market; it's larger than the next several markets combined.

Chinese consumers generated over $3.4 trillion in online sales in 2025, representing roughly 50% of global ecommerce.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** 47%
* **Mobile commerce share:** 92% of online shoppers use smartphones
* **Key platforms:** Taobao, Tmall, JD.com, Pinduoduo

What sets China apart isn't just scale, it's integration.

Social commerce, livestream shopping, and super-apps have blurred the lines between entertainment and shopping in ways Western markets are only beginning to adopt.

### 2. United States ($1.38 trillion)

The US ecommerce market continues steady growth, projected to reach $1.88 trillion by 2029.

While penetration remains lower than China or the UK, the sheer size of the American consumer market makes it the world's second-largest.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** 15.8%
* **Mobile commerce share:** 76% of adults purchase via smartphone
* **Growth rate:** 10.5% YoY
* **Key platforms:** Amazon, Walmart, eBay, Shopify merchants

The US market is mature but far from saturated. With penetration below 16%, there's significant room for growth, particularly in categories like grocery and B2B that have been slower to move online.

### 3. United Kingdom ($195 billion)

The UK is Europe's largest ecommerce market and ranks third globally. British consumers have embraced online shopping at rates exceeding most Western countries.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** 30.6%
* **Mobile commerce:** Projected to hit £100 billion ($125B) in 2025
* **Key platforms:** Amazon UK, ASOS, Tesco, Argos

The UK's high penetration rate means growth is slowing compared to emerging markets, but the market remains highly attractive for established brands.

### 4. Japan ($169 billion)

Japan's ecommerce market is expected to grow at 9.2% CAGR, reaching $263 billion by 2029. The market is characterized by sophisticated consumers and strong domestic platforms.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** ~15%
* **Key platforms:** Rakuten, Amazon Japan, Yahoo! Shopping

Japan presents unique challenges for foreign brands, including language barriers and preference for domestic platforms, but offers strong purchasing power.

### 5. South Korea ($147 billion)

South Korea punches above its weight in ecommerce, with one of the highest mobile commerce adoption rates globally.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** 30%
* **Mobile share:** 77% of ecommerce sales expected via mobile by 2026
* **Key platforms:** Coupang, Gmarket, 11Street

Korean consumers are early adopters of new commerce trends, making the market a testing ground for innovations like quick commerce and social shopping.

### 6. Germany ($140 billion)

Germany is the largest ecommerce market in continental Europe and a gateway for brands expanding across the EU.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** ~18%
* **Growth rate:** 4-5% annually
* **Key platforms:** Amazon.de, Otto, Zalando

German consumers prioritize quality and sustainability, and have strong preferences for local payment methods (invoice payment is common).

### 7. India ($136 billion)

India is the fastest-growing major ecommerce market, with projections showing it could reach $345 billion by 2030. The market has grown from 140 million online shoppers in 2020 to 260 million in 2024.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** ~5%
* **Growth rate:** 17-22% annually
* **Mobile share:** 88% of online shoppers use smartphones
* **Key platforms:** Flipkart, Amazon India, Myntra, Meesho

India's low penetration rate represents enormous opportunity. As internet access expands beyond major cities and digital payment adoption increases, growth will accelerate.

### 8. France ($92 billion)

France rounds out the top European markets with steady growth and strong domestic platform presence.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** ~17%
* **Key platforms:** Amazon.fr, Cdiscount, Fnac, Veepee

### 9. Canada ($88 billion)

Canada benefits from proximity to US supply chains while maintaining its own distinct consumer preferences.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** ~12%
* **Key platforms:** Amazon Canada, Walmart Canada, Canadian Tire

Indonesia is Southeast Asia's largest ecommerce market and one of the fastest-growing globally.

* **Ecommerce penetration:** 31.9%
* **Growth rate:** 20%+ annually
* **Key platforms:** Tokopedia, Shopee, Bukalapak, Lazada

While China and the US dominate in absolute size, the fastest growth is happening elsewhere.

Southeast Asia is growing at a particularly fast rate, as are several markets in Latin America.

**Southeast Asia** is the fastest-growing region for ecommerce, with 18.6% growth and a path to $230 billion GMV by 2026.

By 2027, 88% of the region's population (402 million users) is expected to shop online.

**Latin America** has reclaimed its position as the fastest-growing regional market at 12.2% growth in 2025.

Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina account for 84.5% of regional sales. Mexico is on track to surpass US ecommerce penetration levels by 2026.

**India** remains the standout emerging market opportunity. With only 5% ecommerce penetration in a country of 1.4 billion people, the addressable market for growth is massive.

## Ecommerce Penetration by Country

Penetration rate (the percentage of total retail sales happening online) reveals how dominant ecommerce is in each country - as well as how much room each market has to grow.

Let's take a look at several notable markets, and how dominant online shopping is in each one.

| Country | Penetration Rate | What It Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| China | 47% | Near-saturation in urban areas |
| Indonesia | 31.9% | Leapfrogging traditional retail |
| UK | 30.6% | Mature, steady market |
| South Korea | 30% | Mobile-first consumers |
| Germany | 18% | Room for growth |
| US | 15.8% | Surprisingly low for market size |
| Japan | 15% | Traditional retail still strong |
| Latin America | 12% avg | Significant opportunity |
| India | 5% | Massive upside potential |

### What Penetration Rates Tell Us

**High penetration markets (30%+)** like China, South Korea, and the UK offer less growth upside but stable, predictable demand. Competition is fierce.

**Mid-penetration markets (15-25%)** like the US, Germany, and France have room to grow but face structural challenges (established retail, logistics complexity).

**Low penetration markets (<15%)** like India, Latin America, and parts of Southeast Asia offer the highest growth potential but also higher execution risk (infrastructure, payments, logistics).

## Mobile Commerce: The Dominant Channel

Mobile commerce (mcommerce) accounts for 59% of global ecommerce sales - that's $4 trillion in 2025. In some markets, it's even higher.

### Mobile Share by Country

| Country | Mobile % of Ecommerce |
| --- | --- |
| China | 92% |
| India | 88% |
| South Korea | 77% (projected 2026) |
| UK | 65% |
| US | 45% |

The mobile-first trend is irreversible.

In emerging markets especially, consumers are skipping desktop entirely and shopping exclusively on smartphones.

In the near future, we can only expect mobile shopping to become more dominant.

## What This Means for Ecommerce Brands

Let's take a look at the practical implications of these statistics if you're running an ecommerce company - whether it's in the US, UK, or any other part of the world.

### If you're targeting growth markets:

1. **Prioritize mobile**. In India, Indonesia, and Latin America, mobile-first isn't a strategy; it's a requirement.

1. **Understand local payment preferences**. Credit cards aren't universal. Digital wallets, bank transfers, and even cash-on-delivery dominate in many markets.

1. **Invest in localization**. Language, currency, and cultural preferences vary dramatically. A US-centric approach won't work.

1. **Consider marketplace presence**. In most emerging markets, local marketplaces (Mercado Libre, Shopee, Flipkart) have stronger consumer trust than independent stores.

### If you're in mature markets:

1. **Focus on retention over acquisition**. Growth is slowing. LTV matters more than CAC in saturated markets.

1. **Mobile app investment pays off**. With mobile commerce growing even in mature markets, a native app creates stickier customer relationships.

1. **Differentiation through experience**. When price competition is fierce, experience becomes the differentiator.

# Ecommerce Statistics (2026) — Key Facts and Figures

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='48'%20height='48'%20viewBox='0%200%2048%2048'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Matt Walsh

Whether we’re talking about the rise of social shopping, the role of AI in ecommerce, mobile buying habits, or the real reasons shoppers abandon carts, the story of modern ecommerce is one of scale, speed, and constant reinvention.

So, in this ecommerce statistics roundup, I’ve pulled together the most important facts and figures shaping that story — read on as I cover global market trends, U.S. ecommerce performance, platform share, mobile commerce, fraud, dropshipping economies…and much more.

**Important note**: you are free to cite any of the ecommerce stats or use any of the graphs featured in this post in your own articles. However, we request that you **credit Ecommercetrix as a source** and **link to this post** when doing so. Thank you!

---

## Article highlights

* [What does global ecommerce look like?](#global-ecommerce-statistics)
* [Which models and markets are growing fastest?](#ecommerce-market-growth)
* [How much do shoppers spend per visit?](#online-shopper-spend)

* [Which platforms and marketplaces are most popular?](#ecommerce-platform-popularity)
* [How big is social commerce?](#social-commerce-size)
* [What’s happening in mobile ecommerce?](#mobile-ecommerce)
* [Why do shoppers abandon carts?](#cart-abandonment)
* [How widespread is ecommerce fraud?](#ecommerce-fraud)
* [Is dropshipping and POD still profitable?](#dropshipping-and-pod)
* [How much is AI used in ecommerce?](#how-much-is-AI-being-used-in-ecommerce)
* [Where is ecommerce heading next?](#where-is-ecommerce-heading-next)

---

## **What does the global ecommerce landscape look like right now?**

Global ecommerce is continuing its upward surge — but the growth isn’t evenly distributed. Some regions are accelerating at breakneck speed, while others are expanding more gradually. Asia, in particular, now shapes much of the global ecommerce story, with China acting as the engine behind both user growth and overall market volume.

Here’s how the landscape looks today:

* Global retail ecommerce sales are estimated to have reached $6.42 trillion in 2025. (Source: [Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/ie/blog/global-ecommerce-sales).)
* Worldwide ecommerce revenue is projected to reach **$6.8 trillion** by 2026. (Source: [Emarketer](https://www.emarketer.com/chart/272684/worldwide-ecommerce-sales-growth-will-dip-slightly-2025-mostly-due-softness-china-trillions-retail-ecommerce-sales-worldwide-change-of-total-retail-sales-2022-2028).)
* Asia is the world’s largest ecommerce region, with **nearly $2 trillion** spent on online purchases in 2025 — about **$500 billion** more than the Americas. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/forecasts/1117851/worldwide-e-commerce-revenue-by-region).)
* China remained the world’s largest ecommerce market in 2025, with online retail sales estimated at approximately **$2.2–$2.4 trillion**. Some forecasts suggest the country now accounts for roughly 45% of global ecommerce sales. (Source: [Claight Corp](https://www.expertmarketresearch.com/reports/china-e-commerce-market).)
* There are **904 million** Chinese digital shoppers today (44% of the global total); this will rise to **1.33 billion** by 2027. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/277391/number-of-online-buyers-in-china/).)
* China leads the world in ecommerce penetration, with **46.3%** of all its retail sales occurring online. (Source: [Insider Intelligence](https://www.insiderintelligence.com/content/countries-retail-ecommerce/).)
* The global ecommerce ecosystem is made up of **26.5 million** ecommerce sites. (Source: [Doofinder](https://www.doofinder.com/en/statistics/how-many-ecommerce-sites-are-there#:~:text=There%20are%20more%20than%2026.5,204%25%20growth%20in%202021%20alone.).)

The data paints a clear picture: ecommerce is now a truly global retail force — but China and Asia are setting the pace for growth, innovation, and sheer market scale.

![Global ecommerce statistics infographic.](https://www.ecommercetrix.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/global-ecommerce-at-aglance-infographic.png)

Global ecommerce statistics (Sources: Shopify and Emarketer.)

 

---

## **Which ecommerce models and markets are growing fastest?**

Ecommerce continues to branch into new business models, but two categories still drive the bulk of global activity: **B2C** (business-to-consumer), and **B2B** (business-to-business).

* **B2C ecommerce** is projected to grow at a **CAGR of 8.4%** from 2020 to 2027. (Source: [Research and Markets](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/reports/5140596/b2c-ecommerce-global-strategic-business-report#).)
* China’s B2C sector is expanding even faster, with a forecast **14.3% CAGR**, underscoring the country’s role as a global ecommerce engine. (Source: [Research and Markets](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/reports/5140596/b2c-ecommerce-global-strategic-business-report#).)
* **B2B ecommerce**, meanwhile, dwarfs the consumer market in scale — it’s on track to account for **$47.54 trillion in sales by 2030**, cementing its status as the dominant force in online commerce. (Source: [TechSci Research](https://www.techsciresearch.com/report/b2b-e-commerce-market/27065.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com).)

Growth is also unevenly distributed across global regions:

* **Six of the world’s ten fastest-growing ecommerce markets are in Asia**, led by the Philippines (**24.1% growth**), India (**22.3%**) and Indonesia (**20%**). (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/266064/revenue-growth-in-e-commerce-for-selected-countries/).)
* The UK remains one of the world’s most ecommerce-driven retail economies. According to EMARKETER, online sales are expected to account for more than 28% of all UK retail sales in 2026, rising to nearly 30% by 2030 as ecommerce continues to mature. (Source: [Insider Intelligence](https://www.emarketer.com/content/state-of-uk-ecommerce).)

The data shows a landscape where ecommerce demand is rising everywhere — but accelerating fastest in Asia and in the massive, often overlooked B2B sector.

![Bar chart comparing B2C ecommerce growth rates, showing global CAGR at 8.4% and China at 14.3%.](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1024'%20height='576'%20viewBox='0%200%201024%20576'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Research shows that China’s B2C ecommerce market is expanding dramatically faster than the global benchmark between 2020 and 2027 (Source: Research and Markets.)

 

---

## **How much do online shoppers spend per visit?**

When you dig into the data, the average value of an ecommerce visit is much lower than many merchants imagine — largely because most visits don’t turn into purchases. This makes *visit value* a useful indicator of traffic quality, but a poor reflection of actual revenue generation.

Across the board, the numbers look like this:

* **$2.98** — the average spend per visit in Q2 2025. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/239288/countries-ranked-by-average-b2c-e-commerce-spending-per-online-buyer/?locale=en).)
* **$3.02** — the average spend for the highest-performing category, **Health & Beauty**. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/239288/countries-ranked-by-average-b2c-e-commerce-spending-per-online-buyer/?locale=en).)
* **$2.66** — the average spend for home appliances, the next strongest category. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/239288/countries-ranked-by-average-b2c-e-commerce-spending-per-online-buyer/?locale=en).)

However, these figures only tell part of the story. When shoppers *do* convert, the economics shift dramatically — and that’s where average order value (AOV) becomes a far more meaningful performance measure:

* **$85** — the typical AOV for a Shopify store. (Source: [Littledata.io](https://www.littledata.io/average/average-order-value/Shopify).)
* **$192** — the AOV for the top-performing 20% of Shopify merchants. (Source: [Littledata.io](https://www.littledata.io/average/average-order-value/Shopify).)
* **$311** — the AOV for the top 10% of Shopify stores. (Source: [Littledata.io](https://www.littledata.io/average/average-order-value/Shopify).)

The message is clear: while individual visits generate very little revenue on their own, high-intent buyers still spend solid amounts — so optimizing your store’s conversion rate and AOV will have a far greater impact on revenue than visit-level metrics alone.

![Bar chart comparing average order values: $311 for the top 10% of Shopify stores, $85 for the average Shopify store, and $2.98 as the average ecommerce order value across all platforms.](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1024'%20height='576'%20viewBox='0%200%201024%20576'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Average ecommerce order value statistics (Source: Littledata.io.)

## **How strong is the U.S. ecommerce market?**

The U.S. ecommerce sector continues to expand at a healthy pace — and remains one of the most competitive, platform-driven retail environments in the world. Growth is steady rather than explosive, but the sheer scale of the market and the dominance of a few major players make it a key bellwether for global online retail trends.

* U.S. retail ecommerce sales are estimated to have totaled approximately **$1.23 trillion in 2025**, highlighting the continued scale and resilience of the American online retail market. (Source: [US Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/retail/ecommerce.html).)
* In Q1 2026, U.S. ecommerce sales reached **$326.7 billion** — a **9.8%** increase compared to the same period in 2025. (Source: [US Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/retail/ecommerce.html).)
* Online shopping accounted for **16.9%** of all U.S. retail sales in the first quarter of 2026, continuing ecommerce’s steady expansion within the wider retail sector. (Source: [US Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/retail/ecommerce.html).)
* Amazon remains the dominant starting point for online product discovery. According to Jungle Scout consumer research, 56% of U.S. shoppers now begin product searches directly on Amazon, compared to 42% who start on traditional search engines like Google. Walmart has also strengthened its position, with 29% of shoppers beginning product searches on Walmart.com. (Source: [eMarketer, Jungle Scout 2024, CivicScience retail search surveys](https://www.emarketer.com/content/5-charts-search-2024-google-ai-retail-media?utm_source=chatgpt.com).)
* Amazon continues to dominate U.S. ecommerce by revenue, accounting for an estimated 38% of all online retail sales in the United States. Walmart remains a distant second, although its ecommerce business surpassed $150 billion in annual sales in 2025 following rapid growth in grocery delivery and marketplace operations. (Source: [Oberlo](https://www.oberlo.com/).)
* Looking ahead, U.S. ecommerce is expected to grow at an average annual rate of **7.8%** from 2023 to 2027. (Source: [ecommerce DB](https://ecommercedb.com/markets/us/all).)

Overall, the U.S. market is maturing rather than slowing — with consistent year-over-year gains and a competitive landscape shaped heavily by Amazon’s continued dominance.

US ecommerce key statistics

## **Which ecommerce platforms and marketplaces are most popular?**

The ecommerce ecosystem is increasingly dominated by a small group of platforms and marketplaces, each shaping online retail in very different ways. On the platform side, merchants lean toward flexible site builders like Shopify and WooCommerce; on the marketplace side, Amazon, Alibaba and Pinduoduo command extraordinary global reach.

* Among the world’s top 1 million sites, **Shopify** leads with **27.5%** usage, making it the most popular high-end ecommerce platform. (Source: [Builtwith](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop).)
* **WooCommerce** powers **9.2%** of the top 1M but holds the largest overall platform market share: **39%** of all ecommerce sites. (Source: [Builtwith](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop).)
* **Squarespace** maintains a significant footprint too, accounting for **14.75%** of global ecommerce sites. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/710207/worldwide-ecommerce-platforms-market-share/).)
* In the U.S., Shopify is particularly strong, with **28.34%** of the platform market among the top one million ecommerce sites. (Source: [Builtwith](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop/country/United-States).)
* WordPress users overwhelmingly gravitate toward WooCommerce — it powers **64%** of all WordPress-based ecommerce stores. (Source: [Builtwith](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop/plugin---module).)

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1024'%20height='576'%20viewBox='0%200%201024%20576'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Ecommerce platform market share among the world’s top one million websites (Source: Builtwith.)

(You can learn more about some of these platforms in [our in-depth Shopify review](https://www.ecommercetrix.com/ecommerce-reviews/shopify-review/), [our Wix review](https://www.ecommercetrix.com/ecommerce-reviews/wix-review/), [our Squarespace review](https://www.ecommercetrix.com/ecommerce-reviews/squarespace-review/), and [our Shopify vs Squarespace comparison](https://www.ecommercetrix.com/ecommerce-reviews/shopify-vs-squarespace/).)

On the marketplace side, the picture is even more concentrated:

* **Amazon** is the world’s largest marketplace by market capitalization (**$2.789 trillion**), followed by **Alibaba** (**$325.41B**) and **Pinduoduo** (**$164.39B**). (Source: [Companies Market Cap](https://companiesmarketcap.com/).)
* **Alibaba** has the most active customers — **903 million**, almost **three times** Amazon’s **310 million**. (Sources: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/226927/alibaba-cumulative-active-online-buyers-taobao-tmall/).)
* When it comes to engagement, Amazon dominates again: it receives **2.77 billion** monthly visits — more than **5** times eBay’s **543 million**. (Source: [Semrush](https://www.semrush.com/website/amazon.com/overview/).)

These numbers highlight how a handful of platforms and marketplaces account for the vast majority of ecommerce activity — and that Amazon and Shopify continue to set much of the industry’s direction.

## **How big is social commerce becoming?**

Social commerce is evolving from a discovery channel into a fully fledged shopping ecosystem — and the numbers show just how quickly that shift is happening. With billions of users and increasingly seamless in-app purchasing, social platforms are becoming some of the most influential retail environments in the world.

* Global social commerce sales reached **$700+ billion in 2025**, with forecasts pointing toward **$2.9 trillion** in the years ahead. (Source: [Statista](https://spaces.statista.com/1bea0ce6d0124704887a35377c6a4749.pdf?utm_source=Statista+Webinar+Contacts&utm_campaign=4f39c7ce83-DoS_Webinar_eCommerce_Show_EN_KW38_2022_LHA&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_f5ac47a287-4f39c7ce83-344273366).)
* There are now **5.2 billion** social media users globally — a figure expected to grow to **5.8 billion** by 2027. (Source: [Datareportal](https://datareportal.com/social-media-users?utm_source=chatgpt.com).)
* **9 in 10** social media users purchase from brands they follow, underscoring the commercial power of community and content. (Source: [Marketing Dive](https://www.marketingdive.com/news/90-of-people-buy-from-brands-they-follow-on-social-media-study-says/577882/).)
* **46%** of Chinese and **36%** of American users regularly buy directly through social platforms. (Source: [Statista](https://spaces.statista.com/1bea0ce6d0124704887a35377c6a4749.pdf?utm_source=Statista+Webinar+Contacts&utm_campaign=4f39c7ce83-DoS_Webinar_eCommerce_Show_EN_KW38_2022_LHA&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_f5ac47a287-4f39c7ce83-344273366).)
* In the U.S., social commerce sales **doubled** between 2020 and 2022, rising from **$26.9B** to **$56B**. (Source: [Insider Intelligence](https://on.emarketer.com/rs/867-SLG-901/images/eMarketer%20Social%20Commerce%20Trends%20Roundup.pdf).)

TikTok continues to be the standout driver:

* **20.6%** of TikTok users say they buy through the app “all the time.” (Source: [Insider Intelligence](https://www.insiderintelligence.com/chart/254951/How-Often-Do-Social-Media-Shoppers-Worldwide-Buy-Products-on-Select-Social-Media-Platforms-of-respondents-Jan-2022).)
* The **#TikTokMadeMeBuyIt** hashtag has attracted **30+ billion views**, turning viral shopping into a cultural norm. (Source: [Insider Intelligence](https://www.insiderintelligence.com/chart/254951/How-Often-Do-Social-Media-Shoppers-Worldwide-Buy-Products-on-Select-Social-Media-Platforms-of-respondents-Jan-2022).)

China’s livestream economy shows the future direction of travel:

* China’s livestream shopping market is expected to surpass 6 trillion yuan in 2025, with platforms like Douyin and Taobao Live continuing to drive massive ecommerce engagement and sales. (Source: Research & Markets.)
* Douyin saw a **40× increase** in transaction value between 2019 and 2022 — an indication of how quickly livestream shopping can scale. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/187439/share-of-e-commerce-sales-in-total-us-retail-sales-in-2010/).)

These trends make one thing clear: social platforms are no longer just where shopping journeys begin — they’re increasingly where they end, too.

![Bar chart showing global social commerce growth, with sales at $700 billion in 2024 and projected to reach $2.9 trillion by 2026.](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1024'%20height='576'%20viewBox='0%200%201024%20576'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Global social commerce sales are forecast to rise sharply, growing from $700B in 2024 to $2.9T by 2026.

## **What’s happening with mobile ecommerce?**

Mobile commerce continues to shape how people shop online — it drives the majority of ecommerce traffic and an increasing share of sales. But while mobile usage keeps climbing, conversion rates still trail behind desktop — suggesting plenty of room for optimization.

* Mobile now accounts for **71%** of all ecommerce site traffic. (Source: [SaleCycle](https://www.salecycle.com/blog/strategies/mobile-conversion-rates-lower-desktop/).)
* Conversion rates remain lower on phones: **2% on mobile** vs **3% on desktop**. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/234884/us-online-shopper-conversion-rate-by-device/#:~:text=The%20conversion%20rate%20among%20U.S.,at%20two%20percent%20for%20smartphones.).)
* **79%** of mobile users made a purchase on their phone between July and December 2022, highlighting the role of mobile in everyday shopping. (Source: [OuterBox](https://www.outerboxdesign.com/web-design-articles/mobile-ecommerce-statistics#:~:text=Over%20270%20million%20U.S.%20consumers,were%20made%20on%20a%20smartphone).)
* In the U.S., **65%** of ecommerce sales are now mobile-driven. (Source: [Insider Intelligence](https://www.insiderintelligence.com/insights/mobile-commerce-shopping-trends-stats/).)
* Nearly half of all ecommerce sales worldwide are expected to take place on mobile devices in 2026, highlighting the continued shift toward mobile-first shopping experiences. (Source: [Emarketer](https://www.emarketer.com/).)

Payments are shifting heavily toward digital wallets:

* Digital wallets now account for **around half** of global online transactions. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1111233/payment-method-usage-transaction-volume-share-worldwide/#statisticContainer).)
* **Apple Pay** leads the U.S. market with **43.9 million** users, followed by the Starbucks wallet with **31.2 million**. (Source: [Business of Apps](https://www.businessofapps.com/data/mobile-payments-app-market/).)
* Worldwide, Apple Pay has **500+ million** users and Google Pay exceeds **400 million**. (Source: [Business of Apps](https://www.businessofapps.com/data/mobile-payments-app-market/).)

Overall, the trend is clear: mobile dominates discovery and is steadily growing when it comes to share of purchases — with digital wallets removing friction and making mobile checkouts faster, safer, and more habitual.

---

## **Why do shoppers abandon their carts?**

Cart abandonment remains one of the perennial challenges of ecommerce — and despite improvements in checkout design, payment tooling and delivery options, most shoppers still leave before completing their order. According to the latest Baymard Institute research, the average cart abandonment rate sits at 70.22%, meaning that only a minority of online shopping sessions ever translate into revenue.

A big portion of this comes down to intent: **43%** of shoppers say they were simply browsing and not yet ready to commit. But for those who did intend to buy, several avoidable friction points still push them away.

* **39%** abandoned their purchase because extra costs — shipping, taxes, fees — were higher than expected. (Source: [Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate).)
* **21%** said the delivery timeline was too slow for their needs. (Source: [Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate).)
* **19%** didn’t trust the site with their credit card details. (Source: [Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate).)
* **19%** disliked being forced to create an account. (Source: [Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate).)
* **18%** felt the checkout process was too long or complicated. (Source: [Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate).)
* **14%** couldn’t see the full order cost upfront. (Source: [Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate).)
* **10%** wanted additional payment method options. (Source: [Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate).)

This data highlights a familiar pattern: shoppers reward clarity, speed, and trust. And while you can’t entirely eliminate browsing-based abandonment, simplifying your checkout flow, being transparent about costs and offering secure, flexible payment options can meaningfully reduce the portion of customers who drop off for solvable reasons.

![Most cart abandonment is driven by browsing behavior and checkout friction — particularly unexpected costs and delivery delays.](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1024'%20height='576'%20viewBox='0%200%201024%20576'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Browsing intent, unexpected costs, and slow delivery remain the biggest drivers of cart abandonment in ecommerce (Source: Baymard Institute.)

## **How widespread is ecommerce fraud?**

Ecommerce fraud continues to rise, and its financial impact on merchants is becoming increasingly severe. Despite better tooling and stronger authentication methods, fraudsters are evolving just as quickly — creating a costly cycle of prevention, detection, and recovery for online retailers.

* Global ecommerce fraud losses are projected to exceed $48 billion in 2026, as online retailers continue to face growing threats from account takeovers, payment fraud and AI-driven scams. (Source: [Juniper Research](https://www.juniperresearch.com/press/losses-online-payment-fraud-exceed-362-billion/).)
* For every **$100** in fraudulent orders, merchants end up losing **$207** once chargebacks, shipping costs, and operational overheads costsare factored in. (Source: [Exploding Topics](https://explodingtopics.com/blog/ecommerce-fraud-stats).)
* **29.8%** of attacks involve account takeovers — a sign that credential theft and reused passwords remain major vulnerabilities. (Source: [Finances Online](https://financesonline.com/ecommerce-fraud-statistics/).)
* **24.1%** of fraud attempts come from bot-driven activity, highlighting the scale and automation behind modern fraud operations. (Source: [Finances Online](https://financesonline.com/ecommerce-fraud-statistics/).)
* On the prevention side, around **60%** of merchants now use **payment tokenization**, a significant step toward reducing exposure to sensitive card data. (Source: [Merchant Risk Council](http://chrome-extension//efaidnbmnnnibpcajpcglclefindmkaj/https://info.merchantriskcouncil.org/hubfs/Documents/Reports/Fraud%20Reports/2025_Global_Fraud_and_Payments_Report.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com).)

The takeaway: fraud isn’t just a background risk — it’s a rapidly growing cost center. For most merchants, investing in prevention tools, stronger identity checks and real-time monitoring is no longer optional.

---

## **Are dropshipping and print on demand still profitable?**

Dropshipping and print-on-demand (POD) continue to attract new entrepreneurs for a simple reason: both models remain low-barrier, low-risk and, when executed well, reliably profitable. Recent data shows that neither trend is slowing down — in fact, both are expanding in size and sophistication.

* The global dropshipping market was valued at **$372.47 billion in 2025**, and is expected to reach **$476.10 billion** in 2026. (Source: [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1264272/dropshipping-market-size/).)
* Average dropshipping profit margins fall between **15%–20%**, making it a viable option for lean, inventory-free businesses. (Source: [BlueCart](https://www.bluecart.com/blog/dropshipping-profit-margin#toc-what-s-a-good-profit-margin-for-drop-shipping-).)
* Approximately **27%** of online retailers use dropshipping in some form. (Source: [Ecommerce Platforms](https://ecommerce-platforms.com/ecommerce-selling-advice/setup-drop-shipping-ecommerce-website/).)
* The ecosystem is broad: Shopify supports **865** dropshipping apps, WordPress **213**, BigCommerce **31**, and Wix **48**. (Sources: Shopify, WordPress, BigCommerce, and Wix).

Print-on-demand is growing even faster:

* The global print-on-demand market is estimated to be worth between $13 billion and $15 billion in 2026, with forecasts suggesting it could exceed $45 billion by 2031 as demand for customized products continues to grow. (Source: [Printify](https://printify.com/blog/print-on-demand-statistics/).)
* Consumers are willing to pay **20% more** for personalized POD products, making customization a major revenue lever. (Source: [Com Cap](https://comcapllc.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/ComCaps-Print-on-Demand-Perspectives-Q3-2019.pdf).)
* **Home decor** is the fastest-growing POD category, reflecting strong demand for bespoke, design-led household items. (Source: [Straits Research](https://straitsresearch.com/report/print-on-demand-market).)

Overall, both dropshipping and POD remain strong business models — not get-rich-quick schemes, but scalable, flexible approaches that continue to thrive as ecommerce consumers seek more variety, personalization and convenience.

---

## How much is AI being used in ecommerce?

* The global AI market is projected to reach **$757.6 billion in 2025** and expected to surpass **$1.8 trillion by 2030**.
* The AI-powered ecommerce tools market is projected to reach nearly **$17 billion by 2030**.
* The natural language processing (NLP) market is expected to exceed **$112 billion by 2030**, powered by increasingly accurate chatbots and search tools that better interpret customer intent.
* By 2030, AI is forecast to handle approximately **80% of customer interactions**, reducing support workload while increasing response speed and consistency.
* AI-based product recommendation systems have been shown to increase revenue, conversion rates, and average order value, with some implementations reporting up to **3× revenue growth**, **2× higher conversions**, and **50% increases in order value**.
* In 2025, **34% of US customers said they were comfortable in with the concept of [agentic ecommerice](https://www.ecommercetrix.com/ecommerce-tips/what-is-agentic-ecommerce/) — i.e., letting AI shop for them**.
* Younger consumers are particularly open to agentic commerce, with Gen Z and millennial shoppers showing significantly higher comfort levels around AI-assisted purchasing and product discovery.

![Youtube video](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='480'%20height='360'%20viewBox='0%200%20480%20360'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Source for above statistics: [Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/uk/blog/ai-statistics).

## **Where is ecommerce heading next?**

Ecommerce isn’t just growing — it’s expanding into new behaviors, new devices, and entirely new environments. Over the next few years, online retail is expected to become even more deeply woven into everyday life, with shopping journeys taking place across voice interfaces, immersive digital spaces and a widening ecosystem of connected devices.

* By the end of **2026**, ecommerce is projected to account for **24% of all global retail**, reflecting the steady shift away from traditional brick-and-mortar–only shopping. (Sources: IRP and [Statista](https://www.statista.com/topics/871/online-shopping/#topicHeader__wrapper).)
* AI ecommerce looks set to rise: **by 2030, AI is expected to manage 80% of customer interactions**. (Source: [Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/uk/blog/ai-statistics).)
* Conversational commerce is becoming a major part of that shift. Revenue from voice-activated shopping was wortht over **$164 billion in 202**5, fueled by increasing comfort with conversational interfaces. (Sources: [Finances Online](https://financesonline.com/ecommerce-trends/#voice), [Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/mobile/) and Consulterce.)
* Meanwhile, metaverse-related ecommerce — still a relatively young segment — could grow from **$30.6 billion** to **$678.8 billion**, signaling a long-term move toward more immersive, blended online/virtual shopping experiences. (Source: [Grand View Research](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/metaverse-market-report).)
* Device adoption underpins all of this: **97%** of people in the United States now own a smartphone, and **35%** own a smart speaker, giving retailers more touchpoints than ever before. (Source: [PEW Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/mobile/).)

Taken together, these trends point to an ecommerce future defined not by a single platform or device, but by a fluid, multi-channel environment — one in which discovery, evaluation and purchase can happen anywhere a customer happens to be.

This article from Ecommercetrix presents a comprehensive roundup of key ecommerce statistics for 2026, covering global market trends, U.S. performance, platform shares, mobile commerce, social commerce, fraud, dropshipping, and AI adoption.

**Global Ecommerce Landscape:**
- Global retail ecommerce sales reached ~$6.42 trillion in 2025, projected to hit $6.8 trillion by 2026.
- Asia is the largest ecommerce region (~$2 trillion in 2025), with China as the dominant market (~$2.2–$2.4 trillion, ~45% of global sales).
- China has 904 million digital shoppers (44% of global total), expected to rise to 1.33 billion by 2027.
- There are 26.5 million ecommerce sites globally.

**Growth Markets:**
- B2C ecommerce CAGR: 8.4% globally; China's B2C sector at 14.3% CAGR.
- B2B ecommerce projected to reach $47.54 trillion by 2030.
- Six of the ten fastest-growing markets are in Asia (Philippines 24.1%, India 22.3%, Indonesia 20%).
- UK online sales expected to exceed 28% of retail sales by 2026.

**U.S. Ecommerce:**
- U.S. ecommerce sales: ~$1.23 trillion in 2025; Q1 2026 reached $326.7 billion (9.8% YoY increase).
- Online shopping = 16.9% of all U.S. retail sales (Q1 2026).
- Amazon dominates: 56% of U.S. shoppers start product searches on Amazon; Amazon accounts for 38% of all U.S. online retail sales.
- U.S. ecommerce expected to grow at 7.8% annually (2023–2027).

**Platforms & Marketplaces:**
- Shopify leads high-end platforms (27.5% of top 1M sites); WooCommerce has 39% of all ecommerce sites overall.
- Amazon ($2.789T market cap) vs. Alibaba ($325.41B) vs. Pinduoduo ($164.39B).
- Alibaba has 903M active customers vs. Amazon's 310M; Amazon receives 2.77B monthly visits.

**Social Commerce:**
- Global social commerce sales reached $700+ billion in 2025, forecasted to hit $2.9 trillion.
- 5.2 billion social media users globally; 90% purchase from brands they follow.
- 46% of Chinese and 36% of American users buy directly through social platforms.
- TikTok's #TikTokMadeMeBuyIt hashtag has 30+ billion views.
- China's livestream shopping market expected to surpass 6 trillion yuan in 2025.

**Mobile Commerce:**
- Mobile accounts for 71% of ecommerce traffic; conversion rates: 2% mobile vs. 3% desktop.
- 65% of U.S. ecommerce sales are mobile-driven.
- Digital wallets account for ~50% of global online transactions; Apple Pay has 500M+ users globally.

**Cart Abandonment:**
- Average cart abandonment rate: 70.22%.
- Top reasons: browsing (43%), unexpected costs (39%), slow delivery (21%), trust issues (19%), forced account creation (19%), complicated checkout (18%).

**Ecommerce Fraud:**
- Global fraud losses projected to exceed $48 billion in 2026.
- For every $100 in fraudulent orders, merchants lose $207 after chargebacks and overhead.
- 29.8% of attacks involve account takeovers; 24.1% are bot-driven.
- ~60% of merchants use payment tokenization for prevention.

**Dropshipping & POD:**
- Global dropshipping market: $372.47 billion (2025), expected to reach $476.10 billion in 2026.
- Average dropshipping profit margins: 15%–20%.
- Print-on-demand market: $13–$15 billion in 2026, could exceed $45 billion by 2031.

**AI in Ecommerce:**
- Global AI market projected at $757.6 billion in 2025, surpassing $1.8 trillion by 2030.
- AI-powered ecommerce tools market: ~$17 billion by 2030.
- AI expected to handle 80% of customer interactions by 2030.
- 34% of U.S. customers comfortable with agentic commerce (AI shopping for them).
- AI product recommendations can drive up to 3× revenue growth.

**Future Outlook:**
- Ecommerce projected to account for 24% of all global retail by end of 2026.
- Voice-activated shopping: over $164 billion in 2025.
- Metaverse ecommerce could grow from $30.6B to $678.8B.

## Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales

CB26-133

**Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales Report**  
   
 The Census Bureau of the Department of Commerce announced today that the estimate of U.S. retail e-commerce sales for the second quarter of 2026, adjusted for seasonal variation, but not for price changes, was $340.2 billion, an increase of 3.8 percent (±0.4 percent) from the first quarter of 2026. Total retail sales for the second quarter of 2026 were estimated at $1,986.5 billion, an increase of 2.9 percent (±0.2 percent) from the first quarter of 2026. The second quarter 2026 e-commerce estimate increased 12.2 percent (±0.9 percent) from the second quarter of 2025 while total retail sales increased 6.7 percent (±0.5 percent) in the same period. E-commerce sales in the second quarter of 2026 accounted for 17.1 percent of total sales.  
   
 On a not adjusted basis, the estimate of U.S. retail e-commerce sales for the second quarter of 2026 totaled $329.5 billion, a increase of 9.4 percent (±0.4 percent) from the first quarter of 2026. The second quarter 2026 e-commerce estimate increased 12.4 percent (±0.9 percent) from the second quarter of 2025 while total retail sales increased 6.6 percent (±0.5 percent) in the same period. E-commerce sales in the second quarter of 2026 accounted for 16.4 percent of total sales.

# Is Ecommerce Still Growing?

As of March, 2026, the freshest U.S. numbers are clear. The U.S. Census Bureau says retail ecommerce sales reached $1.2337 trillion in 2025, up 5.4% year over year. Total retail sales also grew, but more slowly, and ecommerce finished the year at 16.4% of all retail sales. In the fourth quarter alone, U.S. ecommerce sales hit $316.1 billion, up 5.3% from a year earlier, while total retail sales rose 2.7%. Ecommerce accounted for 16.6% of all retail in Q4.

***Who are we?****Speed Commerce is an end-to-end provider of outsourced customer experience solutions for eCommerce retailers as well as manufacturers, for close to 20 years. We grow our clients’ businesses by providing winning customer experience strategies such as 24/7/365 eCommerce customer service,*[*order fulfillment*](https://www.speedcommerce.com/ecommerce-order-fulfillment/)*, and warehousing –*[*get a free quote from a fulfillment expert*](https://www.speedcommerce.com/contact/)*.* Refer to our guides on [crowdfunding fulfillment services](https://www.speedcommerce.com/crowdfunding-fulfillment-101/), [east coast fulfillment](https://www.speedcommerce.com/east-coast-3pl-warehousing-and-fulfillment/), and [ecommerce fulfillment](https://www.speedcommerce.com/ecommerce-order-fulfillment/) updated for*2026.*

## $6.88 Trillion and Climbing (with Some Caveats)

Global retail ecommerce sales totaled approximately $6.42 trillion in 2025. For 2026, multiple forecasters converge on a figure near $6.88 trillion, suggesting year-over-year growth of roughly 7.2%. By 2028, that figure is projected to reach $7.89 trillion.

To put that growth rate in context, in-store retail sales grew approximately 3% in 2025. Ecommerce is expanding at more than double the pace of physical retail, and its share of total global retail sales continues to climb. In 2024, ecommerce accounted for 19.9% of all retail. In 2025, that rose to 20.5%. For 2026, the figure is forecast at 21.1%, and by 2028, it should reach 22.5%.

That said, the growth rate has come down from where it was. Ecommerce grew by an estimated 7.7% in 2024, then 6.8% in 2025. The slight deceleration was driven by macroeconomic pressures in China (the world’s largest ecommerce market) and tariff-related uncertainty in North America. But the consensus view from Shopify, eMarketer, and the International Trade Administration is that 2026 looks like a rebound year, with growth accelerating again if conditions stabilize.

## The U.S. Market

The U.S. Census Bureau released its Q4 2025 Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales report on March 10, 2026, and it provides the most authoritative snapshot of the American ecommerce landscape. Here are the headline numbers.

Full-year 2025 – total U.S. retail ecommerce sales reached $1,233.7 billion ($1.23 trillion), an increase of 5.4% from 2024. Total retail sales grew 3.5% over the same period. Ecommerce accounted for 16.4% of total U.S. retail sales, up from 16.1% in 2024.

Q4 2025 -seasonally adjusted ecommerce sales hit $316.1 billion, up 1.7% from Q3 2025. Year-over-year, Q4 ecommerce grew 5.3%, while total retail grew just 2.7%. Ecommerce’s share of total sales for Q4 reached 16.6% on an adjusted basis, and 18.3% on an unadjusted basis (reflecting the holiday spending surge).

January 2026 signal – the Census Bureau’s advance monthly retail report showed nonstore retailers (the category that most closely tracks online sellers) were up 10.9% year-over-year in January 2026, suggesting the momentum is holding into the new year.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Metric** | **2024** | **2025** |
| Total U.S. E-commerce Sales | $1,170.4B (est.) | $1,233.7B |
| YoY E-commerce Growth | ~7.5% | 5.4% |
| E-commerce % of Total Retail | 16.1% | 16.4% |
| Q4 E-commerce Sales (SA) | $300.1B (est.) | $316.1B |
| 2026 Forecast | $1.62 Trillion |

## Where Is Growth the Hottest?

**Asia-Pacific is Still the Center**

APAC is the world’s largest ecommerce region by a wide margin, driven primarily by China. But the growth story is shifting. China’s dominance (it generated $3.45 trillion in ecommerce revenue in 2025 and maintains an 83% share of the APAC market) is increasingly supplemented by India and Southeast Asia. India, with only 5% ecommerce penetration across 1.4 billion people, represents one of the most significant untapped markets in the world. Southeast Asia is the fastest-growing ecommerce region globally, with 18.6% growth and a trajectory toward $230 billion in gross merchandise value by 2026.

**Latin America is The Fastest-Growing Revenue Region**

Latin America leads all regions in revenue growth rate, expanding at 12.2% year-over-year to reach $191.25 billion. Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina account for 84.5% of the region’s ecommerce sales. Mexico’s growth trajectory is particularly notable: it is on track to surpass U.S. ecommerce penetration levels by 2026.

**Mature and Steady** **Europe**

Western Europe’s ecommerce growth has stabilized around 4% annually, which is expected to hold through 2029. The market is on track to surpass $800 billion by the end of the decade. For retailers, Europe is a market where gains come from optimization and execution rather than riding category-level tailwinds.

**North American Tariff Headwinds, But Optimism for 2026**

Growth in North America decelerated in 2025, most due to tariff-related uncertainty and softer consumer confidence. But forecasters point to improvement in 2026 as market conditions stabilize and brands adapt to the new trade environment. The January 2026 retail data (non-store retailers up 10.9% year-over-year) supports the view. As of this writing, geoplotics and trader-related issues will continue to be a wildcard.

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Region** | **2025 Growth Rate** | **Market** | **Penetration** |
| Southeast Asia | 18.6% | Indonesia | 32% |
| Latin America | 12.2% | Mexico/Brazil | Low-mid teens |
| United States | 5.4% | U.S. | 16.4% |
| Western Europe | ~4% | UK/Germany | ~31% (UK) |
| China | ~6% | China | 47% |
| India | 14%+ | India | 5% |

So, is ecommerce still growing in 2026? Yes. The latest data does not support the idea that ecommerce topped out and plateaued. It supports a more accurate conclusion, that ecommerce is still expanding, still outpacing broader retail in important markets, and still taking share from offline commerce.

The webpage, published in March 2026 by Speed Commerce, addresses whether ecommerce is still growing. The answer is yes. Key data points include:

- **U.S. Market (2025):** Total retail ecommerce sales reached $1.2337 trillion, up 5.4% year-over-year, accounting for 16.4% of all retail sales (up from 16.1% in 2024). Q4 2025 ecommerce sales hit $316.1 billion (16.6% of total retail). January 2026 data shows nonstore retailers up 10.9% year-over-year, indicating continued momentum.
- **Global Market:** Global retail ecommerce sales totaled ~$6.42 trillion in 2025, with a 2026 forecast of ~$6.88 trillion (7.2% growth). By 2028, projected to reach $7.89 trillion. Ecommerce's share of global retail rose from 19.9% (2024) to 20.5% (2025), forecast at 21.1% for 2026 and 22.5% by 2028. Ecommerce is expanding at more than double the pace of physical retail.
- **Regional Hotspots:** Asia-Pacific is the largest region, led by China ($3.45T in 2025). Southeast Asia is the fastest-growing region at 18.6%. Latin America leads in revenue growth at 12.2%. India has only 5% ecommerce penetration across 1.4 billion people, representing a major untapped market. Western Europe grows at ~4% annually.
- **Caveats:** Growth has decelerated from 7.7% (2024) to 6.8% (2025) due to macroeconomic pressures in China and tariff uncertainty in North America. However, 2026 is expected to be a rebound year if conditions stabilize.

The article concludes that ecommerce is still expanding, still outpacing broader retail, and still taking share from offline commerce.

# Best AI Tools for Amazon Sellers 2026: Listing, PPC, Repricing & Inventory Automation

![Arishekar N](https://cdn.amzprep.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/arishekar-n-ecommerce-expert.jpeg)
![Arishekar N](https://cdn.amzprep.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/arishekar-n-ecommerce-expert.jpeg)

#### Arishekar N

![Blair Forrest](https://cdn.amzprep.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Untitled-design-15-1.png)
![Blair Forrest](https://cdn.amzprep.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Untitled-design-15-1.png)

#### Blair Forrest

![Best ai tools for amazon sellers](https://cdn.amzprep.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Best-AI-Tools-for-Amazon-Sellers_-Automate-Your-Way-to-Success-1024x576.webp "Best AI Tools for Amazon Sellers 2026: Listing, PPC, Repricing & Inventory Automation 2")
![Get a quote from AMZ Prep – Contact Us](https://cdn.amzprep.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/blog-sidebar-cta-img-v1.webp)

Amazon sellers face increasing operational complexity in 2026. Manual listing optimization, hourly price changes, PPC bid adjustments across hundreds of keywords, and multi-channel inventory forecasting now consume 15-25 hours weekly for brands processing 1,000+ monthly orders.

![Best ai tools for amazon sellers](https://cdn.amzprep.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Best-AI-Tools-for-Amazon-Sellers_-Automate-Your-Way-to-Success-1024x576.webp "Best AI Tools for Amazon Sellers 2026: Listing, PPC, Repricing & Inventory Automation 14")

AI tools automate these workflows. Over 900,000 Amazon sellers adopted AI listing generators in 2025. Adoption accelerated in Q1 2026 following Amazon’s launch of Dynamic Canvas (an AI-powered seller dashboard) and enhanced Rufus search algorithm updates that prioritize semantic content over keyword stuffing.

The 2026 AI landscape for Amazon sellers:

**Amazon’s native tools (free, built into Seller Central)**: AI Listing Generator, Enhance My Listing, Dynamic Canvas for inventory planning, Seller Assistant for forecasting.

**Third-party specialists (paid subscriptions, $49-$695/month)**: Tools focused on specific functions like PPC automation (Perpetua, Quartile), repricing (SellerSnap, Aura), or listing optimization (Helium 10, CopyMonkey).

**The strategic question:** Which tasks justify AI investment versus manual management? PPC automation breaks even at $3,000+ monthly ad spend. Repricing tools pay for themselves at 500+ SKUs. Listing generators save 3-4 hours per product but require human editing for brand voice.

This blog covers AI tools across five categories: listing optimization, repricing, PPC management, inventory forecasting, and review analysis. Each section includes 2026 pricing, ROI thresholds, and when to use free Amazon tools versus paid alternatives.

## When AI Tools Justify Their Cost (And When They Don’t)

AI tools for Amazon sellers range from free (Amazon’s native features) to $695/month (enterprise PPC platforms). The decision to invest depends on three factors: task volume, margin impact, and available human bandwidth.

ROI break-even points by tool category:

### Listing optimization ($0-99/month)

Break-even: 5+ new products monthly OR portfolio of 50+ existing listings needing updates Time savings: 3-4 hours per listing (from research to publication) Free alternative: Amazon’s AI Listing Generator (basic draft quality)

### Repricing ($99-500/month)

Break-even: 500+ SKUs OR high-velocity categories (electronics, books, consumables) where Buy Box flips hourly Revenue impact: 12-18% Buy Box ownership increase = 8-12% sales lift for competitive ASINs Manual alternative: Viable only for under 100 SKUs with weekly price checks

### PPC automation ($250-695/month)

Break-even: $3,000+ monthly ad spend (tools typically save 20-30% on ACoS) Time savings: 8-12 hours weekly on bid management and keyword optimization Manual alternative: Helium 10 Adtomic ($99/month) for basic rule-based automation

### Inventory forecasting ($49-250/month)

Break-even: $50,000+ monthly revenue OR products with 60+ day lead times Cost avoidance: Prevents stockouts (ranking drops cost 20-30% in lost sales) and overstock (long-term storage fees) Free alternative: Amazon Seller Assistant (basic demand forecasting)

### Review analysis ($34-140/month)

Break-even: Product development cycles or competitive intelligence needs Use case: Analyzing 1,000+ competitor reviews to identify feature gaps takes AI 5 minutes versus 8+ hours manually Free alternative: ChatGPT/Claude for one-off analysis (copy-paste review batches)

2026 strategic approach: Start with Amazon’s free tools. Graduate to paid tools only after you can measure the time saved or revenue gained. Most sellers operate profitably with 2-4 paid subscriptions maximum.

## 5 Categories of AI Tools Every Amazon Seller Should Know

AI tools for Amazon fall into five main categories. Each solves a different problem with different cost thresholds.

### 1. Listing Optimization Tools

What they do: Keyword research, SEO-optimized descriptions, title optimization, and A+ Content generation.

When to invest: Launch 5+ products monthly OR manage 50+ existing listings. Single-product sellers use Amazon’s free tools.

Time saved: Drops listing creation from 4 hours to 30-45 minutes per product.

Cost: Free (Amazon native) to $99/month (Helium 10 Platinum).

Business impact: Optimized listings convert 15-35% better. A listing at 8% conversion might jump to 10-12% after AI optimization.

2026 update: Listings need FAQ-style content for Amazon’s Rufus AI. Tools like Helium 10 updated templates to include question-answer formatting.

Why it matters: Your listing is your salesperson. AI tools that help [humanize content](https://unaimytext.com/what-is-ai-text-humanizer) can improve readability and convert browsers into buyers with customer focused messaging and natural language.

Brands selling temperature-sensitive products like supplements or beauty items should ensure listings highlight cold chain capabilities, especially when using specialized [cold storage 3PL services](https://amzprep.com/cold-storage-3pl/) for fulfillment.

### 2. Repricing Tools

What they do: Automatically adjust prices based on competitor activity while protecting profit margins.

When to invest: 500+ SKUs OR high-competition categories (electronics, books, consumables). Private label sellers rarely need this.

Revenue impact: 12-18% Buy Box increase = 8-12% sales lift. Buy Box winner gets 82% of sales.

Cost: $99-500/month depending on SKU count.

Manual alternative: Works for under 100 SKUs with weekly price checks. Repricing strategy depends on your fulfillment model and true unit economics. Sellers using [FBA prep services](https://amzprep.com/fba-prep-services/) must include prep costs, inbound shipping, and placement fees in their minimum price calculations to protect margins.

Why it matters: Buy Box flips hourly in competitive categories. Missing it for 6 hours daily costs 20% of revenue. AI monitors prices every 5-15 minutes and responds instantly.

### 3. PPC and Advertising Management Tools

What they do: Automated bid adjustments, keyword optimization, and campaign management across Amazon ads.

When to invest: $3,000+ monthly ad spend. Below that, use basic automation ($99/month). Above $10,000, enterprise tools are mandatory.

ROI impact: 20-50% ACoS reduction typical. On $5,000 spend at 40% ACoS, a 25% reduction saves $625/month.

Cost: $99/month (basic) to $695/month (enterprise like Perpetua).

Manual alternative: Only viable under $1,000 monthly spend. PPC profitability depends on accurate margin calculations. Brands using [Middle Mile logistics](https://amzprep.com/middle-mile-logistics-fba-fast-track/) to avoid Amazon placement fees can afford more aggressive PPC bids due to lower fulfillment costs per unit.

Why it matters: AI makes thousands of hourly bid adjustments across hundreds of keywords. Manual management means 1-2 daily checks on maybe 50-100 keywords. You’re either missing opportunities or wasting budget.

### 4. Inventory Management and Forecasting Tools

What they do: Predict demand, send restock alerts, plan purchase orders, prevent stockouts and overstock.

When to invest: $50,000+ monthly revenue OR 60+ day lead times. Below this, Amazon’s free Seller Assistant works.

Cost: Free (Seller Assistant) to $250/month (multi-channel platforms).

Problem solved: Stockouts drop rankings 20-30% instantly. Overstock ties up cash. AI finds the balance.

AI advantage: Analyzes seasonal trends, sales velocity, holidays, competitor patterns automatically.

Why it matters: One stockout costs 20-30% in lost sales from ranking drops that take weeks to recover. AI forecasting orders the right amount at the right time.

Multi-channel sellers managing inventory across Amazon, Shopify, and Walmart marketplaces should implement [omnichannel fulfillment strategies](https://amzprep.com/omni-channel-3pl-fulfillment-services/) to prevent stockouts on one channel while holding excess inventory on another.

### 5. Review Analysis and Customer Sentiment Tools

What they do: Track reviews, spot trends, extract insights for product improvements and competitive intelligence.

When to invest: Active product development OR competitive research. For routine monitoring, free tools work.

Cost: $34-140/month.

Scale benefit: AI processes 1,000 reviews in 5 minutes versus 8-12 hours manually. Finds patterns like “23% mention lid leaking after 6 months.”

Strategic use: Competitor analysis for product development. If competitor reviews say “difficult to clean” 47 times, highlight “dishwasher safe” in your listing.

Review analysis becomes especially critical for brands in competitive categories like beauty products, where customer feedback directly informs formulation improvements and packaging decisions for [beauty 3PL fulfillment operations.](https://amzprep.com/beauty-products-3pl-fulfillment-services/)

Why it matters: Reviews tell you what customers actually want. AI identifies patterns impossible to catch manually, driving better product decisions and competitive positioning.

Before paying for third-party tools, test Amazon’s free AI features in Seller Central. The AI Listing Generator and Enhance My Listing handle basic optimization for most sellers. Upgrade to paid tools only when you need bulk automation, competitive intelligence, or advanced features like A/B testing and multi-marketplace sync.

Your product listing determines whether browsers become buyers. These AI tools help you write better listings faster.

This article from AMZ Prep (a 3PL/fulfillment provider) provides a comprehensive guide to the best AI tools for Amazon sellers in 2026. It notes that Amazon sellers face increasing operational complexity, with manual tasks consuming 15-25 hours weekly for brands processing 1,000+ monthly orders. Over 900,000 Amazon sellers adopted AI listing generators in 2025, with adoption accelerating in Q1 2026 following Amazon's launch of Dynamic Canvas and enhanced Rufus search algorithm updates.

The article covers ROI break-even points across five tool categories:
- **Listing optimization** ($0-99/month): Breaks even at 5+ new products monthly or 50+ existing listings. Saves 3-4 hours per listing.
- **Repricing** ($99-500/month): Breaks even at 500+ SKUs. Yields 12-18% Buy Box ownership increase = 8-12% sales lift.
- **PPC automation** ($250-695/month): Breaks even at $3,000+ monthly ad spend. Saves 20-30% on ACoS and 8-12 hours weekly.
- **Inventory forecasting** ($49-250/month): Breaks even at $50,000+ monthly revenue or 60+ day lead times.
- **Review analysis** ($34-140/month): Processes 1,000 reviews in 5 minutes vs. 8+ hours manually.

**Amazon's free native tools** (all included with Seller Central): AI Listing Generator, Enhance My Listing, Dynamic Canvas (launched March 2026), and Seller Assistant for forecasting.

- Listing: Helium 10 ($29-$299/month), CopyMonkey ($49-$99/month)
- Repricing: SellerSnap ($250-$800/month), RepricerExpress ($79-$99/month)
- PPC: Perpetua ($695+/month), Quartile (demo-based pricing)

<webpage_content>
[Log in](/login/)   [Start free](/pricing/)

AI Tools

# 7 Best Amazon AI Tools for Sellers in 2026: From Listing to Pricing

Discover the 7 best Amazon AI tools for sellers in 2026. Compare AI listing builders, repricing tools, and image generators to boost sales and save time.

· Updated

![Ash Metry](/uploads/Ash.jpeg)

Ash Metry·Founder & CEO

**The short answer:** The best Amazon AI tools for sellers in 2026 fall into four categories: listing optimization (Keywords.am, Helium 10), Amazon’s native AI (Listing Builder, Rufus), repricing (Aura, BQool), and PPC automation (Perpetua, Adtomic). AI now compresses a 4-hour listing build into 30 to 45 minutes, but only if the tool is grounded in real search data. Tools that just wrap GPT around a spec sheet produce keyword-stuffed copy that ranks badly and converts worse.

There are over 50 “AI tools for Amazon sellers” on the market today. Most are templates with an LLM bolted on. This guide covers the 7 we’ve actually tested hands-on, what each one is best at, and where the native Amazon options are good enough to skip a paid tool.

## Best Amazon AI Tools for Listing Optimization

Listing optimization? That’s where you’ll see AI tools really shine - immediate ROI. I’ve seen sellers totally transform their product pages.

Here’s what matters: Amazon AI tools help write better copy. They help you find those keywords that will actually get clicks. And they help structure your content for Amazon’s A9 algorithm. That’s key.

The reality is, a well-optimized listing can be a total game changer. Sellers tell me it’s like night and day - from crickets to conversions.

### Tool #1: Keywords.am (Best for Listing-Focused Sellers)

Keywords.am? It’s pretty much laser-focused on Amazon listing optimization. I’ve seen so many tools try to do everything, but Keywords.am doesn’t bundle in product research or inventory stuff. Instead, it’s all about AI writing and keyword research.

**Key Points:**

* **Amber AI 2.0:** This is their Amazon-trained listing copilot. From what I’ve noticed, it really gets the TFSD (Title, Features, Search Terms, Description) structure. Unlike generic AI, it gives you content designed for each part of a listing. \* **Smart Listing Generator:** Here’s what matters - import an ASIN, and bam, you get a brand-aligned draft quickly. The workflow is simple: import, generate, refine with the AI copilot, then publish to Seller Central. \* **IntentIQ:** This feature finds long-tail, high-intent keywords - stuff other tools miss because they only look at search volume. It helps you snag shoppers ready to buy. \* **21 Marketplace Support:** Sellers tell me this is a big deal: intent-aware localization. It’s not just translation; it gets the cultural stuff and local search habits. And it handles tech things like [byte counting](/tools/character-limit-checker/) for Japan and Germany. \* **Pricing:** Monthly plans go from $49 to $299. The reality is that’s way cheaper than the $99 to $279 you’d pay for those do-it-all suites.

**Best for:** Sellers wanting a serious [AI listing copilot](/amazon-seo/amber-ai-for-amazon-ai-listing/) without the extra fluff.

**Limitation:** Thing is though, it’s not a complete package. So, if you need product research or PPC help, you’ll need other tools.

### Tool #2: Helium 10 Listing Builder (Best All-in-One with AI)

Helium 10? It’s pretty much everywhere now. I’ve seen a lot of Amazon sellers using it as their all-in-one platform. Listing Builder is right there as part of the package - uses AI. So, convenient if you’re already in their world.

**Key Points:**

* **ChatGPT-4 Powered:** The [Listing Builder utilizes ChatGPT-4](https://www.helium10.com/blog/helium-10-announces-new-ai-enhanced-listing-builder-tool/) to write your listing. Even AI images! Here’s the thing though - the good AI stuff needs the Diamond plan. That’s $279/month.
* **Competitor Comparison Table:** Shows competitor rankings for keywords. Helps with figuring out where to put your keywords. I’ve seen this be really helpful.
* **Keyword Performance Tool:** Tracks keyword density and placement. Similar to those coverage indicators you see elsewhere.
* **Direct Seller Central Sync:** Pushes listing updates straight to Amazon Seller Central. No more copy-paste!

**Best for:** Sellers who already pay for Helium 10’s other stuff (research, advertising, analytics) and want listing AI all in one place.

**Limitation:** The best AI is stuck on the $279/month Diamond plan. Truth is, the Listing Builder itself doesn’t really make that cost worth it [compared to Helium 10](/blog/keywords-am-vs-helium-10/) alternatives if listing optimization is your main focus.

## Amazon’s Native AI Tools (Free for All Sellers)

Don’t rush into buying extra AI tools right away. Amazon actually gives sellers some free AI tools right inside Seller Central.

These are worth a look before you spend money. They’ve gotten a lot better - seriously. And honestly, they’re a great starting point.

Here’s the thing though: Amazon’s AI tools have grown up. From what I’ve noticed, these tools are pretty useful now. That said, they might cover all your needs. But they’re free. Can’t beat that!

I’ve seen sellers (especially new ones) get a lot of value out of just these Amazon-provided features. So, check them out first.

### Tool #3: Amazon’s AI Listing Generator

Amazon launched this thing in 2023. It’s their own AI listing generator. From what I’ve noticed, it’s gotten a lot of use.

**Key Points:**

* **Generate from URL or Description:** A seller can just paste a link (points to their product on some other website). Or they can write a little description. And Amazon’s AI kicks in. It’ll whip up a draft title, bullet points, even the description.
* **High Adoption:** [Over 900,000 sellers](https://sell.amazon.com/blog/amazon-listing-ai) have given it a shot, sellers tell me. That said, a wild 90% acceptance rate? People are using its suggestions.
* **Best for:** Quickly getting a first draft going. This is for a new product that’s waiting for proper [Amazon listing optimization](/amazon-seo/amazon-listing-optimization-2026-2/).

**Limitation:** The output? Honestly, it’s often pretty generic. Here’s the thing though - it doesn’t have a strong brand voice. And strategic keywords? Forget about it. It doesn’t really do competitive analysis either. So, it’s a tool for creation, not optimization. That’s what it is.

### Tool #4: Enhance My Listing (Announced Accelerate 2025)

## The State of AI for Amazon Sellers in 2026

If you're still doing product research by scrolling bestseller lists, writing listing copy from memory, or managing PPC campaigns with manual bid changes, you are working against the grain of how the top 10% of Amazon sellers operate in 2026.

## AI for Product Research

Product research is where most FBA businesses win or lose — and it is where AI delivers some of its most dramatic efficiency gains. ## AI for Keyword Research and Clustering

Traditional Amazon keyword research was a volume-matching exercise: find high-volume terms, put them in your listing. The approach still works — but it misses a layer that AI unlocks: **semantic clustering by buyer intent**.

AI keyword clustering groups search terms by what the buyer is actually trying to accomplish, not just the surface text. Long-tail keywords typically have lower search volume but carry 2–3 times the conversion rate of broad terms. They're difficult to discover manually at scale — but AI can process thousands of keyword variations and flag the high-intent, lower-competition terms that human researchers routinely miss. This is where AI delivers disproportionate ROI in keyword research.

In 2025, independent sellers created more than 12 million Amazon listings using generative AI. The reason is straightforward: writing a high-converting Amazon listing manually is genuinely difficult, time-consuming, and gets harder as you scale to multiple SKUs. AI changes the economics entirely.

Amazon PPC management at scale is one of the most time-intensive tasks in the seller's workflow.
