[Explore SPS Commerce](https://www.spscommerce.com)[Contact Sales](https://www.spscommerce.com/contact)

# Amazon AI Tools Every Seller Needs for Success in 2025

![The SPS Commerce Team](https://us-east-1.graphassets.com/AaZQD68KNQ46abk6wQUdWz/output=format:webp/cmlsg1iomfeam07iw43lxgg8q)

By[The SPS Commerce Team](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/profile/the-sps-commerce-team), *The SPS Commerce Team*

Last Updated December 26, 2024

8 min read

Amazon sellers increasingly turn to artificial intelligence (AI) to gain a competitive edge. As more sellers seek out the best Amazon AI tools, understanding and implementing these technologies has become essential for success on the platform.

From AI-powered product research to sophisticated chatbot solutions, a wide range of tools are transforming how Amazon businesses operate. In this article, we’ll explore the most impactful Amazon AI tools for sellers.

## ChatGPT: Your Data Analysis Helper

[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/ "https://chatgpt.com/") is an advanced language model designed to analyze and interpret complex business data. Its Advanced Analytics capability has become a standout feature for Amazon sellers, allowing them to upload and analyze spreadsheets, customer reviews, and market data, then export detailed analyses in Excel format.

Recent enhancements allow direct file uploads from platforms like Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive, making it an essential tool for data-driven decision-making. Amazon sellers find particular value in their ability to interpret sales figures, identify seasonal patterns, and uncover hidden opportunities in customer feedback data to drive strategic improvements.

**Related Reading:** [5 Easy Ways Amazon Sellers Can Use ChatGPT to Increase Profits (According to ChatGPT)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/5-ways-amazon-sellers-use-chatgpt-to-increase-profits "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/5-ways-amazon-sellers-use-chatgpt-to-increase-profits")

## Claude: The Listing Optimization Expert

[Claude](https://claude.ai/ "https://claude.ai/") is a sophisticated AI language model developed by Anthropic that excels at creating Amazon AI product descriptions and [optimizing AI Amazon listing content](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/5-amazon-listing-optimization-tips-to-prevent-account-suspension "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/5-amazon-listing-optimization-tips-to-prevent-account-suspension"). When applied to using AI for Amazon FBA, it stands out for its exceptional writing capabilities and deep understanding of context.

What sets Claude apart is its ability to maintain a natural, persuasive tone while incorporating relevant keywords and meeting Amazon’s content guidelines. Sellers report particular success using Claude for crafting product descriptions and [A+ Content](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-guide/retail-edi-glossary "https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-guide/retail-edi-glossary") that converts while maintaining a consistent brand voice across their entire catalog.

## Midjourney: The Lifestyle Image Generator

[Midjourney](https://www.midjourney.com/home "https://www.midjourney.com/home") is an AI-powered image generation tool that creates high-quality, artistic images from text descriptions. This creative platform has reshaped how sellers approach lifestyle photography for their listings.

The tool’s ability to generate unique, high-quality images based on detailed prompts has dramatically reduced the cost and time associated with professional photography.

Sellers are finding particular success using Midjourney for creating seasonal promotional images and developing lifestyle shots that can be combined with Photoshop to showcase their products in authentic settings.

**Related Reading:** [How to Use AI Advertising Tools and Tactics for Ecommerce Growth](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-accelerate-2024-ai-advertising-insights-tips "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-accelerate-2024-ai-advertising-insights-tips")

## Ecomtent: The Amazon Listing Specialist

[Ecomtent](https://www.ecomtent.ai/ "https://www.ecomtent.ai/") generates optimized Amazon product listings, including lifestyle images, A+ Content, infographics and keyword-rich copy at speed and scale. Fresh off a [$1.4M seed funding round](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/max-sinclair-ai_ecomtent-a-gen-ai-startup-founded-by-former-activity-7274707061135880194-CdHm/ "https://www.linkedin.com/posts/max-sinclair-ai_ecomtent-a-gen-ai-startup-founded-by-former-activity-7274707061135880194-CdHm/"), this promising startup has positioned itself as a leader in optimizing for RUFUS, Amazon’s new AI shopping assistant. Unlike other Amazon listing software, Ecomtent understands the nuances of Amazon’s A9 & COSMO ranking algorithms, and uses this knowledge to optimize the visual and written content it generates. The platform both exceeds at increasing the efficiency of design teams; whilst also increasing the discoverability of product listings in organic search on Amazon and [boosting conversion rates](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-improve-ctr-cvr-amazon "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-improve-ctr-cvr-amazon").

## Canva: Your Ecommerce Design Powerhouse

[Canva](https://www.canva.com/ "https://www.canva.com/") is an intuitive, AI-powered design platform that empowers Amazon sellers to create professional-grade visuals for their listings and marketing campaigns.

Unlike complex graphic design software, Canva offers a user-friendly interface with drag-and-drop functionality, pre-designed templates, and customizable elements tailored to ecommerce needs. Sellers can use it to design eye-catching product images, infographics, and A+ content that enhance conversion rates and brand presence.

Canva’s strength lies in its ability to streamline the design process, enabling sellers to produce high-quality visuals quickly and efficiently without needing advanced design skills.

## HeyGen: AI-Powered UGC and Influencer Content Creator

Example of AI-created “UGC” video

[HeyGen](https://www.heygen.com/ "https://www.heygen.com/") is a cutting-edge AI video generation platform tailored to help Amazon sellers create engaging User-Generated Content (UGC) and influencer-style videos.

Leveraging advanced AI technology, HeyGen enables sellers to produce realistic, personalized videos at scale featuring virtual influencers or avatars that resonate with their target audience. This makes it ideal for [crafting authentic product showcases](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-inspire-how-to-increase-sales-with-reel-reviews-from-real-people "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-inspire-how-to-increase-sales-with-reel-reviews-from-real-people"), testimonial-style videos, or promotional campaigns without costly production teams.

## GummySearch: Your Niche Audience Discovery Tool

GummySearch allows you to curate audiences at scale based on a topic

[GummySearch](https://gummysearch.com/ "https://gummysearch.com/") is an AI-powered platform designed to help Amazon sellers uncover niche audience insights and [create targeted marketing strategies](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/data-driven-marketing "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/data-driven-marketing"). By analyzing conversations and trends on platforms like Reddit, GummySearch identifies what potential customers are saying about products, pain points, and preferences.

Sellers can leverage this data to validate product ideas, optimize listings, and create compelling ad campaigns tailored to specific customer needs.

GummySearch is best at providing actionable insights directly from organic discussions, enabling sellers to stay ahead of trends and connect with their ideal audience more effectively.

Expand your reach with [DSP Prime by Carbon6](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/ad-performance "https://www.spscommerce.com/products/ad-performance"). Tap into Amazon’s first-party data to connect with high-intent audiences across websites, apps, and streaming services—all supported by expert management to ensure your campaigns deliver results.

## Perplexity AI: Your Market Research Assistant

[Perplexity AI](https://www.perplexity.ai/ "https://www.perplexity.ai/") is an advanced AI-powered search and research assistant that helps Amazon sellers stay informed about market trends and competitor activities.

Unlike traditional search engines, Perplexity provides real-time, citation-backed insights by analyzing current web data and synthesizing information from multiple reliable sources. Sellers can use it to research product opportunities, understand market dynamics, and [track industry news](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles"). Its strength lies in its ability to provide comprehensive, up-to-date answers to complex business questions while citing its sources, allowing sellers to verify information and dig deeper into topics of interest.

The platform’s Pro features include uploading documents and images for analysis, making it particularly valuable for competitive research and market analysis.

Unlock insights into AI-powered personalization, Amazon’s COSMO system, and advanced strategies to optimize advertising and product research with our [AI in Ecommerce White Paper](https://spscommerce.com/community/resources "https://spscommerce.com/community/resources").

## Accio: The Global Sourcing Game-Changer

Alibaba’s Accio allows you to use AI to product search for sourcing

[Accio](https://www.accio.com/ "https://www.accio.com/") is Alibaba’s AI-powered procurement engine that helps sellers discover and source products globally. With a reported [40% increase in purchase intent compared to traditional search methods](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/alibaba-rolls-out-ai-search-tool-sellers-jo-lambadjieva-d7snc "https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/alibaba-rolls-out-ai-search-tool-sellers-jo-lambadjieva-d7snc"), this tool has streamlined how sellers discover and source products globally. The tool’s integration of market analysis with procurement capabilities makes it particularly valuable for sellers looking to expand their product lines or optimize their supply chains.

## Profasee: The Dynamic Pricing Genie

[Profasee](https://profasee.com/ "https://profasee.com/"), founded by ecommerce [Chad Rubin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/itschadrubin/ "https://www.linkedin.com/in/itschadrubin/"), is an AI-driven dynamic pricing platform that automatically optimizes product prices in real time.

By analyzing billions of data points, including sales trends, competitor pricing, and consumer behaviors, the platform determines optimal pricing in real time. This automated approach eliminates manual price adjustments while ensuring maximum profitability.

The platform boasts its seamless integration with Inventory Management systems and its comprehensive dashboard that makes complex pricing decisions accessible.

**Related Reading:** [How Dynamic Repricing Boosts Profitability for Amazon Private Labels](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/dynamic-pricing-to-maintain-profitability "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/dynamic-pricing-to-maintain-profitability")

## Project Amelia: Your AI-Powered Seller Assistant

[Project Amelia](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-project-amelia "https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-project-amelia"), launched at [Amazon Accelerate 2024](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-accelerate-2024-recap "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-accelerate-2024-recap"), represents Amazon generative AI at its finest – an AI-powered assistant designed to help sellers manage and grow their businesses more efficiently.

To make sellers Amazon AI-ready, this tool is integrated into Seller Central and offers personalized insights and support by learning each seller’s unique business needs.

Sellers can ask Amelia questions about their Amazon AI product performance, inventory, and receive tailored recommendations to enhance productivity and drive growth.

Currently, in beta, Project Amelia is progressively rolling out to US sellers, with plans for broader availability in the future.

## Harnessing AI for Selling in 2025

As we look ahead to 2025, Amazon sellers must embrace AI tools to stay competitive.

The key technologies—ranging from AI-driven data analysis with ChatGPT to dynamic pricing with Profasee—are changing how sellers manage inventory, [optimize listings](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/the-ultimate-guide-to-amazon-creative-listing-optimization-for-conversion "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/the-ultimate-guide-to-amazon-creative-listing-optimization-for-conversion"), and connect with their target audience. By integrating tools like Claude for listing optimization, Midjourney for creative imagery, and HeyGen for personalized video content, sellers can enhance their product presentations and marketing efforts without breaking the bank.

However, success in this AI-powered era requires more than just using these tools—it demands continuous learning and strategic implementation to maximize their potential.

**Actionable Insights:**

* **Optimize Listings and Content**: Leverage Claude for high-quality product descriptions and A+ Content to increase conversions.
* **Boost Marketing with Visuals and Videos**: Use Midjourney and HeyGen to create stunning visuals and engaging UGC videos that resonate with customers.
* **Utilize Market Insights**: Use GummySearch and Perplexity AI to stay informed about market trends and competitor activities.

Want to stay on the cutting edge of AI developments in ecommerce? Join over 32,000 forward-thinking sellers who receive our [Amazon Seller Newsletter](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-seller-news "https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-seller-news") weekly.

**Pro Tip**

Want to learn more about integrating AI into your current selling systems? [Amazing Wave](https://amazingwave.digital/ "https://amazingwave.digital/") helps Amazon and ecommerce businesses with AI consultation, audits, training and implementation.

#### [Article](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/)

# AI for Amazon Sellers: Rufus, Amelia, Reviews, PPC, & Videos

Natalie Ricardo | August 18, 2025

AI continues to grow rapidly, being implemented into tons of software tools and platforms that many of us already use – one of which is Amazon. This extensive artificial intelligence implementation is already transforming various aspects of the ecommerce platform.

In a few previous **artificial intelligence resources**, we explored other AI use cases for Amazon ecommerce sellers:

* [How Ecommerce Brands Can Utilize Adobe AI](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/how-ecommerce-brands-can-use-adobe-generative-ai-to-improve-online-merchandising/)
* [The Use of AI and Differentiation on Amazon](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/webinars/the-use-of-ai-and-differentiation-on-amazon/)

This article will serve more as an overview of how Amazon is implementing AI across the shopping experience, advertising, and seller tools, giving a comprehensive view of what Amazon’s increasing investment in AI means for a seller’s business & overall [marketplace strategy](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/consulting-strategy/marketplace-strategy/). For each Amazon AI addition, we’ll explain what it is, how it works, whether it’s worth testing, and what it means for brands.

As Amazon has continued to implement more artificial intelligence tools to its platform, businesses must understand what these resources offer and whether an investment in testing/usage is worthwhile.

## Amazon Rufus: AI Shopping Assistant (Now “Alexa for Shopping”)

Amazon’s announcement of Rufus (now “Alexa for Shopping”), its AI shopping assistant, is likely the most important artificial intelligence integration to the platform. [Announced in early 2024](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-rufus), Rufus (now “Alexa for Shopping”) has quickly made an impact – for both sellers and consumers – since its launch.

The goal of adding Rufus was to h**elp shoppers find product information, answer questions, and overall improve the shopping experience**. It helps shoppers ask Rufus directly natural-language questions, compare products, and get recommendations from quickly analyzing information directly from live Amazon detail pages. Now, shoppers can simply ask Rufus a general question about a type of Amazon product, down to specific details on how a certain ASIN can be used. This artificial intelligence integration is one of the most impactful additions to the marketplace as it’s now shifting how consumers shop on the platform.

From a seller’s point of view, Rufus (now “Alexa for Shopping”) highlights the ever-growing need for detailed, explanatory product information across all detail pages. In fact, we now think of Rufus as a lever that **impacts sales.** Rufus has the power to tell a shopper “yes, this product fits your needs” or “no, here’s a different product that sounds more like what you’re looking for” based on your product page content. As a result, changes you make to your product page content should be considered in conjunction with Rufus, demonstrating a key AI use case in the Amazon ecommerce landscape.

### Suggested Actions

1. Build a habit of [auditing your ASINs](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/catalog-management/catalog-monitoring-optimization/) monthly for gaps in attributes or other product details.
2. Include FAQs in your [A+ Content](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/the-importance-and-impact-of-a-content-on-an-amazon-product-page-examples-templates/) to reinforce answers Rufus (now “Alexa for Shopping”) can cite.

### How is Amazon Rufus AI Expanding?

In 2024, $164 billion worth of Amazon products were eligible for Rufus features and this is expected to reach $849.8 billion by 2027 while Rufus additionally expands to 13+ new global marketplaces in 2025, [according to AI Track](https://theaitrack.com/amazon-rufus-ai-700m-forecast/). This speaks to Amazon’s broader investment in AI and reiterates further that your product descriptions must be more detailed than ever to convince Rufus – and shoppers – that your products are worth purchasing.

## AI-Summarized Amazon Product Reviews

Amazon now uses generative AI to summarize [product reviews](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/generating-5-star-reviews-understanding-amazon-review-community-guidelines/) on detail pages. These Amazon AI review summaries reduce the time consumers needed for product research, speeding up the decision-making process by allowing shoppers to get a quick read on product quality without having to scroll through each [review](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/catalog-management/review-monitoring-management/) themselves.

These are some additional examples of generative AI implementations in the Amazon ecommerce landscape that have since enhanced the reviews process:

* Shoppers can click on specific features or filters within the AI summary to find personalized product reviews.
* The “shopper like me” filterers can be used to uncover reviews specific to relatable body sizes or other factors.
* Attribute callouts (eg: fit, noise level, battery life, material quality, etc.) can be selected to jump straight to what matters most to a given shopper.

## Project Amelia: Amazon’s AI Assistant for Sellers

Project Amelia (renamed “Seller Assistant” at [Amazon Accelerate 2025](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/amazon-accelerate-conference-2025-strategic-tools-for-brand-growth/)) is Amazon’s AI assistant for sellers. It [launched to beta users in September 2024](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-project-amelia). Amazon’s Amelia AI is designed to streamline support, surface insights, discover missed opportunities, and help resolve issues faster, offering helpful capabilities to sellers.

Amelia AI on Amazon can:

1. Answer natural-language questions about your [account health](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/seller-feedback-ratings-the-impact-of-poor-amazon-account-health/) and [catalog](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/catalog-management/)
2. Look into resolutions for common problems (eg: [inventory](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/logistics-forecasting/inventory-shipping-operational-support/) issues)
3. Provide summarizes of your sales by analyzing [performance data](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/amazon-advertising-reports-performance-data-for-marketing-strategy/)
4. Recommend actions to improve product performance.

Talk to Amazon’s Amelia AI the same way that a shopper would with Rufus; a potentially invaluable tool for [Amazon FBA](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/logistics-forecasting/amazon-fba-management/) sellers’ [operational support](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/catalog-management/operational-support/).

Amelia AI can be a helpful first pass tool when troubleshooting and for easier escalations of issues to Amazon directly, like [case work](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/catalog-management/account-troubleshooting/), that typically slows FBA brands down. However, this also relates to the ongoing question of “**is Amazon’s AI reliable?**” These AI tools for Amazon sellers, like Amelia, represent a significant step forward, however, we still strongly recommend your Amazon team (whether [in-house](https://gobrandwoven.com/solutions/in-housing/) or an [agency](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/agency-vs-in-house-why-hire-an-amazon-marketing-agency-partner/)) is kept in the loop for [consulting](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/consulting-strategy/) and tracking progress. In other words, treat Amelia as a co-pilot, not a pilot. Validate any suggested changes against your brand standards and compliance requirements.

## AI-Generated Amazon Listing Content

[Amazon](https://gobrandwoven.com/solutions/amazon-management/) offers additional generative AI tools for its ecommerce marketplace sellers, including the ability for brands to generate an entire product page with minimal information. Simply provide a prompt, URL, or spreadsheet with product attributes and Amazon will automatically generate the entire listing. From there, you can approve or regenerate the content as needed.

### Is the AI-Generated Amazon Listing Content Tool Worth Using?

This AI tool may be efficient for first drafts to [product page copywriting](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/digital-merchandising/copywriting/), but it can also produce generic language, miss your brand voice, or provide inaccurate claims about your products, raising potential concerns about the reliability of this new Amazon AI tool (especially in regards to generating content without human oversight). If you’re going to use it, we strongly recommend feeding the tool as much product information as you can upfront: exact specs, differentiators, real-world use cases, and certifications (if applicable). Then treat the output like a junior copywriter’s first draft, editing for brand voice, ensuring phrases are clear, and adjusting keywords for [SEO visibility.](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/digital-merchandising/marketplace-seo/)

As a team that has perfected Amazon listings over the past 8+ years, we continue to prioritize a human approach that resonates with shoppers and matches language that makes sense for your audience. Explore [our case studies](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/case-studies/) to see real-world examples of Amazon listings we’ve created for various [industries](https://gobrandwoven.com/industries/) and [reach out to our team](https://gobrandwoven.com/contact-us/) for a conversation if looking for optimization assistance.

## AI Creative Studio: Video, Images, & Audio for Amazon PPC

[In late 2024](https://advertising.amazon.com/resources/whats-new/unboxed-ai-creative-studio), Amazon Ads launched Creative Studio, a suite of AI-powered tools to help advertisers excel on the marketplace. Brands can utilize these AI capabilities to produce on-brand [product images](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/best-practices-for-amazon-listing-images-requirements-limitations-amp-more/), videos, and audio clips from existing [assets](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/dont-let-outdated-digital-assets-hurt-your-brands-sales-potential/), offering quick enhancements to Amazon PPC [campaigns](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/performance-marketing/campaign-management-optimization/). Simply provide “[a single product shot, product page, or existing ad creative](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-ads-generative-ai-video-generator-advertisers)” to generate new campaign creatives using Amazon AI videos, photos, or audio clips.

Videos take time & money to create, which is why many brands opt out of using them. But videos help capture consumers by visually explaining products in an attention-grabbing manner, making them an important investment. For brands that lack videos or [lifestyle images](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/product-listing-images-that-attract-new-customers/), these Amazon AI video tools can serve as a starting point to quickly close that gap and get [campaigns](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/performance-marketing/campaign-strategy-creation/) running sooner rather than later. The Amazon AI video generator can also be useful for seasonal creative refreshes or testing different [product shot environments](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-ads-image-generator-adds-aspect-ratio-capability) (eg: kitchen, gym, outdoors, etc.).

We’ve also seen that, especially in the past few years, shoppers have responded more to lifestyle visuals and [videos](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/news/video-generator) as these formats easily capture attention on the crowded Amazon marketplace, further emphasizing the value of these new PPC AI features that generate such content and may help deploy campaigns faster. Plus, **some ad types require videos** which makes the Amazon AI video generator specifically more valuable to brands without those [creative capabilities](https://gobrandwoven.com/capabilities/digital-merchandising/) already at their disposal.

## Additional Amazon Artificial Intelligence Investments

Amazon’s investment in AI extends beyond its marketplace, also investing heavily in robotics through its logistics network to ship faster, cheaper and with less issues.

* **“Private Investigator” (P.I.) defect detection**. Units pass through an imaging tunnel before shipping to customers; AI flags potential defects and diverts problematic units. Fewer defects should reduce returns and improve customer satisfaction, thanks to efficiencies brought by Amazon’s warehouse AI tools.
* **Autonomous robots in warehouses**. In-warehouse robots can now navigate environments without being required to work in fenced zones, directly relating to the advancements in Amazon’s warehouse AI improvements.
* **AI-driven carrier scheduling**. Automated scheduling speeds up back-and-forth communication on the logistics side.

These examples of artificial intelligence integrations and widespread Amazon implementation are also indirect benefits for sellers: quality control, delivery speed, and consistency. Better operations equal better Rufus AI conversations and customer reviews, leading to more accurate and influential (positive) summaries for shoppers.

## Where is AI for Amazon Sellers Heading?

As we learned during the [2024 holiday season](https://gobrandwoven.com/resources/articles/2024-holiday-season-online-shopping-trends/), shoppers are more open to AI-powered shopping tools than ever before with AI chat bots influencing $229 billion in global online holiday sales (23.5% of total holiday revenue). This significance demonstrates the growing impact and acceptance of artificial intelligence in ecommerce, likely influencing Amazon’s eagerness to launch the additional AI use cases we walked through in this article.

Although Amazon has already started to invest heavily in artificial intelligence, we’re sure that more AI-powered features will arise in the coming months and years, further showcasing the marketplace’s continued investment in the technology.

Despite this growing interest and trust in AI, we still encourage brands to **leverage human oversight** when depending on AI – especially when it relates to how their brand appears publicly and is interpreted by consumers – that is, until we (if ever) get to a point of being able to fully rely on Amazon’s AI tools.

If you would like to connect with our team of Amazon experts to discuss any of the tools mentioned in this article or explore what a partnership with [Brandwoven](https://gobrandwoven.com/about-us/) looks like, [reach out to us](https://gobrandwoven.com/contact-us/) to schedule a consultation where we can discuss any challenges your brand is facing and walk through our customized approach to marketplace management, providing valuable artificial intelligence resources and expertise in how to leverage AI for Amazon sellers.

args.summary:
This article by Natalie Ricardo (August 18, 2025) from Brandwoven provides a comprehensive overview of how Amazon is implementing AI across its shopping experience, advertising, and seller tools, and what these developments mean for Amazon sellers and marketplaces. Key AI tools covered include:

**1. Amazon Rufus (now "Alexa for Shopping")** - Amazon's AI shopping assistant, announced in early 2024. It helps shoppers ask natural-language questions, compare products, and get recommendations directly from live Amazon detail pages. From a seller's perspective, Rufus acts as a sales lever that can recommend or steer shoppers away from products based on detail page content. Suggested actions include monthly ASIN audits for attribute gaps and including FAQs in A+ Content. In 2024, $164 billion worth of Amazon products were eligible for Rufus features, expected to reach $849.8 billion by 2027, with expansion to 13+ new global marketplaces in 2025.

**2. AI-Summarized Product Reviews** - Amazon uses generative AI to summarize product reviews, reducing research time for consumers. Features include clickable feature filters, "shopper like me" filters, and attribute callouts (fit, noise level, battery life, material quality).

**3. Project Amelia (renamed "Seller Assistant" at Amazon Accelerate 2025)** - Amazon's AI assistant for sellers, launched to beta users in September 2024. It can answer natural-language questions about account health and catalog, resolve common problems (e.g., inventory issues), summarize sales data, and recommend product performance improvements. Brandwoven recommends treating Amelia as a "co-pilot, not a pilot," keeping human teams involved.

**4. AI-Generated Listing Content** - Allows brands to generate an entire product page from minimal input (prompt, URL, or spreadsheet). While efficient for first drafts, it can produce generic language and miss brand voice. Recommendation: feed the tool detailed product specs upfront and edit output like a junior copywriter's first draft.

**5. AI Creative Studio** - Launched late 2024, this suite of AI tools helps advertisers generate product images, videos, and audio clips from existing assets for Amazon PPC campaigns. Videos are valuable as some ad types require them, and shoppers increasingly respond to lifestyle visuals.

**Additional Amazon AI investments** include: "Private Investigator" (P.I.) defect detection using imaging tunnels and AI flags; autonomous warehouse robots navigating without fenced zones; and AI-driven carrier scheduling. These logistics improvements indirectly benefit sellers through quality control, delivery speed, and consistency.

**Key context:** During the 2024 holiday season, AI chatbots influenced $229 billion in global online holiday sales (23.5% of total holiday revenue), demonstrating growing consumer acceptance of AI in ecommerce. The article emphasizes that despite AI's growth, brands should maintain human oversight, especially regarding public brand presentation.

# Amazon launches a powerful new generative AI-based selling assistant codenamed Project Amelia

Launching today, this personal AI assistant was built using Amazon Bedrock and offers tailored business insights to boost productivity and drive seller growth.

![Conversations with Amelia seller assistant on a mobile device.](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/dims4/default/8abc6be/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2548x1434+0+0/resize/2640x1486!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.aboutamazon.com%2F5a%2F11%2F31bf9c4a4563a27d358968ee0b3b%2Faa-sept2024-sellingassistant-featured-hero-v1-2550x1125.jpg)

Written by Mary Beth Westmoreland, Vice President, Worldwide Selling Partner Experience

4 min read

Amazon has been investing in machine learning and AI for more than 25 years in nearly every area of our business, from powering awesome shopping experiences to developing innovative solutions for our selling partners. More recently, advancements in generative AI have made it possible to deliver even more innovative experiences, including further simplifying selling in Amazon’s store while providing more powerful avenues for growth. Today, we are introducing in beta a new generative AI-powered personal assistant for sellers, codenamed Project Amelia.

For independent sellers, managing a successful global selling business can require navigating a number of complex and challenging areas. Sellers need to determine how to build amazing products that meet unique customer needs, ensure compliance with different regulations and policies, advertise their products and brands to acquire and retain customers, forecast sales trends while overseeing their supply chains and ensuring appropriate inventory levels and placement, and so much more. While Amazon offers many powerful tools and services to assist with these tasks, we want to make it even easier for sellers to manage and grow their business.

[![Amazon app open on phone, showing Amazon's powerful AI curates your personalized shopping experience](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/80/24/75d83b634010bcba1de0e8a79034/aa-sep2024-aishoppingexp-featured-inline-v1-400kb-2550x1434-2.jpg)](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-generative-ai-seller-growth-shopping-experience)

[## Amazon sellers can now automatically improve product listings with our new Gen AI tool](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-generative-ai-seller-growth-shopping-experience)

Leveraging Gen AI learnings, Amazon is empowering sellers with new Enhance My Listing tool to make listing optimization effortless and effective.

Project Amelia provides sellers with an all-in-one, generative AI-based selling expert that is always available to immediately provide sellers with the answers, advice, and tools they need to succeed. Sellers simply ask Project Amelia a question, and they get a response with accurate information and guidance, allowing sellers to more easily and efficiently manage their business. Project Amelia is an always-available, expert partner to sellers, learning their unique businesses so it can offer personalized insights and support, and available from any page within Seller Central, at any time.

Project Amelia is built using [Amazon Bedrock](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/amazon-bedrock-ai-companies-productivity), which provides scalable access to the latest foundation models and AI tools that make it the most efficient way to build and scale generative AI applications. Additionally, Project Amelia is built using a combination of broad world knowledge that informs many generative AI solutions, coupled with deep expertise and specialized knowledge of selling on Amazon, giving it the unique ability to provide sellers with relevant, tailored responses designed to drive success selling in Amazon’s store. Over time, we will build on Project Amelia’s expertise to provide sellers with more personalized responses to even the most complex questions.

Starting today, Project Amelia can provide valuable responses to sellers’ questions, as well as offer fast access to critical business metrics and reports that are unique to each seller. We will continue to enhance the core, broad knowledgebase for Project Amelia and continue to build on its expertise to ensure it covers the specific domains we know matter most to sellers. As Amelia evolves, it will provide a more personalized experience and will increasingly gain the ability to not only converse with sellers, but anticipate their needs, take actions, and resolve issues on their behalf.

Project Amelia’s capabilities span three key areas:

Knowledge-based questions: Sellers can ask specific questions and receive relevant, summarized information learned from highly accurate and reliable sources on Seller Central and beyond, making it easy to quickly find what they need. Asked a question like, “What are the top things I need to do to prepare for the holiday season?” Project Amelia will quickly produce personalized information and best practices.

![Conversations with Amelia seller assistant on a mobile device.](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/8d/c5/5bdd5f544a219690302618b83315/aa-sept2024-sellingassistant-standard-inline-v1-1600x900.jpg)Example of the type of response Project Amelia will provide to help sellers grow their businesses.

Status updates and metrics: Sellers can quickly retrieve their sales data and customer traffic information, and gain visibility into critical aspects of their business by asking questions like, “How is my business doing?” Project Amelia will provide a summary of recent sales, units sold, and website traffic, and compare this data to the prior year. Sellers can also drill down into the results by asking additional questions like, “What about my cotton t-shirts?” Project Amelia will then offer an overview of that specific product’s sales, growth, customer traffic, and more.

![Conversations with Amelia seller assistant on a mobile device.](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/15/3f/4a4604fb4b3786b56d372f38eb54/aa-sept2024-sellingassistant-standard-inline-v2-1600x900.jpg)An example of the type of data and insights that Project Amelia already provides to help sellers easily manage their business.

Actions and issue resolution: Coming soon, Project Amelia will be able to offer straightforward resolution paths to complex issues and tasks by diagnosing problems and, in some cases, offering to take action on behalf of sellers. By simply asking Project Amelia for help with a task or resolving an issue—such as, “I have 300 units on the way and don’t see that reflected in the report. Can someone look into this?”— sellers will receive personalized guidance, and if needed, assistance investigating the issue or connecting the seller with support to ensure the problem is resolved as quickly as possible. In the future, Project Amelia will provide additional help managing the task or even offer to solve the problem on a seller’s behalf. By streamlining sellers’ operational demands and burdens, Project Amelia will reduce the time and effort required by sellers to manage their business, which they can reinvest in their growth.

![Conversations with Amelia seller assistant on a mobile device.](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/85/3f/bab4b95943018f748f9d71fe2ef9/aa-sept2024-sellingassistant-standard-inline-v3-1600x900.jpg)An example of the type of offer for assistance that Project Amelia will provide to help sellers resolve issues.

Project Amelia is available in beta starting today for an initial set of U.S. sellers, and will progressively roll out to additional U.S. sellers in the coming weeks. Later this year, Project Amelia will begin a phased rollout in additional countries and will start to become accessible in languages other than English.

We are always seeking to equip our selling partners with the most effective tools and capabilities, empowering them to more easily start and grow a successful business. By leveraging the transformative power of generative AI, we are creating and deploying technologies that will improve how sellers can manage and grow their businesses. Innovative solutions like Project Amelia are reducing the time, effort, and resources required from sellers to manage their business, allowing them more time for building great products and delighting customers.

[![Luxury watch on wrist gripping steering wheel at racetrack](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/0e/c1/8e6470924f2dbd59f6755735a77b/aa-062025-aiamazonads-standard-inline-v5-1600x900.gif)](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-ads-generative-ai-video-generator-advertisers)

Amazon Ads’ generative AI tools empower advertisers to elevate creativity, crafting ads that captivate customers.

This is only the beginning for Project Amelia. As sellers begin interacting with it, the technology will learn and evolve, leading to more comprehensive and personalized responses, with deeper insights and advice specific to sellers’ business needs. We are also continuously enhancing and refining Project Amelia with additional knowledge and capabilities, fulfilling a vision to make it an amazing selling assistant and trusted advisor that empowers sellers to thrive and drive even greater success in Amazon's store.

## Research Design and Approach

This study employed a multi-step, mixed-method research approach that integrates:

* Secondary research
* Primary research
* Data triangulation
* Hybrid top-down and bottom-up modelling
* Forecasting and scenario analysis

This approach ensures a balanced and validated understanding of both macro- and micro-level market factors influencing the market.

## Secondary Research

Secondary research for this study involved the collection, review, and analysis of publicly available and paid data sources to build the initial fact base, understand historical market behaviour, identify data gaps, and refine the hypotheses for primary research.

### Sources Consulted

Secondary data for the market study was gathered from multiple credible sources, including:

* Government databases, regulatory bodies, and public institutions
* International organizations (WHO, OECD, IMF, World Bank, etc.)
* Commercial and paid databases
* Industry associations, trade publications, and technical journals
* Company annual reports, investor presentations, press releases, and SEC filings
* Academic research papers, patents, and scientific literature
* Previous market research publications and syndicated reports

These sources were used to compile historical data, market volumes/prices, industry trends, technological developments, and competitive insights.

![Secondary Research](https://www.insightaceanalytic.com/images/Insightace-Data-Triangulation.webp "Secondary Research")

## Primary Research

Primary research was conducted to validate secondary data, understand real-time market dynamics, capture price points and adoption trends, and verify the assumptions used in the market modelling.

### Stakeholders Interviewed

Primary interviews for this study involved:

* Manufacturers and suppliers in the market value chain
* Distributors, channel partners, and integrators
* End-users / customers (e.g., hospitals, labs, enterprises, consumers, etc., depending on the market)
* Industry experts, technology specialists, consultants, and regulatory professionals
* Senior executives (CEOs, CTOs, VPs, Directors) and product managers

### Interview Process

Interviews were conducted via:

* Structured and semi-structured questionnaires
* Telephonic and video interactions
* Email correspondences
* Expert consultation sessions

Primary insights were incorporated into demand modelling, pricing analysis, technology evaluation, and market share estimation.

## Data Processing, Normalization, and Validation

All collected data were processed and normalized to ensure consistency and comparability across regions and time frames.

The data validation process included:

* Standardization of units (currency conversions, volume units, inflation adjustments)
* Cross-verification of data points across multiple secondary sources
* Normalization of inconsistent datasets
* Identification and resolution of data gaps
* Outlier detection and removal through algorithmic and manual checks
* Plausibility and coherence checks across segments and geographies

This ensured that the dataset used for modelling was clean, robust, and reliable.

## Market Size Estimation and Data Triangulation

### Bottom-Up Approach

The bottom-up approach involved aggregating segment-level data, such as:

* Company revenues
* Product-level sales
* Installed base/usage volumes
* Adoption and penetration rates
* Pricing analysis

This method was primarily used when detailed micro-level market data were available.

![Bottom Up Approach](https://www.insightaceanalytic.com/images/Bottomup-Top-Down-Together.webp "Bottom Up Approach")

### Top-Down Approach

The top-down approach used macro-level indicators:

* Parent market benchmarks
* Global/regional industry trends
* Economic indicators (GDP, demographics, spending patterns)
* Penetration and usage ratios

This approach was used for segments where granular data were limited or inconsistent.

### Hybrid Triangulation Approach

To ensure accuracy, a triangulated hybrid model was used. This included:

* Reconciling top-down and bottom-up estimates
* Cross-checking revenues, volumes, and pricing assumptions
* Incorporating expert insights to validate segment splits and adoption rates

This multi-angle validation yielded the final market size.

## Forecasting Framework and Scenario Modelling

Market forecasts were developed using a combination of time-series modelling, adoption curve analysis, and driver-based forecasting tools.

### Forecasting Methods

* Time-series modelling
* S-curve and diffusion models (for emerging technologies)
* Driver-based forecasting (GDP, disposable income, adoption rates, regulatory changes)
* Price elasticity models
* Market maturity and lifecycle-based projections

### Scenario Analysis

Given inherent uncertainties, three scenarios were constructed:

* **Base-Case Scenario:** Expected trajectory under current conditions
* **Optimistic Scenario:** High adoption, favourable regulation, strong economic tailwinds
* **Conservative Scenario:** Slow adoption, regulatory delays, economic constraints

Sensitivity testing was conducted on key variables, including pricing, demand elasticity, and regional adoption.

# AI in eCommerce Statistics (2025)

[SellersCommerce](https://www.sellerscommerce.com/author/sellerscommerce/)

July 31, 2026 

[Statistics](https://www.sellerscommerce.com/blog/category/statistics/)

7 min read

![Ai in eCommerce stats](https://www.sellerscommerce.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Ai-in-eCommerce-stats-1024x576.png)

Decades ago, shopping was mostly done at a few specialized stores. Then, shopping malls became popular, bringing a variety of stores together in one place. Next, online shopping took over, letting people buy anything from the comfort of their homes.

Now, we’re on the edge of another big change. As online shopping gets more competitive, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning are becoming crucial for retailers. These technologies are not just the latest trend—they’re essential for improving customer experiences, making operations more efficient, and changing how businesses operate.

The use of AI in e-commerce will be valued at $8.65 billion in 2025 and $17.1 billion by 2030.

Let’s explore how AI and machine learning are revolutionizing the e-commerce sector – all through up-to-date statistics.

## ****AI-enabled e-commerce market size****

The valuation of the global AI-enabled eCommerce market is $8.65 billion as of 2025. This market is further expected to reach $22.60 billion by 2032, driven by a compound annual growth rate of 14.60% from 2024 to 2032.

North America dominated the market and is likely to maintain its position during the forecast period, owing to its high budget allocations to artificial intelligence solutions in the government and public sector.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Year** | **AI-Enabled Ecommerce Market Size** |
| 2022 | $5.81 billion |
| 2023 | $6.63 billion |
| 2024 | $7.57 billion |
| 2025 | $8.65 billion |
| 2026 | $9.9 billion |
| 2027 | $11.33 billion |
| 2028 | $12.99 billion |
| 2029 | $14.9 billion |
| 2030 | $17.1 billion |
| 2031 | $19.65 billion |
| 2032 | $22.6 billion |

**Source:** [Precedence Research](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/artificial-intelligence-in-e-commerce-market).

## **Use of AI agents in ecommerce**

* 33% of ecommerce enterprises will include agentic AI by 2028. Today, less than 1% do so.
* Around 70% of consumers said they would use AI agents to purchase flights, and 65% would use them to book hotels and resorts.
* 93% of ecommerce businesses see AI agents as a competitive advantage.
* eCommerce retailers generate between 10% and 30% of their revenue from suggestive selling, in which agentic commerce engines can help a lot.

Source: In-house [report on AI agents](https://www.sellerscommerce.com/blog/ai-agents-statistics/).

## **AI Adoption in eCommerce Statistics**

33% of [B2B eCommerce](https://www.sellerscommerce.com/b2b-ecommerce-platform/) companies in the United States have fully implemented AI in their operations, while 47% say they are evaluating the technology.

On the other hand, 3% of B2B eCommerce organizations say they have no intention to use Artificial Intelligence.

The volume of businesses adopting AI has grown by 270% since 2019.

34% of Amazon sellers are using AI the most for writing and optimizing listings. Another 14% say they use the technology for creating marketing and social media content. 7% of Amazon sellers even use Artificial Intelligence for Keyword research and to improve SEO.

As per a Statista study, nearly half of the retail companies in the US are expected to use artificial intelligence (AI) for marketing. Chatbots and virtual shopping assistants are also popular, with 31.4% of respondents mentioning using them.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **AI use case in retail** | **Share of companies** |
| Marketing automation using AI | 48.90% |
| Virtual agents or chatbots | 31% |
| Data analytics using AI | 29% |
| Natural language processing | 21% |
| Text analytics using AI | 20% |
| Machine learning | 17% |
| Recommendation systems based on AI | 17% |
| Image/pattern recognition | 14% |
| Decision making systems based on AI | 13% |
| Speech/voice recognition using AI | 12% |

31% of senior executives in grocery retail think AI will mostly impact customer service in the sector. Another 22% believe it will improve supply chain processes, and 19% see it as important for managing inventory.

**Source:** [Statista](https://www.statista.com/topics/12261/artificial-intelligence-in-us-e-commerce/), [Exploding Topics](https://explodingtopics.com/blog/ai-statistics).

## **Challenges to AI Adoption among eCommerce Companies**

44% of CEOs said that data security and privacy were the biggest challenges in using AI-based solutions in their companies, 53% of managers and employees shared this concern.

Additionally, 43% of employees highlighted a lack of knowledge, understanding, or expertise in using AI tools as a major issue

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Challenges in AI adoption** | **CEOs** | **Manager and Employees** |
| Data security and privacy | 44% | 53% |
| Risk of costly AI-based recommendations and actions | 39% | 21% |
| Business case and ROI Justification | 39% | 26% |
| Fear of workforce impact | 33% | 21% |
| Lack of control/insight to the “AI” part of the solution | 28% | 32% |
| Lack of awareness, understanding, and/or expertise | 28% | 43% |
| Costs (financial, time, skills) | 28% | 34% |
| Unproven and/or unreliable Solutions | 22% | 28% |
| Bad experience with past implementations | 22% | 9% |
| Lack of infrastructure | 17% | 32% |

**Source:** [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1463707/ai-challenges-united-states/).

## ****Benefits of using AI for eCommerce companies****

Companies leveraging AI are seeing an average revenue increase of 10-12%, and the technology is projected to enhance profitability by 59% by 2035.

51% of company heads report that the performance of products improved after implementing AI in their operations. Another 35% say that the technology helps them make better decisions.

There has always been concern about AI taking over jobs, but many eCommerce decision-makers see it differently. About 36% believe that AI helps by handling routine tasks, which allows employees to focus on more creative work.

However, we can’t ignore the fact that AI can also lead to job reductions. Around 23% of companies use AI to cut down their workforce by automating tasks, showing that while AI can create opportunities for creativity, it can also lead to fewer jobs.

**Here is a table showing how businesses think AI has helped them after they started using it:**

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Enhance features, functions and/or performance of products | 51% |
| Make better decisions | 35% |
| Create new products | 32% |
| Optimize internal business operations | 36% |
| Free up workers to be more creative by automating tasks | 36% |
| Pursue new markets | 25% |
| Capture and apply scarce knowledge where needed | 25% |
| Optimize external processes like marketing and sales | 30% |
| Reduce headcount through automation | 23% |

## **AI in eCommerce Statistics by Demographics**

A survey among the United States shoppers found that only 74% of shoppers felt that artificial intelligence (AI) enhanced their shopping experience. Meanwhile, 6% said it made their experience worse, and 21% thought it didn’t change their experience at all.

9% of male and 10% of female US shoppers said that AI improved their shopping experience, while 13% of male and 15% of female shoppers said AI made their shopping experience worse.

22% of male and 20% of female US shoppers said their shopping experience stayed the same after AI usage.

## ****Ecommerce Chatbot Statistics****

* 80% of retail and ecommerce businesses use AI chatbots or plan to use them in the near future.
* Chatbots will be the main customer service tool for 25% of companies by 2027.
* AI is projected to handle 80% of all customer interactions by 2030.
* 24% of US consumers regularly use chatbots while shopping.
* 61% of U.S. consumers feel that chatbots save their time because they are available around the clock. Additionally, 45% of respondents value chatbots for providing immediate answers to their questions.

**Here is a table showing the main advantages of using e-commerce chatbots in the U.S. as per shoppers:**

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Advantage** | **Share of respondents** |
| It is available 24/7 | 61% |
| You get an immediate answer to your question | 45% |
| It gives product information and recommendations | 36% |
| It saves time | 35% |
| You get specific advice on what you are looking for | 21% |
| It offers proactive assistance | 21% |
| It gives access to detailed product information | 19% |
| No need to go to the store for advice | 18% |
| It avoids making mistakes in your purchases | 15% |
| It is able to speak in any language | 12% |
| It helps finding inspiration and good ideas | 9% |
| It helps to spend less | 8% |
| No benefits | 21% |

**Source:** [Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2022-07-27-gartner-predicts-chatbots-will-become-a-primary-customer-service-channel-within-five-years)

## ****AI usage in the ecommerce supply chain****

* About 90% of large companies have tried using AI in their supply chains, and 29% say they plan to invest a lot in this area over the next three years.

* The AI in the supply chain market is projected to reach $11.73 billion in 2025, up from $9.15 billion in 2024. The market will continue growing at a CAGR of 28.2% and reach $40.53 billion by 2030.

* AI-enabled supply chain planning increased revenue by up to 4%, reduced inventory by up to 20%, and lowered supply chain costs by up to 10%.

* 38% of businesses globally think AI adoption in the supply chain is critical, while 30% say they are ready for widespread adoption of the technology.

Source: [McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights/autonomous-supply-chain-planning-for-consumer-goods-companies), [Market.us](https://market.us/report/ai-in-supply-chain-market/), [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1346717/ai-function-adoption-rates-business-supply-chains/).

## **Statistics on AI-powered personalization in eCommerce**

* Approximately 71% of eCommerce sites offer product recommendations. The number is even higher in Nordic countries, where 90% of shoppers have reported finding personalized recommendations on eCommerce sites.
* 91% of consumers are more likely to shop with brands that provide personalized offers and recommendations.
* 80% of consumers are more likely to make a purchase when brands offer personalized experiences.
* 71% of consumers feel frustrated when their shopping experience is not personalized. 66% even say that they would stop purchasing from an eCommerce site when encountering impersonalized content.
* Product recommendations can increase revenue by up to 300%,  conversions can go up by 150%, and average order value can shoot up by 50%.

**Source:** [Grid Dynamics](https://www.griddynamics.com/), [Fresh Relevance](https://www.freshrelevance.com/blog/website-personalization-statistics/), [Statista](https://www.statista.com/), [Monetate](https://monetate.com/resources/).

## **AI technologies that People wish to see in eCommerce**

58% of Millennial consumers and over 40% of Gen X and Baby Boomer respondents expressed a desire for more personalized product recommendations in e-commerce.

51% of Millennial consumers and around 40% of Gen Z, Gen X, and Baby Boomer respondents expressed a desire for frictionless payment options in e-commerce.

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Innovation** | **Gen Z (18-24 years)** | **Millennials (25-40 years)** | **Gen X (41-56 years)** | **Baby Boomers (57-75 years)** |
| Personalized product recommendations | 44% | 58% | 41% | 41% |
| Frictionless payment | 39% | 51% | 43% | 42% |
| Personalized service | 39% | 58% | 40% | 31% |
| Seamless omnichannel experience | 35% | 53% | 25% | 16% |
| VR/AR | 29% | 46% | 28% | 14% |
| Voice assistants | 30% | 45% | 26% | 11% |

Artificial intelligence in payments had not yet gained significant traction among consumers in Western countries. A survey conducted across North America, Europe, and Latin America revealed a general discomfort with the concept. Only 10% of respondents indicated they might consider using AI in payments in a couple of years (after 2025).

The survey identified two main reasons for this hesitation — a lack of awareness and security concerns.

## Key Definitions

- **GMV**: Total dollar value of all orders processed through Shopify's platform, including product costs, taxes, shipping, and fees, reported before deducting returns, refunds, or platform costs.
- **GMV vs. Revenue**: GMV measures total merchant sales volume ($292.3B in 2024), while Shopify's revenue ($8.88B) represents platform earnings (subscription and transaction fees). Shopify's take rate is approximately **3.04%** of GMV.

| Year | Annual GMV | YoY Growth |
|------|-----------|------------|

| 2023 | $235.9B | ~20% |
| 2024 | $292.3B | +24% |

**2024 Quarterly Progression**: Q1 $60.9B → Q2 $67.2B → Q3 $69.7B → Q4 $94.5B (+26% YoY). Black Friday-Cyber Monday 2024 generated $11.5B in GMV alone.

## Growth Drivers

- **Merchant base**: Over 2 million active merchants globally, including 47,000 on Shopify Plus
- **International expansion**: 33% international GMV growth in Q4 2024, particularly in Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America

--- SOURCE 1: Shopify Reports Impressive Q2 2025 Results with 31% Revenue Growth and Strong Cash Flow ---
URL: https://praella.com/da/blogs/shopify-news/shopify-reports-impressive-q2-2025-results-with-31-revenue-growth-and-strong-cash-flow

SUMMARY:
<summary>
Shopify Inc. (NASDAQ, TSX: SHOP) reported its Q2 2025 financial results, showcasing significant growth. The company achieved $2.68 billion in revenue, a 31% increase year-over-year, beating last year's 21% growth rate and outpacing expectations. Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) reached $87.8 billion, up from $67.2 billion in Q2 2024, with particularly strong growth in Europe at 42% on a constant currency basis.

Key financial metrics for Q2 2025 include:
- Gross profit of $1.30 billion (up from $1.05 billion)
- Operating income of $291 million (up from $241 million)
- Free cash flow of $422 million with a 16% free cash flow margin, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit margins
- Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) of $185 million (up from $169 million)

Guidance for Q3 2025: Shopify projects revenue growth in the mid-to-high twenties percentage range, with gross profit dollars expected to increase at a low-twenties percentage rate. Operating expenses are forecast at 38-39% of revenue, and stock-based compensation is expected to reach $130 million in Q3.

Leadership insights: President Harley Finkelstein stated, "Today's results are the payoff from bold bets we made years ago. The investments we're making now will fuel our next chapter." CFO Jeff Hoffmeister noted accelerated GMV and revenue growth rates across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, emphasizing that merchants of all sizes are increasingly choosing Shopify.

The company's success is attributed to geographic diversification, strategic investments in innovation (including AI and machine learning), localized marketing strategies, and enhanced platform capabilities. Challenges ahead include tightening margins from rising operating expenses, fierce competitive pressure in e-commerce, and external risks such as economic uncertainty and potential regulatory changes.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 7: Amazon Third-Party Sellers in 2025: What the Official Q3 & Q4 Data Really Tells Us | AmzMonitor ---
URL: https://amzmonitor.com/blogs/amazon-third-party-sellers-2025-q3-q4-data-analysis

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article, published by AmzMonitor on March 29, 2026, analyzes Amazon's official Q3 and Q4 2025 earnings reports as they relate to third-party (3P) sellers.

KEY DATA POINTS:
- Amazon closed 2025 with $716.9 billion in total net sales, up 12% year-over-year.
- Third-party seller services generated $175.2 billion for the full year ($42.5B in Q3, $52.8B in Q4 — a ~24% quarter-over-quarter surge due to seasonal holiday demand).
- Third-party sellers accounted for 62% (Q3) and 61% (Q4) of all paid units sold ("WW seller unit mix"), while Amazon's first-party business accounts for less than 40% of units moved.
- Advertising: grew 22% YoY in both quarters; Q3 was $17.7B, Q4 was $21.3B (up ~20% QoQ), with annualized ad business approaching $70 billion. Amazon's ad network now extends to Netflix, Spotify, and other platforms.
- Worldwide shipping costs: $25.4B (Q3) to $31.5B (Q4), up ~24% QoQ.
- Over 1.3 million independent sellers are actively using AI-powered tools to create product listings. Amazon's AI shopping assistant Rufus was used by 250 million customers in 2025.
- International segment grew 17% YoY in Q4 2025, reaching $50.7 billion in a single quarter; full-year international revenue hit $161.9 billion (up 13%), with a full-year operating profit of $4.75 billion.

FULL-YEAR 2025 REVENUE BREAKDOWN:
- Online stores (1P product sales): $269B
- Third-party seller services: $175B
- Advertising: $68B
- AWS: $129B
- Subscription services: $50B
- Physical stores: $22B
- Note: 3P seller services + advertising together total roughly $243 billion — more than Amazon's own product sales and more than AWS.

MAIN ARGUMENTS AND TAKEAWAYS:
1. Independent sellers are structurally dominant on Amazon — the platform would collapse without them, giving Amazon a strong incentive to maintain a healthy seller ecosystem.
2. Advertising is no longer optional; the shift toward a pay-to-play model (like Google Shopping/Facebook) means sellers must treat Amazon PPC as a core part of their business.
3. AI is raising the baseline quality of listings; 1.3 million sellers using AI means mediocre listings now compete against AI-optimized copy.
4. Q4 planning lessons: FBA lead times lengthen in Q4 (ship inventory in September), ad budgets need Q4 headroom (CPCs rise), and the Q3-to-Q4 transition is the most important operational moment of the year.
5. International markets (Germany, UK, Japan, India) offer underrated opportunities with lower competition than the US.
6. What Amazon's reports DON'T show: no data on seller profitability, average seller revenue, or attrition rates — the aggregate numbers don't guarantee individual seller success.
7. Conclusion: Amazon remains a powerful channel for sellers with strong margins, differentiated products, and operational capacity; but it's harder for those with thin margins, commoditized products, and reliance on organic rank alone.

The article is published by AmzMonitor, which offers Amazon product/competitor/keyword monitoring tools, alerts, and a 14-day free trial.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 9: Amazon 2025 Commerce Earnings - Ads, Subscription, Physical Retail, Rufus ---
URL: https://thesilkroadnexus.substack.com/p/amazon-2025-commerce-earnings-ads

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This analysis of Amazon's Q4 2025 earnings, written by Nikhil Varshney, focuses on the commerce business rather than AWS or AI infrastructure. Although Amazon's stock fell nearly 9% after hours due to $200 billion in planned 2026 capital expenditures (mostly AWS/AI), the author highlights four key commerce drivers: advertising, subscriptions, physical retail, and Rufus (agentic commerce).

Key financial figures: Amazon generated $213.4 billion in total Q4 revenue, with $177.8 billion from commerce. The combined Stores segments generated $34.3 billion in operating income vs. AWS's $45.6 billion. North America operating income was $11.5 billion in Q4 (up 24%, margin expanding to 9.0% from 8.0%), while international operating income declined 21% to $1.0 billion (45% lower on FX-adjusted basis) due to intentional investments in "sharper prices" and quick commerce.

1. ADVERTISING: Q4 ad revenue grew 23% YoY to $21.2B (full year $68.9B), exceeding YouTube's $40B. Ads sit at the point of purchase with margins estimated at 50-70%. This creates a "double-extraction model" — Amazon earns referral fees plus advertising fees from 3P sellers.

2. SUBSCRIPTIONS: Prime grew 14% to $13B in Q4 (~$50B full year). New additions include Alexa+ (free for Prime members, but the author calls Alexa "the world's most expensive weather telling and timer setting machine"), expanded grocery delivery, and NBA on Prime Video.

3. PHYSICAL RETAIL: Stores revenue was $5.9B, with the story being the closure of Go and Fresh stores and consolidation around Whole Foods. Amazon will open a mega center to compete with Walmart, and is expanding to 1,000 same-day grocery delivery locations (2,300 by year's end). The author argues grocery provides frequent, habitual engagement and operational synergies via last-mile economies of scale.

4. RUFUS: Used by over 300 million customers in 2025, driving nearly $12 billion in incremental annualized sales (up from $10 billion). Customers using Rufus are 60% more likely to complete a purchase. The "Buy For Me" capability allows Rufus to shop and purchase items from other online stores, turning Amazon into a universal purchasing agent. Amazon's walled-garden approach to product data and cross-sell advantages give it an edge over competitors. Amazon Lens usage grew 45% YoY, and Amazon Haul (1 million+ items under $10, in 25+ countries) competes with Temu and SHEIN.

3P BUSINESS: Third-party sellers accounted for 61% of all paid units sold (just off the all-time high of 62%). The author argues the shift to 3P is misunderstood — when a 3P seller uses FBA, Amazon earns referral commissions (8-15%), FBA fees, advertising spend, and storage fees, making the total take rate 40-50% vs. low single digits on 1P sales. Over 1.3 million independent sellers use Amazon's generative AI tools. Amazon's Multi-Channel Fulfillment (MCF) lets sellers fulfill orders from Walmart, Shopify, and SHEIN, turning Amazon's logistics into an "arms-dealer service."

PROFITABILITY LOOP: Amazon achieved operating leverage — Q4 shipping costs grew 10% ($31.5B) vs. 12% paid unit growth, marking three consecutive years of this pattern. The adjusted North America margin is approaching double digits, driven by mix shift toward high-margin 3P/advertising, cost reduction, and fulfillment network density.

Key risks and future outlook: The Q1 2026 guidance of $16.5-21.5B operating income spooked markets but includes $1 billion in Amazon Leo (satellite) costs. Grocery strategy is entering its decisive phase, Rufus/agentic commerce represents a paradigm shift, international is the biggest wildcard, and tariff risk (especially for Amazon Haul's Chinese-sourced goods) is a material uncertainty.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
**Amazon.com, Inc. Second Quarter Results (announced July 30, 2026)**

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) announced financial results for Q2 ended June 30, 2026, showing strong growth across all segments.

**Key Financial Highlights:**
- **Net sales** increased 20% year-over-year to $200.6 billion (vs. $167.7 billion in Q2 2025), excluding a $0.1 billion favorable FX impact.
  - North America segment: $116.2 billion (+16% Y/Y)
  - International segment: $42.2 billion (+15% Y/Y)
  - AWS segment: $42.2 billion (+37% Y/Y) — fastest growth in 18 quarters, reaching a $169 billion annualized revenue run rate
- **Operating income** increased to $27.5 billion (up 43% from $19.2 billion in Q2 2025), with segment operating income of: North America $9.1B, International $1.7B, AWS $16.6B
- **Net income** increased to $62.6 billion ($5.75 per diluted share) vs. $18.2 billion ($1.68 per diluted share) in Q2 2025. Q2 2026 net income includes non-operating pre-tax other income of $53.4 billion primarily from investments in Anthropic.
- **Operating cash flow** increased 33% to $161.4 billion for trailing twelve months (TTM)
- **Free cash flow** decreased to an outflow of $7.6 billion TTM, driven primarily by a $66.1 billion increase in purchases of property and equipment (reflecting AI investments), vs. inflow of $18.2 billion TTM ended June 30, 2025.

**Q3 2026 Guidance:**

* Deeper **design customization** requires coding knowledge. Merchants without a developer on hand say they can't easily build unique storefronts.[(6 reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/bigcommerce/reviews?filters%5Bsentiment_snippet%5D=1345117&qs=pros-and-cons#reviews)

## [Expert Analysis: BigCommerce Growth Trends & Key Signals for Sales Teams in 2026](#expert-signals)

![Mehmet Suleyman](/images/team/mehmet-suleyman-ceo.jpg)

[Mehmet Suleyman](/authors/mehmet-suleyman)CEO & Co-founder, TechnologyChecker

With 10+ years in web crawling and technographic data analysis, I've examined BigCommerce's position in the ecommerce platform market using data from **7,073 enriched companies** matched against LinkedIn profiles, combined with historical detection data spanning 14+ years. This analysis draws on our crawl of 50M+ domains and 40K+ tracked technologies to provide actionable sales intelligence.

### 1. Growth Trajectory

BigCommerce first appeared in our crawl data in **January 2011 with 30 active domains**, roughly two years after its 2009 founding in Sydney. The platform grew steadily to **11,675 active domains by March 2025**. A 389x increase over 14 years. Unlike Shopify's explosive growth curve, BigCommerce's trajectory has been gradual and linear, averaging about 800 new active domains per year.

The 2020-2021 period saw modest acceleration coinciding with BigCommerce's August 2020 IPO on Nasdaq. Since March 2025, active domains have dipped slightly to 11,010 by July 2025, though this is consistent with seasonal patterns we see across ecommerce platforms.

**Sales Signal:** BigCommerce's steady but slow growth suggests a mature platform with loyal merchants rather than a viral acquisition engine. Sales teams targeting BigCommerce merchants should position around stability and feature depth. The slight plateau signals merchants who stay are committed. They don't churn quickly.

### 2. Customer Profile

BigCommerce skews heavily toward micro-businesses: **73.2% of customers have 1-10 employees**, with another 18.6% in the 11-50 range. That's 91.8% small business. But the enterprise tail is real. AMD, Pearson, National Grid, and Gildan Activewear all run BigCommerce stores with 10,000+ employees.

The age distribution tells a different story than most ecommerce platforms. **Only 6.5% of BigCommerce customers were founded in the 2020s**, compared to 31.78% in the 2010s and 24.65% in the 2000s. Nearly **57% of customers are companies founded before 2010**. These are mature organizations, not startups.

**Sales Signal:** The established-company profile means BigCommerce merchants have existing revenue, operational complexity, and budget for tools. Target companies founded 2000-2019 with 1-50 employees. They're the core segment and likely have decision-making authority concentrated in the founder or a small leadership team.

### 3. Industry & Geographic Concentration

Retail at **19.59%** is BigCommerce's core vertical, nearly 1 in 5 customers. Manufacturing (4.39%) and Wholesale (4.35%) together add another 8.7%. BigCommerce is one of the more B2B-friendly ecommerce platforms. Sporting Goods Manufacturing at 2.92% and Motor Vehicle Manufacturing at 1.85% highlight a physical-product focus.

Geographically, BigCommerce is overwhelmingly English-speaking: **the US accounts for 74.5%** of enriched customers, followed by the UK (9.0%) and Australia (7.9%). Together, English-speaking markets represent over **95%** of the customer base. Brazil at 1.9% is the only non-English market in the top 5.

**Sales Signal:** The manufacturing and wholesale concentration is BigCommerce's differentiation. Companies selling B2B through BigCommerce need ERP integrations, custom pricing, and catalog management tools, high-value services. The Australian presence (7.9%) likely reflects the platform's Sydney founding; partners and agencies in ANZ have a natural advantage.

### 4. Migration Patterns

Migration data reveals BigCommerce's biggest strategic challenge. **2,976 companies** left BigCommerce for Shopify. A **7.6:1 loss ratio** against only 393 companies moving in the opposite direction. This is one of the most lopsided migration patterns in our ecommerce dataset.

The bright spot: BigCommerce gained **620 companies from Magento** while losing only 122, a **5.1:1 gain ratio**. WooCommerce migration is closer to balanced at 0.76:1 (683 gained, 898 lost). BigCommerce has become the natural upgrade path from self-hosted platforms, even as it loses ground to Shopify.

**Sales Signal:** Two opportunities exist. First, Magento merchants actively migrating represent warm leads, 620 have already made the switch. Target Magento agencies and system integrators for referral partnerships. Second, the Shopify outflow creates a retention market, BigCommerce merchants considering Shopify need compelling reasons to stay, particularly around B2B features and transaction fee savings.

### 5. Technology Ecosystem

**Google Analytics at 72.74%** is nearly universal among BigCommerce merchants. **Facebook Pixel (47.71%)** shows almost half run paid social advertising. In email marketing, **MailChimp leads at 24.93%** with Klaviyo at 15.33%, the Klaviyo adoption rate suggests an ecommerce-savvy merchant base willing to pay for specialized tools.

[LiveChat](/technology/livechat) (4.24%) leads support tools, followed by [Tawk.to](/technology/tawk-to) (2.66%) and [Tidio](/technology/tidio) (2.43%). [Gorgias](/technology/gorgias) at 1.63% is an ecommerce-specific helpdesk, a sign of merchant sophistication. The low live chat adoption overall (under 5%) suggests most BigCommerce stores handle support through email or phone.

**Sales Signal:** The 85% of BigCommerce merchants without Klaviyo represent an upsell opportunity for ecommerce email marketing. The low live chat adoption (under 5% for any single tool) signals a gap, chat and conversational commerce tools have room to grow in this merchant base.

### G2 Review Signals for Buyers

The G2 data adds a buyer-perspective layer to our technographic analysis. Across **143 review mentions**, BigCommerce scores highest for **ease of use** (41 mentions). Where it falls short: **pricing** (10 mentions). If you're in a sales conversation about BigCommerce, users who stick with BigCommerce do so because of ease of use; be prepared to address concerns about pricing in any evaluation.

### 6. Key Takeaways

BigCommerce occupies a defined niche: **established small businesses in retail, manufacturing, and wholesale**, predominantly in the US, UK, and Australia. It's not competing with Shopify for DTC startups. It's competing with Magento for B2B-capable hosted commerce. The 5.1:1 gain ratio from Magento validates this positioning. The platform's challenge is the persistent Shopify migration at 7.6:1 loss ratio, which suggests merchants seeking simplicity and ecosystem breadth choose Shopify over BigCommerce's feature depth.

### 7. Sales Applications

**Prospecting template:** "We analyzed {company}'s BigCommerce store and noticed you're in the {industry} vertical, one of BigCommerce's core segments. Our data shows {specific insight, e.g., '4.39% of BigCommerce merchants are in Manufacturing'}. We help companies like yours with {specific service}."

**Targeting strategy on TechnologyChecker.io:** Filter for BigCommerce + no Klaviyo to find merchants with basic email marketing setups ready for an upgrade. Filter for BigCommerce + Manufacturing/Wholesale industries to find B2B merchants needing ERP and catalog tools.

**Competitive angle:** Monitor Magento merchants (our data shows 620 already switched to BigCommerce), these are companies actively evaluating hosted alternatives. Position your services as part of the migration package.
