**Pricing overview (US):**
- **Starter:** $5/month - for social selling and influencers; no standalone store; 5% transaction fee on Shopify Payments
- **Basic:** $39/month (annual) or $49 monthly - entry tier for new stores; 2.9% + 30c online card rate
- **Grow:** $105/month (annual) or $135 monthly - for scaling businesses; 2.7% + 30c card rate; adds professional reporting, Shopify Flow, 5 staff accounts
- **Advanced:** $399/month (annual) or $525 monthly - for established merchants; 2.5% + 30c card rate; custom reports, calculated shipping, 15 staff accounts
- **Plus:** From $2,300/month (1- or 3-year term) - enterprise tier; negotiated rates typically 2.15-2.25% + 30c; checkout customization, Shopify Scripts, up to 9 expansion stores, 200 POS locations, B2B features

- Annual billing saves 25% on Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans
- New merchants get first 3 months for $1/month on Basic, Grow, Advanced

## How much does Shopify Plus cost in 2026?

Shopify Plus costs from $2,300 per month on a 3-year term, or $2,500 per month on a 1-year term, for standard setups and integrations.

Higher-volume businesses with more complex structures switch to a variable platform fee based on revenue and business model. Shopify does not publish the exact variable percentage or threshold and directs merchants to its sales team.

The widely cited figures of a 0.25% to 0.40% revenue share above roughly $800,000 in monthly sales come from agency blogs, not Shopify. Treat them as directional.

## Shopify Plus pricing: the full cost model

The Shopify Plus monthly fee is one line item. Three more drive your true cost: transaction fees, extra stores, and any custom development.

**Base platform fee.** From $2,300 per month (3-year term) or $2,500 per month (1-year term).

**Transaction fees.** With Shopify Payments, Plus carries the lowest card rates of any plan, from 2.25% + 30¢ online, and third-party transaction fees are waived globally. If you use an outside payment gateway, you pay your processor plus 0.20% per transaction to Shopify ([Shopify Plus](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing)).

**Extra stores.** Your main store plus 9 expansion stores are included. Additional stores cost $300 per month each, or a revenue share across all stores ([Shopify Plus](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing)).

**Custom development and apps.** Shopify lists no other mandatory fees. Optional costs are one-time themes, third-party apps, and Shopify Plus Partner development ([Shopify Plus](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing)).

## Shopify payment plans compared: where Plus sits

Shopify Plus is the top tier, above Basic, Grow, and Advanced. The table below uses current published figures.

| Plan | Monthly price | Shopify Payments card rate (online) | Staff accounts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $19 | from 2.9% + 30¢ | limited |
| Grow (formerly Shopify) | $54 | from 2.7% + 30¢ | up to 5 |
| Advanced | $299 | from 2.5% + 30¢ | up to 15 |
| Plus | from $2,300 | from 2.25% + 30¢ | unlimited |

Source: [Shopify pricing](https://www.shopify.com/pricing) and [Shopify Plus pricing](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing), accessed June 23, 2026.

The jump that matters is Advanced to Plus. The monthly fee rises from $299 to $2,300, so the lower card rate and Plus-only features have to earn back roughly $2,000 per month.

## What you get on Plus that you do not get on Advanced

Shopify reserves a specific feature set for Plus. These are the deltas that justify the price for the right store.

**B2B on Shopify.** Run wholesale and DTC from one back office. Company accounts, custom price lists, and payment terms are built in, replacing third-party wholesale apps.

**Checkout customizations.** Plus opens up Shopify’s checkout through Checkout Extensibility, the framework that replaced the deprecated checkout.liquid file. You add custom fields, upsells, and branding without editing checkout code.

**Shopify Functions.** Write custom back-end logic for discounts, shipping, and cart rules, deployed as apps rather than legacy scripts.

**Headless commerce.** Build a custom front end on Shopify’s APIs, or deploy a React-based headless stack at no extra cost.

**Managed Markets.** A localization suite for cross-border selling: duties, taxes, and currency handling across markets.

**Other Plus inclusions.** Shopify POS Pro, Shopify Audiences, ShopifyQL Notebooks, unlimited staff accounts, and higher API limits round out the tier.

## Is Shopify Plus worth it? The revenue thresholds

Shopify Plus makes financial sense once your savings and feature needs clear the roughly $2,000 monthly gap over Advanced. Use these signals, not a single revenue number.

**You likely justify Plus when:**

1. Transaction-fee savings are material. At high GMV, moving from a 2.5% to a 2.25% card rate recovers real money each month.
2. You need a built-in B2B. A wholesale channel on Plus removes a $200 to $500 per month app, plus its maintenance.
3. You run multiple storefronts. Four or more regional or brand stores get cheaper to manage under one Plus contract than as separate Advanced stores.
4. You run flash sales or drops. Load-tested checkout handles 10,000+ checkouts per minute ([Shopify Plus](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing)).

**Advanced is still enough when:**

1. You operate one store with no expansion plans.
2. Your current checkout converts well and needs no customization.
3. Your wholesale volume is light, and a third-party app covers it.

A common rule of thumb puts the break-even point near $5M in annual revenue once fee savings and removed apps are counted.

## The hidden and variable costs to plan for

The base fee understates the real bill. Four variable costs decide your total.

### The variable platform fee

Past a high revenue level, Shopify replaces the flat fee with a variable fee that is revenue-based and set per contract. You cannot model this from public data, so request the terms before you commit.

### Payment processing fees

Outside gateways add 0.20% per transaction cost on top of your processor’s fees. At scale, staying on Shopify Payments usually costs less ([Shopify Plus](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing)).

### Expansion stores

Each store beyond the included ten adds $300 per month ([Shopify Plus](https://www.shopify.com/plus/pricing)).

### Development and apps

Headless builds, checkout extensions, and integrations carry agency or in-house engineering costs. Budget for a Shopify Plus Partner if you customize heavily.

## How migrating to Shopify Plus works

Shopify does not charge a platform fee to migrate to Plus, though paid services are available for custom needs.

Your existing store upgrades in place. Products, orders, customers, and most apps carry over, and you gain Plus-only features once provisioning completes. Migration responsibility sits with you, and a Shopify representative can scope the work.

**What to review after upgrading:**

1. Wholesale apps: native B2B may replace them.
2. Checkout customizations built on legacy checkout.liquid: rebuild them on Checkout Extensibility ([checkout.liquid docs](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture/layouts/checkout-liquid)).
3. Analytics and script-based tools: confirm they support the current checkout framework.

## When Shopify Plus is the wrong move

Shopify Plus is a poor fit for some stores, even profitable ones. Skip it in these cases.

* Revenue is low, and fee savings stay below the $2,000 monthly premium over Advanced.
* One store, no multi-brand or B2B plans, and a checkout you do not intend to customize.
* A working third-party wholesale setup that costs less than Plus adds.

In each case, the money is better spent on conversion levers you can run today on any plan.

## The conversion lever you do not need Plus to pull

An AI sales agent runs the same on Advanced as on Plus, so you can raise revenue per visitor before committing to a $2,300 monthly platform fee. That matters because Plus often gets justified by revenue you have not captured yet.

[Zipchat](zipchat.ai) acts as a revenue engine across both tiers: it answers product questions, recommends products in chat, and recovers carts on website chat and WhatsApp. The same setup carries into Plus, including multi-store, headless, and B2B configurations, from one knowledge base.

Cricket-Hockey manages 21,000 SKUs, including B2B distributor accounts, with one AI system serving wholesale and DTC questions ([Cricket-Hockey story](https://www.zipchat.ai/success-stories/cricket-hockey)). For setup options, see the [AI chatbot for Shopify guide](https://www.zipchat.ai/blog/ai-chatbot-for-shopify) and tactics in [how to increase average order value](https://www.zipchat.ai/blog/increase-average-order-value).

## Where Shopify Plus is heading in 2026

Shopify is pushing Plus deeper into B2B, headless, and AI-assisted checkout, while Commerce Components sits above Plus for modular enterprise builds.

Checkout Extensibility is now the only supported path for checkout customization, so app ecosystems are consolidating around it. Expect more B2B portal depth and tighter AI features at checkout through 2026 to 2027.

For [agentic commerce](https://www.zipchat.ai/blog/agentic-commerce-2026-guide), AI agents will handle more of the B2B loop, from inquiry and quote to approval and order, where Plus merchants run the most complex workflows.

## FAQ

### How much is Shopify Plus per month in 2026?

From $2,300 per month on a 3-year term, or $2,500 per month on a 1-year term, for standard setups. High-volume stores move to a variable platform fee instead.

### What are Shopify Plus transaction fees?

With Shopify Payments, online credit card processing rates start at 2.25% + 30¢, and third-party transaction fees are waived. Using an outside gateway adds 0.20% per transaction to Shopify.

### Shopify Plus vs Advanced: what is the difference?

Advanced costs $299 per month; Plus starts at $2,300. Plus adds built-in B2B, Checkout Extensibility, Shopify Functions, headless tools, multi-store, and unlimited staff.

### What are the requirements for Shopify Plus?

Shopify sets no public revenue minimum. Most stores adopt Plus for transaction-fee savings, native B2B, multi-store, or checkout customization, typically past mid-seven-figure revenue.

### Does migrating to Shopify Plus cost extra?

Shopify charges no platform fee to migrate, but optional paid services exist for custom work. The store upgrades in place with data and apps carried over.

## Bottom line

Price Shopify Plus on the total cost, not the sticker fee. Add the $2,300 base, your real transaction-fee savings, extra-store fees, and development, then compare that to what Advanced costs you today.

If the math is close, raise revenue per visitor first with an AI sales agent that runs on any standard Shopify plan, then upgrade once Plus clearly pays for itself.

# Shopify Pricing (2026): Plans, Fees & Real Cost Breakdown

Most brands that ask "How much does Shopify cost?" are asking the wrong question.

They land on the pricing page. They see $39/month for Basic or $2,300/month for Plus and start comparing. But "what they pay today" on Magento or Shopware is never a single number. It's scattered across hosting invoices, DevOps salaries, agency retainers, emergency patches at 2am on a Saturday, and that one Black Friday when the site went down for six hours. And then there are the costs that never get a price tag: the content team afraid to touch the system without a developer, the campaign that launched a week late because the sprint was full, the features that stayed in the backlog because shipping anything new felt like a risk.

The better question is: what is my total cost of ownership today, and how does it compare to what I would actually spend on Shopify?

We walk through why brands migrate to Shopify, the fears that hold them back, what every plan actually costs with real example calculations, the hidden costs most self-hosted platforms bury in your P&L, and when Shopify is not the right choice. By the end, you should be able to build a defensible TCO case for your CFO, or rule Shopify out for the right reasons.

## Contents

[1.How Much Does Shopify Cost in 2026?](/insights/shopify-pricing#How%20Much%20Does%20Shopify%20Cost%20in%202026?)[2.Shopify Pricing Plans: Tier-by-Tier Breakdown](/insights/shopify-pricing#Shopify%20Pricing%20Plans:%20Tier-by-Tier%20Breakdown)[3.What You Actually Get at Each Tier](/insights/shopify-pricing#What%20You%20Actually%20Get%20at%20Each%20Tier)[4.Shopify Fees Explained: Transaction Fees, Payment Processing & Surcharges](/insights/shopify-pricing#Shopify%20Fees%20Explained:%20Transaction%20Fees,%20Payment%20Processing%20&%20Surcharges)[5.Shopify POS Pricing: In-Store Selling Costs](/insights/shopify-pricing#Shopify%20POS%20Pricing:%20In-Store%20Selling%20Costs)[6.When should you evaluate Shopify Plus?](/insights/shopify-pricing#When%20should%20you%20evaluate%20Shopify%20Plus?)[7.Costs most brands overlook when budgeting for Shopify](/insights/shopify-pricing#Costs%20most%20brands%20overlook%20when%20budgeting%20for%20Shopify)[8.Why brands migrate to Shopify](/insights/shopify-pricing#Why%20brands%20migrate%20to%20Shopify)[9.Common objections to migrating to Shopify](/insights/shopify-pricing#Common%20objections%20to%20migrating%20to%20Shopify)[10.Hidden costs of staying on a self-hosted platform](/insights/shopify-pricing#Hidden%20costs%20of%20staying%20on%20a%20self-hosted%20platform)[11.When Shopify might not be the right move](/insights/shopify-pricing#When%20Shopify%20might%20not%20be%20the%20right%20move)[12.Shopify Pricing FAQ](/insights/shopify-pricing#Shopify%20Pricing%20FAQ)

Written by

[![Simon avatar](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7)

Simon Wesierski

Co-founder at Commerce-UI, a Shopify Plus Agency](https://www.linkedin.com/in/simonwesierski/)

## How Much Does Shopify Cost in 2026?

The short answer: $5 to $2,300+ per month depending on your plan, plus transaction fees on every sale. The real answer depends on your revenue, your team size, whether you sell internationally, and whether you need B2B or checkout customization.

Here's the tier overview:

| Plan | Monthly | Annual (/mo.) | Online CC Rate | 3rd-Party Fee | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Starter | $5 | - | 5% | - | Creators |
| Basic | $39 | $29 | 2.9% + 30c | 2.0% | New stores |
| Grow | $105 | $79 | 2.7% + 30c | 1.0% | Growing brands |
| Advanced | $399 | $299 | 2.5% + 30c | 0.6% | Scaling brands |
| Plus | $2,300 on 3-year, $2,500 on 1-year | Negotiable | ~2.15% + 30c | 0.20% | Mid-market & Enterprise |

## Shopify Pricing Plans: Tier-by-Tier Breakdown

### Starter: $5/month

This is not really a "store." It is a checkout link you can share on Instagram, TikTok, or WhatsApp. No full storefront, no theme customization, no real analytics. The transaction fee is 5%, which adds up fast.

Good for creators testing a product idea or someone selling merch through a link-in-bio. Not relevant for any brand seriously evaluating Shopify as a platform.

### Basic: $39/month ($29/month on annual billing)

This is where Shopify becomes a real store. You get a full online storefront with themes, a blog, product management, and 24/7 support. The catch: no staff accounts. Only the store owner can access the admin. If you have even one team member who needs backend access, you are already looking at the next tier.

Credit card rates are 2.9% + 30c per online transaction through Shopify Payments. Use a third-party payment gateway instead, and Shopify adds an extra 2.0% on top of whatever your gateway charges. You also do not get real-time carrier-calculated shipping rates. That is an Advanced feature.

Best for: Solo founders or very early-stage D2C brands doing under $50K/month.

> Back-of-napkin math: At $30K/month in revenue, you are looking at $39 in subscription fees + roughly $900 in credit card processing = about $939/month total. That is your entire platform cost.

### Grow: $105/month ($79/month annual)

This is the plan most growing brands land on. You get 5 staff accounts, professional reports that actually tell you something useful, multi-market selling support, and up to 88% shipping discounts. Credit card rates drop to 2.7% + 30c, and the third-party gateway surcharge falls to 1.0%.

The jump from Basic to Grow is really about team access and data. The moment you have a marketing person, a fulfillment lead, or a co-founder who needs to log in, Basic does not cut it.

Best for: Brands doing $50K to $200K/month with a small team.

> At $150K/month: $105 subscription + ~$4,080 in CC fees = ~$4,185/month.

### Advanced: $399/month ($299/month annual)

Advanced is for brands that sell internationally or need serious reporting. You get 15 staff accounts, custom report builders, third-party calculated shipping rates (finally), and automatic duties and import tax calculation. The checkout can handle 10x the capacity of Basic/Grow, which matters if you run flash sales or have seasonal spikes.

This tier also gives you up to 3 markets included (scalable to 50) and 10 inventory locations. Credit card rates are 2.5% + 30c, and the third-party gateway fee drops to 0.6%.

Best for: Brands doing $200K to $800K/month, especially if you ship internationally.

> At $500K/month: $399 subscription + ~$12,800 in CC fees = ~$13,199/month total. Sounds like a lot until you compare it to the self-hosted alternative.

### Shopify Plus: $2,300-$2,500

Plus is where Shopify gets serious for bigger brands. The pricing structure is different: $2,300/month on a 3-year term ($2,500 on a 1-year term) as a floor, but once you cross roughly $800K/month in GMV, it switches to 0.35% of revenue, capped at $40,000/month.

What you get for that: full checkout customization through Checkout Extensibility (this is Plus-only, there is no way to customize the checkout on lower tiers), up to 10 expansion stores for different countries or brands, unlimited staff accounts, Shopify Flow for automation, a native B2B wholesale channel, dedicated support, and Shopify Audiences for ad targeting. Checkout capacity is 40x standard plans.For brands considering a headless architecture on Plus, the framework choice matters. We compared both options here: [Hydrogen vs. Next.js: How to Choose a Shopify Headless Stack](https://commerce-ui.com/insights/hydrogen-vs-nextjs-how-to-choose-a-shopify-headless-stack).

Shopify reportsthat merchants using Audiences see up to 50% lower customer acquisition costs, and published case studies back this up: Nathan James saw a 52% CAC decrease and 5.6x ROAS after switching to Audiences-powered targeting. For brands spending $20K+ per month on paid ads, that kind of reduction helps justify the Plus price tag on its own."

Credit card rates are negotiable at volume, typically around 2.15% + 30c. Third-party gateway surcharge is just 0.20%.

Best for: Brands doing $1M+ in annual revenue, anyone running B2B alongside D2C, multi-brand or multi-market operations.

> At $2M/month GMV: ~$7,000/month platform fee (0.35%) + ~$43,300 in CC processing = ~$50,300/month. Yes, that is a real number.

![](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7)

↑ Shopify pricing, tier-by-tier

## What You Actually Get at Each Tier

Price is only half the story. A lot of brands pick Basic because the monthly fee is low, then hit a wall two months later when they need staff accounts, or realize they cannot customize checkout, or find out Expansion Stores are only available on Plus.

| Feature | Basic ($39) | Grow ($105) | Advanced ($399) | Plus ($2,300+) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Staff Accounts | 0 | 5 | 15 | Unlimited |
| Reports | Basic analytics | Professional | Custom / Advanced | Custom + ShopifyQL |
| Checkout Capacity | Standard | Standard | Standard | 40x |
| Checkout Customization | No | No | No | Yes (Checkout Extensibility) |
| B2B / Wholesale | Yes\* | Yes\* | Yes\* | Yes (Native B2B channel) |
| Expansion Stores | No | No | No | Yes (Up to 9 expansion stores) |
| Shopify Flow | Full access | Full access | Full access | Full access + advanced |
| Carrier-Calc. Shipping | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Duties & Import Tax | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Shopify Audiences | No | No | No | Yes (Included) |
| POS Pro | $89/mo per loc. | $89/mo per loc. | $89/mo per loc. | 20 locations free\*\* |

*\***Disclaimer:** As of April 2, 2026, [Shopify made foundational B2B features available on all plans.](https://www.shopify.com/news/b2b-for-all) However, advanced B2B capabilities (unlimited catalogs, partial payments, deposits) remain exclusive to Shopify Plus. Feature availability may change. Check Shopify's official pricing page for the most current plan comparison.\*\*Unlimited POS Pro locations available for Plus merchants processing through Shopify Payments.*

## Shopify Fees Explained: Transaction Fees, Payment Processing & Surcharges

This section consolidates everything you actually pay per transaction.

| Fee Type | Basic | Grow | Advanced | Plus |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Online credit card rate | 2.9% + 30c | 2.7% + 30c | 2.5% + 30c | ~2.15% + 30c (negotiable) |
| In-person credit card rate | 2.6% + 10c | 2.5% + 10c | 2.4% + 10c | Negotiable |
| 3rd-party gateway surcharge | 2.0% | 1.0% | 0.6% | 0.20% |
| Currency conversion fee | 1.5% | 1.5% | 1.5% | 1.5% |
| Shopify Payments requirement | No (but surcharge if not) | No (but surcharge if not) | No (but surcharge if not) | No (but surcharge if not) |

Quick rule of thumb: use Shopify Payments. It eliminates the extra transaction surcharge (0.2% to 2.0% depending on your plan). The only reason to use a third-party gateway is if Shopify Payments is not available in your market, or you have a specific contractual requirement with another processor.

At scale, the fee differences add up. A brand doing $500K/month saves roughly $1,000/month just by being on Advanced instead of Basic, purely from the lower credit card rate. That savings alone covers the plan upgrade three times over.

According to [research Shopify commissioned from a Big Three consulting firm](https://www.shopify.com/blog/shop-pay-checkout), Shop Pay converts up to 50% better than guest checkout, and up to 91% better on mobile.". That is not a cost reduction, it is a revenue increase, but it directly impacts your cost per acquisition and your effective transaction cost as a percentage of revenue.

## Shopify POS Pricing: In-Store Selling Costs

If you have physical retail, or plan to, POS pricing is a big part of the equation.

POS Lite is free and included with every Shopify plan. Basic payment processing, product management, and customer tracking. Fine for a single location with simple needs or occasional pop-ups. But it does not do multi-location inventory, staff permissions, or buy-online-pick-up-in-store (BOPIS).

POS Pro costs $89/month per location ($79/month on annual billing). This is the real retail product. Multi-location inventory tracking, stock transfers between stores, staff roles and permissions, BOPIS, ship-from-store, and detailed sales reports by employee and location.

POS Pro on Shopify Plus: 20 locations included at no extra charge. For a brand with 10 stores, that is $890/month in POS fees you are not paying. That's $10,680/year.

| Scenario | Plan | POS Cost | Annual POS Spend |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 pop-up shop | Basic ($39/mo) | $0 (POS Lite) | $0 |
| 3 retail stores | Grow ($105/mo) | $267/mo (3 x $89) | $3,204/year |
| 10 stores | Advanced ($399/mo) | $890/mo (10 x $89) | $10,680/year |
| 10 stores | Plus ($2,300+/mo) | $0 (20 included) | $0 |

For retail brands with 5+ locations, Plus can pay for itself through POS Pro savings alone, before you count the lower transaction fees.

## When should you evaluate Shopify Plus?

Plus starts at $2,300/month on a 3-year term. That's a real number, and not every brand needs to pay it. Advanced at $399/month covers a lot. The question is whether you've hit the specific walls that only Plus removes. Here are the signals that you've outgrown Advanced.

### You're expanding internationally and need separate storefronts

If your go-to-market strategy requires expansion stores (different brands, different regions, different currencies with localized operations), that's Plus territory. Shopify Markets handles a lot on lower plans, but when you need true multi-entity with separated stores, inventory, and pricing, you need the Plus organization structure. As Astrid from Shopify put it: four years ago, expansion stores were the only option for internationalization. Now Markets and multi-entity exist, but for complex international operations, Plus is still where you land.

### You need checkout customization

This is one of the biggest myth-busters against the "Shopify is rigid" objection. On Plus, checkout extensibility lets you customize the checkout experience deeply without forking core code. Shopify Functions let you rewrite pricing logic, discount rules, and shipping calculations. If your business requires custom checkout flows, Plus is the only plan that gives you that level of control.We wrote a detailed breakdown of what this looks like in practice: [Upgrading to Shopify Checkout Extensibility](https://commerce-ui.com/insights/new-shopify-checkout-upgrading-to-checkout-extensibility).

### You're running serious B2B operations

As of April 2026, foundational B2B features are available on all plans. But advanced B2B (unlimited catalogs, direct catalog assignment to companies, partial payments, deposits) remains Plus only. If you're running wholesale with many buyer accounts and complex payment terms, the lower plans won't cover it.

### Your integrations are hitting API limits

If you run a PIM, an ERP, or multiple data feeds that sync with your store, you'll hit API rate limits on lower plans before you hit them on Plus. For brands with complex tech stacks, this is the kind of bottleneck that slows down operations without anyone realizing why things feel sluggish. Plus gives you higher API rate limits, and for some brands, that alone justifies the upgrade.

### You have 5+ retail locations

We covered this in the POS section, but it's worth repeating here. POS Pro costs $79/month per location on annual billing. Plus includes 20 POS Pro locations at no extra charge. A brand with 10 stores saves $9,480/year in POS fees on Plus. At that point, the POS savings alone close a meaningful chunk of the gap between Advanced and Plus pricing.

### You want dedicated support

On lower plans, you get standard Shopify support. On Plus, you get a dedicated Merchant Success Manager. For brands running complex operations, having someone at Shopify who knows your account, your setup, and your roadmap is worth more than it sounds on paper. Especially during peak seasons or when you're mid-migration and something needs to be resolved fast.

![](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7)

↑ 6 signals you've outgrown Shopify Advanced

## Costs most brands overlook when budgeting for Shopify

### Third-party apps.

Shopify's subscription covers the platform. But every store runs apps on top of it, and those costs add up. This is one of the most common surprises for brands coming from monolithic platforms where "everything is built in" (until you realize how much you pay your dev team to maintain all those built-in features). Most mid-market brands spend $350 to $1,400/month on apps. Build that into your budget from day one, not halfway through a migration.

Here are the apps most brands actually run, with realistic monthly costs:

| App / Tool | What It Does | Approx. Monthly Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Klaviyo | Email & SMS marketing | $20 to $1,500+ | Scales with list size. ~100,000 contacts — about US $1,380/month |
| Rebuy | Personalization & upsells | $99 to $499 | AI-powered product recs, checkout upsells. $499/month includes: Full access to Rebuy’s personalization features (recommendations, upsells, cross-sells, smart cart, etc.). |
| Microsoft Clarity | Observability/Analytics | Free | Solid free analytics tool |
| CookieBot or you can also use out of the box cookie consent from Shopify | GDPR and ePrivacy compliant cookie solution | $34 Or Free | Required for EU compliance. |
| Global-e / Swap | Cross-border commerce | Revenue share model | Handles duties, localized pricing, local payment methods |
| Elevar (if youf you need near-perfect conversion tracking accuracy. Not required for most brands) | Data Tracking | $150 to $500 | First-party data for Meta, Google, TikTok ads. |
| Matrixify | Operations | $20 to $200 | Streamlines product updates and operations |
| Shopify Discounts | Native discount engine | Free | Built-in |
| Supaeasy | Discounts | $49 to $399 | For more advanced discounts |
| Swish (Wishlist) | Wishlists & save-for-later | $0 to $99 | Free plan available |

### Payment processing fees.

If you use a third-party payment gateway instead of Shopify Payments, Shopify charges an additional 0.5% to 2% per transaction. Most brands commit to Shopify Payments during the sales process, then switch providers mid-implementation and get hit with fees nobody budgeted for. Decide on your payment setup before you sign, not during the build.

### Implementation cost: design and development

There are two paths here, and the right one depends on where your brand is.

A ready theme ($150 to $400 one-time) with basic customization gets you live in two to three weeks for roughly $10,000 to $30,000. A custom build with a development partner runs $70,000 to $140,000 over 2 to 3 months. The theme route is faster and cheaper. The custom route gives you full control over performance, brand expression, and room to grow. It can also reduce ongoing app costs by building key functionality directly into the theme.

We wrote a detailed comparison of both approaches, including why we never build on pre-made themes: [Why We Don't Build on Pre-Made Shopify Themes, and Never Will](https://commerce-ui.com/insights/why-we-dont-build-on-pre-made-shopify-themes-and-never-will).

Don't forget to price in time. A Shopify Plus implementation typically runs 3 to 6 months. A Magento or Shopware replatform can run up to 18 months. Every extra month is a month you're paying for two platforms and delaying the revenue gains that come with a better storefront.

## Why brands migrate to Shopify

Brands rarely replatform for fun. When they do, it starts with a number. The renewal quote, the hosting bill, the agency retainer, the total cost of keeping the current platform running. Someone adds it all up and realizes they're spending more to maintain the status quo than they would on a fully managed alternative.

The real trigger is when the platform stops being infrastructure and starts being a bottleneck. Every sprint goes to maintenance, patches, and keeping things running. Nothing goes to growth.

Three triggers that we see:

### Cost of ownership

The platform renewal quote arrives and the number is higher than last year. But the sticker price is only part of it. Add the hosting bill, the license fee, the implementation partner's retainer, security patching, and DevOps salaries. Then add the costs that never make it into the spreadsheet: slow iterations because every change needs a developer, delayed campaigns because the sprint is full, and the lack of confidence to ship new features because on a self-hosted stack, even small changes carry real risk of breaking something in production.

When the CFO or Head of eCommerce adds all of that up and compares it against a fully managed platform, the gap is usually bigger than the pricing page suggests.

For some brands, the total spend doesn't drop after migrating. It shifts. The monthly platform cost goes up, but the OPEX disappears. The line items change, not necessarily the total. But the money that used to go to keeping things running now goes to a platform that runs itself.

### The site went down when it mattered most

Black Friday traffic spikes. A flash sale goes viral. A celebrity post sends 10x normal volume to the checkout. The site crashes, or the checkout queues, or orders sit in limbo for hours. The lost revenue is real, but the bigger cost is what happens next: the team stops being aggressive with marketing because they don't trust the platform to handle the traffic. You stop running flash sales. You cap ad spend during peak. You leave money on the table not because of demand, but because of infrastructure.

If you don't trust your platform to handle your best days, it's the wrong platform.

Shopify's checkout handles around 4,000 checkouts per minute at baseline, and Plus customers get up to 40x that capacity. For brands coming off a failed peak, that number matters.

### The team can't move fast enough

The marketing manager wants to launch a landing page, swap a hero banner, or test a new promotion. On a self-hosted platform, that requires coordination between your internal dev team and an external agency. Non-technical people can't own the content, can't move fast, and end up waiting on engineering for things that should take an afternoon.

The cost of being slow doesn't show up on an invoice. It shows up in revenue you never capture: campaigns that miss the window, tests that never ran, ideas that died in the backlog.

## Common objections to migrating to Shopify

### *"We'll need apps for basic features and costs will add up"*

This one has truth to it, but it's more nuanced than it sounds. Shopify covers more natively than most people expect. Search and filtering comes free through Shopify Search & Discovery. Basic subscriptions are handled by Shopify Subscriptions, also free. Loyalty can go surprisingly far with customer tags, segments, and Shopify Functions for discount logic. Reviews is the one category that genuinely needs a paid app from day one.

Where costs grow is when you outgrow the basics. A mid-market brand scaling up might run Klaviyo for email ($150 to $500/month), Yotpo or Judge.me for reviews ($50 to $300/month), Smile.io for a full points-and-tiers loyalty program ($100 to $400/month), and Algolia for advanced search and merchandising ($50 to $200/month). That's $350 to $1,400/month, but it's a scaling cost, not a launch cost.

Two trade-offs people miss. First, on a self-hosted platform, those same features exist as plugins or custom code that your team maintains, updates, and fixes when something breaks after a platform upgrade. That cost is hidden in developer hours. On Shopify, the app cost is visible and predictable. Second, because it's an ecosystem of independent tools, you're not stuck maintaining something that doesn't fit. If an app underperforms, you swap it. On a monolith, replacing a built-in feature means rebuilding it.

### *"We'll lose control over our infrastructure."*

This comes up most with CTOs and technical directors whose job has been managing servers, deployments, and uptime. Moving to Shopify means handing that to a vendor. For some, that feels like giving up ownership.

The counterpoint: control over infrastructure is not the same as control over the business. The hours your team spends on server maintenance, security patching, and performance tuning are hours they're not spending on features that drive revenue. Shopify handles the infrastructure so your team can focus on the store.

### *"We'll pay extra fees if we don't use Shopify Payments."*

This is real and worth knowing upfront. If you use a third-party payment gateway instead of Shopify Payments, Shopify charges an additional transaction fee on top of what your payment provider already charges. Depending on your plan, that ranges from 0.5% to 2% per transaction. On Plus, both the credit card processing rates and the third-party gateway surcharge are negotiable based on volume. On all other plans, the surcharge is fixed to your tier.

Most competitors don't charge this. It's one of the few areas where Shopify's pricing is less transparent than the rest of the market.

For many brands, Shopify Payments is the better deal anyway because the rates are competitive and you avoid the extra fee entirely. But if your business requires a specific payment provider for regional or contractual reasons, factor this into your cost calculation from day one.

### *"Migration will tank our SEO."*

Every replatform causes a short-term drop in organic rankings. Google needs to reindex the new URL structure, follow redirects, and recrawl the site. This is true for any migration, not just to Shopify.

What matters is the recovery. With a proper redirect strategy and clean technical setup, most brands recover within 2 to 3 months. Some see improvements because Shopify's page speed and Core Web Vitals tend to score better out of the box than a legacy self-hosted stack.

## Hidden costs of staying on a self-hosted platform

These costs don't always show up in a platform comparison because they're spread across departments, vendors, and contracts. They vary a lot depending on your setup and team size, but they're worth accounting for.

### Hosting and infrastructure: $500 to $2,000+/month.

A mid-market brand on Magento or Shopware needs managed hosting, typically on AWS or Azure through a specialized provider. That covers your baseline traffic. Peak traffic (Black Friday, flash sales) is a separate problem. You either overprovision year-round or scramble to scale up manually. On Shopify, hosting is included and auto-scales.

### DevOps and system administration: $1,000 to $5,000/month outsourced, or $60,000 to $120,000/year in-house.

Someone needs to keep servers running, apply security patches, configure caching, and respond when things break. For most mid-market brands, this is an outsourced team or a part-time responsibility spread across developers who could be building features instead.

### Security and PCI compliance: $5,000 to $25,000/year.

If you accept card payments on a self-hosted platform, PCI DSS compliance is your responsibility. Security audits, penetration testing, vulnerability scanning. On Shopify, the platform is Level 1 PCI DSS compliant. Every store inherits that automatically. No audits, no extra cost.

## When Shopify might not be the right move

We'd lose credibility if we didn't acknowledge the situations where Shopify is not the answer. Every platform has limits, and knowing where those limits are saves you more money than any pricing comparison.

**Complex B2B operations.** Shopify's B2B features are improving fast (foundational B2B is now available on all plans as of April 2026). But if you need highly specialized quoting engines, complex approval chains, punchout catalogs, or custom ERP integrations that go beyond what APIs can handle, a self-hosted solution might still be necessary.

**Marketplaces.** If your core business model is a multi-vendor marketplace where third-party sellers list, manage inventory, and fulfill their own orders, Shopify is not built for that. It's possible with apps and workarounds, but it's not native. That said, if you run an external ERP and Shopify serves as one sales channel within a larger ecosystem, that works. But as a standalone marketplace platform, it's not the right fit.

**Full source code ownership.** Some brands, especially in regulated industries, need to own every line of code and control exactly where their data lives. Shopify is a SaaS platform. You're renting, not owning. For most brands this is a feature, not a bug. But if your legal or compliance team requires full code ownership, that's a hard constraint no amount of TCO savings can override.

**Brands that need everything fully custom at checkout.** Checkout extensibility on Plus covers a lot. But if your business requires rebuilding the checkout from the ground up, redefining every step and every interaction, Shopify's architecture has boundaries.

If you're weighing Shopify but unsure about the architecture, we published a full breakdown of where each approach fits: [The State of Shopify: Headless vs Liquid (Spring 2026)](https://commerce-ui.com/insights/the-state-of-shopify-headless-vs-liquid-spring-2026).

## Shopify Pricing FAQ

### How much does Shopify take per sale?

On Basic using Shopify Payments, you pay 2.9% + 30c per online transaction. On a $100 sale, that's $3.20. On Grow, $3.00. On Advanced, $2.80. On Plus with negotiated rates, roughly $2.45. If you use a third-party gateway instead of Shopify Payments, add an extra 0.2% to 2.0% surcharge on top of your gateway's fees.

### What is the cheapest Shopify plan for a real store?

Basic at $39/month ($29/month on annual billing). It's the cheapest plan that gives you a full online storefront. The $5/month Starter plan only gives you a checkout link, not a store.

### How much does Shopify cost per month?

The platform fee ranges from $39/month (Basic) to $2,300+/month (Plus). But the platform fee is not your total cost. Add credit card processing (2.15% to 2.9% + 30c per transaction), apps ($350 to $1,400/month for most mid-market brands), and your theme or custom build. A realistic total monthly cost for a brand doing $150K/month on the Grow plan is around $4,200 to $5,500.

### Is Shopify Plus worth it?

For most brands doing $1M+ in annual revenue, the math tends to work. The lower transaction fees, 20 included POS Pro locations, checkout customization, advanced B2B features, and Shopify Audiences can offset the higher subscription cost. If you're checking two or three of the boxes in our "When to evaluate Plus" section above, run the numbers for your specific setup. For many brands at that scale, Plus pays for itself. For others, Advanced at $399/month covers enough.

### Does Shopify have hidden fees?

No. But three costs surprise most brands: third-party apps ($350 to $1,400/month), the extra transaction surcharge if you don't use Shopify Payments (0.2% to 2.0%), and implementation costs ($10,000 to $150,000 depending on theme vs custom build). None of these are on the pricing page. All of them should be in your budget.

### Does Shopify charge transaction fees?

If you use Shopify Payments, you only pay the credit card processing rate (2.15% to 2.9% + 30c depending on your plan). No additional transaction fee from Shopify. If you use a third-party payment gateway, Shopify adds a surcharge of 0.2% to 2.0% on top of whatever your gateway charges. Most brands use Shopify Payments to avoid this.

### How much does it cost to migrate to Shopify?

$5,000 to $15,000 for simple SaaS-to-SaaS migrations. $70,000 to $150,000+ for complex migrations from Magento or Shopware. $100,000 to $250,000 for enterprise Plus migrations with an agency. Timeline: 4 to 8 weeks for simpler builds, 3 to 6 months for Plus.

### How does Shopify pricing compare to Magento or WooCommerce?

On sticker price, WooCommerce and Magento Open Source are "free."A studyof 250+ enterprises found Shopify's total cost of ownership is 33% lower on average. WooCommerce's operating costs are 41% higher, and Adobe Commerce's platform costs are 42% higher than Shopify's when you factor in hosting, DevOps, security, and maintenance.

### Is Shopify worth it for a small business?

If you're doing under $50K/month and selling primarily online, the Basic plan at $39/month is hard to beat. You get a full storefront, Shopify Payments, and 24/7 support without managing hosting, security, or infrastructure. The total cost (subscription + processing fees) on a $30K/month store is roughly $940/month. Compare that against the time and money you'd spend running WooCommerce or any self-hosted alternative, and the math works for most small businesses.

1. Identify and preserve the main topic or purpose of the webpage.
2. Retain key facts, statistics, and data points that are central to the content's message.
3. Keep important quotes from credible sources or experts.
4. Maintain the chronological order of events if the content is time-sensitive or historical.
5. Preserve any lists or step-by-step instructions if present.
6. Include relevant dates, names, and locations that are crucial to understanding the content.
7. Summarize lengthy explanations while keeping the core message intact.

When handling different types of content:

- For news articles: Focus on the who, what, when, where, why, and how.
- For scientific content: Preserve methodology, results, and conclusions.
- For opinion pieces: Maintain the main arguments and supporting points.
- For product pages: Keep key features, specifications, and unique selling points.

Your summary should be significantly shorter than the original content but comprehensive enough to stand alone as a source of information. Aim for about 25-30 percent of the original length, unless the content is already concise.

Present your summary in the following format:

```

}
```

This acceleration is primarily attributed to melting ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica. The study projects that if current trends continue, global sea levels could rise by up to 2 meters by 2100, posing significant risks to coastal communities worldwide.",

The rate of ice sheet melt in Greenland and Antarctica has tripled since the 1990s, the study reports. Without immediate and substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, we are looking at potentially catastrophic sea-level rise by the end of this century, warned co-author Professor Michael Green."

This article from Commerce-UI (a Shopify Plus agency) provides a comprehensive breakdown of Shopify pricing for 2026, arguing that brands should evaluate total cost of ownership (TCO) rather than just monthly plan fees. The article covers all plan tiers with real cost examples, transaction fees, POS pricing, overlooked costs, migration triggers, common objections, hidden costs of self-hosted platforms, and scenarios where Shopify may not be the right fit.

**Plan tiers (monthly price, online CC rate, 3rd-party fee):**
- Starter: $5/mo, 5% rate — checkout link only, for creators
- Basic: $39/mo ($29 annual), 2.9%+30c, 2.0% surcharge — full storefront, no staff accounts, for solo founders under $50K/mo (example: $30K/mo revenue ≈ $939/month total)
- Grow: $105/mo ($79 annual), 2.7%+30c, 1.0% surcharge — 5 staff accounts, professional reports, for brands doing $50K–$200K/mo (example: $150K/mo ≈ $4,185/month)
- Advanced: $399/mo ($299 annual), 2.5%+30c, 0.6% surcharge — 15 staff accounts, international features, carrier-calculated shipping, for $200K–$800K/mo (example: $500K/mo ≈ $13,199/month)
- Plus: $2,300/mo (3-year term) or $2,500/mo (1-year), switches to 0.35% of revenue capped at $40K/mo above ~$800K GMV, ~2.15%+30c negotiable rates — checkout customization via Checkout Extensibility, 10 expansion stores, unlimited staff, B2B channel, Shopify Audiences, 40x checkout capacity (example: $2M GMV/month ≈ $50,300/month)

**Key Plus-only features:** Checkout customization (not available on lower tiers), expansion stores, unlimited staff accounts, Shopify Audiences, 20 free POS Pro locations, dedicated Merchant Success Manager, higher API limits.

**POS pricing:** POS Lite free on all plans; POS Pro $89/mo per location ($79 annual). A 10-store brand saves $9,480–$10,680/year on Plus (20 locations included) versus paying on Advanced.

**Fees:** In-person rates are 2.6%+10c (Basic) down to 2.4%+10c (Advanced). Currency conversion is 1.5% on all plans. Using Shopify Payments avoids the 0.2%–2.0% third-party gateway surcharge. A $500K/mo brand saves ~$1,000/mo on Advanced vs. Basic just from lower card rates.

**Overlooked costs:** Third-party apps ($350–$1,400/month for mid-market; e.g., Klaviyo up to ~$1,380/mo, Rebuy $99–$499, Yotpo $50–$300, Algolia $50–$200); implementation ($10K–$30K for ready theme, $70K–$140K custom build); migration ($5K–$15K simple, $70K–$150K+ from Magento/Shopware, $100K–$250K enterprise).

**Hidden costs of self-hosted platforms:** Hosting ($500–$2,000+/mo), DevOps ($1K–$5K/mo outsourced or $60K–$120K/year in-house), security/PCI ($5K–$25K/year — Shopify is Level 1 PCI compliant automatically).

**Six signals to evaluate Plus:** international expansion needing separate storefronts, checkout customization, serious B2B operations, API rate limits, 5+ retail locations, need for dedicated support.

**Why brands migrate:** Lower total cost of ownership, failed peak traffic (Shopify handles ~4,000 checkouts/minute baseline, 40x on Plus), and slow teams blocked by developer dependencies.

**Where Shopify isn't right:** Highly complex B2B (custom quoting, approval chains, punchout catalogs), multi-vendor marketplaces, brands needing full source code ownership, or fully custom checkout rebuilds.

**Notable stats:** Shopify reports merchants using Audiences see up to 50% lower CAC (Nathan James saw 52% decrease, 5.6x ROAS); a study of 250+ enterprises found Shopify's TCO is 33% lower on average, with WooCommerce operating costs 41% higher and Adobe Commerce platform costs 42% higher; Shop Pay converts up to 50% better than guest checkout. As of April 2, 2026, foundational B2B features are available on all plans, but advanced B2B remains Plus-only.

The article concludes with an FAQ covering per-sale costs, cheapest real store plan, total monthly costs, Plus value, hidden fees, transaction fees, migration costs, and comparison to Magento/WooCommerce.

BigCommerce Pricing 2026: Plans, Fees & TCO

4

## Summary

### Key takeaways

* BigCommerce pricing in 2026 starts at **$29.95 per month for Standard**, **$79.95 for Plus**, and **$299.95 for Pro**, while Enterprise pricing is custom.
* BigCommerce automatically moves merchants to higher plans when annual online sales exceed the relevant threshold.
* The current annual sales limits are **under $50,000 for Standard**, **up to $180,000 for Plus**, **up to $400,000 for Pro**, and **above $400,000 for Enterprise**.
* BigCommerce does not charge platform transaction fees, but merchants still pay payment-processing fees to providers such as PayPal, Stripe, or other gateways.
* Hosting, bandwidth, PCI compliance, and core platform maintenance are included in the subscription, which simplifies the operating model compared with self-hosted platforms.
* The subscription is only one part of total cost. Merchants may also need paid themes, apps, custom development, integrations, migration, and partner support.
* Paid BigCommerce themes generally cost around **$150–$300**, while apps can add anything from a small monthly fee to several hundred dollars per month.
* Plus and Pro plans may feel expensive relative to the additional native features, especially when similar capabilities are already available through external marketing or customer-experience tools.
* Enterprise is intended for high-volume and more complex merchants that need custom price lists, stronger API capacity, priority support, and customer-success services.
* BigCommerce is usually more cost-effective for merchants prioritizing SaaS simplicity, while Adobe Commerce may be a better fit when deep customization and complex workflows matter more than predictable hosting and maintenance.

### When this applies

This applies when a merchant is evaluating BigCommerce as a hosted ecommerce platform and needs to understand the real cost beyond the advertised monthly fee. It is especially relevant for growing businesses whose sales may trigger automatic plan upgrades, as well as for teams comparing BigCommerce with Shopify, Adobe Commerce, or another enterprise platform. It also applies when budgeting for apps, themes, integrations, migration, headless development, or external technical support.

### When this does not apply

This does not apply when the business only wants a rough entry-level subscription price and does not need to model growth, customization, or total cost of ownership. It is also less relevant for merchants requiring extensive backend control, highly specialized workflows, or deep code-level customization, because the platform’s SaaS structure may become a more important constraint than its pricing.

### Checklist

1. Estimate current and projected annual online sales.
2. Match projected sales to the correct BigCommerce pricing tier.
3. Account for automatic upgrades when revenue thresholds are exceeded.
4. Compare monthly and annual billing options.
5. Separate BigCommerce transaction fees from payment-processing fees.
6. Select the required payment gateways and model their processing costs.
7. Review which features are native to Standard, Plus, Pro, and Enterprise.
8. Check whether abandoned cart, customer groups, stored cards, reviews, and filtering justify a higher plan.
9. Estimate paid theme costs.
10. List the apps required for marketing, shipping, search, loyalty, and operations.
11. Map ERP, CRM, PIM, OMS, tax, and fulfillment integrations.
12. Budget migration, redirects, SEO stabilization, and data validation.
13. Define any custom checkout, storefront, or headless development requirements.
14. Include ongoing developer or agency support in the operating budget.
15. Test critical workflows during the free trial before committing.

### Common pitfalls

* Treating the subscription fee as the complete cost of running the store.
* Ignoring revenue thresholds that can force an automatic plan upgrade.
* Confusing zero BigCommerce transaction fees with zero payment-processing fees.
* Choosing Plus or Pro without checking whether the additional features justify the price.
* Underestimating recurring app costs.
* Assuming paid themes require no customization or technical work.
* Delaying ERP, CRM, or fulfillment integration planning until after platform selection.
* Ignoring migration, redirect, and SEO recovery costs.
* Comparing BigCommerce and Adobe Commerce only by annual license price.
* Choosing a platform based on headline pricing rather than long-term operating fit.

**Quick answer:** BigCommerce pricing in 2026 starts at $29 per month when Core is billed annually, while Performance starts at $1,499 per month under an annual contract. The subscription is only one part of the budget. A realistic total must include GMV-based upgrades or overages, payment-provider fees, BigCommerce’s Open Payment Provider Fee, additional storefronts, B2B Edition, applications, design, development, migration, integrations, and support.

**Important 2026 change:** BigCommerce renamed its plans on June 1, 2026. Standard became Core, Plus became Growth, Pro became Scale, and Enterprise became Performance. The company also changed GMV thresholds and introduced an Open Payment Provider Fee for self-service plans. Older pricing guides that still use Standard, Plus, Pro, and Enterprise figures are no longer suitable for budgeting.

BigCommerce uses **Inclusive GMV** to evaluate thresholds and fees. In its current documentation, this means gross order value after a 10% reduction. The number can therefore differ from the revenue or payment volume shown in a merchant’s own financial reports.

## What changed in the 2026 BigCommerce pricing model?

| Previous name | Current name | Main pricing change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | Core | The monthly price remains $39 or $29 with annual billing, but the GMV threshold moved from $50,000 to $30,000 and phone support is no longer included. |
| Plus | Growth | The monthly price remains $105 or $79 with annual billing, while the GMV threshold changed from $180,000 to $100,000. |
| Pro | Scale | The base price remains $399 or $299 with annual billing. Fixed GMV blocks were replaced by a continuous 0.9% overage above $33,333 in monthly Inclusive GMV. |
| Enterprise | Performance | The plan remains contractual, with published annual pricing starting at $1,499 per month. |

The 2026 update also introduced a BigCommerce fee for self-service stores using Open Payment Providers. This means the old statement that BigCommerce never charges a platform-level order fee is no longer accurate for every payment configuration.

## How automatic upgrades and overages work

### Core and Growth use automatic upgrades

Core is available while trailing-12-month Inclusive GMV stays at or below $30,000. Once the threshold is exceeded, BigCommerce can automatically move the store to Growth. Growth follows the same model at $100,000 and can automatically move to Scale.

Plan eligibility is evaluated from sales volume. A merchant can also choose a higher plan early when advanced features, support, or service options are required. Annual billing lowers the effective monthly rate, but it does not remove GMV eligibility rules.

### Scale uses a monthly overage

Scale includes up to $33,333 in monthly Inclusive GMV. BigCommerce charges 0.9% on the amount above that monthly cap instead of moving the merchant through fixed revenue blocks.

**Illustrative Scale calculation:** if Inclusive GMV is $50,000 in one month, the over-cap amount is $16,667. The Scale overage is approximately $150 for that month:

`($50,000 − $33,333) × 0.9% = approximately $150`

This example excludes the subscription, payment processing, and Open Payment Provider Fee. If the same orders are processed through an Open Payment Provider, the separate 0.6% fee may also apply to the eligible GMV.

### Performance uses contracted terms

Performance starts at $1,499 per month when billed annually, but the actual platform price, included GMV, overage, service level, storefronts, B2B Edition, and add-ons belong in the merchant contract. Do not use an unofficial “average enterprise price” as a substitute for a BigCommerce quote.

Before signing, request a pricing schedule that identifies:

* base annual platform fee;
* included Inclusive GMV or order volume;
* overage calculation;
* payment-provider treatment;
* included and additional storefronts;
* B2B Edition and Buyer Portal licensing;
* API and support entitlements;
* professional and success services;
* renewal, notice, and price-adjustment terms.

## BigCommerce payment fees in 2026

There are two separate payment cost layers:

1. **Payment-provider processing fees.** The gateway or processor charges for card, wallet, bank, or alternative-payment transactions.
2. **BigCommerce Open Payment Provider Fee.** BigCommerce charges this additional fee on eligible orders processed through a provider outside its current Embedded Payment Provider program.

### Embedded Payment Providers

Orders processed through a provider on BigCommerce’s current embedded list do not incur the additional BigCommerce order fee. The provider still charges its own processing fees. The embedded list can change, so verify the selected gateway on the current [BigCommerce pricing page](https://www.bigcommerce.com/pricing/) before calculating TCO.

### Open Payment Providers

If an order is processed through an Open Payment Provider, BigCommerce applies the following fee to eligible order GMV:

* Core: 2.0%;
* Growth: 1.0%;
* Scale: 0.6%;
* Performance: governed by contracted terms.

BigCommerce states that offline and manually paid orders, including purchase orders, can be subject to the fee. This is especially important for wholesalers and B2B merchants that accept account payments, offline terms, or procurement orders.

### Open Payment Provider Fee example

A Growth store has $80,000 in annual Inclusive GMV. Twenty-five percent of that GMV is processed through an Open Payment Provider:

`$80,000 × 25% × 1.0% = $200 annual BigCommerce fee`

The merchant would also pay the processor’s own fees on those transactions. If every order is processed through Embedded Payment Providers, the BigCommerce Open Payment Provider Fee is zero.

| Plan | Best fit | Upgrade before the threshold when… | Main budget risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core | A new or low-volume store that needs standard ecommerce functionality and can operate with chat and email support | Customer groups, abandoned-cart tools, stored cards, phone support, or a higher GMV ceiling are operationally important | The $30,000 threshold and 2.0% Open Payment Provider Fee can make the cheapest subscription an expensive payment configuration. |
| Growth | An established B2C store needing segmentation, abandoned-cart recovery, persistent carts, stored cards, and phone support | The store needs advanced product filtering, more inventory locations, or expects to exceed $100,000 TTM GMV | The plan can automatically move to Scale as GMV grows. |
| Scale | A growing store needing stronger filtering, more locations, and a usage-based path above the base GMV allowance | Price Lists, advanced promotions, enterprise service, B2B Edition, or a negotiated commercial structure are required | Monthly GMV overage and the 0.6% Open Payment Provider Fee can both apply. |
| Performance | A high-volume, B2B, multi-storefront, headless, or integration-heavy program that requires contractual service and enterprise capabilities | The merchant needs contract-specific volume, support, B2B, storefront, API, or success-service terms | The published starting price does not represent the complete contract or implementation TCO. |

## How much does BigCommerce B2B Edition cost?

BigCommerce does not publish a universal B2B Edition list price. The official B2B product page directs merchants to request a demo and speak with the B2B team. Budgeting should therefore use the actual quote rather than an agency estimate presented as a vendor fee.

BigCommerce B2B Edition can include buyer-portal, company-account, credit, quote, invoice, shared-list, reorder, role, approval, and sales-representative workflows. The platform fee is not the full B2B implementation cost.

Also budget for:

* Buyer Portal customization and branding;
* company, user, role, and account-hierarchy migration;
* customer-specific pricing and Price Lists;
* quotes, invoices, payment terms, and credit workflows;
* ERP, PIM, CRM, OMS, WMS, tax, payment, and shipping integration;
* PunchOut, EDI, or procurement connectivity where required;
* B2B search, quick order, shared lists, and reorder UX;
* data reconciliation, monitoring, and post-launch support.

See BigCommerce’s [official B2B commerce overview](https://www.bigcommerce.com/solutions/b2b-ecommerce-platform/). For implementation planning, use Elogic Commerce’s [B2B ecommerce development and consulting services](https://elogic.co/services/b2b-ecommerce-development-and-consulting/).

## Three BigCommerce total-cost-of-ownership scenarios

The scenarios below are transparent Elogic Commerce planning examples. They are not BigCommerce quotes, market averages, or promises. Payment processing, taxes, internal salaries, and revenue opportunity cost are excluded. Each scenario assumes that orders use Embedded Payment Providers, so no Open Payment Provider Fee is included.

| Scenario | Assumptions | One-time implementation | Annual platform or contract | Annual apps and middleware | Annual support and improvement | Illustrative three-year TCO |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Growth B2C | One Growth storefront billed annually; customized theme; up to 10,000 SKUs; standard product and customer migration; email, reviews, and search apps; no ERP; embedded payments | $70,000 | $948 | $9,600 | $36,000 | $209,644 |

The formula is:

`Three-year TCO = implementation + 3 × (platform contract + apps and middleware + support and improvement)`

This article from Elogic Commerce provides a comprehensive guide to BigCommerce pricing in 2026, covering plans, fees, and total cost of ownership (TCO). The key change in 2026 is that BigCommerce renamed its plans on June 1, 2026: Standard became Core, Plus became Growth, Pro became Scale, and Enterprise became Performance. The company also changed GMV (gross merchandise value) thresholds and introduced a new Open Payment Provider Fee for self-service plans.

**2026 Pricing Plan Details:**
- **Core** (formerly Standard): $39/month or $29/month billed annually. GMV limit up to $30,000 trailing-12-month Inclusive GMV with automatic upgrade to Growth above the threshold. 2.0% Open Payment Provider Fee. 24/7 chat/email support only (no phone).
- **Growth** (formerly Plus): $105/month or $79/month annually. GMV up to $100,000 with automatic upgrade to Scale. 1.0% Open Payment Provider Fee. 24/7 phone, chat, email.
- **Scale** (formerly Pro): $399/month or $299/month annually. $33,333 monthly Inclusive GMV cap with 0.9% overage above the cap; moves to Performance at $2 million trailing-12-month GMV. 0.6% Open Payment Provider Fee.
- **Performance** (formerly Enterprise): Custom pricing starting at $1,499/month billed annually; contractual terms govern actual pricing.

BigCommerce uses "Inclusive GMV" meaning gross order value after a 10% reduction. Automatic upgrades occur when revenue thresholds are exceeded. Scale uses a monthly overage model (illustrated example: $50,000 monthly GMV results in approximately $150 overage = ($50,000 - $33,333) x 0.9%).

**Payment Fees:** There are two cost layers—payment-provider processing fees (charged by gateways like PayPal/Stripe) and the BigCommerce Open Payment Provider Fee (2.0% Core, 1.0% Growth, 0.6% Scale on eligible GMV processed through Open Payment Providers). Orders through Embedded Payment Providers incur no BigCommerce fee. Offline/manual/Purchase Orders may also be subject to the fee, which is important for B2B/wholesale merchants.

**Costs Not Included:** Payment processing, Open Payment Provider Fee, scale/Performance overages, B2B Edition, additional storefronts, premium themes, custom development, apps, ERP/PIM/CRM/OMS/WMS integrations, migration, testing, training, and ongoing support.

**TCO Scenarios (three-year, Elogic planning examples assuming embedded payments):**
- Growth B2C: $70K implementation + $948 platform + $9,600 apps + $36K support = $209,644
- Mid-market B2B: $250K + $60K + $60K + $120K = $970,000
- Integration-heavy enterprise: $650K + $180K + $240K + $300K = $2,810,000

**Comparisons:** Against Shopify Plus ($2,300-$2,500/month), BigCommerce offers lower entry pricing but GMV-driven upgrades and Open Payment Provider Fees as risks. Against Adobe Commerce (quote-based), BigCommerce offers SaaS simplicity with less customization flexibility. Implementation costs range from $20K-$60K for theme-led launches to $300K-$750K+ for enterprise headless/multi-region implementations. The article is written by Paul Okhrem, Co-Founder & CEO of Elogic Commerce.

# BigCommerce's 2026 Pricing Update: What's Changing & How Merchants Should Respond

![BigCommerce's 2026 Pricing Update: What's Changing & How Merchants Should Respond](//netalico.com/cdn/shop/articles/bigcommerce-pricing-updates.png?v=1776796517&width=1500)

**TL;DR:** BigCommerce is introducing a new 2% transaction fee (the Open Payment Provider Fee), renaming every plan, and lowering GMV thresholds. The changes take effect June 1, 2026. If you're a BigCommerce merchant, you have roughly 52 days to understand the impact and decide how to respond.

If you run a store on BigCommerce, the pricing page you signed up for no longer exists. On a quietly published page at [bigcommerce.com/dm/plan-pricing-updates-2026](https://www.bigcommerce.com/dm/plan-pricing-updates-2026/), BigCommerce has announced sweeping changes to its plan structure that take effect June 1, 2026. This BigCommerce 2026 pricing update introduces transaction fees for stores that don't use approved payment processors, renames every plan, and pulls GMV thresholds downward so more merchants get pushed into higher tiers.

The bigger story: "no transaction fees" was the single loudest argument BigCommerce used against Shopify. That argument is now retired. Agencies, analysts, and merchants across the eCommerce community have already called out both the substance of the changes and the quiet way they were published.

## The New BigCommerce Transaction Fees, Explained

A new **Open Payment Provider Fee** applies to any order processed through a gateway that isn't on BigCommerce's approved Embedded Payment Providers list (Stripe, PayPal/Braintree, Adyen, Checkout.com, and a handful of others). On the rebranded **Core** plan, that fee is 2%. On **Growth**, it's 1%. On **Scale**, it's 0.6%. **Performance** is custom. At $500,000 in annual GMV, those rates work out to $10,000, $5,000, and $3,000 per year respectively.

The kicker: the fee also applies to offline orders and manual payment methods, including B2B purchase orders. If your business runs on POs, every one of those transactions is now fee-eligible.

## BigCommerce Plan Changes & Lower GMV Thresholds

GMV thresholds are dropping alongside the rename. Core drops from $50,000 to $30,000. Growth drops from $180,000 to $100,000. Scale moves from $400,000 per year to $33,333 per month with a 0.9% overage charge. A merchant doing $150K on the old Plus plan ($79/month) is now headed for Scale at $299/month. That's a 278% jump in platform cost before any transaction fee is layered on top.

Phone support is also gone from the entry-level Core plan. Chat and email only, unless you upgrade to Growth or buy an add-on.

## What BigCommerce Merchants Should Do Before June 1

You have roughly 52 days. Here are three steps we'd recommend.

1. **Pull your trailing 12-month GMV** and compare it against the new thresholds. If you're above the cap for your current plan, your monthly bill is going up whether or not the new fee touches you.
2. **Audit your payment stack.** If your gateway isn't on BigCommerce's Embedded list, calculate 0.6% to 2% of that GMV. That's your new annual line item. B2B merchants with purchase-order workflows should run this math carefully, because those transactions are explicitly covered.
3. **Run an honest total-cost-of-ownership comparison** against your alternatives. The merchants most exposed are in the $400K to $2M range, the exact segment that chose BigCommerce because of the no-fee positioning. At that size, a [BigCommerce to Shopify migration](https://netalico.com/pages/bigcommerce-to-shopify-migration) often lands at a similar or lower total cost, with a deeper app and developer ecosystem.

If replatforming is on the table, start with a [site planning and strategy engagement](https://netalico.com/pages/site-planning-strategy) so you know what a move actually looks like for your stack. You can also browse [our BigCommerce and Shopify client work](https://netalico.com/blogs/portfolio) for a sense of the stores we've moved and the outcomes we've delivered.

## A Word On Trust

Platforms raise prices. That's not the story. The story is how this was announced: a URL buried outside the main navigation, no press release, no blog post, no executive framing. That's a choice, and as your agency partner, we think it's worth naming.

If you'd like help modeling your total cost under the new structure or scoping a [BigCommerce to Shopify migration](https://netalico.com/pages/bigcommerce-to-shopify-migration), [book a free strategy call](https://netalico.com/pages/contact). No pressure, just numbers.

## FAQ: BigCommerce 2026 Pricing Update

### When do the new BigCommerce prices take effect?

June 1, 2026. Merchants on annual contracts transition at their renewal date.

### What is the BigCommerce Open Payment Provider Fee?

It's a new transaction fee BigCommerce charges when you process orders through any payment gateway that isn't on its approved Embedded Payment Providers list. Rates are 2% on Core, 1% on Growth, 0.6% on Scale, and custom on Performance.

### What are the new BigCommerce plan names for 2026?

Standard is now Core. Plus is now Growth. Pro is now Scale. Enterprise is now Performance.

### Does the BigCommerce transaction fee apply to B2B purchase orders?

Yes. Offline orders and manual payment methods, including POs, are subject to the Open Payment Provider Fee.

### Is it worth migrating from BigCommerce to Shopify in 2026?

That depends on your GMV, your payment stack, and your roadmap. For merchants in the $400K to $2M GMV range, the math has shifted meaningfully. Run a full total-cost-of-ownership comparison before deciding, or [talk to our team](https://netalico.com/pages/contact) and we'll model it with you.
