# Average Customer Retention Rates by Industry in 2025

Understanding the average customer retention rate by industry helps businesses gauge performance.

![](https://www.gravatar.com/avatar/d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e?s=200&d=404)

[by Shopify Staff](/blog/authors/shopify-staff)Sep 11, 2024 • 18 min read

![a mirror, bag, and computer in boxes on blue background](https://cdn.shopify.com/b/shopify-brochure2-assets/30101d0ab71fbbeecd262d5c91ee6fc3.png?originalWidth=1848&originalHeight=782)

If you’re on a mission to boost [customer retention](/enterprise/blog/ecommerce-customer-retention), you’ve probably crunched the numbers to figure out your customer retention rate (CRR)—the percentage of customers who come back for more over a given period. But knowing your CRR is just the beginning. To truly understand how you’re doing, you need to see how your retention rates stack up against others in your industry.

In this article, we’ll dive into the average customer retention rates by industry, giving you the insights you need to take your customer retention game to the next level.

## How to calculate customer retention

If you haven’t yet identified your business’s customer retention rate, you can use the following formula to do so:

Customer retention rate = [(customers at the end of the period – customers acquired during the period) / customers at the start of the period] x 100.

Let’s say you own an online houseplant store and want to determine your retention rate over a six-month period. At the beginning of this period, you had 150 customers. By the end, you had 120 customers, having acquired 5 new customers during these six months. Here’s how you’d calculate your CRR:

[(120 – 5) / 150] x 100 = 76.67%

So, your customer retention rate over the six-month period is approximately 76%. Ahead, you can find averages per industry to help you contextualize that number to determine whether your CRR is on track.

## What is the average customer retention rate by industry?

* [Media companies](#6)
* [Professional services](#7)
* [Automotive and transportation](#8)
* [Insurance](#9)
* [IT services](#10)
* [Construction and engineering](#11)
* [Financial services](#12)
* [Telecom](#13)
* [Health care](#14)
* [Software](#15)
* [Banking](#16)
* [Customer services](#17)
* [Manufacturing](#18)
* [Hospitality](#19)
* [Ecommerce](#20)

Customer retention rates vary significantly across different industries, typically ranging between 70% and 80%. However, these averages can fluctuate widely depending on the specific industry in question.

For instance, the banking industry enjoys a relatively high average retention rate of around 75%. Customers tend to maintain long-term relationships with their banks, often due to the convenience of staying put and the costs associated with switching providers. On the other hand, the hospitality industry, which includes restaurants, has a lower average retention rate of about 55%. Despite frequent dining out, the plethora of choices available to consumers leads to less consistent customer loyalty.

This disparity illustrates that comparing retention rates across different industries can be akin to comparing apples to oranges. Each sector has its unique dynamics influencing how and why customers stay loyal. According to [metrics](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1041645/customer-retention-rates-by-industry-worldwide/) by Statista, here is the average CRR by industry:

### Media companies: 84%

Whether it’s television, film, publishing, or digital platforms, maintaining a captivated audience is key. With an impressive customer retention rate of 84%, media companies thrive on their ability to engage viewers and readers consistently through compelling content and innovative delivery methods.

In the highly competitive media landscape, it’s all about sustaining customer satisfaction and fostering loyalty. If your CRR isn’t up to par, here are some strategies to consider:

* **Leverage data analytics.** [Data analytics](/blog/marketing-analytics) can improve your understanding of your audience’s preferences and help you tailor content accordingly, thus keeping your visitors clicking on your content.
* **Interactive content.** Engage your audience with [interactive content](/blog/interactive-content) such as live polls, Q&A sessions, and interactive storylines. This fosters a sense of participation and investment in your content.
* **Personalized recommendations.** Implement algorithms that provide [personalized content recommendations](/blog/ecommerce-product-recommendation) based on viewer history and preferences, enhancing user experience and satisfaction.

### Professional services: 84%

The professional services industry—which includes consulting firms, legal services, and accounting businesses—boasts an impressive average customer retention rate of 84%. This high CRR can be attributed to the deep, trust-based relationships that professionals build with their clients over time.

In the competitive landscape of professional services, maintaining customer satisfaction and fostering long-term relationships is crucial for sustainable success. If your CRR isn’t up to snuff, here are a few [research-backed strategies](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3805469) for improving it:

* ****Use a CRM.**** If you can barely keep track of all of your clients, let alone know them well enough to tailor your services to their needs, [customer relationship management](/blog/crm) (CRM) software could be a huge help. It can help you track client interactions, preferences, and feedback, ensuring that your services reliably meet high standards.
* **Request client feedback.** There are [apps in the Shopify App Store](https://apps.shopify.com/search?q=store%20reviews) that automates feedback requests, making it easier to collect and analyze customer opinions. Regularly gathering and acting on feedback shows that you value client input and are committed to continuous improvement.
* **Connect with clients.** People often stick with their hairdressers for years, not just for their skills but for the personal relationships they build. Building strong, trust-based relationships can foster long-term commitments and significantly [increase retention rates](/blog/how-to-increase-retention-rate).

### Automotive and transportation: 83%

With a solid customer retention rate of 83%, businesses in this sector excel by delivering reliable services and building trust over time. Whether it’s ensuring timely repairs or providing seamless transport solutions, keeping customers on the move is key.

To maintain and improve this retention rate, consider the following strategies:

* **Send regular maintenance reminders.** Send [automated reminders](/blog/reminder-email) for vehicle maintenance and service appointments. This not only ensures vehicle longevity but also keeps customers engaged with your services.
* **Improve the customer experience.** Enhance your customer offering by providing complementary services that add convenience and value. These can include free vehicle pickup and drop-off for service appointments, complimentary car washes with every service, or providing a comfortable waiting area with amenities such as Wi-Fi and refreshments.
* **Ask for feedback.** It’s likely your customers have specific concerns regarding your business that might make them go elsewhere. Use [customer satisfaction](/blog/75022277-how-to-read-your-customers-minds-with-one-email) feedback to make tangible improvements in your services, whether it’s reducing wait times, improving communication, or addressing any recurring issues.

### Insurance: 83%

In the world of insurance, peace of mind is paramount. Boasting a customer retention rate of 83%, insurance companies succeed by fostering trust that they’ll provide support in the face of disasters and emergencies. Clients depend on their insurers to protect what matters most, and maintaining this trust is crucial for long-term loyalty.

To further improve customer retention, consider adopting these strategies:

* **Policy review meetings.** Schedule regular policy review meetings with clients to discuss their coverage needs and ensure they have the best policies in place.
* **Educational resources.** Provide clients with educational resources about insurance options, policy benefits, and industry trends so they can better understand the resources at their disposal.
* **Claim process transparency.** Ensure that the claims process is transparent and easy to navigate with regular updates, exceptional [user experience design](/blog/user-experience-design), and clear communication channels.

### IT services: 81%

In the dynamic realm of IT services, staying ahead of technological advancements is vital. With a commendable customer retention rate of 81%, IT service providers thrive by offering robust support and innovative solutions tailored to client needs. Ensuring systems run smoothly and securely keeps clients coming back.

To enhance customer retention, consider these strategies:

* **Be proactive with support.** Implement proactive IT support to address potential issues before they become major problems. This minimizes downtime and enhances client satisfaction.
* **Offer customized solutions.** Offer customized IT solutions tailored to the specific needs of each client. Personalized service demonstrates a commitment to meeting client needs and fosters loyalty.
* **Conduct regular performance reviews.** Keeping an ongoing dialogue with your clients not only shows your commitment to their success but also helps you identify budding issues before they become problematic. Consider scheduling performance reviews with your clients quarterly or semi-annually, depending on the client’s needs and the complexity of the services you provide.

### Construction and engineering: 80%

In the construction and engineering industry, building firm foundations isn’t just about structures—it’s about relationships too. With an impressive customer retention rate of 80%, firms in this sector succeed by delivering quality projects and maintaining client trust through every phase of development.

To improve customer retention, consider these strategies:

* **Use project management tools.**[Project management tools](/blog/best-task-management-apps) will help you make sure you’re completing your projects on time and within budget. This reliability enhances client trust and satisfaction.
* **Involve clients.** Regular updates and involvement ensure clients feel valued and informed, fostering loyalty.
* **Provide post-project support.** Post-project support services such as maintenance and troubleshooting will show clients that you’re invested in their success beyond the initial transaction.

### Financial services: 78%

The financial services industry—which includes banks, insurance companies, investment firms, and credit unions—boasts an impressive average customer retention rate of 78%. Financial products like mortgages, savings accounts, and insurance policies often come with long-term commitments, plus, the hassle and costs of switching providers can be a big deterrent.

Even with these factors working in favor of financial institutions, there’s always room for improvement. A [2021 study](https://journal.binus.ac.id/index.php/BBR/article/view/6546/4245) found that financial service companies can boost retention by focusing on customers who live closer to their branches and by offering higher loan amounts relative to the collateral value. These strategies enhance convenience, perceived value, and trust—key elements in keeping customers happy and loyal.

According to a [2020 study of financial services](https://doi.org/10.33168/jsms.2020.0206), the following factors play a significant role in customer retention:

* **Convenience.** Make the customer experience as smooth as possible by streamlining the onboarding process, simplifying your digital platform, offering educational resources, and enhancing your customer support.
* **Profitability.** Keep your long-term customers engaged by offering incentives like cashback, lower fees, or higher interest rates on savings accounts. These rewards show appreciation and encourage continued business.
* **Security.** Besides ensuring you have proper protections in place, transparency about product features, fees, and policies is paramount.
* **Flexibility.** Offer customizable solutions and flexible options that can cater to diverse financial situations. Whether it’s personalized financial planning or adaptable investment options, flexibility can set your service apart.

### Telecom: 78%

In the fast-paced telecom industry, keeping the lines of communication open is essential. With a customer retention rate of 78%, telecom companies thrive by providing reliable services and maintaining strong customer relationships. Connectivity and support are key drivers of customer loyalty in this sector.

To improve customer retention, consider these strategies:

* **Make your plans more flexible.** Customize plans to meet individual customer needs, enhancing satisfaction and retention. Allow customers to upgrade, downgrade, or modify their plans easily based on their usage patterns and preferences, making your services more adaptable to their changing needs.
* **Provide 24/7 customer support.** Ensure round-the-clock customer support to address any issues or concerns promptly. Quick and reliable support fosters trust and loyalty, showing customers that they can rely on you whenever they need help.
* **Enhance network reliability.** Invest in infrastructure to ensure minimal downtime and high-quality connections. Regularly update and maintain your network to prevent outages and provide a seamless experience.

### Health care: 77%

In health care, the well-being of patients is paramount. With a customer retention rate of 77%, health care providers excel by delivering personalized care and building trust with patients. Long-term relationships are built through compassionate care and consistent, quality service.

To enhance customer retention, consider these strategies:

* **Implement patient follow-ups.** Develop a system for regular patient follow-ups to ensure continued care and address ongoing health concerns. Personalized attention fosters patient trust and loyalty, showing patients that their well-being is a priority.
* **Offer health education programs.** Provide health education programs and resources to empower patients with knowledge about their conditions and treatments. Educated patients are more likely to stay loyal to their health care providers, as they feel more in control of their health and confident in the care they receive.
* **Focus on patient-centered care.** Personalized care enhances patient satisfaction and retention by ensuring each individual feels valued and understood. Consider what you want in a care provider, whether it’s transparent straightforward communication, acknowledging cultural preferences, or offering holistic care that addresses social and emotional well-being, as well as physical care.

### Software: 77%

The IT and software industry is at the forefront of innovation, constantly evolving to meet client needs. With a customer retention rate of 77%, companies in this sector succeed by offering cutting-edge solutions and exceptional [customer support](/blog/the-easy-answer-for-your-most-common-support-questions). To improve customer retention, consider these strategies:

* **Provide continuous software updates.** Ensure clients can access the latest features and security measures by providing automatic software updates and improvements. This reliability enhances client trust and satisfaction, demonstrating your commitment to maintaining the highest quality and security standards.
* **Offer user training programs.** Help clients make the most of your software solutions by offering comprehensive user training programs. The more users feel confident and capable using your products, the more likely they’ll be to stick around.
* **Assign dedicated account managers.** Provide personalized support and promptly address client concerns by assigning dedicated account managers. Personalized support services foster strong client relationships and loyalty, showing clients that their needs are a top priority and ensuring they have a direct point of contact for any issues or questions.

### Banking: 75%

Trust and reliability are the cornerstones of customer relationships in the banking industry. With a customer retention rate of 75%, banks succeed by offering personalized financial services and maintaining [strong client relationships](/partners/blog/20159683-infographic-how-to-build-long-term-client-relationships). Ensuring financial security and providing expert advice keep clients loyal. To boost customer retention, consider these strategies:

* **Offer personalized financial advice.** Help clients achieve their financial goals by providing personalized financial advice and planning services. This personalized attention fosters trust and loyalty, showing clients that their financial well-being is a top priority of yours.
* **Enhance online banking convenience.** Ensure your online banking platform is user-friendly and offers a wide range of services. Convenience enhances client satisfaction and retention, making it easier for clients to manage their finances and stay engaged with your services.
* **Host financial wellness workshops.** Organize workshops, seminars, and [online courses](/blog/how-to-create-an-online-course) focused on financial literacy and wellness. These events can educate clients on managing their finances, investing wisely, and planning for the future, thereby strengthening their trust and loyalty to your bank.

### Consumer services: 67%

Consumer service businesses like travel agencies, spas, cleaners, and tutors may have a lower average CRR because of high competition among those offering the services and low switching costs for consumers. Price sensitivity and personal preferences can also come into play, leading customers to shop around. To address these issues, consider the following strategies:

* **Offer flexible pricing and packages.** Provide [competitive pricing](/blog/competitive-pricing) and flexible service packages to cater to different customer needs and budgets. Offer discounts for bundled services or long-term commitments to encourage repeat business.
* **Implement a referral program.** Encourage your existing customers to refer new clients by offering incentives like discounts, free services, or special offers. [Referral programs](/blog/referral-program-ideas) leverage word-of-mouth marketing and reward loyal customers for promoting your business, fostering a community of satisfied clients.
* **Provide convenient scheduling and booking.** Make it easy for customers to book and [manage appointments online](https://apps.shopify.com/search?q=appointment%20booking). Offer flexible scheduling options to accommodate busy lifestyles and reduce friction in the booking process.

### Manufacturing: 67%

With a customer retention rate of 67%, manufacturers succeed by consistently delivering high-quality products and maintaining strong relationships with their clients. Here are some tricks of the trade tha wi’ll help you give your CRR a boost:

* **Quality assurance.** Implement stringent [quality assurance](/in/blog/quality-assurance) processes to ensure your products consistently meet high standards. Reliability enhances customer trust and satisfaction.
* **Product customization.** Offer product customization options to meet the unique needs of different customers. Personalized products demonstrate a commitment to customer needs and encourage loyalty.
* **After-sales support.** Provide comprehensive after-sales support, including maintenance, troubleshooting, and replacement services. Post-purchase support enhances [customer satisfaction](/blog/customer-satisfaction) and retention.

### Hospitality: 55%

In the hospitality sector, customer retention stands at 55%. The vast array of choices available to consumers means that maintaining loyalty is more challenging. Establishments succeed by offering exceptional service and unique experiences to stand out in a competitive market.

To improve customer retention, hospitality businesses can consider prioritizing these factors:

* **Enhanced digital engagement.** Leverage technology to stay connected with your customers. Use mobile notifications or [email newsletters](/blog/create-a-newsletter) to provide updates on special events, new menu items, and exclusive offers. Engage with customers by sharing behind-the-scenes content or hosting interactive sessions on social media.
* **Community involvement.** Become an active part of the local community by participating in or [sponsoring events](/retail/event-marketing), collaborating with local businesses, or supporting local charities. Building a reputation as a community-oriented establishment can foster a sense of loyalty among local customers who appreciate businesses that give back.
* **Unique dining experiences.** Create distinctive dining experiences that go beyond just food and service by launching themed dining nights, live entertainment, chef’s table experiences, or interactive cooking classes. Offering something out of the ordinary can make your establishment a destination and encourage repeat visits.

### Ecommerce: 30%

Decile, a customer data and analytics solution, revealed in its [*2023 Ecommerce Benchmarking Guide*](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/decile-releases-2023-benchmarking-guide-140000187.html) that the average retention rate for all the brands on its platform was 30%. This figure may seem dismal compared to other sectors, but it reflects the unique challenges and opportunities within the digital marketplace. High competition, the ease of switching between stores, and the constant hunt for better deals can make customer retention tricky.

That said, you certainly shouldn’t see 30% as the limit. Mark Ainsworth, digital PR and marketing director for digital marketing agency [Max Web Solutions](https://maxwebsolutions.co.uk/), says the average CRR for their clients is 62%. “This is largely because of our focus on personalized customer experiences and robust after-sales support, which encourages repeat business and fosters long-term loyalty,” explains Mark.

Here are some [ecommerce retention strategies](/enterprise/ecommerce-customer-retention) that will help you get your CRR to where you want it to be:

* **Optimize your online presence.** Easy navigation, fast site speed, and a simple checkout process are crucial elements that can make or break a sale. Shopify offers tools to streamline site performance, [enhance mobile optimization](/partners/blog/74754051-5-simple-hacks-for-an-optimized-mobile-ecommerce-design), and simplify the checkout process.
* **Stay top of mind.**[Email marketing](/blog/email-marketing), retargeting ads, and a solid social [content calendar](/blog/content-calendar) will keep your brand in customers’ purview. [Shopify’s marketing tools](/market) and integrations make it easy to set up and manage these campaigns, helping you maintain a presence in your customers’ minds.
* **Keep customers happy.** A tedious return process or poor [ecommerce customer service](/blog/13251973-creative-ways-to-improve-ecommerce-customer-experience-that-also-boost-loyalty-and-sales) can make or break the customer experience. Shopify can help with tools like [returns management apps](https://apps.shopify.com/search?q=returns), [customer service integrations](/blog/crm-integration), and [social media engagement](/blog/social-media-engagement) features, ensuring a seamless and satisfying experience that keeps customers coming back.

## 10 factors influencing customer retention rates

1. [Trust](#21)
2. [Customer service](#22)
3. [Customer lifetime value](#23)
4. [Community](#24)
5. [Expert support](#25)
6. [Values](#26)
7. [Convenience](#27)
8. [Price](#28)
9. [Perks](#29)
10. [Quality](#30)

A satisfied customer will return to an establishment to make more purchases, raising the customer retention rate. While customer satisfaction is a key factor affecting customer retention rates, it’s not the only one.

These 10 factors help determine a business’s customer retention rate:

### 1. Trust

Customers return to businesses that they trust and that provide a certain amount of transparency. Indeed, a 2020 study found that, by demonstrating a commitment to social responsibility, financial service companies could increase trust by 12%.

It’s easier to cultivate [brand](/blog/brand-loyalty) [loyalty](/blog/brand-loyalty) when customers know they can easily return items and won’t be slapped with hidden fees or experience other unwelcome business practices. Whether it’s an insurance company or another type of service provider, customers are more likely to be loyal to a brand if they are confident the company will be accountable should something go wrong.

### 2. Customer service

Customer-centric employees and [attentive service](/blog/customer-service) also attract [repeat customers](/retail/repeat-customers). Whether it’s a fancy online shoe boutique or a chaotic grocery store, customers notice kind, polite, individualized customer assistance. According to a Gartner [report](https://www.gartner.com/en/customer-service-support/insights/customer-loyalty), when customers feel they’ve received value from a customer service interaction, there is an 82% probability of repurchasing or renewal, and a 97% probability of positive [word of mouth](/retail/word-of-mouth-marketing).

### 3. Customer lifetime value

When customers peruse an ecommerce platform, app, or [brick-and-mortar](/retail/brick-and-mortar) shop and feel like the product selection and marketing visuals speak to them, they’ll likely return. Repeat customers have a higher [customer lifetime value](/blog/what-is-customer-lifetime-value) (CLV), which assesses the total amount a customer spends over the course of their relationship with the business. More specialized services or products tend to have fewer customers, but those customers tend to be loyal because they feel [valued](/blog/predict-customer-value) by the businesses.

### 4. Community

Customers often return to businesses when they feel a sense of community with fellow customers, the brand, and the employees. The Local, a small news platform in Europe catering to foreigners, has reduced [its churn rate to less than 4%](https://whatsnewinpublishing.com/the-power-of-community-how-a-small-publisher-hit-50000-paying-members-through-audience-engagement/)—nearly unheard of in the media industry—by actively engaging with readers and analyzing data to see what keeps them subscribing. You can start [building community](/blog/building-community) by reaching out and collaborating with your most loyal followers.

### 5. Expert support

When a customer shops and they feel the products or a particular service will help them reach their goals and achieve success, they come back. If someone is actively making DIY home improvements, for example, they will be more receptive to a housewares store that offers expert support and storage solutions. Effective [customer service training](/blog/customer-service-training) involves making all of your employees experts in your business.

### 6. Values

Customer loyalty can blossom when [brand values](/blog/brand-values) align with customers’ beliefs. For example, customers may want to know if a business is paying its employees a living wage and treating them fairly, or that the business is a certified [B Corp](/blog/what-is-b-corporation).

### 7. Convenience

Some customers prioritize convenience above all else—if a store is on their way to work or a product will arrive more quickly than a competitor’s, that often may trump other factors such as values or community. To appeal to those in your ZIP code, consider location-based marketing and make sure to have an updated [Google Profile](/retail/google-business-profile). You can also offer contactless or digital payment options, as well as buy online, pickup in-store ([BOPIS](/retail/bopis)). Adjusting your hours so that it opens an hour before or one to two after a regular workday can make all the difference.

### 8. Price

For the average consumer, lower prices often attract repeat customers—who doesn’t like to pay less? Having periodic sales or offering incentives like a percentage off for a first purchase can attract new customers who then transition into repeat customers that will appreciate a new level of loyalty in the form of perks.

### 9. Perks

Sometimes it’s the little things: specials, samples, and freebies that create loyal customers. [Discounts](/blog/discounts-and-coupons)—as well as incentives, sales, free delivery, and [loyalty programs](/blog/loyalty-program)—often make retained customers feel appreciated and are helpful strategies when acquiring customers just walking in the physical or virtual door.

### 10. Quality

The quality of products or services is a fundamental factor in customer retention. When customers perceive that they are getting high-quality products or services, they are more likely to return. Quality not only meets but exceeds customer expectations, ensuring satisfaction and loyalty. Investing in both your product and the marketing/publicity for your product is the only way to find success with this strategy. Beyond product development, make sure you have a strong influencer marketing program.

* **Invest in retention software.** Tools like [Zendesk](https://www.zendesk.com/) and [Gainsight](https://www.gainsight.com/) can help you retain existing customers by streamlining customer service and tracking engagement. These platforms offer comprehensive solutions to address customer concerns quickly and efficiently.

## Average customer retention rate FAQ

### What is customer retention?

[Customer retention](/blog/customer-retention-strategies) is the percentage of returning customers to a business measured over a particular time—weeks, months, quarters, or years.

### What is a realistic retention rate?

A realistic customer retention rate depends on your industry. Comparing your retention rate averages to previous periods can show if your retention strategies are attracting current customers to make more purchases or not.

### What is a KPI (key performance indicator) for customer retention?

There are several [KPIs](/blog/what-is-kpi) for customer retention, including repeat purchase rate, which is when a customer transitions from buying the same product once a month, for example, to three times a month. Another KPI is analyzing simple customer satisfaction scores that potentially improve over time. A painful (yet informative) KPI is a business’s customer churn rate, which is the rate current customers stop purchasing goods or services.

### How does customer retention rate impact a company’s profitability?

Retaining existing customers is generally more cost-effective than acquiring new ones because the cost of marketing and onboarding new customers is often higher. Loyal customers tend to make repeat purchases and spend more over time, and are more likely to refer new customers through word of mouth. This increases [customer lifetime value](/blog/what-is-customer-lifetime-value) and reduces costs associated with [customer acquisition](/blog/customer-acquisition). High retention rates also lead to more stable and predictable revenue streams, enhancing overall profitability.

### How does customer retention correlate with customer loyalty?

Retention measures the rate at which customers continue to do business with a company over a specific period, while loyalty is about the emotional attachment and commitment customers feel toward a brand. High retention rates often indicate strong customer loyalty, as loyal customers are more likely to continue purchasing from the same company. Loyalty drives retention by fostering repeat business, higher lifetime value, and positive word-of-mouth referrals, which all contribute to sustained customer relationships.

This Shopify blog article (published September 11, 2024, last updated by Emily Shwake) provides average customer retention rates (CRR) by industry for 2025, based on Statista metrics, helping businesses benchmark their performance. The customer retention formula is: CRR = [(customers at end of period − customers acquired during period) / customers at start of period] × 100, illustrated with a houseplant store example yielding ~76%. Retention rates typically range between 70% and 80% across industries.

Average CRR by industry: Media companies (84%), Professional services (84%), Automotive and transportation (83%), Insurance (83%), IT services (81%), Construction and engineering (80%), Financial services (78%), Telecom (78%), Health care (77%), Software (77%), Banking (75%), Consumer services (67%), Manufacturing (67%), Hospitality (55%), and Ecommerce (30%).

Key details per industry: Professional services succeed through trust-based relationships (strategies: use CRM, request client feedback, build personal connections). Financial services benefit from convenience, profitability incentives, security, and flexibility. Ecommerce (30% average per Decile's 2023 Ecommerce Benchmarking Guide) faces high competition and low switching costs; however, Max Web Solutions reports a 62% average CRR for its clients due to personalized experiences and after-sales support.

The article also lists 10 factors influencing retention: 1) Trust, 2) Customer service (Gartner report: 82% probability of repurchase when customers feel service value), 3) Customer lifetime value, 4) Community (The Local news platform reduced churn to under 4%), 5) Expert support, 6) Values, 7) Convenience, 8) Price, 9) Perks, 10) Quality.

General improvement strategies include investing in retention software (Zendesk, Gainsight), engaging with entrepreneurs, implementing new marketing strategies (email, feedback tools, loyalty programs), and leveraging Shopify tools like reengagement automations.

The FAQ clarifies: Customer retention measures returning customers over a period; realistic rates depend on industry; KPIs include repeat purchase rate, satisfaction scores, and churn rate. ## Shopify’s global ecommerce impact

Let’s look at Built With, which tracks global usage statistics and gives us an answer to how many people use Shopify. We can see that the number of stores using Shopify has increased by more than two million`[13]` from January 2025 **to November 2025** (circa 4.5 million to 6.5 million).

Its live country totals also increased across all key markets. The top five:

| **Rank** | **Country** | **Store count (November 2025)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **One** | United States | 3,549,339 |
| **Two** | United Kingdom | 240,926 |
| **Three** | Germany | 182,285 |
| **Four** | Australia | 170,002 |
| **Five** | Canada | 134,646 |

Those numbers show us that Shopify has more than **14x the number of stores in the US** as it does in its second biggest market, the UK, and that impressive volume translates to it being the most popular ecommerce platform in the US`.``[14]`

Shopify’s market share in the UK`[15]` is greater than ever as of September 2025, sitting at over 20%, behind only Wix. WooCommerce comes third for Brits.

Looking at **Shopify Plus**, Shopify’s enterprise product, Built With`[16]` shows it powers 76,607 stores as of November 2025, including 41,137 in the US, and 5,534 in the UK.

On a global scale, Statista data shows that Shopify lags behind WooCommerce,`[17]` Squarespace Online Stores, and WooThemes as of 2024. The stats:

* WooCommerce powers 39.05% of stores
* Squarespace Online Stores powers 14.75%
* Woo Themes powers 13.96%
* Shopify’s 10.56% share is over 3x less than WooCommerce’s

So, Shopify definitely has work to do if it wants to dominate the global ecommerce scene, but it’s already making excellent strides with its latest figures. These show 24% GMV growth and 33% international revenue growth`[18]` in 2024.

A recent success example is **Black Friday 2024**, during which its merchants generated $11.5 billion in global sales,`[19]` a 24% increase in sales from 2023.

It isn’t just smaller retailers using Shopify, either, with JB Hi-Fi, Meta, Estée Lauder, Gymshark, ButcherBox, SKIMS, Supreme, and many more **leading brands** using it.

The core factor behind that relentless Shopify market share growth is its stable, cost-effective ecosystem, but also its **investment in commerce features** that its merchants want.

For instance, a 2025 Smartly study found that 73% of marketers`[20]` plan to increase their **conversational commerce** investments by up to 50% by 2027. Then, in September 2025, Shopify announced that it’s bringing commerce to ChatGPT.`[21]`

## Shopify merchant performance and average earnings

Now that you know all about Shopify’s growth (impressive, isn’t it?), the questions on your lips will probably be around how much does the average Shopify store make per month, and how much money you can make on Shopify.

The answer? Some serious money, but there’s plenty of revenue, profit, and earnings insights to unpack, which we’ll cover now:

* **Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) trends:** The trend is upwards. Merchants hit the $1 trillion milestone in cumulative GMV`[22]` in 2024, with 2.4x more GMV than in 2020, set against annual growth rates of 26% in 2024, 26% in 2023, and 21% in 2020.
* **Black Friday/Cyber Monday stats:** Merchants served 76+ million customers`[23]` and generated $11.5 billion in sales during BFCM in 2024, an increase of 24% from 2023. At its peak, customers were spending $4.6 million per minute.
* **Average Shopify store revenue**: Average revenues are niche and model dependent, but True Profit reckons thatmost Shopify stores make under $1,000/month,`[24]` with at least 20% reaching the $10,000/month milestone.
* **Profitability and success rate:** Shopify says that its merchants make their very first sale every 26 seconds,`[25]` and that overall, they have generated more than $1.4 trillion in revenue. According to most Reddit users,`[26]` they average 15-30% net profit.
* **Dropshipping and high-end earnings:** The global dropshipping market`[27]` could reach $435 billion by the end of 2025, and with Shopify Collective,`[28]` Shopify makes finding high-quality suppliers easy. Earnings range from a few hundred dollars/month to over $100k/month.
* **Average Order Value (AOV):** Research platform Dynamic Yield`[29]` puts the AOV from consumer goods at $296 as of October 2025. However, AOVs are niche dependent, with the luxury and jewelry niche having the highest AOV of $328.
* **Repeat Purchase Rate:** According to Smile.io,`[30]` a customer has a 27% chance of returning to your store`[31]` after one purchase. With an email marketing app, such as Omnisend, it’s possible to follow-up, cross-sell, and maximize repeat purchases on Shopify.
* **Product Return Rate:** The National Retail Federation’s 2024 report on consumer trends found that 16.9% of customers`[32]` returned products. Shopify says this can be as high as 30%,`[33]` although it depends entirely on your products and service quality.

## FAQs

**What is the success rate of Shopify stores?**

Five to 10% is the average for Shopify merchants, although it depends on the niche and ecommerce model (e.g., dropshipping and white label).

**Is Shopify still relevant in 2026?**

It’s more relevant than any other ecommerce platform in the US, capturing 30% of sales with growing influence across additional key markets, including Europe, the UK, and Asia.

**How much does an average Shopify store make?**

Less than $1,000/month, though 20% of stores reach the $10k/month milestone. Some stores, such as Gymshark, do hundreds of millions in sales.

**Who is Shopify’s biggest competitor?**

WooCommerce for standard Shopify plans, and on the enterprise side, Adobe Commerce and Salesforce Commerce Cloud.

**Is Shopify bigger than Amazon?**

Nope, and it’s nowhere near close. Shopify’s market cap is $188.19 billion. Amazon’s is $2.32 trillion, equating to a percentage gap of around 1,132% (Shopify is around 12x smaller than Amazon).

**How much does Shopify make from a $100 sale?**

For a typical $100 online sale, Shopify charges between $2.80 and $3.20 in transaction fees, with Basic plan users paying 2.9% plus 30 cents.

**Does Tesla still use Shopify?**

No, neither on its primary site nor in its shop. The official Tesla Shop is often quoted as using Shopify Plus, but CMS checks show it uses Drupal (with a custom build).

**How can I see which apps a Shopify store uses?**

You can check an app’s reviews on the Shopify App store to find stores using it, or inspect the source element of a website for any app mentions.

This article from Omnisend's blog provides comprehensive Shopify statistics for 2026, covering market position, merchant performance, financials, usage trends, app store data, and enterprise-level insights.

- Shopify captured 30% of US ecommerce businesses in 2025, with over 875 million shoppers purchasing from its stores in 2024
- Cumulative gross merchandise volume (GMV) exceeded $1 trillion in 2024, with a 26% revenue increase
- 6,519,105 active stores as of November 2025 (up from ~4.5 million in January 2025)
- An entrepreneur makes their first sale every 26 seconds

- Q3 2025 showed 32% revenue and GMV growth; international revenue surged 33%

**Global Presence:**
- Top countries by store count (Nov 2025): US (3,549,339), UK (240,926), Germany (182,285), Australia (170,002), Canada (134,646)

- Global market share lags competitors: WooCommerce (39.05%), Squarespace Online Stores (14.75%), Woo Themes (13.96%), Shopify (10.56%)

**Merchant Performance:**
- Average store revenue is under $1,000/month, with 20% reaching $10,000/month milestone
- Average net profit: 15-30%
- Average Order Value for consumer goods: $296 (luxury/jewelry highest at $328)
- 27% repeat purchase rate after first purchase; 16.9% product return rate
- Dropshipping market could reach $435 billion by end of 2025

**Corporate Financials:**
- Stock up 41.95% year-to-date (Nov 2025) to $152.73; market cap of $188.19 billion (vs Amazon's $2.32 trillion)
- $1.1 billion operating income and $1.6 billion free cash flow in 2024
- 8,100 employees at end of 2024
- Most prominent 2025 acquisition: Vantage Discovery for $59 million

**Usage Trends:**
- Top store categories: Fashion (101,763), Apparel (83,421), Jewelry (69,529), Bags (40,101), Coffee (29,054)
- Average conversion rate: 1.4%; above 3.2% places in top 20%
- 68% of traffic from mobile; mobile checkout accounts for 79% of purchases
- Instagram used by 46.6% of stores, Facebook 28.7%, TikTok 12.1%
- USPS is the most-used carrier (31% of domestic shipments)

**App Store Statistics (Nov 2025):**
- Over 13,000 apps available; 1,091 "Built for Shopify" apps; 39 native Shopify apps
- Three in four merchants use apps, installing 6 on average
- 3,800+ developers, 16 million installs since 2020, generating $230+ million in developer revenue
- Most-installed apps: Judge.me (513,470 stores), Klaviyo (383,014), Shopify Inbox (382,082)
- Omnisend rated 4.8/5 based on 2,863 reviews (vs Klaviyo's 4.7/5)

**Shopify Plus (Enterprise):**
- Costs $2,300/month for three-year term; 76,607 live stores (41,137 in US)
- Merchants generating $1m-$500m growing 126% YoY on average (690% above industry average)
- Offers up to 36% better total cost of ownership than competitors

**Platform Facts:**
- Dawn is the most popular theme (16.65% of stores)
- 150+ new features released every six months; $1.4 billion spent on R&D in 2024
- 42.2% of new enterprise launches chose Shopify; 1,200+ enterprise brands added annually

The article concludes that Shopify's trajectory is sharply upward, with expectations of continued growth in 2026, though it notes Shopify is not bigger than Amazon (roughly 12x smaller by market cap).

19. 82% of sellers use FBA
20. 64% use FBA only, 22% merchant fulfilment only, only 14% run both; the 49% 3PL figure circulating has no traceable source

Ecommerce M&A in 2026 has consolidated dramatically since the 2020-2021 aggregator gold rush, following the collapse or restructuring of Thrasio, Perch, and Razor. The active buyer universe consists of four segments: (1) strategic acquirers (Amazon, Walmart, Shopify, plus large consumer brands like e.l.f. Beauty, Anker, Edgewell, and P&G) paying the highest multiples; (2) lower-middle-market private equity (L Catterton, Stripes, Bansk Group) buying profitable 7-8 figure brands at 5-8x EBITDA for platforms and 3-5x EBITDA for add-ons; (3) remaining aggregators (Heroes, Berlin Brands Group, Olsam) buying at 10-20% of 2021 cadence; and (4) operator buyers (family offices, search funds) using seller financing.

Current valuation multiples in 2026 are channel-specific: Amazon FBA brands trade at 2.5-3.5x SDE (vs 5-7x in mid-2021); profitable Shopify DTC brands trade at 3-5x SDE (or 4-6x EBITDA above ~$2M EBITDA); subscription/recurring revenue businesses trade at 4-7x EBITDA with premiums for sub-5% monthly churn; and content-plus-commerce hybrids trade at 5-8x EBITDA. The market has shifted from growth-first to profit-first underwriting, with SDE standard below ~$3M bottom-line earnings and EBITDA above that threshold, both measured on trailing twelve months (TTM).

The 2021 aggregator bust was caused by four factors: multiple inflation (3x to 7x SDE bidding war), post-pandemic demand normalization, Amazon cost inflation (fees, ads, storage), and operational complexity. Over 90 FBA aggregators raised capital between 2020-2022 (Thrasio $3.4B+, Razor $1B+, Perch $908M, etc.), most of which failed or restructured.

Key diligence red flags for ecommerce deals include: Amazon Seller Central data integrity mismatches, IP gaps (utility patents, registered trademarks), supplier concentration (over 60% of COGS), SKU concentration (over 50% of revenue cuts multiples by at least half a turn), channel concentration (over 80% Amazon or 60% single paid channel), and subscription churn over 10% monthly. The Amazon Seller Central account transfer is a critical operational risk — entity-level acquisitions preserve account history, while asset deals reset performance metrics and ad campaigns (4-8 week revenue dips).

Recommended preparation for sale (12-24 months) covers financial cleanup, operational documentation, customer data hygiene, inventory rationalization, customer concentration mitigation, legal/IP cleanup, and buyer-readiness research. Typical sale processes run 4-9 months (3-6 for aggregators/operators, 6-9 for strategic/PE), with most deals falling apart over diligence findings, inventory surprises, IP gaps, or buyer-founder fit issues.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from Webiano Digital (published June 4, 2026, by Jan Bielik) analyzes the recent regulatory enforcement actions against Chinese-linked ultra-low-price e-commerce platforms Shein and Temu in Europe. The piece argues that European authorities are treating these platforms as infrastructure that must bear the same legal duties as any consumer business selling at scale.

**Key regulatory actions covered:**
- **France fined Shein approximately €22.5 million** (announced June 3, 2026, by the DGCCRF) through two administrative fines: €16,733,190 against Infinite Styles Services Co Limited (site operator) for non-compliant order confirmations sent to consumers, and €5,764,500 against Infinite Styles Ecommerce Co Limited (seller) for violations of withdrawal rights and environmental information requirements (including absence of information on product traceability and plastic microfibres). These followed a July 2025 DGCCRF fine of €40 million against Shein for misleading discounts and environmental claims, where investigators found 57% of verified discount announcements offered no actual price reduction, 19% offered smaller reductions, and 11% were price increases.
- **The European Commission fined Temu €200 million** (May 28, 2026) under the Digital Services Act for failing to properly identify, analyze and assess systemic risks linked to illegal products on its platform. The Commission gave Temu until August 28, 2026, to present a credible action plan.
- Separately, the CNIL (French data protection authority) fined Infinite Styles Services Co Limited €150 million in September 2025 for cookie compliance failures, noting the Shein site averaged 12 million France-resident visitors per month.

**Key legal and policy themes:**
- The Shein fines center on basic consumer information required by EU/French distance-selling law: the price of goods, delivery dates, seller identity and contact details, legal guarantee information, mediation access, withdrawal forms, and 14-day withdrawal rights. The DGCCRF argues that missing statutory information constitutes legal harm to consumers even before financial loss is shown.
- Order confirmations are described as legal evidence trails and due on a "durable medium"; the article emphasizes that with millions of low-value transactions, small omissions become platform-wide systemic compliance failures.
- Temu's DSA penalty targets risk governance and platform architecture — recommender systems, algorithmic amplification of illegal products, and design that increases visibility of unsafe goods — marking a shift where "the DSA turns platform architecture into evidence."
- The article notes enforcement is cumulative across multiple legal frameworks: consumer law (DGCCRF), platform law (DSA), data protection (CNIL), product safety (General Product Safety Regulation), and environmental rules (AGEC law on waste-generating products).
- Both Shein (108 million average monthly EU users) and Temu (75 million) are designated Very Large Online Platforms under the DSA (threshold: 45 million), with Ireland as their Digital Services Coordinator jurisdiction.
- Context noted: EU textile consumption rose from 17 kg per person in 2019 to 19 kg per person in 2022; the European Commission's textiles strategy says "fast fashion should be 'out of fashion'."
- Enforcement timeline included the October 2024 Commission investigation into Temu, November 2024 CPC Network notification to Temu, May 2025 CPC notification to Shein, February 17, 2026 Commission investigation into Shein over addictive design, recommender transparency and illegal products, and the November 2025 French government removal of illicit products from Shein (including childlike sex dolls and banned weapons).
- A DGCCRF product test in 2025 found 75% of 600+ products from seven foreign online platforms failed EU rules, with 46% both non-compliant and dangerous.
- The article frames these actions as level-playing-field enforcement rather than protectionism: "any platform selling into the EU must meet EU consumer and safety standards," noting principles could apply to AliExpress, Amazon Marketplace, TikTok Shop, Wish and dropshipping sites.
- Shein disputes the sanctions as disproportionate and has said it will contest them; the article notes French courts rejected total marketplace suspensions in December 2025 and March 2026 while ordering tighter controls.

--- SOURCE 2: EU Turns to Online Marketplaces After Record AliExpress ... ---
URL: https://techpolicy.press/eu-turns-to-online-marketplaces-after-record-aliexpress-fine

SUMMARY:
<summary>
The European Commission fined AliExpress €550 million on Monday (July 20, 2026) for failing to adequately assess and mitigate risks posed by illegal, unsafe, and counterfeit products on its platform — the largest penalty issued to date under the Digital Services Act (DSA), and the third overall. The fine surpasses the €200 million penalty against Temu (May 2026) and the €120 million against X (December 2025).

AliExpress, which had 193 million European users last year, called the decision disproportionate and stated it is reviewing its options, arguing the fine ignored its "sound risk management framework and the significant, proactive enhancements." The Commission found AliExpress failed to properly evaluate whether it had enough resources to monitor potentially illegal products, overstated the effectiveness of its detection and removal systems, and did not adequately consider how its recommendation and advertising tools could increase visibility of illegal goods. Investigators found counterfeit products, unsafe toys, and dangerous cosmetics remaining available after being flagged.

The decision reflects a broader shift in the EU's enforcement focus under the DSA — moving beyond social media platforms toward online marketplaces facilitating physical goods sales. The European Board for Digital Services' second annual risk report (July 1) identified illegal products sold through online marketplaces as one of the most persistent systemic risks, including challenges of sellers evading controls by modifying listings or returning under new identities.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This blog post by Professor Steve Peers (Royal Holloway University of London) provides a comprehensive summary and resource links regarding the EU's Digital Services Act (DSA), published February 20, 2026. The DSA regulates online platforms and search engines generally, but imposes special requirements on 'very large online platforms' (VLOPs) and 'very large online search engines' (VLOSEs) — those visited by 10% of the EU population monthly, designated by the European Commission. Designated companies include US firms (Meta, X, Google, LinkedIn), Chinese firms (AliExpress, TikTok, Temu, Shein), EU firms (Booking.com, Zalando, two porn sites), and Canada's Pornhub; nearly half of designated VLOP/VLOSE operators are non-American.

Enforcement against VLOPs can involve requests for information, investigations, preliminary findings, and final breach decisions with fines up to 6% of worldwide annual turnover, or binding commitments (settlements) to avoid fines. Non-compliance can trigger daily fines of up to 5% of global turnover. A ban on a platform requires a very high threshold. Substantive obligations (Articles 33-43) include systemic risk assessment, risk mitigation, crisis response, independent audits, non-profiling recommender system options, advertising repositories, researcher data access, algorithm explanations to regulators, compliance bodies, and annual supervisory fees.

Key court developments: Amazon and Zalando lost General Court challenges to their VLOP designation (appeals to CJEU pending); porn companies' challenges are pending. In the Amazon judgment, the General Court rejected arguments that the VLOP regime breached Charter rights to conduct business, property, equal treatment, freedom of expression, and privacy, but upheld justified limitations. Regulation fee decisions for 2023 were struck down by the General Court (TikTok, Meta), with Commission appeals pending. X, X.AI, and Elon Musk challenged the December 2025 non-compliance decision against X. The Commission is suing Spain for non-enforcement at national level.

Enforcement actions: The Commission made its first final non-compliance decision against X in December 2025, fining it €120 million for deceptive 'blue tick' practices, restricted researcher data access, and advertiser repository issues; proceedings continue on illegal content, disinformation, recommender systems, and 'nudification' apps. --- SOURCE 21: 7 User Retention Metrics for Shopify Stores in 2025 ---
URL: https://www.buildwithtoki.com/blog-post/user-retention-metrics

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a 2025 guide for Shopify merchants on seven critical user retention metrics, published by Toki (a Shopify retention app). The article argues that sustainable e-commerce growth comes from converting first-time buyers into loyal repeat customers through data-driven retention strategies rather than guesswork. The seven metrics covered are:

1. **Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)** - Total net profit expected from a customer over their entire relationship. Formula: Average Purchase Value × Average Purchase Frequency Rate × Average Customer Lifespan (example: $75 × 3 × 2 = $450). Actionable tips include segmenting customers into VIPs and low-value segments, keeping the CAC-to-CLV ratio at 1:3 or better, and informing product/upsell strategies.

2. **Churn Rate** - Percentage of customers who stop doing business over a period. Formula: (Customers Lost During Period / Total Customers at Start) × 100. Example: 50 lost out of 1,000 = 5% monthly churn. Tips include differentiating voluntary vs. involuntary churn, implementing early warning systems, and using exit surveys.

3. **Net Promoter Score (NPS)** - Measures loyalty via "how likely to recommend" on a 0-10 scale. Promoters (9-10), Passives (7-8), Detractors (0-6). Formula: % Promoters - % Detractors (example: 50% - 20% = 30). Tips include following up with open-ended questions, closing the loop with detractors, leveraging promoters for referrals, and tracking trends over time.

4. **Cohort Retention Rate** - Tracks percentage of a user group (grouped by sign-up/first purchase date) that returns over time. Formula: (Users from cohort active in Period N / Total users in cohort) × 100. Example: 150 of 1,000 January customers returning in March = 15% Month 3 retention. Useful for pinpointing onboarding issues, validating product improvements, and optimizing acquisition channels.

5. **Product Stickiness (DAU/MAU Ratio)** - Measures daily engagement. Formula: (Daily Active Users / Monthly Active Users) × 100. A ratio above 20% is good; Facebook exceeds 50%. Tips include creating non-transactional content, using push notifications/email for daily value, and identifying stickiest features.

6. **Revenue Retention Rate** - Measures recurring revenue kept from existing customers. Two formulas: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) = ((Starting MRR + Expansion MRR - Churn MRR - Contraction MRR) / Starting MRR) × 100, and Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) = ((Starting MRR - Churn MRR - Contraction MRR) / Starting MRR) × 100. Example: starting at $10,000 MRR with $1,500 expansion, $500 contraction, $1,000 churn yields NRR of 100% and GRR of 85%. A rate over 100% (NRR) indicates revenue growth from existing customers outpacing losses.

7. **Customer Health Score** - A predictive composite metric combining multiple indicators (purchase frequency, support interactions, email engagement) into a single score. It's unique per business, with a weighted-point model example (e.g., +20 points for a purchase in last 30 days, +15 for >3 lifetime purchases, -5 for negative support interaction). Used to proactively identify at-risk customers before they churn.

The article includes a comparison table rating each metric on implementation complexity, resource requirements, expected outcomes, ideal use cases, and key advantages. It concludes by emphasizing that the metrics work best as an interconnected system (e.g., low NPS from a high-CLV segment signals unhappy valuable customers; high churn with low stickiness suggests a weak store experience) and promotes Toki as a tool that tracks these KPIs and provides tiered memberships, points, and gamified rewards to improve loyalty.
</summary>

<summary>
Ecommerce M&A in 2026 has consolidated dramatically since the 2020-2021 aggregator gold rush, following the collapse or restructuring of Thrasio, Perch, and Razor. The active buyer universe consists of four segments: (1) strategic acquirers (Amazon, Walmart, Shopify, plus large consumer brands like e.l.f. Beauty, Anker, Edgewell, and P&G) paying the highest multiples; (2) lower-middle-market private equity (L Catterton, Stripes, Bansk Group) buying profitable 7-8 figure brands at 5-8x EBITDA for platforms and 3-5x EBITDA for add-ons; (3) remaining aggregators (Heroes, Berlin Brands Group, Olsam) buying at 10-20% of 2021 cadence; and (4) operator buyers (family offices, search funds) using seller financing.

Current valuation multiples in 2026 are channel-specific: Amazon FBA brands trade at 2.5-3.5x SDE (vs 5-7x in mid-2021); profitable Shopify DTC brands trade at 3-5x SDE (or 4-6x EBITDA above ~$2M EBITDA); subscription/recurring revenue businesses trade at 4-7x EBITDA with premiums for sub-5% monthly churn; and content-plus-commerce hybrids trade at 5-8x EBITDA. The market has shifted from growth-first to profit-first underwriting, with SDE standard below ~$3M bottom-line earnings and EBITDA above that threshold, both measured on trailing twelve months (TTM).

The 2021 aggregator bust was caused by four factors: multiple inflation (3x to 7x SDE bidding war), post-pandemic demand normalization, Amazon cost inflation (fees, ads, storage), and operational complexity. Over 90 FBA aggregators raised capital between 2020-2022 (Thrasio $3.4B+, Razor $1B+, Perch $908M, etc.), most of which failed or restructured.

Key diligence red flags for ecommerce deals include: Amazon Seller Central data integrity mismatches, IP gaps (utility patents, registered trademarks), supplier concentration (over 60% of COGS), SKU concentration (over 50% of revenue cuts multiples by at least half a turn), channel concentration (over 80% Amazon or 60% single paid channel), and subscription churn over 10% monthly. The Amazon Seller Central account transfer is a critical operational risk — entity-level acquisitions preserve account history, while asset deals reset performance metrics and ad campaigns (4-8 week revenue dips).

Notable deals worth studying include: e.l.f. Beauty's acquisition of Naturium (August 2024, ~$355M, ~5x trailing revenue), Razor-Perch merger (mid-2024), Thrasio's Chapter 11 filing (February 2024, ~$3B debt), and Liquid Death's ~$1.4B valuation. Recommended preparation for sale (12-24 months) covers financial cleanup, operational documentation, customer data hygiene, inventory rationalization, customer concentration mitigation, legal/IP cleanup, and buyer-readiness research. Typical sale processes run 4-9 months (3-6 for aggregators/operators, 6-9 for strategic/PE), with most deals falling apart over diligence findings, inventory surprises, IP gaps, or buyer-founder fit issues.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 1: Temu and Shein face the rulebook that European retailers live with every day ---
URL: https://webiano.digital/temu-and-shein-face-the-rulebook-that-european-retailers-live-with-every-day

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from Webiano Digital (published June 4, 2026, by Jan Bielik) analyzes the recent regulatory enforcement actions against Chinese-linked ultra-low-price e-commerce platforms Shein and Temu in Europe. The piece argues that European authorities are treating these platforms as infrastructure that must bear the same legal duties as any consumer business selling at scale.

**Key regulatory actions covered:**
- **France fined Shein approximately €22.5 million** (announced June 3, 2026, by the DGCCRF) through two administrative fines: €16,733,190 against Infinite Styles Services Co Limited (site operator) for non-compliant order confirmations sent to consumers, and €5,764,500 against Infinite Styles Ecommerce Co Limited (seller) for violations of withdrawal rights and environmental information requirements (including absence of information on product traceability and plastic microfibres). These followed a July 2025 DGCCRF fine of €40 million against Shein for misleading discounts and environmental claims, where investigators found 57% of verified discount announcements offered no actual price reduction, 19% offered smaller reductions, and 11% were price increases.
- **The European Commission fined Temu €200 million** (May 28, 2026) under the Digital Services Act for failing to properly identify, analyze and assess systemic risks linked to illegal products on its platform. The Commission gave Temu until August 28, 2026, to present a credible action plan.
- Separately, the CNIL (French data protection authority) fined Infinite Styles Services Co Limited €150 million in September 2025 for cookie compliance failures, noting the Shein site averaged 12 million France-resident visitors per month.

**Key legal and policy themes:**
- The Shein fines center on basic consumer information required by EU/French distance-selling law: the price of goods, delivery dates, seller identity and contact details, legal guarantee information, mediation access, withdrawal forms, and 14-day withdrawal rights. The DGCCRF argues that missing statutory information constitutes legal harm to consumers even before financial loss is shown.
- Order confirmations are described as legal evidence trails and due on a "durable medium"; the article emphasizes that with millions of low-value transactions, small omissions become platform-wide systemic compliance failures.
- Temu's DSA penalty targets risk governance and platform architecture — recommender systems, algorithmic amplification of illegal products, and design that increases visibility of unsafe goods — marking a shift where "the DSA turns platform architecture into evidence."
- The article notes enforcement is cumulative across multiple legal frameworks: consumer law (DGCCRF), platform law (DSA), data protection (CNIL), product safety (General Product Safety Regulation), and environmental rules (AGEC law on waste-generating products).
- Both Shein (108 million average monthly EU users) and Temu (75 million) are designated Very Large Online Platforms under the DSA (threshold: 45 million), with Ireland as their Digital Services Coordinator jurisdiction.
- Context noted: EU textile consumption rose from 17 kg per person in 2019 to 19 kg per person in 2022; the European Commission's textiles strategy says "fast fashion should be 'out of fashion'."
- Enforcement timeline included the October 2024 Commission investigation into Temu, November 2024 CPC Network notification to Temu, May 2025 CPC notification to Shein, February 17, 2026 Commission investigation into Shein over addictive design, recommender transparency and illegal products, and the November 2025 French government removal of illicit products from Shein (including childlike sex dolls and banned weapons).
- A DGCCRF product test in 2025 found 75% of 600+ products from seven foreign online platforms failed EU rules, with 46% both non-compliant and dangerous.
- The article frames these actions as level-playing-field enforcement rather than protectionism: "any platform selling into the EU must meet EU consumer and safety standards," noting principles could apply to AliExpress, Amazon Marketplace, TikTok Shop, Wish and dropshipping sites.
- Shein disputes the sanctions as disproportionate and has said it will contest them; the article notes French courts rejected total marketplace suspensions in December 2025 and March 2026 while ordering tighter controls.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Low prices do not dilute legal duties. Scale raises the duty, because failures at platform level reach millions of consumers at once."
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: EU Turns to Online Marketplaces After Record AliExpress ... ---
URL: https://techpolicy.press/eu-turns-to-online-marketplaces-after-record-aliexpress-fine

SUMMARY:
<summary>
The European Commission fined AliExpress €550 million on Monday (July 20, 2026) for failing to adequately assess and mitigate risks posed by illegal, unsafe, and counterfeit products on its platform — the largest penalty issued to date under the Digital Services Act (DSA), and the third overall. The fine surpasses the €200 million penalty against Temu (May 2026) and the €120 million against X (December 2025).

AliExpress, which had 193 million European users last year, called the decision disproportionate and stated it is reviewing its options, arguing the fine ignored its "sound risk management framework and the significant, proactive enhancements." The Commission found AliExpress failed to properly evaluate whether it had enough resources to monitor potentially illegal products, overstated the effectiveness of its detection and removal systems, and did not adequately consider how its recommendation and advertising tools could increase visibility of illegal goods. Investigators found counterfeit products, unsafe toys, and dangerous cosmetics remaining available after being flagged.

The decision reflects a broader shift in the EU's enforcement focus under the DSA — moving beyond social media platforms toward online marketplaces facilitating physical goods sales. The European Board for Digital Services' second annual risk report (July 1) identified illegal products sold through online marketplaces as one of the most persistent systemic risks, including challenges of sellers evading controls by modifying listings or returning under new identities.

All three major Chinese e-commerce platforms in Europe now face DSA oversight: Temu was fined in May and must submit an action plan by Aug. 28; Shein faces formal proceedings (no fine yet) over illegal products, addictive design features, and recommendation transparency; and AliExpress now has its fine. One in five Europeans shops from the three platforms at least monthly. These enforcement actions run alongside a new €3 customs charge on parcels below €150 from China (effective July 1).

The fine does not conclude the DSA process: AliExpress must submit a remedial action plan by Oct. 20, the Board has one month to issue an opinion, followed by a further month for the Commission to adopt a final decision. Failure to comply could trigger additional periodic penalty payments. This process will test how the EU's post-fine enforcement model works, particularly the gap between the Board's independent opinions and the Commission's final decisions (as seen with X's accepted plan). The Commission noted the relatively early stage of DSA enforcement was considered in calculating the penalty, meaning future cases could see higher sanctions. AliExpress had prior June 2025 binding commitments, but the Commission found they lacked specific, measurable targets and external verification mechanisms — which did not prevent Monday's fine.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"The spread of counterfeit clothing, unsafe toys, dangerous cosmetics and other illegal and harmful products is not an unavoidable cost of shopping online," said Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission's executive vice president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy. "Scale is not an excuse; risks must be identified and addressed systematically to ensure consumers can safely shop online."
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 3: EU Law Analysis: Digital Services Act: summary and links ---
URL: http://eulawanalysis.blogspot.com/2026/02/digital-services-act-summary-and-links.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This blog post by Professor Steve Peers (Royal Holloway University of London) provides a comprehensive summary and resource links regarding the EU's Digital Services Act (DSA), published February 20, 2026. The DSA regulates online platforms and search engines generally, but imposes special requirements on 'very large online platforms' (VLOPs) and 'very large online search engines' (VLOSEs) — those visited by 10% of the EU population monthly, designated by the European Commission. Designated companies include US firms (Meta, X, Google, LinkedIn), Chinese firms (AliExpress, TikTok, Temu, Shein), EU firms (Booking.com, Zalando, two porn sites), and Canada's Pornhub; nearly half of designated VLOP/VLOSE operators are non-American.

Enforcement against VLOPs can involve requests for information, investigations, preliminary findings, and final breach decisions with fines up to 6% of worldwide annual turnover, or binding commitments (settlements) to avoid fines. Non-compliance can trigger daily fines of up to 5% of global turnover. A ban on a platform requires a very high threshold. Substantive obligations (Articles 33-43) include systemic risk assessment, risk mitigation, crisis response, independent audits, non-profiling recommender system options, advertising repositories, researcher data access, algorithm explanations to regulators, compliance bodies, and annual supervisory fees.

Key court developments: Amazon and Zalando lost General Court challenges to their VLOP designation (appeals to CJEU pending); porn companies' challenges are pending. In the Amazon judgment, the General Court rejected arguments that the VLOP regime breached Charter rights to conduct business, property, equal treatment, freedom of expression, and privacy, but upheld justified limitations. Regulation fee decisions for 2023 were struck down by the General Court (TikTok, Meta), with Commission appeals pending. X, X.AI, and Elon Musk challenged the December 2025 non-compliance decision against X. The Commission is suing Spain for non-enforcement at national level.

Enforcement actions: The Commission made its first final non-compliance decision against X in December 2025, fining it €120 million for deceptive 'blue tick' practices, restricted researcher data access, and advertiser repository issues; proceedings continue on illegal content, disinformation, recommender systems, and 'nudification' apps. Other actions include: accepted commitments from AliExpress (plus preliminary finding on risk assessment), proceedings against porn sites on child protection, preliminary findings against Meta (researcher access, content moderation flagging) and Temu (illegal products), accepted TikTok commitments (Lite suspension, advertising transparency) plus preliminary findings on researcher access and addictive design, and an investigation into Shein (illegal content, recommender systems, addictive design).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"The DSA contains rules that govern online platforms generally, regardless of size, but its most prominent rules concern a special regulatory regime for the biggest platforms, defined as 'very large online platforms' (VLOPs) and 'very large online search engines' (VLOSEs)."
</key_excerpts>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This page from the European Commission describes enforcement actions and dialogues by the Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Network against various digital marketplaces and online services to ensure compliance with EU consumer law.

Key actions include:

- **SHEIN (May 2025):** The CPC Network notified the online marketplace of practices infringing EU consumer law, covering a broad range of shopping practices. SHEIN remains under investigation and must provide further information. The CPC is also assessing compliance with obligations on rankings, reviews, ratings, and transparency about third-party sellers. This action is complementary to a separate Commission enforcement action under the Digital Services Act (DSA).

- **Apple (November 2024):** The CPC Network notified Apple of geo-blocking practices on Apple Media Services (App Store, Apple Arcade, Music, iTunes Store, Books, Podcasts) that unlawfully discriminate European consumers based on residence. The actions invoke the Geo-blocking Regulation and the Services Directive.

- **Temu (November 2024):** The CPC Network notified Temu of practices infringing consumer law and directed it to bring practices in line with EU law. The investigation covers shopping practices as well as additional obligations on seller transparency, non-misleading rankings/reviews/ratings, correct price reductions, and substantiated environmental claims.

- **Vinted:** Following dialogue, Vinted modified its website and app to better inform consumers about total prices and refunds, addressing complaints about automatic 'buyer protection fees' added at check-out. However, Vinted did not agree on informing consumers that displayed prices exclude delivery fees or minimum delivery fees at the start of purchase.

- **Viagogo (dialogue since April 2021):** The secondary ticket marketplace committed to better inform consumers about resale conditions and avoid excessive countdown pressure, addressing complaints about unclear taxes and fees. It agreed to changes by end of August 2024 but did not commit to all CPC Network requests.

- **Tinder (dialogue since July 2022, led by Swedish Consumer Agency and Netherlands ACM):** Tinder committed to informing consumers how discounts for premium services are personalised using automated means. The issue was revealed in a Swedish study showing varying prices with no clear pattern. Tinder committed to changes by mid-April 2024.

- **PayPal:** Following dialogue led by the German Environment Agency, PayPal committed to making its terms and conditions more transparent. Changes were notified via Policy Update on 21 February 2024, effective 28 May 2024.

- **Shopify (led by Belgium's DG Economic Inspection):** Shopify agreed to create a fast notice and action procedure for Consumer Authorities and change templates to increase trader transparency ('compliance by design'), amid complaints about fake offers, fake scarcity, counterfeit goods, and delivery issues from hosted stores.

- **Amazon Prime:** Following a complaint by BEUC, the Norwegian Consumer Council and Transatlantic Consumer Dialogue, Amazon committed to enabling EU/EEA consumers to unsubscribe with two clicks via a prominent cancel button, implemented on all EU websites and devices by 1 July 2022.

- **Parship:** The dating website improved information on right of withdrawal and automatic contract renewal following dialogue coordinated by the Belgian DG for Economic Inspection.

- **AliExpress and Wish (led by Netherlands ACM):** Obtained EU-wide commitments. AliExpress committed (2021 and 2022) to better inform consumers about legal action/complaint options and improved terms of service transparency and import fee information. Wish increased price transparency, implemented a new interface against misleading discounts, and stopped personalised pricing in the EU as of 1 June 2022.

For ongoing actions, if companies fail to address concerns, national authorities can take enforcement measures including sanctions.

This article by Manuela Tchoe (Senior Strategic Content Manager at commercetools), published March 27, 2026, outlines eight best practices for enterprise-grade B2B commerce implementation, emphasizing the shift from monolithic to modern composable commerce platforms.
